Reasons, in this order: per family, the other variant's tables — `<tool>-<other> table <t>: <incompatible note>`, `<tool>-<other> table <t> chain <c> holds <n> rule(s) outside the <variant> variant UFW uses`, `<tool>-<other> table <t> chain <c> has policy <P> outside the <variant> variant UFW uses`; then, when `nf_tables` is loaded, `install the nftables package so Darkpanel can read every rule` (no `nft`), `nft list tables printed "<line>", which Darkpanel cannot read`, `nft table "<name>" in family "<family>": table name not readable safely`, `nft table <family> <name>: <parse error>`, `nft table <family> <name>: base chain "<c>" on hook "<h>" has <n> rule(s) and policy <p>` (`(none printed)` when nft printed no policy). Tables of a family whose `ip`/`ip6` tables a save tool read (own variant `nft`, or own `legacy` with `nf_tables` loaded) are not listed again. Unexported: `type famState struct{ f family; variant string; rs *netfilter.Ruleset }`, `func foreign(ctx context.Context, x core.Runner, procNet string, nftLoaded bool, fams []famState) ([]string, error)`, `foreignTables`, `nativeTables`, `nfTablesLoaded`, `otherVariant`, `nftSafeName`, `nftFamilies`, `nftModule`, `nftMissing`.

**Task 60 — sysctl values, `internal/modules/firewall/loaded/sysctl_read.go`, `read.go`.** `Read` sets `Loaded.Sysctl` to the values of `net/ipv4/ip_forward` and, for `all`, `default` and each non-loopback interface of `Interfaces()` in its order, `net/ipv6/conf/<x>/forwarding`, `net/ipv6/conf/<x>/accept_ra`, `net/ipv4/conf/<x>/rp_filter`, `net/ipv4/conf/<x>/accept_source_route` — keys in `/proc/sys` form, values as `ReadSysctl` returns them. A key whose read fails wrapping `fs.ErrNotExist` is absent; another failure is `loaded: <error>`; an `Interfaces` failure is `loaded: <error>`. An interface named `all` or `default`, or not matching `^[A-Za-z0-9_.@-]{1,15}$`, adds the reason `interface "<name>": Darkpanel cannot read its sysctl values` and is not read. `Sysctl` is non-nil after a successful `Read`. Unexported: `module = "firewall"`, `keyIPForward`, `sysctlIface`, `sysctlParams`, `func sysctlKeys(ifaces []netstat.Interface) (keys, reasons []string)`, `func readSysctl(ctx context.Context, files core.FileWriter, keys []string) (map[string]string, error)`.

**Task 49 — sysctl prediction, `internal/modules/firewall/loaded/sysctl_predict.go`.**

```go
func PredictSysctl(cfg fwstate.Config, cur map[string]string, tr fwstate.Transition) (map[string]string, error)
```

Returns a new map (never `cur`, never nil on success). It applies `cfg.Sysctl` only for `TransEnable`, and for `TransReload` when `cfg.Enabled`; otherwise it returns a copy of `cur`. Settings for which `conf.SupportedSysctl` is false are ignored; a supported setting whose value does not match `^[01]$` (`ip_forward`, `forwarding`, `accept_source_route`) or `^[012]$` (`accept_ra`, `rp_filter`) is refused, whether or not `cur` holds the key; otherwise a key `cur` lacks is skipped; `net/ipv6/conf/all/forwarding` also sets every `net/ipv6/conf/*/forwarding` key `cur` holds; a changed `net/ipv4/conf/default/{rp_filter,accept_source_route}` is refused while some interface key of that parameter (not `all`, not written earlier in the file) equals the old default. Refusals are `*errcode.Error{Code: errcode.FirewallUnsupportedConfiguration}` with the details `<SysctlFile> sets <key> to "<value>"; Darkpanel supports only values matching <pattern>` and `<SysctlFile> sets <key> to <value>, which the kernel may also copy to <interface key>; Darkpanel cannot predict that, so set the interface's own value earlier in the file`.

**Task 50 — comparison, `internal/modules/firewall/loaded/compare.go`.**

```go
func Compare(a, b fwstate.Loaded, keep func(f fwstate.Family, table, chain string) bool) []fwstate.ChainDiff
```

One `ChainDiff` per differing chain that `keep` selects (nil: all), ordered by family (`v4`, `v6`), table (`netfilter.Tables()` order, then other names sorted) and chain name; nil when nothing differs. A nil ruleset is a family without tables. Keys are `netfilter.Key(rule, family == fwstate.V6)`. `PolicyA`/`PolicyB` are set only when the built-in policies differ, a missing built-in chain counting as `ACCEPT`; `OnlyA`/`OnlyB` are the keys the other side lacks, counting duplicates, in each side's order (nil when none); `OrderDiffers` is true when the keys both sides hold appear in a different order. A missing built-in chain with no rules and policy `ACCEPT` on the other side is no difference; a user chain on one side only is always a difference, even with nothing else set.

#### How the next parts use it

- **Reading the host (status, plan, apply, verify, snapshots).** `st, err := loaded.Reader{}.Read(ctx, env)` with the module's `env` (`env.Exec` the agent's runner, `env.Files` the agent's `Files`). An error means the loaded state is unreadable: status reports it and every plan fails; it is never an empty firewall. `len(st.Unsupported) > 0` is spec 2.1's unsupported configuration, exactly like `len(cfg.Unsupported) > 0`: status shows the reasons, every guard verdict is `unknown`, every mutating action refuses with `firewall.unsupported_configuration`. The firewall manifest must declare the five sysctl owned paths of spec 2.1 (`net/ipv4/ip_forward` `^[01]$`, `net/ipv6/conf/<iface>/forwarding` `^[01]$`, `net/ipv6/conf/<iface>/accept_ra` `^[012]$`, `net/ipv4/conf/<iface>/rp_filter` `^[012]$`, `net/ipv4/conf/<iface>/accept_source_route` `^[01]$`); without them `ReadSysctl` refuses and `Read` fails with `loaded: platform: module firewall does not declare sysctl …`.
- **Tests of later parts** construct `loaded.Reader{Interfaces: …, NFTablesLoaded: func() bool { return false }}` and an `env` with fake `Exec` and `Files`; with golden nft captures (no legacy warning) `Read` touches nothing of the host. With the legacy variant, or a save output carrying the legacy warning, it reads the host's `/proc/net/ip*_tables_names`.
- **In sync (2.3).** `pred` is the predict part's loaded state for the current configured state, computed from `st`; then `diffs := loaded.Compare(pred, st, nil)`: any diff marks the host out of sync and the plan lists `Family Table Chain`, the policies and the keys. The repair exception is decided by the caller from the diffs' chain names (UFW's `ufw-*`/`ufw6-*` and Darkpanel's `DOCKER-USER`, `darkpanel-*`, `dp-b-*` only).
- **Verify (2.3).** After apply: `after, err := loaded.Reader{}.Read(ctx, env)`, then `loaded.Compare(predicted, after, keep)` with `keep` selecting the UFW chains, the built-in chains and every chain a protected flow traverses; a non-empty result fails verify with `firewall.prediction_mismatch`. A repair's verify compares against its loaded-state before-image the same way.
- **Sysctl (2.1).** `next, err := loaded.PredictSysctl(cfgAfter, st.Sysctl, tr)`: an error is returned as is (it is already `firewall.unsupported_configuration`, a hard refusal); every key whose value differs between `st.Sysctl` and `next` is shown in the plan. The guard evaluates the target state with `next` (for example `rp_filter` eligibility: the maximum of `net/ipv4/conf/all/rp_filter` and `net/ipv4/conf/<iface>/rp_filter`), and `ip_forward` 0 under a forwarded protected flow fails it; an IPv6 forwarding change on a host whose default IPv6 route came from router advertisements is `unknown` (the guard part's rule). Snapshots record `st.Sysctl` as the before-values; revert writes them back with `WriteSysctl`, `all` and `default` first.
- **Predictor.** `predict.Predict` takes `st` as `cur`: the tables `Read` returns are the save tool's view, so a table the kernel lacks under the nft variant is present with empty built-in chains and policy `ACCEPT`, and `Compare` treats that the same as an absent table.

### Part P contracts (Tasks 38, 46, 51, 57, 58, 61, 104)

**Task 38 — rendering, `internal/modules/firewall/predict/render.go`.**

```go
func Files(cfg fwstate.Config) (map[string][]byte, error)
```

`Files` returns exactly four entries, keyed `/etc/ufw/user.rules`, `/etc/ufw/user6.rules`, `/etc/ufw/ufw.conf` and `/etc/default/ufw`. They hold the bytes UFW writes for `cfg` the next time it writes each file:

- `user.rules` from `cfg.Rules4` and `user6.rules` from `cfg.Rules6`, as `_write_rules` writes them: the header's 14 chain declarations, then `ufw[6]-user-limit` and `-limit-accept`; `### RULES ###`; for each tuple a blank line, its `### tuple ###` line (from the tuple's fields, the comment re-encoded as lower-case hex) and its iptables lines; then `### END RULES ###`, the `### LOGGING ###` section for `cfg.LogLevel` and the default policies, the `### RATE LIMITING ###` section, and `COMMIT`. Rate limiting is taken as available in IPv4, and in IPv6 when IPv6 is on. With IPv6 off, UFW holds no IPv6 rules and skips the IPv6 capability check, so `user6.rules` renders with no limit chains, no tuples, no logging rules and no rate-limit section.
- `ufw.conf` and `/etc/default/ufw` are `cfg.Files`' bytes with each key rewritten only when UFW would read its value differently from `cfg`. UFW reads them as `_get_defaults` does: lower-cased, quotes stripped, last assignment wins. The keys are `ENABLED` (`yes`/`no`), `LOGLEVEL` and `DEFAULT_{INPUT,OUTPUT,FORWARD}_POLICY`, the policies written quoted. A rewrite works as `set_default` does: every `KEY=` line is replaced, or the line is appended when none exists.
- Errors: a log level other than `off`, `low`, `medium`, `high` or `full`, or a policy other than `ACCEPT`, `DROP` or `REJECT`.

Unexported names later tasks use: `const userRules, userRules6, ufwConf, defaultsUFW` (the four paths); `var logLevels map[string]int` (off 0, low 100, medium 200, high 300, full 400); `checkRenderable(cfg fwstate.Config) error` (the errors above); `chainPrefix(v6 bool) string` (`"ufw"` or `"ufw6"`); `renderUser(cfg fwstate.Config, v6 bool) []byte`; `tupleLine(t model.Tuple) string`; `multiPort(t model.Tuple) bool` (a list or range in either port); `formatRule(t model.Tuple) string` (`format_rule`); `rulesFromFormatted(frule, prefix, suffix string) []string` (`_get_rules_from_formatted`, each line ending in `\n`); `loggingRules(cfg fwstate.Config, p string) [][]string` (`_get_logging_rules` for chain prefix `p`, each rule as the argument list UFW passes to iptables, the chain second); `setDefault(data []byte, opt, value string) []byte`; `ufwDefaults(data []byte) map[string]string`.

**Task 46 — vectors, `internal/modules/firewall/predict/vector.go` (all unexported).**

```go
type vector struct {
	kind     string       // vecRule, vecDefault, vecLogging, vecEnable, vecDisable or vecReload
	rule     model.Tuple  // rule: Src/Dst "0.0.0.0/0" for any, Family unset, Raw empty
	iptype   model.Family // rule: FamilyV4, FamilyV6 or FamilyBoth
	remove   bool         // rule: delete
	position int          // rule: insert position, 0 to append
	policy   string       // default: allow, deny or reject
	chain    string       // default: INPUT, OUTPUT or FORWARD
	level    string       // logging: off, on, low, medium, high or full
}
func parseVector(args []string) (vector, error)
func forFamily(t model.Tuple, fam model.Family) (model.Tuple, error)
func normalizeTuple(t model.Tuple) (model.Tuple, error)
func normalizeAddr(s string, v6 bool) (string, error)
func sortPorts(s string) string
```

`parseVector` accepts `--force enable`, `disable`, `reload`, `default <allow|deny|reject> <incoming|outgoing|routed>`, `logging <off|on|low|medium|high|full>`, and the rule form `[route] [delete | insert <n≥1>] <allow|deny|reject|limit> [in|out [on IF]] [in|out on IF (route only)] [log|log-all] {proto P | from A [port P] | to A [port P] | comment C}`. A rule's family follows UFW: both when both addresses are any, otherwise the family of the address given; `0.0.0.0/0` is v4 and `::/0` is v6; `ipv6` and `igmp` force v4. It refuses, with `predict: ufw <args>: <why>`: any other vector; ports that are not numeric; more than 15 multiport slots; a list or range without tcp or udp; ports with a port-less protocol; an IPv4-only protocol with IPv6; mixed families; zones; dotted netmasks; interface names outside `^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_.+-]{0,14}$`; a comment containing `'` or invalid UTF-8; and a rule with neither an address nor an interface clause. `forFamily` turns any into the family's form, normalizes, sets `Family` and sets `Raw` to `tupleLine`. `normalizeAddr` drops a host prefix length, prints the address in its standard text form, masks an IPv4 network (IPv6 keeps its host bits) and turns a contiguous dotted mask into a prefix length. `sortPorts` sorts a list as `human_sort` does.

Shared test helper (`vector_test.go`): `func predictShellSplit(line string) []string` splits a `commands.txt` line on spaces, with single quotes grouping.

**Task 57 — the command simulator, `internal/modules/firewall/predict/edit.go`.**

```go
func Edit(cfg fwstate.Config, args []string) (fwstate.Config, error)
```

`Edit` returns the configured state after ufw runs `args` on `cfg`. `Enabled`, `LogLevel`, `Default*`, `Rules4` and `Rules6` are as UFW leaves them. In `Files`, every file the command writes takes its new bytes and keeps its metadata; a file the command leaves alone keeps its bytes. The commands write:

- a rule command writes `user.rules` and/or `user6.rules`, only for a family whose list changed. Existing tuples are normalized as `set_rule` normalizes them, and every tuple of a rewritten family gets `Raw = tupleLine`, so the result equals `conf.Read` of the files ufw writes. An existing identical rule (or a matching insert) and a delete that matches nothing change nothing;
- `logging` writes `LOGLEVEL` and both rule files; `on` keeps the level, or chooses `low` when logging is off;
- `--force enable` writes `ENABLED=yes` when it was off, and both rule files;
- `disable` writes `ENABLED=no` when it was on;
- `reload` writes `ENABLED` no then yes, and both rule files, when enabled; it does nothing otherwise;
- `default` writes the quoted policy and switches `UFW BLOCK`/`UFW ALLOW` in `after.rules` and `after6.rules`, as `set_default_policy` does for any chain. When UFW is enabled it also writes both rule files.

With IPv6 off, writing `user6.rules` empties it and sets `Rules6` to nil. Errors (`predict: `): every `parseVector` refusal; an unrenderable `cfg`; an invalid position or an IPv6 rule with IPv6 off (ufw prints `Invalid position` or `IPv6 support not enabled`); and a file the command must write that is absent. Unexported names: `cloneConfig(c fwstate.Config) fwstate.Config` (copies the slices and the `Files` map); `const afterRules, afterRules6`; `matchTuple(x, y model.Tuple) int` (`UFWRule.match`: 0, -2, -1 or 1); `ruleCount(rules []model.Tuple) int`; `appTuple(t model.Tuple) string`.

**Task 51 — translation, `internal/modules/firewall/predict/translate.go` (unexported).**

```go
var directions = []string{"input", "output", "forward"}
var primaryChains []string // the 18 chains ufw_start creates once, without the prefix
func restoreText(cfg fwstate.Config, v6 bool) (string, error)
func translate(cfg fwstate.Config, v6 bool) (*netfilter.Ruleset, error)
```

`restoreText` is the restore input `ufw_start` loads for one family on a host without UFW's chains, in its order: primary chains and their 18 jumps; `-A ufw[6]-reject-<d> -j REJECT` for each REJECT policy; the two track rules for each ACCEPT policy; the logging-deny and logging-allow chains; the skip-to-policy chains `-j <POLICY>`; `before[6].rules`, `after[6].rules`; the eight user chains; `user[6].rules`; the three hooks into the user chains; and the built-in policies, with REJECT loaded as DROP. Every file is taken from `cfg.Files`, with a newline added if missing. A missing or empty before, after or user file is an error. `translate` parses it with `netfilter.ParseRestore`; its filter table holds UFW's chains, and another table appears only when `before.rules` or `after.rules` write to one.

Shared test helpers (`translate_test.go`): `func predictLoaded(t *testing.T, image, scenario string) fwstate.Loaded` (the ten save captures through `netfilter.Parse`, `sysctl.txt`, `Variant "nft"`); `func predictDiff(a, b *netfilter.Ruleset, v6 bool) []string` (every table or chain on one side only, every differing built-in policy, every chain whose `netfilter.Key` list differs); `func predictKeys(c *netfilter.Chain, v6 bool) []string`.

**Task 58 — transitions, `internal/modules/firewall/predict/predict.go`.**

```go
func Predict(cfg fwstate.Config, cur fwstate.Loaded, tr fwstate.Transition) (fwstate.Loaded, error)
```

`Predict` returns the loaded state after `tr`. `Variant`, `Sysctl` and `Unsupported` are copied from `cur`; every chain UFW does not manage keeps its rules and position; `cur` is not modified.

- `TransEnable` (`start_firewall`). For each family ip6tables serves (`cur.V6 != nil`):
  - with IPv6 off, the IPv6 filter table becomes exactly `:INPUT DROP`, `:FORWARD DROP`, `:OUTPUT DROP`, `-A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT`, `-A OUTPUT -o lo -j ACCEPT`;
  - otherwise the translation is loaded with `--noflush` semantics: UFW's user chains take the translation's rules; built-in chains get the translation's rules appended, with the translation's policies. The filter table's built-in jumps are appended only when `ufw[6]-before-logging-input` does not exist yet; otherwise `delete_chains` runs first and the existing jumps stay put. Then the live part of `update_logging` runs: the before, after and misc logging chains are flushed and refilled for `cfg.LogLevel` and the policies, the user logging chains' bare RETURN is removed (or reinserted when logging is off), and the limit LOG rule moves to the top of `ufw[6]-user-limit` (or is removed when logging is off).
  - It is an error when `ufw-user-input` is loaded already (`ufw_start` would skip; use `TransReload`).
- `TransReload`: stop, then start; `cur` unchanged when `!cfg.Enabled`.
- `TransDisable` (`ufw_stop`): UFW's chains of `chains_command` are flushed; its secondary chains are deleted unless a rule still jumps to them; INPUT, OUTPUT and FORWARD get policy ACCEPT. A host where UFW never started gets no UFW chain.
- `TransNone`: a copy of `cur`.
- Errors: `cur.V4 == nil`, an unknown transition, `len(cfg.Unsupported) > 0` for a start, and every `translate` error.

Unexported names: `var filterBuiltins = []string{"INPUT", "FORWARD", "OUTPUT"}`; `cloneRuleset(rs *netfilter.Ruleset) *netfilter.Ruleset`. Shared test helper (`predict_test.go`): `func predictTestChain(t *testing.T, table, chain, policy string, rules ...string) *netfilter.Chain` parses rules written as `iptables -S` prints them, declaring each `ufw*` jump target.

**Task 61 — the IPV6=no refusal, `internal/modules/firewall/predict/refusal.go`.**

```go
func IPv6Refusal(cfg fwstate.Config, cur fwstate.Loaded, tr fwstate.Transition) error
```

`IPv6Refusal` returns nil unless all of these hold: `!cfg.IPv6`; `tr` is `TransEnable`, or `TransReload` with `cfg.Enabled`; and `cur.V6`'s filter table holds a chain that is neither built-in nor `ufw6-*`, or a built-in-chain rule that is neither a bare jump to a `ufw6-` chain nor the plain table's `-i lo -j ACCEPT` (INPUT) / `-o lo -j ACCEPT` (OUTPUT). In that case it returns `errcode.New(errcode.FirewallUnsupportedConfiguration, detail)`. The detail names every such item, as `chain <name>` or `<CHAIN> rule <n> (<rule text>)`, and ends with `set IPV6=yes in /etc/default/ufw`.

#### How the next parts use it

- **Configured state of an action (actions part).** `cfg0, err := conf.Read("/")`. For each ufw vector the action runs, in order (`model.AddArgs`, `DeleteArgs`, `InsertArgs`, `default …`, `logging …`), compute `cfgI, err := predict.Edit(cfgPrev, args)`. An error refuses the plan, because Darkpanel cannot predict that command. Each effect's expected before-state hash is `sha256(cfgPrev.Files[p].Data)` and its after-state hash is `sha256(cfgI.Files[p].Data)`, for every path whose bytes differ (spec 2.5). Call the result `cfgN`.
- **Transition.** The actions part chooses `tr`: `TransReload` after rule, default or logging changes when `cfgN.Enabled`; `TransEnable` for `state.enable` and for a restore that starts UFW (the 2.5 table); `TransDisable`; `TransNone`. Then:
  1. `predict.IPv6Refusal(cfgN, cur, tr)` → a hard refusal (not overridable), for enable, reload and restore alike;
  2. `pred, err := predict.Predict(cfgN, cur, tr)`, with `cfgN` taken before the transition's own command;
  3. `cfgFinal, err := predict.Edit(cfgN, []string{"--force", "enable"} | {"reload"} | {"disable"})` gives the configured state and post-apply file hashes after that command (none for `TransNone`);
  4. `pred.Sysctl, err = loaded.PredictSysctl(cfgFinal, cur.Sysctl, tr)` (part C);
  5. `guard.Check(ctx, env, pred, in)` (part G);
  6. after apply, `loaded.Compare(pred, after, keep)`; a difference fails verify with `firewall.prediction_mismatch`.
- **Restore (part A1).** Build `cfgS` from the snapshot's entries (`conf.Read` of the restored files, or the snapshot's logical state). The transition follows 2.5's table from `cfgS.Enabled` and the current state. The prediction is `Predict(cfgS, cur, tr)`, preceded by `IPv6Refusal(cfgS, cur, tr)`.
- **In sync (spec 2.3) and repair.** For an enabled UFW, compare `predict.Predict(cfg0, cur, fwstate.TransReload)` with `cur` through `loaded.Compare`; `firewall.state.repair` plans exactly that reload. One exception, which part A2 resolves by running `ufw reload` right after a first enable (controller ruling): right after the first `ufw --force enable` on a fresh install, the loaded IPv6 limit chains come from the package's template `user6.rules` (Assumptions), so this comparison reports `ufw6-user-limit` and `ufw6-user-limit-accept` until the next reload.
- **Rendering.** `predict.Files(cfg)` is what UFW writes at its next full write. For a configuration UFW wrote last it equals `cfg.Files`; the tests prove this for every golden scenario.

An invalid packet or a nil ruleset returns `{Verdict: Unknown, Reason: "eval: …"}` with an empty trace. `route` may be nil when nothing on the path rewrites the destination or the mark.

- `type markSpec struct{ setVal, setMask, nfmask, ctmask uint32; set, save, restore bool }`; `func parseMarkTarget(tg netfilter.Target) (markSpec, bool)`; `func (w *walker) markTarget(tg netfilter.Target, ref string) outcome`; `func (w *walker) uncertainCopy(tg netfilter.Target) bool`.
- `module` dispatches `mark`/`connmark` to `markMatch`; `target` dispatches `MARK`/`CONNMARK` to `markTarget`; `walkChain` lets `uncertainCopy` absorb an undecidable `CONNMARK --save-mark`/`--restore-mark`; `reroute` also runs when the mark changed and passes the current mark in `Packet.Mark`.

**Task 42 — `match.go`, the source-port contract.** `Packet.SrcPort == 0` means the source port is unknown: the guard's flows describe connections that do not exist yet, whose source port the kernel has not chosen. `portOption` then returns `maybe` with the reason "the source port of a connection that does not exist yet is unknown" for `--sport` and `--sports` (in `tcp`, `udp` and `multiport`), negated or not, so the walk treats the rule as any undecidable rule: `Unknown` (`<ref>: the source port …`) when its target decides, ignored for no target, `LOG`, `TCPMSS`, `SNAT` and `MASQUERADE`; a false match elsewhere in the rule still makes it miss. A non-zero `SrcPort` is matched as before.

**Task 39, Task 47, Task 55** produce test files and fixtures only (`ufw_golden_test.go`; `docker28_test.go` and `testdata/docker28/{capture.sh,v4.save,v6.save,version.txt}`; `tailscale_test.go` and `testdata/tailscale/{v1.82-v4,v1.102-v4,v1.102-v6}.save`).

#### How the next parts use it

- **Guard (part G)** consumes the evaluator only through `guard.Input.Eval`, whose type is `Evaluate`'s signature. The wiring part (actions) passes `guard.Input{…, Eval: eval.Evaluate}`; nothing else imports `eval`.
- For each protected flow and each eligible in-interface the guard builds one `fwstate.Packet`: `Family` from the addresses; `Src`, `Dst`, `DstPort` from the flow; `SrcPort` 0, because the flow is a connection that does not exist yet (Task 42: a `--sport`/`--sports` rule that decides then makes the flow `unknown`); `Proto` `"tcp"` or `"udp"`; `CtState` `"NEW"`; `InIface` the candidate in-interface; `Path` and `OutIface` from a route lookup of `Dst` (`netstat.RouteGet(netstat.RouteQuery{Dst, Src, IIF: InIface, Mark})`: `Type` `"local"` → `Path` `"input"`, `OutIface` `""`; otherwise `"forward"` with `Route.OutIface`; a locally generated flow is `"output"` with the looked-up `OutIface`, `"lo"` for a local destination); `Mark` 0, except tailscaled's own flows, whose sockets carry tailscaled's bypass mark `0x80000` (tailscale `util/linuxfw/linuxfw.go`, `TailscaleBypassMark`).
- It then calls `Eval(st.V4, p, router)` or `Eval(st.V6, p, router)` on the predicted or loaded state, where `router` is a `fwstate.Router` wrapping the same `netstat.RouteGet` lookup (with `p.Mark` and `IIF` `p.InIface` for incoming packets) and returning `("input", "", nil)` for a local route, `("forward", OutIface, nil)` otherwise, `("output", OutIface, nil)` when `p.Path` is `"output"`, and an error when the lookup fails or `OutIface` is empty. The router is called at most once per walk.
- A `Result` whose `Verdict` is not `fwstate.Accept` fails the flow; `Reason` names the deciding rule and `Trace` the rules walked, for the guard's message. `fwstate.Loaded.V6` is nil when ip6tables is absent: `Evaluate` then returns `Unknown` ("eval: no ruleset for the packet's family"), so the guard decides before calling whether a missing IPv6 ruleset means "no IPv6 filtering" (Assumptions, controller item).
- Predictor and loaded-state reader (parts P, C) need nothing from part E; their `fwstate.Loaded` values are what the guard passes in.

**Task 36 — eligibility and routing (`internal/modules/firewall/guard/route.go`).** Unexported, used by Task 43:

```go
type probe struct {
	desc    string         // FlowResult.Flow
	pkt     fwstate.Packet // with its in- and out-interface
	unknown string         // non-empty: not evaluated, and why
}
type router struct{ host Host; f facts; st fwstate.Loaded; local map[netip.Addr]bool }
func newRouter(h Host, f facts, st fwstate.Loaded) *router
func (r *router) probes(fl flow) []probe
func (r *router) route(p fwstate.Packet) (string, string, error) // the fwstate.Router given to Eval
func describe(label string, p fwstate.Packet) string
```

`probes`: an incoming flow without a fixed in-interface yields one probe per eligible in-interface (every up, non-loopback interface; for IPv4, an interface whose effective `rp_filter` — the larger of `all` and the interface, each from `st.Sysctl` when it holds the key, else from the live facts — is 1 only when `RouteGet{Dst: source, Src: destination if local}` leaves through it); a fixed in-interface yields one probe; an output flow takes its out-interface (and an unspecified source, its preferred source) from `RouteGet{Dst, Src}`; a forwarded flow takes its out-interface from `RouteGet{Dst, Src, IIF}`. An unspecified destination becomes `RouteGet{Dst: source}.PrefSrc`. A failed lookup, a multipath answer (empty `OutIface`), no eligible interface, a non-numeric `rp_filter` in `st`, or `st.Sysctl` holding `net/ipv4/ip_forward` (IPv6: `net/ipv6/conf/all/forwarding`) `"0"` for a forwarded flow makes the flow one unknown probe; a stand-in destination whose lookup fails with `netstat.ErrNoRoute` yields no probe.

`route(p)` is called by the evaluator with the packet after nat `PREROUTING` (destination possibly rewritten): a loopback or host destination answers `"input", ""`; an `output` packet answers `"output"` and `RouteGet{Dst, Src}.OutIface`; any other packet errors when forwarding is off in `st`, and otherwise answers `"forward"` and `RouteGet{Dst, Src, IIF: p.InIface}.OutIface`, or `"input"` for a `local` route. A failed lookup or a multipath route is an error (`firewall:` prefix, wrapping the lookup error).

`describe`: `"<label>[ <proto> unless tcp] from <src> to <dst:port>[ on <in>][ out <out>]"`, for example `ssh from 203.0.113.7 to 192.0.2.1:22 on eth0`, `exposure exp2 tunnel udp from 172.30.0.3 to 198.51.100.1:7844 on dp-panel out eth0`.

Shared test helpers in `route_test.go`: `func rtQuery(dst, src, iif string) netstat.RouteQuery` (empty `src` leaves `Src` invalid), `func rtVia(iface, prefSrc string) netstat.Route` (type `unicast`).

**Task 43 — the guard (`internal/modules/firewall/guard/guard.go`).**

```go
const GuardID = "firewall.lockout"
// FlowResult is one protected flow on one in-interface and its verdict.
type FlowResult struct {
	Flow   string // human-readable: "ssh from 203.0.113.7 to 192.0.2.1:22 on eth0"
	Result fwstate.Result
}
// Checker runs the lockout guard against a host.
type Checker struct {
	Host Host // nil: LiveHost{}
}
func Check(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, st fwstate.Loaded, in Input) (core.Guard, []FlowResult, error) // Checker{}.Check
func (c Checker) Check(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, st fwstate.Loaded, in Input) (core.Guard, []FlowResult, error)
```

`Check` errors (zero guard, nil results) when `in.Eval` is nil or `gatherFacts` fails. Otherwise it evaluates every probe of every flow: an unknown probe is `Result{Verdict: Unknown, Reason}` without calling `Eval`; a probe whose family's ruleset (`st.V4`, `st.V6`) is nil is `Unknown` with reason `no v6 ruleset was read` (or `v4`); every other probe is `in.Eval(ruleset, pkt, router.route)`. The guard is `{ID: "firewall.lockout", OK: true, Message: "every protected flow passes (<n> checked)"}`, `{…, OK: true, Message: "no protected flow to check"}` with no flow, or `{ID: "firewall.lockout", OK: false, Message: "the change would cut " + "<flow>: <verdict>[ (<reason>)]" joined by "; "}` for every result whose verdict is not `accept` (an empty verdict prints `no verdict`).

**Task 44 — eligibility rulings (`facts.go`, `route.go`).** Unexported:

```go
func readRPFilter(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, name string) (int, error) // reads net/ipv4/conf/<name>/rp_filter; wraps the read error with %w
const tailnetIface = "tailscale0"
var tailnetRanges = []netip.Prefix{netip.MustParsePrefix("100.64.0.0/10"), netip.MustParsePrefix("fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48")}
func (r *router) fromTailnet(src netip.Addr) bool // src (unmapped) is in tailnetRanges and an interface named tailscale0 in r.f.ifaces is Up
```

`gatherFacts` reads `all` first (any error, missing key included, is an error), then each up, non-loopback interface; an interface whose read error matches `fs.ErrNotExist` is left out of both `facts.ifaces` and `facts.rpFilter`, and any other error is still an error. `facts.ifaces` keeps every other interface, loopback and down ones included, in `Interfaces` order. `(*router).eligible` answers `[]string{"tailscale0"}` without any `rp_filter` lookup when `fromTailnet(p.Src)`; otherwise it is unchanged. Flows with a fixed in-interface are unaffected. The shared fake `gFiles` gains `errs map[string]error`, consulted per key before `err` and `sysctl`.

**How the next parts use it.** The actions part, for every mutating firewall action:

1. Declares in the firewall manifest the external unit `core.ExternalUnit{Name: "darkpanel-controller.service", Ops: []string{core.UnitOpState}}` and the sysctl owned path `net/ipv4/conf/<iface>/rp_filter` (`^[012]$`, spec 2.1). Without both, `env.Units.State` and `env.Files.ReadSysctl` refuse and `Check` returns an error.
2. At plan (and at the apply recheck), after computing the target loaded state `st` (`predict.Predict` with `st.Sysctl` from `loaded.PredictSysctl`, or the repair target), calls `g, flows, err := guard.Check(ctx, env, st, guard.Input{Plan: input.Guard, Refresh: env.Call.GuardRefresh, Retired: env.Call.Retired, Eval: eval.Evaluate})`. An `err` fails the plan; it is not a guard verdict and cannot be overridden.
3. Applies the hard refusals itself: on an unsupported configuration or an out-of-sync host it reports `firewall.lockout` failed whatever `Overrides` says; otherwise the engine copies `Overridable` from the action's `GuardSpec`. It may show `flows` in the plan's diff.
4. A timer revert or a break-glass plan calls `guard.Check` with `Input{Plan: nil, Refresh: nil, …}`; `Check` gathers the live facts afresh (owner ruling R3).
5. Its end-to-end test calls `guard.Checker{Host: <fake Host>}.Check` with the real `eval.Evaluate` against a golden capture; this part cannot, because part E drafts in parallel.

Part E's `Evaluate` must call the `fwstate.Router` it is given with the packet after nat `PREROUTING`, and treat a Router error as `unknown`. Part E infers address types (`-m addrtype`) from the route, so it requires every `input` packet to be addressed to a local unicast address (evaluator ruling R-E1); after Task 53 the guard guarantees that (Assumptions give the flow-by-flow argument). Part E reads `SrcPort` 0 as an unknown source port: a `--sport` match against it is undecidable.

### Part A1 contracts (Tasks 32, 37, 45, 54, 59, 62, 63, 64, 106, 114, 117, 119)

**Task 32 — before-images (`image.go`).**

```go
type beforeImage struct {
	V4 []imageTable `json:"v4,omitempty"`
	V6 []imageTable `json:"v6,omitempty"`
}
type imageTable struct {
	Name   string       `json:"name"`
	Chains []imageChain `json:"chains"`
}
type imageChain struct {
	Name    string      `json:"name"`
	Builtin bool        `json:"builtin,omitempty"`
	Policy  string      `json:"policy,omitempty"`
	Rules   []imageRule `json:"rules"` // never nil
}
type imageRule struct {
	Text string `json:"text"`          // the -A line as *-save printed it
	Key  string `json:"key"`           // netfilter.Key of the rule, taken in its whole table
	Own  bool   `json:"own,omitempty"` // a jump to a UFW or Darkpanel chain
}
type chainRef struct {
	Family fwstate.Family
	Table  string
	Chain  string
}
func (c chainRef) String() string // "v4 filter/INPUT"
type imagePlan struct {
	Restore4, Restore6 []byte     // *-restore -n input; nil when the family loads nothing
	Excluded           []chainRef // built-in chains left as they are
}
var builtinChains = []string{"INPUT", "FORWARD", "OUTPUT"}
func firewallChain(name string) bool // ufw-*, ufw6-*, DOCKER-USER, darkpanel-*, dp-b-*
func takeImage(st fwstate.Loaded) *beforeImage
func planImage(img *beforeImage, st fwstate.Loaded) imagePlan
func imageMismatch(img *beforeImage, st fwstate.Loaded, excluded []chainRef) []chainRef
func restoreProgram(fam fwstate.Family, variant string) string // "/usr/sbin/ip6tables-nft-restore"
```

`takeImage` keeps every chain `firewallChain` accepts, in every table, and the filter table's built-in `INPUT`, `FORWARD` and `OUTPUT` chains, in save order. A table with none of these chains is left out, and so is a family whose ruleset is nil. In `planImage`'s input, each table lists its chain declarations first: `:<chain> - [0:0]` for a user chain, which `-n` flushes, and `:<chain> <policy> [0:0]` for a built-in chain. Then come `-F <chain>` for each built-in chain and then every rule's `Text`, in image order, ending with `COMMIT`. A built-in chain is loaded only when its rules that are not jumps to firewall chains have the same keys, in order, as the image's. Otherwise it is in `Excluded` and the input leaves it out entirely. When the current state lacks a family, every chain of that family in the image is excluded. `imageMismatch` lists, in image order, every image chain not in `excluded` that is missing in `st`, has another policy (built-in chains only), or has rule keys that differ in number or order.

**Task 37 — store (`migrations/agent/0001_firewall.sql`, `store.go`).** The table `firewall_snapshots` has these columns: `id` TEXT primary key; `created_at`; `change_id` nullable; `actor`; `system`, `pinned` and `baseline`, each 0 or 1; `entries`, JSON of `[]core.RestoreEntry` with Data in base64; `state`, JSON `snapshotState`; `hashes`, a JSON object mapping path to `fileHash`; and `post_hashes`, the same shape, nullable. It is STRICT, with the indexes `firewall_snapshots_retention (system, pinned, baseline, created_at)`, `firewall_snapshots_change (change_id)` and the unique partial index `firewall_snapshots_baseline (baseline) WHERE baseline = 1`. The table `firewall_restores` has `snapshot_id`, the primary key and a reference to `firewall_snapshots`; `transition`, one of `none`, `reload`, `enable` or `disable`; and `started_at`.

```go
func agentMigrations() fs.FS // Manifest.Migrations[core.SideAgent]
const snapshotTimeFormat = "2006-01-02T15:04:05.000000000Z"
const keepSnapshots, keepSystemSnapshots = 50, 10
var errSnapshotNotFound = errors.New("firewall: snapshot not found") // wrapped by every lookup that finds none
type snapshot struct {
	ID         string
	CreatedAt  time.Time
	ChangeID   string // "" until attached
	Actor      string
	System     bool
	Pinned     bool
	Baseline   bool
	Entries    []core.RestoreEntry // nil from listSnapshots
	State      snapshotState
	Hashes     map[string]string
	PostHashes map[string]string // nil until recorded
}
type snapshotState struct {
	Enabled bool               `json:"enabled"`
	Sysctl  map[string]string  `json:"sysctl"`                // supported keys in /proc/sys form, live values at capture
	Guard   *core.GuardContext `json:"guard,omitempty"`
	Image   *beforeImage       `json:"beforeImage,omitempty"` // repair snapshots only
	Docker  bool               `json:"docker"`                // false until wave 2
}
type snapshotFilter struct {
	System *bool // nil: both kinds
	Limit  int   // 0: all
}
func fileHash(e core.RestoreEntry) string // "sha256:<hex of Data>", or "absent" when !Present
func formatSnapshotTime(t time.Time) string
func saveSnapshot(ctx context.Context, db *store.DB, s snapshot) (snapshot, error)
func pruneSnapshots(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx) (int64, error)
func getSnapshot(ctx context.Context, db *store.DB, id string) (snapshot, error)
func listSnapshots(ctx context.Context, db *store.DB, f snapshotFilter) ([]snapshot, error)
func attachSnapshot(ctx context.Context, db *store.DB, id, changeID string) error
func attachNewest(ctx context.Context, db *store.DB, changeID string) (string, error)
func snapshotOfChange(ctx context.Context, db *store.DB, changeID string) (string, error)
func setPostHashes(ctx context.Context, db *store.DB, id string, hashes map[string]string) error
func setPinned(ctx context.Context, db *store.DB, id string, pinned bool) error
func beginRestore(ctx context.Context, db *store.DB, id string, tr fwstate.Transition, now time.Time) error
func restoreIntent(ctx context.Context, db *store.DB, id string) (fwstate.Transition, bool, error)
func pendingRestore(ctx context.Context, db *store.DB) (string, bool, error)
func endRestore(ctx context.Context, db *store.DB, id string) error
```

`saveSnapshot` makes `s` the baseline when no baseline row exists, inserts it and prunes, all in one transaction. It returns `s` with `Baseline` set. `pruneSnapshots` deletes every snapshot that is not pinned, not the baseline and not in `firewall_restores`, whose change is not `pending`, `applying` or `needs_repair` in `core_changes`, and that is not among the newest `keepSnapshots` (`system = 0`) or `keepSystemSnapshots` (`system = 1`) unpinned, non-baseline snapshots. Newest means `created_at DESC, id DESC`. `listSnapshots` orders the same way. `attachSnapshot` sets `change_id` when it is NULL or already `changeID`, and copies `core_changes.system` when that change row exists. A snapshot attached to another change is refused. `attachNewest` returns the snapshot already attached to `changeID`, or attaches the newest unattached one (highest rowid); with neither it fails wrapping `errSnapshotNotFound`. `setPostHashes` and `setPinned` fail wrapping `errSnapshotNotFound` when no row matches. `beginRestore` deletes every restore record and inserts one for `id`.

**Task 45 — the dependency seam and capture (`deps.go`, `snapshot.go`).** `deps` is exactly the part brief's struct: `root`, `readConfig`, `readLoaded`, `predict`, `edit`, `files`, `compare`, `sysctl`, `lockout`.

```go
func snapshotEntries(cfg fwstate.Config) ([]core.RestoreEntry, error) // StateFiles order, then other /etc/ufw files sorted
func fileHashes(files map[string]core.RestoreEntry) map[string]string
func systemActor(actor string) bool // "system:firewall.<task>"
func capture(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, d deps, gc *core.GuardContext, withImage bool) ([]byte, error)
func attach(ctx context.Context, env core.Env) (string, error)
func recordPostHashes(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, d deps, id string) error
```

`capture` reads `d.readConfig(d.root)` and `d.readLoaded`, then saves a snapshot through `saveSnapshot`. The snapshot holds a new ULID at `env.Clock.Now()`; the actor `env.Principal.Actor`; `System` set from `systemActor`; the entries; `fileHashes(cfg.Files)`; and the state: `cfg.Enabled`, a copy of `Loaded.Sysctl` (never nil), `gc`, and `takeImage` of the loaded state when `withImage`. It returns the id as bytes and saves nothing on any error. `attach` needs `env.ChangeID` and calls `attachNewest`. `recordPostHashes` stores `fileHashes` of the configuration as it stands now.

**Task 54 — observer (`observe.go`).**

```go
const nounRule, nounDefault, nounLogging, nounState, nounFile, nounSysctl = "firewall.rule", "firewall.default", "firewall.logging", "firewall.state", "firewall.file", "firewall.sysctl"
const resourceLogging = "firewall.logging:level"
const resourceEnabled = "firewall.state:enabled"
func ruleResource(id string) string     // firewall.rule:<rule id>

	V6      string `json:"v6,omitempty"`      // the user6.rules tuple line

}
type ufwVersion struct {
	Files map[string]string `json:"files"`          // fileHash of each of ufwFiles
	Pos4  int               `json:"pos4,omitempty"` // 1-based place among user.rules' tuples
	Pos6  int               `json:"pos6,omitempty"`

	Rule   model.Rule
	I4, I6 int // indexes into Config.Rules4 and Rules6; -1 when absent
}

func mustJSON(v any) json.RawMessage
func policyOf(cfg fwstate.Config, dir string) (string, error)
func ufwDoc(cfg fwstate.Config, hashes map[string]string, resource string) (core.StateDoc, []ruleGroup, error)
func groupDoc(cfg fwstate.Config, g ruleGroup, hashes map[string]string) core.StateDoc

func observe(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, d deps, e core.Effect) (core.Observation, error)
```

Each kind's `State` and `Version`:

- **Rule:** the State is `{"v4":…,"v6":…}`, `null` when the rule is absent, or `{"matches":n}` when the id names several rules. The Version is `ufwVersion` with the rule's positions.
- **Default:** the State is the policy as `/etc/default/ufw` spells it (`"DROP"`). The Version is `ufwVersion` without positions.
- **Logging:** the State is the level (`"low"`). The Version is as for a default.
- **Enabled:** the State is `true` or `false`. The Version is as for a default.
- **File:** the State is the file's `fileHash`. There is no Version.
- **Sysctl:** the State is the value (`"1"`), or `null` when the key does not exist. There is no Version.

`observe` answers `Matches: 1, Exclusive: true` for every effect except a rule creation. For a creation it answers `Matches` with the number of rules carrying the id, `Resource: ruleResource(id)` when there is exactly one, and one `Candidate` per rule with `Exclusive: false` when there are several.

```go
func enableOp(enable bool) ufwOp                  // modify, ["--force", "enable"] or ["disable"]
func jsonEqual(a, b json.RawMessage) bool         // canonical comparison; empty is null
func stateEqual(a, b core.StateDoc) bool
func docEqual(a, b core.StateDoc) bool
func ufwFailure(args []string, res core.CmdResult, err error) error
func runUfw(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, d deps, op ufwOp) error
func runJournaled(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, d deps, e core.Effect, resource string, call func() (core.CmdResult, error)) (core.CmdResult, error)
func writeFileEffect(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, d deps, entry core.RestoreEntry) error
func writeSysctlEffect(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, d deps, key, value string) error
```

`runUfw` reads the configuration, then sets `Before = ufwDoc(cfg, ufwHashes(cfg.Files), op.Resource)` and `After = ufwDoc(d.edit(cfg, op.Args), <hashes of d.files(next)>, op.Resource)`. For a creation, an id that already exists is refused before anything is journaled. The effect is intended as `firewall.rule:?<id>` with `Recovery{marker, <id>}` and a `null` Before State. Then ufw runs. `runJournaled` intends the effect (an `Intend` failure runs nothing), makes the call and observes. A successful call whose observation is State-equal to `After` (for a creation, exactly one match) is recorded `Made(seq, resource, observation)`. An observation equal to `Before` (for a creation, no match) is recorded `Skipped`, whatever the exit. Anything else is left `intended`, with an error, for the engine's settle step. `runUfw` also fails on any ufw failure. `writeFileEffect` writes through `env.Files.Restore` (State: the file hash). `writeSysctlEffect` writes through `env.Files.WriteSysctl`, and refuses a key that does not exist.

**Task 62 — restore (`restore.go`).**

```go
type restoreReport struct {
	Transition fwstate.Transition
	Vanished   []string   // per-interface sysctl keys not written back
	Excluded   []chainRef // before-image built-in chains left as they are
}
func chooseTransition(snapEnabled, curEnabled bool) fwstate.Transition // reload, enable, disable, none
func transitionArgs(tr fwstate.Transition) []string                   // ["reload"], ["--force","enable"], ["disable"], nil
func restoreKeep(f fwstate.Family, table, chain string) bool          // firewallChain, or a filter built-in chain
func restore(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, d deps, snap snapshot) (restoreReport, error)
func writeBackSysctl(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, want, present map[string]string) ([]string, error)
```

`restore` runs in this order:

1. It takes the transition from the restore record, or chooses one and calls `beginRestore`. For a before-image the transition is `none`. When the current configuration cannot be read, it is `enable` if the snapshot is active and `disable` if not. Otherwise it is `chooseTransition(snap.State.Enabled, cur.Enabled)`.
2. It writes every entry with `env.Files.Restore(ctx, "firewall", entry)` and reads the loaded state.
3. For a before-image it runs `restoreProgram(fam, Variant)` with `-n` and the `planImage` input as stdin. Otherwise it runs ufw with `transitionArgs`.
4. It reads the loaded state again and calls `writeBackSysctl(snap.State.Sysctl, loaded.Sysctl)`.
5. It verifies: `ENABLED` and every entry's `fileHash`; then `imageMismatch` for a before-image, or `d.compare(d.predict(cfg, before, tr), after, restoreKeep)` otherwise.
6. It calls `endRestore`. Built-in chains the before-image excluded then fail the restore, naming them.

Any earlier failure keeps the record. `writeBackSysctl` writes in this order: `net/ipv4/ip_forward`, then `conf/all` keys, then `conf/default` keys, then per-interface keys, sorted within each rank. It skips, and returns, a per-interface key that is absent from `present`. Then it reads every written key back and fails on a different value.

**Task 63 — inverses (`inverse.go`).**

```go
func inverse(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, d deps, snap snapshot, e core.Effect) error
func ufw(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, args []string) error
func stateTuples(raw json.RawMessage) (rs ruleState, v4, v6 []model.Tuple, err error)
func ruleOf(v4, v6 []model.Tuple) (model.Rule, error) // exactly one representable rule
func deleteAdded(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, e core.Effect) error
func reinsert(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, d deps, e core.Effect) error
func restoreFile(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, snap snapshot, path string, before core.StateDoc) error
func writeBackLive(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, d deps, snap snapshot) error
```

`inverse` undoes one effect by its kind:

- **Rule added:** `model.DeleteArgs` of the rule in `Post`.
- **Rule deleted:** the IPv4 half goes in with `model.InsertArgs(Pos4, r4)`, or `AddArgs` when `Pos4` is past the current number of IPv4 rules. Then the IPv6 half goes in with `InsertArgs(len(Rules4)+Pos6, r6)`, or `AddArgs`.
- **Default, logging:** the ufw vector that sets the `Before` value again.
- **Enabled:** the opposite of the change: the ufw vector for the `Before` flag, then `writeBackLive`.
- **File:** the snapshot's entry whose hash is the `Before` State.
- **Sysctl:** `WriteSysctl` of the `Before` value.

It then observes the resource and fails unless the State equals the `Before` State.

**Task 64 — revert (`revert.go`).**

```go
type overrideDetail struct {
	At       time.Time         `json:"at"`
	Snapshot string            `json:"snapshot"`
	Guard    string            `json:"guard"`
	Files    []fileOverwrite   `json:"files,omitempty"`          // {path, was, now} hashes
	Chains   []chainOverwrite  `json:"chains,omitempty"`         // {family, table, chain, policyWas, policyNow, removed, added, reordered}
	Effects  []effectOverwrite `json:"effects,omitempty"`        // {seq, resource, was}
	Vanished []string          `json:"vanishedSysctl,omitempty"`
}
func revert(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, d deps, snapBytes []byte) (core.RevertOutcome, error)
func hashesAsApplied(d deps, snap snapshot, made []core.Effect) bool
func expectedHashes(snap snapshot, made []core.Effect) map[string]string
func undoNewestFirst(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, d deps, snap snapshot, made []core.Effect, conflicts map[int]core.EffectOutcome) error
func ufwEffect(e core.Effect) bool
func reloadIfActive(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, d deps) error
func unpinChangeSnapshot(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, changeID string) error
```

`revert` behaves as follows. Its doc comment carries steps 1 to 5.

- **Setup.** It loads the snapshot and attaches it to `env.ChangeID`; a missing snapshot or one attached to another change is an error. Then it lists the effects. `unresolved` and `intended` effects block every write; `made` effects are the ones it may undo.
- **Interrupted restore.** A restore record on this snapshot is finished first. With nothing blocked, every made effect is reported `undone`. Otherwise the result is `Override` and the blocked effects stay `unresolved`.
- **Check.** It observes each made effect. One that cannot be observed is left `unresolved`/`uncertain`. One whose State is not equal to its `Post` is left `unresolved`/`conflict`, with `Current` set.
- **Whole restore or inverses.** With nothing blocked or conflicting and `hashesAsApplied` true, it calls `restore`. Otherwise it calls `undoNewestFirst`.
- **Connectivity exception.** When anything was left or a write failed, it pins the snapshot and evaluates `d.lockout` on `d.readLoaded` with `snap.State.Guard`. An error from either counts as a failing guard. A failing guard restores whole and returns `Override: true`. Its effects are the blocked ones and the conflicts as `unresolved`, with what was overwritten in `Current`, and the rest as `undone`. `Detail` is the `overrideDetail`. A passing guard returns an error when anything was blocked or a write failed. Otherwise it returns the conflicts plus `undone` for the rest.
- **Result.** A complete revert reports every made effect `undone` and does not pin.

`expectedHashes` returns `snap.Hashes` overlaid, in seq order, with each made effect's `Post.Version.Files`, and with a file effect's `Post.State` hash. It returns nil when no made effect recorded a hash. `unpinChangeSnapshot` unpins the snapshot of `changeID`.

#### How the next parts use it

The actions part (manifest, actions, Verify) uses this part as follows:

- **Manifest.** Set `Migrations: map[core.Side]fs.FS{core.SideAgent: agentMigrations()}`. Declare an `OwnedPath` of kind `core.OwnedRestore` for every `fwstate.StateFiles` path and for `/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf`. Declare the sysctl owned paths of spec 2.1: `net/ipv4/ip_forward` (`^[01]$`), `net/ipv6/conf/<iface>/forwarding` (`^[01]$`), `net/ipv6/conf/<iface>/accept_ra` (`^[012]$`), `net/ipv4/conf/<iface>/rp_filter` (`^[012]$`) and `net/ipv4/conf/<iface>/accept_source_route` (`^[01]$`). `restore` and `writeBackSysctl` write the `all` and `default` instances, and every present interface's, through these paths.
- **Production deps.** The production `deps` is `deps{root: "/", readConfig: conf.Read, readLoaded: loaded.Reader{}.Read, predict: predict.Predict, edit: predict.Edit, files: predict.Files, compare: loaded.Compare, sysctl: loaded.PredictSysctl, lockout: <adapter>}`. The adapter calls `g, flows, err := guard.Check(ctx, env, st, guard.Input{Plan: gc, Eval: eval.Evaluate})` and returns `g.OK`, then `g.Message` (or the failing flows' names), then `err`. Leave `Refresh` and `Retired` empty: a revert has no apply-time refresh.
- **Snapshot.** Every revertible action's `Snapshot(ctx, env, in)` returns `capture(ctx, env, d, in's plan GuardContext, isRepair)`. `isRepair` is true only for `firewall.state.repair`.
- **Apply.** Every revertible action's `Apply(ctx, env, in)` first calls `id, err := attach(ctx, env)`. It then journals each mutation through `runUfw(ctx, env, d, op)`, with `op` from `addRuleOp`, `deleteRuleOp`, `defaultOp`, `loggingOp` or `enableOp`, stopping at the first error. When a rule changed on an active UFW, it runs ufw's `reload` (the rule-change-with-reload transition). Last, it calls `recordPostHashes(ctx, env, d, id)`. A `firewall.snapshot.restore` apply should journal each differing file with `writeFileEffect`, the transition with `runUfw(enableOp(...))` or a reload, and each differing sysctl key with `writeSysctlEffect`, rather than call `restore`. Its own snapshot then stays revertible by `revert`.
- **Observe and Revert.** Every firewall handler's `Observe(ctx, env, e)` returns `observe(ctx, env, d, e)`. Every firewall handler's `Revert(ctx, env, snapshot)` returns `revert(ctx, env, d, snapshot)`.
- **Repair.** `firewall.state.repair` with `outcome: restore` finds the target's snapshot with `snapshotOfChange(ctx, env.DB, env.Call.RepairOf)`, loads it with `getSnapshot`, and restores it with `restore`. After a successful repair apply it calls `unpinChangeSnapshot(ctx, env, env.Call.RepairOf)`. Retention keeps the target's snapshot anyway while the target is `needs_repair`.
- **Resources and CLI.** `firewall.snapshots` lists with `listSnapshots` (the System filter selects the reconcile task's snapshots). `firewall.snapshot.compare` loads with `getSnapshot`. The break-glass `rollback --local --change <id>` finds a change's snapshot with `snapshotOfChange`.

`predictTarget` edits `cfg0` with each op (an edit error is `request.invalid_input`, `Darkpanel cannot predict ufw <args>: <error>`), takes a restore's configuration (`snapshotConfig`), and chooses the transition from UFW's state before (`cfg0.Enabled`) and the wanted one: start (`TransEnable`; commands `[--force enable]`, plus `[reload]` when `ufwNeverStarted(cur)` — the prediction is then `Predict(final-after-enable, Predict(cfgN, cur, Enable), Reload)` — or, when `ufwRunning(cur)`, `[--force enable, reload]` predicted as `Predict(Edit(cfgN, enable), cur, Reload)`); stop (`TransDisable`, `[disable]`, also for a repair of a running UFW configured off); reload (`TransReload`, `[reload]`, when ops, a restore or a repair meet an enabled UFW); or none (`Predict(cfgN, cur, TransNone)`, no command). Before each predicted start or reload it asks `f.ipv6Refusal` with the configuration before the command. The sysctl values are a copy of `f.d.sysctl(final, cur.Sysctl, tr)` with a restore's values over every key the copy holds. `snapshotConfig` writes the snapshot's present entries under a temporary directory, reads it with `f.d.readConfig`, removes it, and puts the snapshot's own entries (metadata included) in `Files`.

```go
func stateHash(input any, cfg fwstate.Config, cur fwstate.Loaded, repairOf string) (string, error)
func loadedKeys(st fwstate.Loaded) []string
```

`prepare` reads both states, refuses any unsupported reason (`firewall.unsupported_configuration`, `the host is an unsupported configuration: <reasons>`), builds the change, predicts its target and refuses a target configuration with reasons. `plan` then refuses manual changes without `manual` (`firewall.manual_required`, naming the ids); its diff is `stateDiff(cfg0+cur.Sysctl → tg.final+tg.pred.Sysctl)` followed by `{" ", "out of sync: " + chainDiffText(d)}` for each `syncDiffs` difference; its one guard is `planGuard`: on an out-of-sync host `{ID: firewall.lockout, OK: false, Message: outOfSyncMessage(…)}` unless `c.repair` and `confinedDiffs`; otherwise `f.check(ctx, env, tg.pred, guard.Input{Plan: gd.Guard, Refresh: env.Call.GuardRefresh, Retired: env.Call.Retired, Eval: eval.Evaluate})`, overridden when failing and listed in `gd.Overrides`. Its state hash is the SHA-256 of the JSON of the input, every configured file's hash, the variant, every loaded chain with its policy and rule keys, the sysctl values and `env.Call.RepairOf`.

**Task 73 — the shared handler (`handler.go`).**

```go
const lockKey, repairAction, applyTimeout = "firewall", "firewall.state.repair", 45 * time.Second
type ChangeOutput struct {
	Snapshot      string   `json:"snapshot"`                // the logical snapshot taken before the change
	Rules         []string `json:"rules,omitempty"`         // the ids of the Darkpanel rules the change adds
	RepairOutcome string   `json:"repairOutcome,omitempty"` // firewall.state.repair of a change: restored or kept
}
type mutation[In any] struct {
	f       fw
	image   bool // the snapshot holds a loaded-state before-image
	guarded func(in In) core.Guarded
	manual  func(in In) bool // nil: never
	build   func(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, in In) buildFunc
	check   func(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, in In, cfg fwstate.Config) error           // nil: none
	finish  func(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, in In, out *ChangeOutput) error // nil: none
}
func defineMutation[In any](spec core.ActionSpec, m mutation[In]) core.ActionDef
func (m mutation[In]) Plan(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, in In) (core.PlanOutcome, error)
func (m mutation[In]) Snapshot(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, in In) ([]byte, error)
func (m mutation[In]) Apply(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, in In) (ChangeOutput, error)
func (m mutation[In]) Verify(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, in In, _ ChangeOutput) error
func (m mutation[In]) Revert(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, snapshot []byte) (core.RevertOutcome, error)
func (m mutation[In]) Observe(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, e core.Effect) (core.Observation, error)
func (f fw) run(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, p prepared) error
func transitionOp(args []string) ufwOp
func (f fw) writeRestored(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, p prepared) error
func (f fw) restoreSysctl(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, want map[string]string) error
```

`defineMutation` keeps the caller's `Name`, `Summary` and `Converges` and sets the rest of the shared declaration. `run` makes, as journaled effects and stopping at the first error: a restore's files (`writeRestored`: each entry whose hash differs from the host's, once, with `ufw.conf` carrying the current `ENABLED` while the restore changes the state), each op (`runUfw`), each transition command (`runUfw(transitionOp(args))`: `enableOp(true)`, `enableOp(false)` or a reload on `firewall.state:enabled`), and a restore's sysctl values (`restoreSysctl`: each existing key whose live value differs, `net/ipv4/ip_forward`, then `all`, `default` and interfaces).

**Task 74 — state, defaults and logging (`actions_state.go`).** Inputs: `StateInput{core.Guarded}`; `DefaultsInput{core.Guarded; Incoming, Outgoing, Routed string}` (JSON `incoming`, `outgoing`, `routed`, each optional, enum `ACCEPT|DROP|REJECT`; none set is `request.invalid_input` at `/incoming`); `LoggingInput{core.Guarded; Level string}` (JSON `level`, enum `off|low|medium|high|full`). `func mismatch(format string, args ...any) error` (a `firewall.prediction_mismatch`); `func (f fw) stateEnable() core.ActionDef` (`firewall.state.enable`), `stateDisable()` (`firewall.state.disable`), `defaultsSet()` (`firewall.defaults.set`: one `defaultOp` per direction whose policy differs), `loggingSet()` (`firewall.logging.set`: a `loggingOp` when the level differs). Each is a no-op when nothing differs; each verify checks the configuration shows the requested value.

**Task 75 — one rule (`actions_rule.go`).** Inputs: `RuleAddInput{core.Guarded; Rule model.Rule}` (JSON `rule`) and `RuleDeleteInput{core.Guarded; ID string; Manual bool}` (JSON `id`, the rule id pattern, and `manual`). `func changeRuleID(env core.Env) string`; `func fieldErrors(err error, prefix string) error`; `func newRule(r model.Rule, id, path string) (model.Rule, error)` (refuses an `id` or a manual origin, then `Normalize`, the id and origin `darkpanel`, `Validate` with paths under `path`); `func (f fw) addOp(cfg fwstate.Config, r model.Rule, path string) (ufwOp, fwstate.Config, error)` (refuses a rule UFW would skip as a duplicate); `func deleteOp(cfg fwstate.Config, id, path string) (ufwOp, error)` (refuses an unknown id, an id of several rules and an unrepresentable rule); `func (f fw) ruleAdd() core.ActionDef` (`firewall.rule.add`, output `Rules: [change id]`); `func (f fw) ruleDelete() core.ActionDef` (`firewall.rule.delete`).

**Task 76 — batches (`actions_rules.go`).** `RulesApplyInput{core.Guarded; Label string; Add []model.Rule; Delete []string; Manual bool}` (JSON `label`, `add`, `delete`, `manual`). `func batch(in RulesApplyInput) ([]model.Rule, error)`; `func (f fw) rulesApply() core.ActionDef` (`firewall.rules.apply`, `Converges`, output `Rules` = the input's add ids); `func (f fw) batchChange(cfg fwstate.Config, in RulesApplyInput) (change, error)`. Each rule to add carries its own ULID and no comment; the label becomes its comment. Adds come first, in order, skipping a rule present with the same `ruleText`; then deletes, skipping an absent id. A present id with another definition is `request.invalid_input` at `/add/<i>`.

**Task 77 — restore (`actions_snapshot.go`).** `SnapshotRestoreInput{core.Guarded; ID string; Manual bool}` (JSON `id`, a ULID, and `manual`). `func loadSnapshot(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, id, path string) (snapshot, error)` (an unknown id is `request.invalid_input` at `path`); `func (f fw) snapshotRestore() core.ActionDef` (`firewall.snapshot.restore`: `change{restore: &snapshot}`; verify checks `ENABLED` equals the snapshot's).

**Task 78 — snapshots and comparison (`snapshots.go`).**

```go

}

}

}

func (f fw) snapshots(ctx context.Context, env core.Env) (SnapshotList, error)
func (f fw) snapshotCompare() core.ActionDef // firewall.snapshot.compare, read, agent
func (f fw) compareSnapshots(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, in SnapshotCompareInput) (SnapshotComparison, error)
func fileChanges(a, b map[string]core.RestoreEntry) []FileChange
```

**Task 79 — repair (`actions_repair.go`).** `RepairInput{core.Guarded; Outcome string}` (JSON `outcome`, optional, enum `restore|keep`). `const outcomeRestore, outcomeKeep = "restore", "keep"`; `func (f fw) stateRepair() core.ActionDef` (`firewall.state.repair`, snapshot with a before-image); `func repairChange(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, in RepairInput, cfg fwstate.Config) (change, error)`; `func repairedSnapshot(ctx context.Context, env core.Env) (snapshot, error)`; `func changedFiles(cfg fwstate.Config, want map[string]string) []string`. Without `env.Call.RepairOf` the change is `{repair: true}` and an outcome is `request.invalid_input` at `/outcome`. Repairing change R: `restore` (the default) is `{repair: true, restore: &<R's snapshot>}`, reports `restored`; `keep` needs R's post-apply hashes and every file still hashing so (else `request.invalid_input` at `/outcome` naming the files), is `{repair: true}`, and reports `kept`. A completed apply unpins R's snapshot (a failure is logged at Warn). Verify of `keep` checks the files still hash as R recorded; of `restore`, that `ENABLED` is the snapshot's.

**Task 80 — uninstall (`uninstall.go`).** `func (module) UninstallOptions() []core.UninstallOption` (`{Key: "rules", Values: [remove keep baseline], Default: "remove", Help: …}`) and `func (m module) Uninstall(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, keepData bool, opts map[string]string) error`, so `module` is a `core.Uninstaller`. `remove` deletes every representable Darkpanel rule with `ufw delete …` and then reloads an active UFW (only when it deleted one); `keep` does nothing; `baseline` logs, at Info, each manual rule the restore removes or adds, then restores the baseline snapshot with A1's `restore`; no baseline, or no `/usr/sbin/ufw`, does nothing. Any other value is an error. Helpers: `func (f fw) removeRules(ctx, env) error`, `func (f fw) restoreBaseline(ctx, env) error`.

**Task 81 — registration (`firewall.go`).** `func (f fw) actions() []core.ActionDef` returns, in order, `firewall.state.enable`, `state.disable`, `state.repair`, `defaults.set`, `logging.set`, `rules.apply`, `rule.add`, `rule.delete`, `snapshot.restore`, `snapshot.compare`; `func (f fw) resources() []core.ResourceDef` returns `firewall.status` (`Status`) and `firewall.snapshots` (`SnapshotList`). The manifest sets `Actions: m.f.actions()` and `Resources: m.f.resources()`; `schemas/firewall.*/v1.json` are their generated snapshots.

#### How the next parts use it

- **Web pages and CLI (part U).** Read `firewall.status` (`Status`) for the configured and loaded state, the rules with their origin (`rules[].origin`, read-only `rules[].raw`), and the `active`, `inSync` (with `outOfSync` and `syncError`) and `supported` (with `unsupported`) flags; read `firewall.snapshots` (`SnapshotList`) for the snapshot list. Plan and apply the actions with the inputs of the Part contracts: `firewall.rule.add {rule}`, `firewall.rule.delete {id, manual}`, `firewall.rules.apply {label, add, delete, manual}`, `firewall.defaults.set {incoming, outgoing, routed}`, `firewall.logging.set {level}`, `firewall.state.enable {}`, `firewall.state.disable {}`, `firewall.snapshot.restore {id, manual}`, `firewall.state.repair {outcome}` (only through `change repair`, or `{}` on its own), and the read `firewall.snapshot.compare {from, to}` (`SnapshotComparison`). Every mutating action answers `ChangeOutput`; its `snapshot` is the logical snapshot taken before it, which `firewall.snapshot.restore` brings back. A plan's single guard is `firewall.lockout`: `--override firewall.lockout` (CLI) or the change dialog's override control re-plans with `overrides: ["firewall.lockout"]`; a guard whose message starts `the host is out of sync` or names chains outside UFW's cannot be overridden. A plan refused with `firewall.manual_required` is re-planned with `manual: true` after the operator agrees.
- **Break-glass rollback.** `rollback --local --change <id>` of a pending change reverts it through the agent socket's revert; of a confirmed change it plans `firewall.snapshot.restore` with the change's snapshot: `ChangeOutput.Snapshot` of the change, or the `SnapshotInfo` whose `changeId` is the change.
- **Wave 2 (Docker integration).** A Docker action is another `mutation[In]` with `defineMutation`; it adds its effects to `change` (for example a field for the Docker block) and `fw.run`, its rows to `snapshotState`, and itself to `fw.actions`. The in-sync comparison already covers `DOCKER-USER`, `darkpanel-*` and `dp-b-*` through `restoreKeep`, and `confined` counts them as Darkpanel's. The uninstall's Docker cleanup (spec 2.9) is added to `Uninstall`.

#### Part A2 contracts: the sysctl follow-up

As part A2, plus:

**Task 87 — the sysctl prediction of a change (`verify_sysctl.go`).**

```go
type sysctlRecord struct {
	started bool              // the change started UFW
	written map[string]string // /proc/sys key to the value the change's made sysctl effect observed
}
func sysctlRecordOf(effects []core.Effect) sysctlRecord
func (f fw) expectedSysctl(cfg fwstate.Config, before map[string]string, r sysctlRecord) (map[string]string, error)
func sysctlMismatches(want, live map[string]string) []string
```

`sysctlRecordOf` ignores every effect that is not made or has no `Post`; `started` is true when the last made effect on `firewall.state:enabled` has `Post` `true`; `written` holds the made `firewall.sysctl:<key>` effects whose `Post` is a JSON string (a `null`, a key that has gone, is skipped). `written` is never nil. `expectedSysctl` takes the configuration `cfg` after the change and `before`, the live values before it (the change's snapshot's `State.Sysctl`): when `r.started` it asks `f.d.sysctl(cfg, before, fwstate.TransEnable)` (an error is wrapped, `firewall: predict the sysctl values: …`, and keeps its `firewall.unsupported_configuration` code) and keeps the keys whose predicted value differs from `before` or that `cfg.Sysctl` names; then `r.written` overrides. `sysctlMismatches` returns, sorted by key, `<key>: live "<live>", predicted "<want>"` for each key of `want` that `live` holds with another value; a key `live` lacks is skipped.

**Task 91 — verify (`handler.go`).** `func (f fw) verifySysctl(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, cfg fwstate.Config, live map[string]string) error`. `mutation.Verify` calls it last, after the chain comparison, with the configuration it read and `st.Sysctl` of the loaded state it read. It lists `env.Effects`, returns nil when the record shows no start and no write, otherwise reads the snapshot of `env.ChangeID` (`snapshotOfChange`, `getSnapshot`), predicts with `expectedSysctl` over that snapshot's `State.Sysctl` and fails with `firewall.prediction_mismatch` (`mismatch`), `the loaded sysctl values differ from the prediction: ` followed by the `sysctlMismatches` joined by `"; "`. Every other failure (the journal, the snapshot, the prediction) is a plain error `firewall: verify: …`. Test helpers: `func eeEngineRunning(t *testing.T, h *e2eHost, exec core.Runner) *lifecycle.Engine` (`eeEngine` calls it with `h`) and `eeSkewed{*e2eHost; key, value string}`, a runner whose `ufw reload` leaves `key` at `value`.

**Task 88 — `conf.Read` (`conf/conf.go`).** Behaviour change, no new name: `Read` records `/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf` in `Files` on every host. With `IPT_SYSCTL` unset it records the file (or an absent entry) and sets neither `SysctlFile` nor `Sysctl`, and the file's content raises no `Unsupported` reason. With `IPT_SYSCTL` naming another path it behaves as before. A `/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf` that is a symbolic link, not a regular file or larger than `fwstate.MaxFileSize` is now an error whatever `IPT_SYSCTL` says. Test helper: `fhState.NoSysctl bool` (the fake ufw leaves `IPT_SYSCTL` out of `/etc/default/ufw`; `fhStateOf` sets it from `cfg.SysctlFile == ""`).

##### How the next parts use it

- **Wave 2 (Docker integration) and every later mutating action.** A new action is checked without further work when it starts UFW through `ufw --force enable` or `ufw reload` journaled as an effect on `firewall.state:enabled` (`fw.run`, `transitionOp`), and when it writes a sysctl key through `writeSysctlEffect` (`fw.restoreSysctl`). An action that starts or stops UFW by another resource must journal it on `firewall.state:enabled` for the check to see it; one that writes a sysctl key by another path must journal a `firewall.sysctl:<key>` effect.
- **Part U (web and CLI), break-glass.** No surface changes. `firewall.snapshot.compare` now lists `/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf` among the files of a snapshot on every host (`absent` when the host has no such file); `firewall.status` reports `configured.sysctlFile` as before (the file `IPT_SYSCTL` names, empty when unset). A change whose sysctl values are not what the prediction said is reverted by the engine with `firewall.prediction_mismatch`, naming the key, the live and the predicted value.

##### Contracts of Task 26 — `internal/cli/firewall.go` (package `cli`)

- `firewallCommands(a *app) []*cobra.Command` — the frozen `modules.go` entry for module `firewall`; returns `[]*cobra.Command{a.firewallRollbackCommand()}`. Safe to call with a zero `*app` (it only builds closures).
- Command `darkpanel firewall rollback`: flags `--change <id>`, `--yes`, `--manual`, `--override <guard id>` (repeatable), `--json`, and the root's persistent `--local`, which it requires (without it: usage error, exit 2). Annotated `darkpanel.local` so `guardLocal` lets `--local` through.
  - Target: the change `--change` names, which must be a `firewall.*` change (else refused, exit 3); otherwise the newest change on the agent socket (`Client.Changes`, pages of `firewallChangePage`, `Before` paging) whose action starts with `firewall.`, whose actor does not start with `system:` and which is not a composite step (`ParentChangeID == ""`). None: refused "this host has no firewall change to roll back".
  - `pending`: prints "Change <id> (<action>) is pending: it will be reverted now.", asks `Apply? [y/N]` (`--yes` skips; no terminal and no `--yes`: refused), then `Client.Revert`; the change must end `reverted`.
  - `confirmed`: reads the snapshot id from the change's output field `snapshot` (part A2's `ChangeOutput`); none: refused. Plans the latest version of `firewall.snapshot.restore` with `{"id": <snapshot>}` plus `"manual": true` with `--manual` and `"overrides"` with `--override`, through `localCalls` and `planAndApply` (plan printed, guards checked, `Apply? [y/N]`), and applies with `ConfirmNow: true`; the change must end `confirmed`.
  - Any other state: refused naming the state. Output: `printChange`, or the change's JSON with `--json` (the plan then goes to standard error).
- Constants `firewallRestoreAction = "firewall.snapshot.restore"`, `firewallModulePrefix = "firewall."`, `systemActorPrefix = "system:"`; variable `firewallChangePage = 100` (tests shorten it).
- Unexported functions: `(*app).firewallRollbackCommand() *cobra.Command`, `(*app).runFirewallRollback(cmd) error`, `firewallTarget(ctx, c *api.Client, id string) (core.ChangeView, error)`, `(*app).firewallRevert(cmd, c, ch core.ChangeView) error`, `(*app).firewallRestore(cmd, c, ch core.ChangeView) error`, `firewallSnapshotOf(ch core.ChangeView) (string, error)`, `firewallInfo(cmd) io.Writer`, `firewallShow(cmd, ch changeWire, want string) error`, `firewallOutcome(ch changeWire, want string) error`. The existing `latestAction` (`enroll.go`) is reused.
- The break-glass snapshot restore is the generated command of `firewall.snapshot.restore`: `sudo darkpanel firewall snapshot restore --local --id <snapshot id> --yes --confirm` (a test proves `--local` and `--confirm` reach the agent socket with `ConfirmNow`).
