### Part E assumptions (Tasks 30, 35, 39, 41, 42, 47, 52, 55)

- Every task's code was run on base `537c4eb` (branch `p2-base`, the merge of parts F1 and F2) before this text was written, on 2026-10-24: after each task's commit the six checks of the common brief — `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test -count=1 ./...`, `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/modules/firewall/eval/`, `golangci-lint run --allow-serial-runners ./...` and `go mod tidy -diff` — passed in a clean worktree of that commit (commits Task 30 `0b64c29`, Task 35 `f54ae75`, Task 41 `a83ff23`, Task 52 `ec31811`, Task 39 `aa1ff37`, Task 47 `d627ca3`, Task 55 `bc2b117`, Task 42 `9b70b7b`; each run: build and vet silent, 58 `ok` and 2 `?` packages from `go test ./...`, race `ok`, `0 issues.`, tidy silent). Task 39's first run failed in unrelated packages with SQLite "database or disk is full" while the shared host's disk filled up; the rerun on the same commit passed. Each Step 2 output is real: it was produced by running the task's test files on the commit of the task before it.
- Tasks 39, 42, 47 and 55 depend on less than the previous task. Each was rebuilt on a branch of `537c4eb` plus only its dependencies with `git cherry-pick` (Task 39 on Task 30, Task 35; Task 47 on Task 30, Task 35, Task 41; Task 55 on Task 30 to Task 52; Task 42 on Task 30, Task 35) and passed the same six checks on 2026-10-24 (branches `dep-E-5` `edca6a3`, `dep-E-6` `eda4ba8`, `dep-E-7` `d3a1261`, `dep-E-8` `2b33c91` in the clone).
- Hook order is the kernel's priority order: raw −300, conntrack −200, mangle −150, nat DNAT −100, filter 0, security 50, nat SNAT 100 (`include/uapi/linux/netfilter_ipv4.h`, `enum nf_ip_hook_priorities`, Linux v6.12, fetched from git.kernel.org on 2026-10-24). So a raw table sees a packet before connection tracking attaches a connection to it, and `xt_conntrack` reports a packet without a connection as INVALID (`net/netfilter/xt_conntrack.c` v6.12, `conntrack_mt`: `statebit = XT_CONNTRACK_STATE_INVALID`); the evaluator makes conntrack matches in raw undecidable (ruling R-E5).
- POSTROUTING has no in-device: `ip_output` calls `NF_HOOK_COND(NFPROTO_IPV4, NF_INET_POST_ROUTING, net, sk, skb, NULL, skb->dev, …)` (`net/ipv4/ip_output.c` v6.12). The walker exposes no in-interface in OUTPUT and POSTROUTING and no out-interface in PREROUTING and INPUT.
- The nat table's chains run only while a connection's NAT binding is uninitialized, which for `IP_CT_NEW` and for `IP_CT_RELATED` falls through to the same code (`net/netfilter/nf_nat_core.c` v6.12, `nf_nat_inet_fn`: `case IP_CT_RELATED: … case IP_CT_NEW: if (!nf_nat_initialized(ct, maniptype))`). The walk runs nat chains for `NEW` only; a `RELATED` packet facing nat rules is `Unknown`; later packets skip nat (ruling R-E6). The DNAT and SNAT conntrack states come from `IPS_DST_NAT`/`IPS_SRC_NAT` (`xt_conntrack.c`), so a new connection has `DNAT` after a DNAT rule and never `SNAT` before nat POSTROUTING, the last hook walked.
- `-m rt` never matches a packet without an IPv6 routing header, negated or not: `rt_mt6` returns false when `ipv6_find_hdr(skb, &ptr, NEXTHDR_ROUTING, …)` fails (`net/ipv6/netfilter/ip6t_rt.c` v6.12). The guard's flows carry no extension headers, so UFW's `-m rt --rt-type 0 -j DROP` never drops them (ruling R-E4).
- Mark semantics: `mark_mt` returns `((skb->mark & info->mask) == info->mark) ^ info->invert` (`net/netfilter/xt_mark.c` v6.12); `CONNMARK` set is `(ct->mark & ~ctmask) ^ ctmark`, save `(ct->mark & ~ctmask) ^ (skb->mark & nfmask)`, restore `(skb->mark & ~nfmask) ^ (ct->mark & ctmask)` (`net/netfilter/xt_connmark.c` v6.12, `connmark_tg_shift`; the shift options are outside the parser's contract). `markTarget` implements exactly these.
- A packet with a local source arriving on a non-loopback interface fails reverse-path validation unless `accept_local` is set (`net/ipv4/fib_frontend.c` v6.12, `__fib_validate_source`: `if (res.type != RTN_UNICAST && (res.type != RTN_LOCAL || !IN_DEV_ACCEPT_LOCAL(idev))) goto e_inval;`). `addrtype --src-type LOCAL` is therefore true only on `lo` or for a locally generated packet (ruling R-E1).
- iptables 1.8.11's TCP flag names are `SYN ACK FIN RST URG PSH ALL NONE` (`iptables -p tcp -m tcp --help`, run in a throwaway `docker:28.5.2-dind` container on 2026-10-24); `ALL` is the six flags `0x3f`.
- tailscaled's rules were read from `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tailscale/tailscale/v1.82.0/util/linuxfw/iptables_runner.go`, `…/v1.82.0/wgengine/router/router_linux.go`, `…/v1.102.0/util/linuxfw/iptables_runner.go`, `…/v1.102.0/wgengine/router/osrouter/router_linux.go` and both versions' `util/linuxfw/linuxfw.go` (fetched 2026-10-24). Facts used: `AddHooks` inserts `-j ts-input`/`-j ts-forward` at position 1 of filter INPUT/FORWARD and `-j ts-postrouting` at position 1 of nat POSTROUTING; `AddLoopbackRule` inserts `-i lo -s <addr> -j ACCEPT` at position 1 of `ts-input`; 1.82's `addBase4` builds `ts-input` as ChromeOS `RETURN`, CGNAT `DROP`, `-i tailscale0 -j ACCEPT`, while 1.102's starts with the tailscale0 ACCEPT and `AddExternalCGNATRules` appends the ChromeOS/CGNAT rules after `AddMagicsockPortRule`'s `-p udp --dport <port> -j ACCEPT`; `ts-forward` is `-i tailscale0 -j MARK --set-mark 0x40000/0xff0000`, `-m mark --mark 0x40000/0xff0000 -j ACCEPT`, (IPv4 only) `-o tailscale0 -s 100.64.0.0/10 -j DROP`, `-o tailscale0 -j ACCEPT`; `AddStatefulRule` inserts `-o tailscale0 -m conntrack ! --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j DROP` before the final ACCEPT; `AddSNATRule` appends `-m mark --mark 0x40000/0xff0000 -j MASQUERADE` to `ts-postrouting`; 1.102's `AddConnmarkSaveRule` (always on with netfilter on) inserts the mangle PREROUTING restore and mangle OUTPUT save rules with masks `0xff0000`; `ClampMSSToPMTU` is called only by containerboot, not by the host router, so the host fixtures have no `TCPMSS` rule; exit-node advertisement adds routes (`0.0.0.0/0`, `::/0`) and no rule of its own.
- Docker 28's chains are real output: `docker:28.5.2-dind` (image id `2a232a42256f`, Docker 28.5.2, iptables v1.8.11 nf_tables) with `--bip=172.18.0.1/16` and `busybox:1.37` publishing `8080:80`, captured by Task 47's `capture.sh` twice on 2026-10-24 with identical checksums. An earlier unpinned run of `docker:28-dind` (same image id) without `--bip` gave the same chain structure with the bridge at 172.18.0.0/16 by chance.
- UFW's loaded state is part F2's golden capture (`internal/modules/firewall/testdata/golden/`, commit `5d5a310`): the `rules`, `ipv6no` and `disabled` scenarios on `debian-12`, `debian-13`, `ubuntu-22.04` and `ubuntu-24.04`. The four images' filter tables differ only in a trailing space on one `recent --set` line on ubuntu-22.04 (`diff` of the captures, 2026-10-24), so one expectation set covers all four.
- Ruling R-E1 (address types, no `Options`): `-m addrtype` is decided from the routing decision the packet already carries — destination `LOCAL` on the input path or on the output path through `lo`, `UNICAST` on the forward and other output paths, `MULTICAST` by address, `BROADCAST` only for 255.255.255.255; source `LOCAL` only on `lo` or on the output path; a non-local source's `UNICAST` and every other type are undecidable. The cost: an input-path packet to a subnet-directed broadcast address reads as `LOCAL`; the guard's flows are unicast, which the Part constraints make a caller duty. This avoids an `Options` parameter the fixed `Input.Eval` type could not carry.
- Ruling R-E2 (marks): an incoming packet's mark is `Packet.Mark` exactly, so a mark match on an incoming packet is always decided; only a locally generated packet with mark 0 has unknown bits (a socket option), and an earlier packet's connection mark is unknown for a non-`NEW` packet. A match that holds with the unknown bits at zero is taken as holding; one that needs an unknown bit set is undecidable (the brief's "nothing on the path set it and the match needs non-zero"). Marking by `tc` on ingress is not modelled. Treating incoming marks as unknown too would make `ts-forward`'s `-m mark --mark 0x40000/0xff0000 -j ACCEPT` undecidable for every forwarded packet not from `tailscale0`, contradicting the brief's expected stateful-filtering drop; controller item below.
- Ruling R-E3 (deciding targets): a rule whose match is undecidable is `Unknown` unless its target is none, `LOG`, `TCPMSS`, `SNAT` or `MASQUERADE` (the last two run only in nat POSTROUTING, the last hook walked, and nat INPUT, which is refused); jumps and `RETURN` count as deciding, which is why UFW's limited port is `unknown` (`ufw-user-limit` rejects). An undecidable `CONNMARK --save-mark`/`--restore-mark` makes the copied bits unknown instead (tailscaled 1.102's mangle OUTPUT save rule would otherwise make every unmarked local flow unknown).
- Ruling R-E7 (rerouting): after the pre-routing hooks (raw, mangle, nat PREROUTING or OUTPUT) the walk asks the router again when DNAT rewrote the destination or a rule changed the mark; the router receives the rewritten packet with `Path` still the original path and `Mark` the current mark. A mark change after routing (filter FORWARD's tailscaled MARK) does not reroute, as in the kernel.
- Ruling R-E8: `Ruleset.LegacyPresent` is ignored (part C reports a populated foreign variant as unsupported, spec 2.1); a table with an incompatible-table note is `Unknown` when the walk reaches it; an absent table or built-in chain registers no hook and passes the packet, as `iptables-nft` creates no hook for a table it never loaded.
- Ruling R-E10: ICMP types and the IPv6 hop limit are undecidable (`fwstate.Packet` has no field for them); they matter only to ICMP packets, since UFW's ICMP rules also match `-p icmp`/`-p ipv6-icmp`.
- Ruling R-E12: the brief's "the stateful-filtering drop of new forwarded connections from tailscale0" is read from the source: `AddStatefulRule` drops new connections forwarded **into** `tailscale0` (`-o tailscale0`) from another interface; connections from `tailscale0` are marked and accepted. Task 55 expects exactly that.
- Ruling R-E13: the tailscaled fixtures put tailscaled's chains in front of a small stand-in host firewall (lo, established, SSH accept, port 3000 reject, default drop) instead of UFW's full chains, so each expectation names one tailscaled rule; UFW's own chains are covered by Task 39.
- Ruling R-E14: the brief's single golden-fixtures task is split into Task 39 (UFW, no container), Task 47 (Docker capture with a privileged container) and Task 55 (hand-written tailscaled fixtures) under Rule S, because a reviewer can accept one while rejecting another.
- Ruling R-E15: Task 39 is coverage over existing code and has no red phase; its Step 2 expects PASS and says so.
- Ruling R-E16: the Docker capture pins `docker:28.5.2-dind`, `busybox:1.37` and `--bip=172.18.0.1/16` so that its output is byte-for-byte reproducible; Task 47 checks the output's SHA-256 instead of trusting the pasted copy.
- Ruling R-E18: an invalid packet and a nil ruleset return `Unknown` with an `eval:` reason and an empty trace rather than an error, because `fwstate.Result` is the only channel the fixed signature has.
- Controller ruling C-E1 (2026-10-24, on R-E2): accepted as implemented. Incoming packets carry the caller's mark; marks that `tc` sets on ingress are out of scope and recorded by the controller as a deferred register row.
- Controller ruling C-E2 (2026-10-24): an absent ruleset (`fwstate.Loaded.V6` nil when ip6tables is missing) stays `Unknown`; `Evaluate` already returns `Unknown` with "eval: no ruleset for the packet's family".
- Controller ruling C-E3 (2026-10-24), implemented by Task 42: `Packet.SrcPort == 0` means the source port is unknown (a connection that does not exist yet); a `--sport`/`--sports` match against it is undecidable and follows R-E3. No earlier test or golden expectation used port 0 with a source-port rule: the whole package passed unchanged after the change (2026-10-24).
- Brief sanity: every Docker container part E started (`dp-w1-E-1`, `dp-w1-E-2`, `dp-w1-E-docker28` twice) was removed; `docker ps -a --filter name=dp-w1-E` printed nothing afterwards (2026-10-24).

### Part G assumptions (Tasks 17, 31, 36, 43, 44, 53, 94, 95, 105, 112, 113)

- Owner ruling R3 (spec "Owner decisions", 2026-10-24): the firewall gathers its own live guard facts through `internal/platform/netstat` and its scoped unit client; a timer revert calls `Check` again and gathers afresh. `Check` therefore takes no facts from its caller.
- Flow 5 is the agent's own outbound TCP sessions: every established TCP socket held by `Host.PID()` (production: `os.Getpid()`) that was not accepted on a listening socket (part brief ruling).
- OpenSSH process names, verified on 2026-10-24 in containers `debian:13` (OpenSSH_10.0p2) and `ubuntu:24.04` (OpenSSH_9.6p1) with `openssh-server`, a running `sshd` and an `ssh root@127.0.0.1` session, by listing `/proc/<pid>/comm` of every socket holder: on Debian 13 the established session socket is held by two `sshd-session` processes and the listener by `sshd`; on Ubuntu 24.04 the session socket and the listener are held by `sshd`. `sshd-auth` (OpenSSH 10.0's pre-authentication process) is kept in the list as the part brief asks. Containers `dp-w1-G-debian-13` and `dp-w1-G-ubuntu-24-04` were removed in the same step.
- A socket-table error makes `Check` return an error (part brief: "error when the table read fails, including netstat's new no-tables error", register row 259), where F1's "How the next parts use it" says the guard "fails as `unknown`". Ruling: error, because an error fails the plan and cannot be overridden while an `unknown` flow could be. `TestLiveHostNoSocketTables` reads an empty proc root through the real `netstat.Table` and `TestCheckErrors` checks `Check`.
- `Units.State` reports a missing unit as `LoadState "not-found"` without an error (`internal/platform/systemd.go:238-243`, test `systemd_test.go:506`), and `MainPID` is 0 for a unit that is not a running service (`internal/core/units.go:48-51`). The scoped unit client refuses `State` of a unit the manifest does not declare with op `state` (`internal/platform/units_scope.go:149-155`).
- `ReadSysctl` accepts only a key the module declares as kind `sysctl`, and an `<iface>` segment matches `all` and any name of `^[A-Za-z0-9_.@-]{1,15}$` (`internal/platform/files_sysctl.go:29-46,97-126`).
- tailscaled's `ts-input` drops `100.64.0.0/10` arriving on any interface other than `tailscale0` (`internal/platform/netfilter/testdata/tailscaled-v4.save:26`, `-A ts-input -s 100.64.0.0/10 ! -i tailscale0 -j DROP`). Without a special case, with `rp_filter` 0 or 2 an SSH session over the tailnet would be checked on `eth0` too and fail there.
- Controller ruling (2026-10-24, decision 1; the controller adds it to spec 2.3): a protected flow whose source is in Tailscale's ranges, `100.64.0.0/10` for IPv4 and `fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48` for IPv6, is eligible only on `tailscale0` when that interface exists and is up, because tailscaled drops such sources on every other interface by design and checking them there is a false refusal. Without `tailscale0` the normal eligibility rule applies; this part reads "exists and is up" so that a `tailscale0` that is down also falls back to the normal rule. Implemented in Task 44 (`TestProbesTailscaleSource`).
- Controller ruling (2026-10-24, decision 4): an interface that disappears between `Interfaces()` and its `rp_filter` read is dropped from eligibility instead of making `Check` return an error; any other read error stays an error. `ReadSysctl` reports a missing key as the `openat2` errno wrapped with `%w` (`internal/platform/files_sysctl.go:169-171`, `internal/platform/files.go:197`), and `syscall.Errno(ENOENT)` matches `fs.ErrNotExist` (Go `syscall.Errno.Is`), so the guard tests `errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist)`. A missing `all` key is still an error. Implemented in Task 44 (`TestGatherFactsVanishedInterface`).
- Plan-time rulings of this part (each covered by a test row):
  - Flows 2, 3 and 4 from the guard context need the controller on this host: a local controller unit with a main process, or a `PanelListen` **or `AgentListen`** address that is a host address (the brief names `PanelListen`; an agent listener is equally a controller address). Flow 3 is gated too, because an exposure lives on the controller's host (spec 8) and on any other host `dp-panel` does not exist, so every plan there would fail as `unknown`.
  - Flow 2 comes only from a context whose `Via` is nil (spec 2.3: "when the request came directly"); its clients are paired with the union of both contexts' `PanelListen`.
  - A `Refresh` whose `Complete` is false fails the guard like a `Plan` one (F1's Part constraints: the same `Complete` rule at apply).
  - A session is inbound when a listening TCP socket of any process has its port and its address or an unspecified address (under socket activation systemd holds sshd's listener). This drops `sshd-session`'s outbound port-forwarding sockets from flow 1 and the agent's accepted sessions from flow 5.
  - A flow from a loopback or host address is skipped: it traverses only `lo`, which is never an eligible interface.
  - An unspecified `::` listener is dual-stack (Go's listeners are); an unspecified destination becomes the preferred source of the route back to the client, and a failed lookup makes the flow `unknown`.
  - Stand-ins: `198.51.100.1` and `2001:db8:ffff::1` (RFC 5737 / RFC 3849 documentation ranges) for "an internet address"; Tasks 31, 36, 43 and 44 give a connection that does not exist yet the stand-in source port 49152; Task 53 replaces it with 0 (next bullet).
- Evaluator ruling (2026-10-24, from part E): `fwstate.Packet.SrcPort == 0` means an unknown source port, and the evaluator treats a `--sport` match against it as undecidable. Task 53 therefore gives source port 0 to every flow for a connection that does not exist yet: a new SSH connection and a new controller session come from a port the peer has not chosen yet (the observed session's peer port is not it), and the panel, agent-link, exposure and tailscaled TCP 443 flows have no socket at all. The agent's outbound sessions (flow 5) keep their observed local port and tailscaled's UDP flows keep the port of its socket, because that port is genuinely known. `TestCheckEachFlowRefusingAlone` asserts both halves over every flow.
- Evaluator ruling R-E1 (2026-10-24, from part E): the evaluator infers address types from the route, so every `input` packet must be addressed to a local unicast address. After Task 53 the guard's flows satisfy it: flow 1 and the live controller sessions use the socket's local address (an address of this host); flows 2 and 4 use a listener that is a host address (a specified listener of another host is skipped) or an unspecified listener, which `probes` resolves to the route's preferred source (a host address); NPM's public flow uses a host address, or the preferred source for an unspecified or upstream-NAT address; the exposure's proxy flow uses `ListenerAddr`, the runtime listener on `dp-panel`. A destination that still is not a host address (a proxy listener absent from this host, an established socket bound to a non-local address through a `local` route) makes the flow `unknown` before evaluation, and the Router answers `input` only for a host or loopback destination. `localAddrs` holds interface addresses only, which the kernel assigns as unicast. The Check tests' host (`ckIfaces`) gains the `dp-panel` bridge so the proxy listener is local, which adds `dp-panel` probes to every incoming flow there.
  - A stand-in destination (tunnel egress, Tailscale) whose lookup fails with `netstat.ErrNoRoute` yields no flow, since a host without a route of that family has no such traffic to cut; any other lookup error is `unknown`.
  - Tailscale flows are IPv4 only, as the brief's stand-in: one UDP flow per distinct non-zero, non-loopback, unconnected UDP port held by `tailscaled`, and one TCP 443 flow whenever any socket is held by `tailscaled`.
  - The exposure's proxy flow and its tunnel egress enter on `dp-panel` (the `ProxyAddr` is the proxy container's address on the panel network); NPM's public flow is an `input` packet to the `Public` address that the evaluator's Router turns into a forwarded one after DNAT.
  - `rp_filter` comes from the checked state (`st.Sysctl`) when it holds the key, so a predicted change of UFW's sysctl file counts; the live value otherwise.
  - A forwarded flow is `unknown` ("forwarding is off") when `st.Sysctl` holds `net/ipv4/ip_forward` (IPv6: `net/ipv6/conf/all/forwarding`) `"0"` (spec 2.1's example: `ip_forward=0` under a forwarded panel path fails the guard).
  - A missing ruleset of the packet's family, and a flow with no eligible in-interface, are `unknown`.
- Part E (the evaluator) drafts in parallel and had no code in `clone-E` on 2026-10-24, so no test here runs the real `Evaluate`; `TestCheckRouterGiven` proves the Router `Check` hands to `Eval` resolves a DNAT-rewritten destination per in-interface. The actions part adds the end-to-end test.

- Tasks 17, 31, 36 and 43 each depend on every earlier task, so base plus their dependencies is exactly their parent commit. Task 44 depends on Tasks 17, 31 and 36 only: on 2026-10-24 its commit was cherry-picked onto Task 36's commit (base plus Task 17, Task 31, Task 36), its RED output was captured there with only its test edits, and all six checks passed there too, so Task 44 and Task 43 may run in parallel; applied after Task 43 (the drafted order) they also pass. Task 53 depends on every earlier task (it edits `guard_test.go` of Task 43 and lines of `route_test.go` that Task 44 added), so base plus its dependencies is its parent commit; its RED output was captured on Task 44's commit with only its test edits.

### Part A1 assumptions (Tasks 32, 37, 45, 54, 59, 62, 63, 64, 106, 114, 117, 119)

- Part brief rulings, taken as given. The snapshot bytes the engine stores are the snapshot row's id. Every firewall effect is `Local: true`. Container rules (`firewall_container_rules`) are wave 2, so no table exists for them now.
- **How the engine calls the handler.**
  - Snapshot: `begin` runs under `applyMu` (`internal/core/lifecycle/apply.go:69-70`). It builds the Env without a change (`env := e.env(p, def)`, `apply.go:190`), chooses the change id but does not pass it (`apply.go:197`), and calls `Snapshot` (`apply.go:209`). It seals the bytes (`apply.go:215`) and stores them in `core_changes.snapshot_ct` in the intent transaction (`apply.go:240`).
  - Apply: Apply gets an Env with `ChangeID` and `Effects` set (`apply.go:383`, `:391`; `effects.go:55-61`).
  - Revert: `runRevert` opens the snapshot and calls `Revert` with the change's Env (`apply.go:477-510`). It is reached from a failed apply after `settle` (`apply.go:431-447`), from the timer or an operator through `revertPending` (`revert.go:86-114`), and at startup through `revertAtStart`, also after `settle` (`recover.go:445-466`).
  - Observe: the engine uses it in settle (`settle.go:42-77`) and undo (`undo.go:102`). `Intend` refuses an action without an Observer (`effects.go:76`).
  - Recording the revert: `recordRevert` applies `RevertOutcome.Effects` only when `Revert` returned no error (`revert.go:155-161`). `revertEffect` turns `undone` on a `made` effect into `undoing` then `undone`. It turns `unresolved` on a `made` or `intended` effect into `unresolved` (reason `conflict`, or `uncertain` otherwise), and on an `unresolved` one it only updates `Current` (`revert.go:224-268`).
- **System changes.** The engine's system flag is not visible to a handler: `isSystem(ctx)` is unexported (`internal/core/lifecycle/system.go:44`). Background tasks act as `system:<task id>` (`internal/agent/runtime/background.go:282`). Ruling: `capture` marks a snapshot system when its actor starts with `system:firewall.`, and `attach` copies `core_changes.system` (`internal/core/store/migrations/agent/0007_platform_surfaces.sql:3`) once the change row exists.
- **Finding the snapshot in Apply.** Ruling: `attach` takes the newest unattached snapshot (highest rowid). This is safe because `begin` runs under `applyMu`, which also holds the snapshot and the intent, and the change holds the `firewall` lock from its intent on. No other firewall snapshot can be captured in between. Older unattached rows come from applies whose intent failed, and retention prunes them like any other unattached row. `revert` attaches by id as well, so a change cut off before Apply still owns its snapshot.
- **Module migrations.** The agent applies a module's migrations from `Manifest.Migrations[core.SideAgent]` (`internal/agent/runtime/runtime.go:208`, `internal/install/install.go:351`). Module tables use the `<module id>_` prefix (`docs/adr/0005-storage-and-secrets.md:33`). The tests apply the core set plus `agentMigrations()` exactly as the runtime does.
- **Inverse data.** `core.Effect` has no free-form field for handler data (`internal/core/contract.go:362-386`). Ruling: the inverse vector is derived from the effect's own `Before` and `Post`, which hold the rule's tuple lines and positions, the policy, the level, the flag, the file hash or the value. That is "stored in the effect State" without the change's input. A file inverse also needs the previous bytes, which come from the change's snapshot by hash.
- **Effect kinds.** Ruling on the mapping to the engine's kinds:
  - A rule added is `create`. Its recovery identity is the `marker` of its tag ULID, and the resource is `firewall.rule:?<id>` until made (`effects.go:134-168` requires this). An existing id is refused before anything is journaled.
  - A rule deleted is `delete`.
  - Every other effect is `modify`, with the resources of the Part contracts.
  - Settle then classifies a creation by its match count and everything else by Before and After (`settle.go:61-70`).
- **State and Version.** Ruling, following the engine's comparisons. Settle's `skipped` needs equal State and Version; its `made` and the revert's conflict check need State only (`settle.go:67-69`). So the file hashes and a rule's positions go in `Version`, the resource's own value in `State`. A manual edit elsewhere in `user.rules` is then no conflict and goes to step 3, as spec 2.5 intends. The predicted `After.Version` comes from the hashes of `d.files`, which the part brief names for this.
- **File hashes.** Ruling: a hash is `sha256:<hex>` of the file's bytes, or `absent`. Mode and owner are not part of it, because ufw rewrites files in place and keeps both.
- **Retention.** Ruling: the snapshot rows of changes in `pending`, `applying` and `needs_repair` are kept. `awaiting_confirmation` is a composite's state, and composites run on the controller. Retention counts an unattached snapshot by its own `system` flag, and prunes inside `saveSnapshot`'s transaction, so the new row is always among those kept. The baseline is the host's first snapshot row itself, flagged and never pruned; a unique partial index allows only one.
- **Restore record.** Ruling: a small table `firewall_restores` rather than a column, so the record can carry the UFW transition. With that, a restore cut off after it wrote `ENABLED=no` but before `ufw disable` still disables when run again. Recomputing the transition would see "both inactive" and leave UFW running (`TestRestoreFinishesARecordedRestore`). A new restore deletes any older record, so at most one exists. Retention never deletes a snapshot with a record, which the foreign key also enforces.
- **Unreadable configuration.** Ruling: when the current configuration cannot be read, `restore` runs `ufw --force enable` or `ufw disable` according to the snapshot. Both work whatever the current state is (`ufw-src/ufwspike-debian-13/ufw/frontend.py:191-236`: `set_enabled` always starts or stops the firewall). `ufw reload` on an inactive firewall only skips, which is why spec 2.5 has the transition chosen.
- **Before-image scope and loading.** Ruling: the image holds the UFW and Darkpanel chains of every table, but the built-in `INPUT`, `FORWARD` and `OUTPUT` chains of the filter table only, because UFW hooks only there. Each rule's `netfilter.Key` is taken at capture, in its whole table, so a jump compares as it did. A software update cannot change `Key` in between, because update reservations are refused while a change holds a lock (spec 1.3).
  - `*-restore -n` flushes a user chain it declares but not a built-in one (F1's `ParseRestore` contract, Task 11), so `planImage` flushes a loaded built-in chain with `-F`.
  - Verified on 2026-10-24 in a privileged `ubuntu:24.04` container (`dp-w1-A1-img-plain` and `dp-w1-A1-img-foreign`, ufw 0.36.2-6, iptables 1.8.10 nf_tables, both removed). Setup: `ufw allow 22/tcp`, `ufw --force enable`, and a foreign chain `fw-foreign` jumped to from `INPUT` in both families; then the image was saved. Perturbation: `ufw allow 8080/tcp`, an extra `ufw-user-input` rule, the `INPUT -j ufw-before-logging-input` jump deleted, and `iptables -P INPUT ACCEPT`. `planImage`'s output fed to `iptables-nft-restore -n` and `ip6tables-nft-restore -n` exited 0, and `imageMismatch` against the result was empty: the policy was `DROP` again, the jump was back, and `fw-foreign` was intact.
  - With a foreign `INPUT` rule added as well, `planImage` excluded `v4 filter/INPUT`. The load left `INPUT` as it was (policy `ACCEPT`, the foreign rule kept) and restored every other chain (`imageMismatch` empty with `INPUT` excluded). The scratch test that ran `takeImage` and `planImage` on the captured output was not committed.
- **Verify set and transition.** Ruling: `restore` compares with `d.predict` over the UFW and Darkpanel chains plus the filter table's built-in chains (`restoreKeep`). For a before-image it runs no UFW transition and compares with the image instead (spec 2.3: the files are normally unchanged by a repair, and the image is what must come back).
- **Sysctl write-back.** Ruling: the write order is `net/ipv4/ip_forward`, then `all`, then `default`, then each interface (spec 2.1). An interface counts as gone when its key is absent from the live keys `d.readLoaded` returns after the transition. Its keys are skipped and returned in `restoreReport.Vanished`. `RevertOutcome` has no field for them except `Detail`, so a revert logs them at Warn and an override's `Detail` lists them (`vanishedSysctl`).
- **Re-adding a deleted both-family rule** (controller ruling: two inserts). Verified on 2026-10-24 in privileged containers `dp-w1-A1-ubuntu-24-04` (ufw 0.36.2-6, iptables 1.8.10), `dp-w1-A1-ubuntu-22-04` (0.36.1-4ubuntu0.1, 1.8.7) and `dp-w1-A1-debian-13` (0.36.2-9, 1.8.11), all removed. The script is `A1-scratch/inverse-exp.sh`; the drafter's scratch, not committed.
  - Setup: five rules, a tagged both-family 22/tcp, a v4 rule from 10.0.0.0/8, a commented both-family 25/tcp, a v6-only deny from 2001:db8::/32 and a both-family rule on eth0.
  - Each deleted rule was re-inserted the way `reinsert` does it: the IPv4 half as `insert <pos4> … from 0.0.0.0/0 to 0.0.0.0/0 …`, then the IPv6 half as `insert <IPv4 count + pos6> … from ::/0 to ::/0 …`, or as a plain add when the position is past the end. Cases: a middle rule, the first rule (tagged), the last rule (appended), and the v6-only rule.
  - In every case, on every image, `cmp` found `user.rules` and `user6.rules` byte-identical to the originals.
  - `ufw insert 5` with four IPv4 rules answered `ERROR: Invalid position '5'` and exit 1 (`frontend.py:457-478`, `backend_iptables.py:996-999`), which is why `reinsert` appends there.
  - A duplicate insert answered `Skipping inserting existing rule` with exit 0. `inverse`'s check after the call turns that into an error (`TestInverseFailsWhenUfwSkipsTheInsert`).
- **Rulings on the inverse path.**
  - Undoing an enable or a disable also writes the snapshot's sysctl values back, because UFW's start applies its sysctl file (spec 2.1).
  - Step 3 ends with `ufw reload` when a rule, default or logging inverse ran and the configuration says UFW is active, so the loaded state is UFW's full reload of the files. This is the "rule change with reload" transition the predictor models (spec 2.3).
- **Rulings on the revert.**
  - A guard that cannot be evaluated, or a loaded state that cannot be read, counts as a failing guard (spec 2.3: `unknown` fails the guard), so the connectivity exception restores whole.
  - An effect still `intended` at revert time blocks writes as an `unresolved` one does. The engine settles before every revert that follows a failed or cut-off apply, so only a settle that itself failed could leave one.
  - A made effect that cannot be observed is left in place as `unresolved`/`uncertain`.
  - The emergency restore of a before-image still never flushes a changed built-in chain. Those rules belong to other programs, not to manual UFW edits, and the restore then fails naming the chains.
  - A revert pins its snapshot on every ending other than `reverted`. A failed pin is only logged, because retention keeps the snapshot of every `needs_repair` change anyway. The actions part unpins it with `unpinChangeSnapshot` when a repair completes.
- **No Docker hook.** Docker chains are wave 2, and the part brief prefers no seam, so the code has none.
- **Cross-part assumption.** `predict.Files` returns its map keyed by the four absolute paths of `ufwFiles`. `runUfw` refuses a prediction without them, so a drift shows in the actions part's first test.

### Part A2 assumptions (Tasks 65, 66, 67, 68, 69, 70, 71, 72, 73, 74, 75, 76, 77, 78, 79, 80, 81, 82, 84, 87, 88, 91, 96, 97, 98, 99, 100, 108, 109)

- **Rulings of the part brief, taken as given.** The revert timeout is per apply (owner ruling R2): no settings store exists, the confirm timeout comes from the apply request (`internal/core/lifecycle/apply.go:292-303`, `confirmTimeout`), and the module declares only its `ApplyTimeout`. Manual rule changes need `manual: true` (spec 2.2). Parts G's and E's rulings bind: guard packets target local unicast addresses, an absent IPv6 ruleset is `unknown`, and source port 0 is unknown (`guard`'s and `eval`'s Part constraints in `clone-G/PLAN-PART.md` and `clone-E/PLAN-PART.md`).
- **Controller rulings after phase 2, implemented.** After `ufw --force enable` on a host where UFW never started, Apply runs `ufw reload` at once as a journaled effect (`target.go`, `fw.start`; `TestTargetTransitions` "first enable"). Part P's call order is followed exactly: `Edit` per command, then `IPv6Refusal` and `Predict` with the configuration from before the transition command, then `Edit` of the transition command for the post-apply configuration (`fw.predictTarget`, `fw.transition`; `TestTargetCommands` checks the refusal is asked about the transition). Every batch on an active UFW ends with `ufw reload` (`TestDefaultsAndLogging`, `TestRulesApply`). Part C's conservative IPv4 `default` refusal reaches plans as a plan error (`TestTargetCommands`, "sysctl refusal"); part A1's `attach` is used as is.
- **How the engine drives a guarded, revertible action** (read on 2026-10-24 in the base). Plan runs the handler, then `checkGuards` (`internal/core/lifecycle/overrides.go:46-72`), which sets each guard's `Overridable` from its `GuardSpec` and rejects a guard reported `Overridden` that is not overridable, not listed in `overrides` or not `OK`; hence the module reports a hard refusal as `OK: false, Overridden: false` and an overridden guard as `OK: true, Overridden: true` (`TestPlanGuardOverrides`, `TestPlanOutOfSync`). A plan with a failing guard is stored, not refused (`engine.go:391-424`, `makePlan`); apply refuses it with `plan.guard_failed` (`apply.go:333-352`, `checkReplan`; `TestE2EApplyGuard`). Apply first re-runs Plan with `env.Call.GuardRefresh` set to the apply's topology (`apply.go:190-195`, and `recheck` at `:310-328`), and refuses a changed state hash or a guard that passed and now fails (`plan.state_changed`); then it calls Snapshot, before the change exists (`apply.go:200-216`); Apply, Verify and Revert get `env.ChangeID` and `env.Effects`. A repair plan gets `env.Call.RepairOf` from the stored `repairs` (`repair.go:209-218`) and an input of `{}` when the request has none (`repair.go:85-93`).
- **Plan-time ruling: actions and resources are registered by the last implementation task (Task 81).** Registering each action in its own task would add `firewall.go` and regenerated `schemas/` files to every action task, which Rule S does not allow next to a new implementation and test file. The action tasks test their handlers directly (and `TestMutationDefinition` checks the registry accepts a mutation); Task 81 registers all of them and regenerates the schemas, which `TestSnapshotsCurrent` (`internal/modules/modules_test.go`) requires.
- **Plan-time ruling: the in-sync comparison** (`fw.syncDiffs`). An enabled UFW is compared with the prediction of a reload over UFW's and Darkpanel's chains and the filter table's built-in chains (A1's `restoreKeep`); a disabled UFW with the prediction of a stop over UFW's chains only. Two facts decide the scope. A `*nat` block of `before.rules` is re-appended to `nat` built-in chains on every start (part P's Assumptions, container run `dp-w1-P-5`), so comparing those chains would mark such a host out of sync forever; UFW hooks only the filter built-ins. A built-in policy someone sets while UFW is off is not UFW's state. The prediction copies every chain UFW does not manage from the loaded state, so foreign chains never differ.
- **Plan-time ruling: verify** (`mutation.Verify`). Verify gets only the input and output, and startup recovery calls it with a zero output (`internal/core/contract.go`, `Mutator.Verify`), so it does not compare with the plan's stored prediction: it runs the action's own check of the configuration, then the in-sync comparison on the state after apply. A loaded state that is not what the model predicts for the files on disk fails it with `firewall.prediction_mismatch`; the files themselves were checked effect by effect against the predicted after-state hashes (A1's `runJournaled`).
- **Plan-time ruling: transitions** (`fw.predictTarget`). Start when the wanted state is enabled and `ENABLED` is no; stop when the wanted state is disabled and `ENABLED` is yes, or for a repair of a running UFW configured off; reload when commands, a restore or a repair meet an enabled UFW; otherwise none (a request that changes nothing plans an empty diff and runs nothing). After `ufw --force enable`, a reload also follows when UFW's chains are loaded already, because `ufw_start` then prints "Firewall already started" and loads nothing (`.dforge/drafts/v1-w1-firewall/ufw-src/ufwspike-debian-13/ufw/ufw-init-functions:111-115`); that start is predicted as `Predict(Edit(cfg, enable), cur, TransReload)`, since `Predict` refuses `TransEnable` with UFW's chains loaded (part P's contract). `ufw --force enable` on a running UFW exits 0 and only runs `update_logging` (`frontend.py:191-243`, `set_enabled`), so the reload effect's inverse is harmless.
- **Plan-time ruling: `firewall.rule.add` tags its rule with the change id.** The change id is a ULID the engine makes (`internal/core/lifecycle/engine.go:240-245`, `newID`), unique to the change and stable across the apply, verify and a recovery; the plan, which has no change, uses `planRuleID` and shows `rule new`, and the id does not enter the state hash.
- **Plan-time ruling: one output type, `ChangeOutput`,** for every mutating action, with `rules` and `repairOutcome` empty where they do not apply; the repair's outcome must be in the output for `repairOutcomeOf` (`internal/core/lifecycle/repair.go`, part F1's Task 16).
- **Plan-time ruling: `firewall.snapshot.restore` journals its steps** rather than calling A1's `restore`, as part A1 advises (`clone-A1/PLAN-PART.md`, "How the next parts use it"), so its own revert works: each differing file once, then the transition, then each differing sysctl value. A1's file inverse restores the entry of the change's own snapshot whose hash is the effect's before-state (`inverse.go`, `restoreFile`), so each file must be written before any ufw command rewrites it. When the restore changes UFW's state, `ufw.conf` is written with the current `ENABLED` (computed with `predict.Edit`, as UFW's `set_default` rewrites the key), and the following `--force enable` or `disable` sets it as its own effect, whose inverse sets it back (`TestMutationRestore` checks the enable's before-state is disabled).
- **Plan-time ruling: the repair's outcomes.** Run on its own (`RepairOf` empty) the repair reloads or stops UFW from its configuration and takes no outcome. Repairing change R, `restore` restores R's snapshot as `firewall.snapshot.restore` does; `keep` needs R's post-apply hashes (A1 records them at the end of R's Apply) and every file still hashing so, because the module cannot rebuild files it has only hashes of; it then reloads, and verify checks the hashes again. The repair unpins R's snapshot at the end of its own apply: retention keeps the snapshot of every `needs_repair` change anyway (`store.go`, `pruneSnapshots`), so a repair that is reverted later loses nothing.
- **Plan-time ruling: `firewall.rules.apply`.** The label is every added rule's comment, so the rules a composite adds share one tag text; adds come before deletes, so a replaced allow rule is in place before the old one goes; a rule present with the same definition and an id already absent are skipped (`Converges`, spec 1.2); a present id with another definition is refused rather than replaced.
- **Plan-time ruling: preflight** reads UFW's version from `/var/lib/dpkg/status`, because `ufw version` is not on the exec allowlist (`internal/platform/exec_rules.go`, `execUfwVerbs`), and compares the upstream part of the Debian version (epoch and revision removed) by dotted numbers. The tools check asks `<tool> --version` through `env.Exec` (allowlisted) and needs the save and restore tools of that variant, the ones part C's reader and part A1's before-image load run.
- **Plan-time ruling: status `active`** means UFW's chains are loaded (`filter/ufw-user-input`), separately from `configured.enabled` (the file), so the page can show a host whose UFW failed to start.
- **Plan-time ruling: uninstall.** The uninstall step has no output of its own (`internal/install/uninstall.go:569-590`, `runModules`, gives it an Env with a logger), so `baseline` "prints" the manual rules it adds or removes as Info log lines; `keepData` does not change the rules option, since rules are the host's firewall rather than Darkpanel's data; a host without `/usr/sbin/ufw` has nothing to do. The Docker integration's chain cleanup (spec 2.9) belongs to wave 2.
- **Plan-time ruling: diff lines** compare rules by their whole text (`ruleText`), so a rule whose definition changed shows as removed and added, and a reordering of the rules both states hold is one line listing the new order.
- **The end-to-end host** (Tasks 82 and 84) reads the golden capture's tables with the real `loaded.Reader` once, then models the kernel with part P's predictor: a predicted ruleset cannot be written back as save output, because its rules come from restore syntax, which `netfilter.Parse` reads as opaque. The golden `rules` scenario of ubuntu:24.04 is in sync with its own files (`TestE2EGuardCutsSSH` checks status `inSync`), and the `enabled` scenario's tables differ from the `rules` files only in UFW's chains (`TestE2EOutOfSync`). A scratch run on 2026-10-24 showed the guard's message for the SSH case, `ssh from 203.0.113.7 to 192.0.2.1:22 on eth0: drop (filter/INPUT policy DROP)`, and the repair plan's eight differing UFW chains.
- **No container was needed.** Every UFW behaviour this part relies on is part F2's, P's or A1's measurement or a cited UFW source line; this part started no Docker container (`docker ps -a --filter name=dp-w1-A2` printed only the header on 2026-10-24).
- **Frozen files and controller decisions.** No task needed a frozen file, a new error code, an allowlist rule or an extension point.
- **Every task's code was run** before this text was written, on 2026-10-24, from base `55536b3` on branch `a2-part` of the clone. Each task was written test first; each Step 2 output is the real output of the task's test files applied to its parent commit (the two test-only tasks, Task 82 and Task 84, pass there, since the code they cover exists). After each task's commit, a separate worktree at that commit passed all six checks with `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` and a `TMPDIR` under `/root/.cache/w1-tmp/`: `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` (no output), `go test -count=1 ./...` (61 `ok`, 2 `?`, no `FAIL`), `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/modules/firewall/` (`ok`), `golangci-lint run --allow-serial-runners ./...` (`0 issues.`) and `go mod tidy -diff` (no output). #### Part A2 assumptions: the sysctl follow-up

- **Plan-time ruling: Verify reads the change's journal and snapshot.** Verify gets only the input and a zero output at recovery, and the host cannot tell a reload that re-applied UFW's sysctl file from a change that ran no command (a request that changes nothing plans no transition, `target.go`, `fw.predictTarget`, and a host whose live values drifted from the file must not fail verify for it). The record of what the change ran is its effect journal, which the module's Revert reads the same way (`revert.go`); the values from before the change are in its snapshot (`State.Sysctl`, `snapshot.go`, `capture`); the engine's recovery env carries both (`internal/core/lifecycle/effects.go:55-61`, `changeEnv`, used at `recover.go:491`). The brief's "only the host and the module's own store" is read as "no write and no call outside the agent": the journal read is `env.Effects.List`, a read.
- **Plan-time ruling: which keys are checked.** A start that applies UFW's sysctl file predicts the keys the file sets (even at their current value) and every key whose predicted value differs from the one before (the kernel's side effects, for example IPv6 `forwarding` of every interface after `all/forwarding` is written, `loaded/sysctl_predict.go`, `PredictSysctl`). The other supported keys are not compared: other programs change them at any time (Docker, interface hot-plug), and the transition does not set them. A key the kernel no longer has (an interface that has gone) is skipped, as `restoreSysctl` skips it.
- **Plan-time ruling: a change started UFW when its last made effect on `firewall.state:enabled` has `Post` `true`.** `runUfw` records a reload on an enabled UFW as made, because its before and after states are equal (`effects.go`, `runJournaled`), an enable as made with `true` and a disable with `false`; a restore that disables UFW, and a stop, predict no sysctl value (`PredictSysctl` copies the values on `TransDisable`). `TransEnable` is asked whether the start was an enable or a reload: `PredictSysctl` applies the file the same way for both (`sysctl_predict.go`), and `predictTarget` asks it once per change for the same reason.
- **Plan-time ruling: a restore's own writes replace the prediction.** The plan overlays a restore's snapshot values on the prediction (`target.go`, `predictTarget`); `restoreSysctl` writes each snapshot value that differs from the live one after the transition, as a made effect whose `Post` is the value read back (`handler.go`, `restoreSysctl`; `effects.go`, `writeSysctlEffect`), so Verify takes those values from the journal. A key the transition already left at the snapshot's value has no effect and is compared with the prediction of UFW's file: when the kernel disagrees with that prediction but happens to hold the snapshot's value, Verify reports a mismatch although the state is what the plan promised. That case needs a wrong prediction and is rare; it fails safe (the engine reverts), and fixing it needs the restore's own snapshot id in Verify, which the engine does not give a revertible action's Verify beyond its input.
- **Plan-time ruling (gap b): `/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf` is part of the logical state on every host.** Reproduced first, through the module's real restore and revert (`TestRestoreSysctlFileUnset`, Task 88): a snapshot taken while `/etc/default/ufw` set `IPT_SYSCTL` is restored on a host whose `/etc/default/ufw` leaves it unset and whose `/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf` differs. The restore writes `/etc/default/ufw` (which makes `IPT_SYSCTL` set again) and then the sysctl file as an effect whose before-state is the host's file. The change's own snapshot, taken from `conf.Read` while `IPT_SYSCTL` was unset, holds no entry for the file, so (1) a revert that restores the snapshot whole leaves the host's file as the restore wrote it, silently, and (2) a revert that undoes the effects one by one stops at the file's effect with `snapshot <id> holds no entry of /etc/ufw/sysctl.conf with hash "sha256:…"` (`inverse.go`, `restoreFile`), which ends the change in `needs_repair`. The real outputs are in Task 88, Step 2. The cause is `conf.Read` recording the file only while `IPT_SYSCTL` is set (`conf/conf.go`, `reader.sysctl`): a snapshot is the state a restore may bring back, and a restore of `/etc/default/ufw` can switch the file on, so the file must be in the state whether or not it is applied now. The fix records it always (Task 88); the settings are still read only for the file `IPT_SYSCTL` names, and the unsupported-configuration checks on those settings stay tied to it.
- **Evidence for the semantics of an unset `IPT_SYSCTL`.** UFW's init script applies the file only when the variable is non-empty and the file is non-empty: `ufw-init-functions:386-387` (`if [ ! -z "$IPT_SYSCTL" ] && [ -s "$IPT_SYSCTL" ]; then sysctl -e -q -p $IPT_SYSCTL`, `.dforge/drafts/v1-w1-firewall/ufw-src/ufwspike-debian-13/ufw/`). Measured on 2026-10-26 in a privileged container `dp-w1-A2x-1` (ubuntu:24.04, ufw 0.36.2-6, removed afterwards): with the `IPT_SYSCTL` line deleted from `/etc/default/ufw` and `/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf` holding `net/ipv4/ip_forward=1`, `ufw --force enable` and `ufw reload` left `/proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward` at 0; `ufw default deny incoming`, `ufw logging low` and `ufw allow 22/tcp` left `/etc/default/ufw` without an `IPT_SYSCTL` line (ufw edits only the keys it owns); after adding `IPT_SYSCTL=/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf` again, `ufw reload` set `ip_forward` to 1. The fake ufw of `host_test.go` therefore keeps `IPT_SYSCTL` out of `/etc/default/ufw` when it was out (`fhState.NoSysctl`).
- **Plan-time ruling: the fix is in part F2's `conf.Read`, as a recorded fix task.** Part A2's brief allows a subpackage edit only through an explicit fix task whose title says which part's code it fixes (Task 88's title does); the brief of this part asks for the fix at the cause. Doing it in the module root instead (reading the file separately in `capture`, `writeRestored` and `snapshotConfig`) would leave `Config.Files` and the snapshots disagreeing about the file again. The comment of `fwstate.Config.Files` is corrected in the same task. Part F1's test `TestReadDefaults` asserted the old behaviour ("Files holds a sysctl file although IPT_SYSCTL is unset") and now asserts the new one.
- **Consequence for controller review: `conf.Read` now fails on an unusable `/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf` even when `IPT_SYSCTL` is unset.** A symbolic link, a directory or a file over 4 MiB there is an error, as it already was while `IPT_SYSCTL` named it and as it is for every other state file (`readEntry`, `conf/conf.go`). The default Debian and Ubuntu packages ship a regular file (`ufw-src/*/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf`), so none of the four golden hosts is affected (`conf/golden_test.go` passes). No snapshot made before this task exists in any released build, so none needs migrating; a snapshot without the entry still restores, because restore and verify iterate only the entries a snapshot holds.
- **No frozen file, error code, allowlist rule or extension point was needed.** The new check uses `errcode.FirewallPredictionMismatch`, which exists; `env.Effects.List` is in `core.EffectJournal`.

- Owner ruling R2 (spec, Owner decisions): the revert timeout is per apply, `confirmTimeoutSeconds` 10–900 s, default 60. The bounds match `lifecycle.MinConfirmTimeout`/`MaxConfirmTimeout`/`DefaultConfirmTimeout` (`internal/core/lifecycle/apply.go:17-19`), the API refuses others (`internal/controller/api/actions.go:161`), and the engine ignores the field for a class other than revertible (`internal/core/lifecycle/apply.go:292`). The CLI already has `--confirm-timeout` on every revertible action (`internal/cli/mutate.go`, `addConfirmTimeoutFlag`). Brief ruling.
- Rollback semantics (brief ruling): the newest non-system firewall change or the named one; pending → revert through the agent's revert route (`api.Client.Revert`, `internal/agent/api/client.go:271`); confirmed → plan `firewall.snapshot.restore` with that change's snapshot, apply, confirm. "Confirm in the same command" is the apply option `ConfirmNow`, which the engine turns into a confirmation right after verify passes (`internal/core/lifecycle/apply.go:416-421`).
- Plan-time ruling: rollback reads the snapshot taken before a change from the change's own output field `snapshot`, which every mutating firewall action returns (part A2, `internal/modules/firewall/handler.go`, `ChangeOutput.Snapshot`, clone-A2 commit `a2da643`), instead of searching `firewall.snapshots` for the change id.
- Plan-time ruling: when no `--change` is given, rollback skips background-task changes (actor `system:…`, as `systemActor` in `internal/modules/firewall/snapshot.go` defines them) and composite steps (`ParentChangeID` set), and refuses a newest change that is neither pending nor confirmed (for example `reverted` or `needs_repair`) instead of looking past it; `--change` names an older one. The agent lists changes newest first, at most 500 per page, `Before` paging (`internal/core/lifecycle/engine.go:600-620`).
- Plan-time ruling: the break-glass snapshot restore is the **generated** command of `firewall.snapshot.restore` (`darkpanel firewall snapshot restore --local --id <id> --yes --confirm`), not a hand-written one: the generated command already lives at `firewall snapshot restore` (`CommandPath`, `internal/cli/names.go`) and serves agent-side actions over `--local` (`internal/cli/root.go`, `annotationLocal`), and a hand-written `snapshot` under `firewall` is refused by `addHandWritten` as a clash (`internal/cli/modules.go`). Controller ruling 2 (2026-10-24): spec 2.5 is amended on `main` to this generated form; the code stays as it is.
- Controller ruling 3 (2026-10-24): `applyPlan` in `web/src/api/client.ts` gains the optional third parameter `ApplyOptions` (Part constraints say why); the file is not frozen (spec 1.12).
- Plan-time ruling: the change dialog asks for the timeout only when its caller sets `target.revertible`, because a plan does not carry the action's class (`Plan` in `web/src/api/types.ts`).
- Plan-time ruling: a manual rule's deletion first asks "Delete a manual rule?" and then plans with `manual: true`; a snapshot restore asks with a warning and a checkbox whether manual rules may change, and plans with `manual: true` only when ticked, so a restore that would touch manual rules is otherwise refused by the action with `firewall.manual_required` and shown in the dialog (spec 2.2, 2.5).

### Review fix Gfix assumptions (Tasks 94, 95, 105, 112, 113)

- Base and clone: the integration tree at `59fcd8f` (`fix(firewall): always record UFW's sysctl file`, every part merged), cloned into `clone-Gfix`, branch `gfix-part`. `df -h /` showed 78% on 2026-10-26, so no build cache was trimmed. Commits in task order: `9688db6` (Task 105), `f3d9cea` (Task 112), `d3ccbf8` (Task 94), `a8566c7` (Task 113), `1f322da` (Task 95).
- Marks (review finding, Tasks 31 and 36). The plan header's Part E guidance says tailscaled's own flows carry its bypass mark `0x80000` (tailscale `util/linuxfw/linuxfw.go`, `TailscaleBypassMark`) and that the Router wraps the route lookup with `p.Mark`; spec 2.3 (`docs/dforge/specs/2026-10-21-v1-completion-design.md:2783`, at `28598fa`; later spec line numbers are from the same revision) says the out-interface comes from "a forward lookup including policy rules". The evaluator hands the Router the packet with its mark (`internal/modules/firewall/eval/hooks.go:103-104`: `w.pkt.Mark = w.mark.val`, then `w.route(w.pkt)`), and it starts a locally generated packet whose `Mark` is 0 with every mark bit unknown (`eval/mark.go:24-33`), so tailscaled's `-m mark --mark 0x80000/0xff0000` rules are decidable only when the guard gives the packet the mark. Ruling: every lookup of `probes` and `route` passes `p.Mark`, including the reverse-path and reply lookups of incoming flows, whose mark is 0 today, so that the rule has no exception.
- Local output destination (review minor, Task 36). The evaluator accepts only `path == "output" && out != ""` from the Router for an output packet (`eval/hooks.go:109-111`), so the old answer `("input", "")` for an output packet to a local address made the verdict `unknown`; the plan header says `"lo"` is the out-interface of a locally generated flow to a local destination. Ruling: `("output", "lo")`, handled before the non-local cases.
- Controller listeners (spec 1.5, `design.md:1593-1599`: with a controller on the host "the agent adds its listening sockets as protected flows (direct panel, runtime and agent listeners) and its established agent sessions' peers"). Rulings: (a) a listener is a TCP socket in LISTEN state held by the process `facts.controller`, the main process of `darkpanel-controller.service`; a guard context that names a listener of this host while no unit runs gives no listener flows, because the process is unknown. (b) A loopback listener is skipped like every flow from a local address (`fromHere`), a listener bound to another host's address like `listenFor` skips it, and an unspecified IPv6 listener yields both families, as Go's dual-stack listeners accept both. (c) The stand-in sources are `internet4` and `internet6` with `SrcPort` 0, as the brief says. (d) Departure from the brief for one listener: the runtime listener is on the panel bridge's gateway address, and the only rule that opens it is `allow in on dp-panel from <proxy> to <gateway> port 9443` (spec 8, `design.md:4216`); with a gateway `.1` and proxy `.2` (`design.md:4201-4203`). A stand-in internet source would be dropped by that rule on every host with a panel exposure, so every firewall change there would fail the guard. The flow for a listener on an address of `dp-panel` therefore enters on `dp-panel` from the next address of the bridge's network (`.2`, the proxy); when the exposure's guard context names the same proxy and listener, flow 3 builds the identical packet first and keeps its label. The owner confirmed this ruling on 2026-10-26. (e) A panel or agent port that a rule restricts to certain sources fails the stand-in flow, which is overridable; the NPM public flow behaves the same way.
- IPv6 forwarding (spec 2.1, `design.md:2587-2593`: "an IPv6 interface with `accept_ra=1` stops accepting router advertisements while it forwards" and "a change to IPv6 forwarding on a host whose default IPv6 route was learned from router advertisements fails the guard as `unknown`"). How `Check` gets the predicted values today: the plan passes the predicted loaded state `p.tg.pred` (`internal/modules/firewall/plan.go:126`), whose `Sysctl` comes from `loaded.PredictSysctl` (`plan.go:92`, `loaded/sysctl_predict.go:49`), and `Check` takes it as `st`. It gets the live values from nothing yet, so the guard reads them itself through `env.Files.ReadSysctl`, which the firewall manifest allows for `net/ipv6/conf/<iface>/forwarding` (`internal/modules/firewall/firewall.go:27`); `Input` is unchanged. Rulings: "a change" is any supported `net/ipv6/conf/*/forwarding` value of `st` that differs from the live one, in both directions and for `all`, `default` or any interface, because the spec states the rule for the host and `PredictSysctl` spreads a write of `all` to every interface; the rule does not look at `accept_ra` or at the route's interface, so it errs toward refusing, and an `unknown` is overridable (spec 2.3). A default route is a route whose protocol is `netstat.RouteProtoRA` (`RTPROT_RA`, 9, `internal/platform/netstat/routes.go:24`) and whose prefix length is 0, in any table. A key the kernel lacks (`fs.ErrNotExist`, IPv6 off or the interface gone) is no change; any other read error is an error. The routes are read only when a value differs. The owner confirmed this ruling, including that it errs toward refusing, on 2026-10-26.
- Why `Routes` is not a method of `Host`: adding a method to `Host` changes a shared interface (ladder coupling 3), which Rule S cannot score with the rest of the task. Ruling: a separate optional interface, `routeDumper`, with the fail-closed rule above. The end-to-end tests do change forwarding: with `Routes` missing from `e2eNet`, `go test -count=1 ./internal/modules/firewall/` on 2026-10-26 failed with `--- FAIL: TestE2EVerifySysctl` and `plan firewall.logging.set: firewall: the lockout guard: firewall: the host cannot list routes`, so Task 113 adds the method to the fake (the task depends on Task 82, which created that file).
- `TestLiveHost` (review minor, Task 17). Evidence of the defect, 2026-10-26: the unedited test binary run in a private network namespace (`unshare -n sh -c 'ip link set lo up; guard-old.test -test.run "TestLiveHost$" -test.v'`; the namespace is empty, nothing on the host changes) printed `facts_test.go:254: the host has no sockets` and `--- FAIL: TestLiveHost`; the edited binary printed `--- PASS: TestLiveHost` in the same namespace and in this host's own.
- Not done, by the part brief: the review's minor findings on the `firewall:` error prefix and on the unlisted unexported names are outside this part.
