func TestParseRestoreSyntax(t *testing.T) {
	rs, err := ParseRestore(strings.NewReader(rsSample))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(rs.Tables) != 1 || rs.Tables[0].Name != "filter" {
		t.Fatalf("tables = %+v, want filter once", rs.Tables)
	}
	f := rs.Table("filter")
	if names := chainNames(f); !slices.Equal(names, []string{"ufw-a", "ufw-b", "INPUT", "ufw-late"}) {
		t.Fatalf("chains = %v", names)
	}
	a := f.Chain("ufw-a").Rules
	if len(a) != 6 || a[0].Line != 9 || a[0].Target.Name != "RETURN" {
		t.Fatalf("ufw-a = %+v, want the -I rule first", a)
	}
	want := Rule{
		Line: 5, Text: "-A ufw-a -p tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m recent --set",
		Proto: NameMatch{Name: "tcp"},
		Matches: []Match{
			{Module: "tcp", Options: []Option{{Name: "dport", Values: []string{"22"}}}},
			{Module: "conntrack", Options: []Option{{Name: "ctstate", Values: []string{"NEW"}}}},
			{Module: "recent", Options: []Option{{Name: "set"}}},
		},
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(a[1], want) {
		t.Errorf("implicit tcp rule:\n got %+v\nwant %+v", a[1], want)
	}
	udp := a[2]
	if udp.Source.Prefix != netip.MustParsePrefix("10.0.0.1/32") || len(udp.Matches) != 1 ||
		!reflect.DeepEqual(udp.Matches[0], Match{Module: "udp", Options: []Option{
			{Name: "sport", Values: []string{"67"}}, {Name: "dport", Values: []string{"68"}}}}) {
		t.Errorf("udp rule = %+v, want a host source and one implicit udp match", udp)
	}
	icmp := a[3]
	if icmp.Dest.Prefix != netip.MustParsePrefix("192.0.2.0/24") || icmp.Matches[0].Module != "icmp" ||
		!icmp.Target.Chain || icmp.Target.Name != "ufw-b" {
		t.Errorf("icmp rule = %+v, want a masked destination, an implicit icmp match and a jump", icmp)
	}
	logRule := a[4]
	if logRule.Target.Name != "LOG" || len(logRule.Target.Options) != 1 || logRule.Matches[0].Module != "limit" ||
		len(logRule.Matches[0].Options) != 2 {
		t.Errorf("LOG rule = %+v, want the target's option and the limit match after it", logRule)
	}
	if a[5].Proto.Name != "tcp" || a[5].Matches[0].Module != "multiport" {
		t.Errorf("protocol 6 = %+v, want tcp", a[5])
	}
	b := f.Chain("ufw-b").Rules
	if len(b) != 3 || b[1].Line != 18 {
		t.Fatalf("ufw-b = %+v, want the redeclared chain's three rules with the -I at position 2", b)
	}
	if b[0].Proto.Name != "ipv6-icmp" || b[0].Matches[0].Module != "icmp6" || b[0].Source.Prefix != netip.MustParsePrefix("fe80::1/128") ||
		!b[0].Target.Chain {
		t.Errorf("icmpv6 rule = %+v, want ipv6-icmp, an implicit icmp6 match, a host source and a jump to a later chain", b[0])
	}
	if b[2].Proto != (NameMatch{}) {
		t.Errorf("-p all = %+v, want no protocol", b[2].Proto)
	}
	in := f.Chain("INPUT")
	if !in.Builtin || in.Policy != "DROP" || len(in.Rules) != 1 || !in.Rules[0].Target.Chain {
		t.Errorf("INPUT = %+v, want the built-in chain with its policy and the rule appended before it was declared", in)
	}
	for _, c := range f.Chains {
		for _, r := range c.Rules {
			if r.Opaque() {
				t.Errorf("line %d opaque: %q", r.Line, r.Unsupported)
			}
		}
	}
}

func chainNames(t *Table) []string {
	var out []string
	for _, c := range t.Chains {
		out = append(out, c.Name)
	}
	return out
}

func TestParseRestoreChains(t *testing.T) {
	in := "*nat\n-A POSTROUTING -j MASQUERADE\n:POSTROUTING ACCEPT [0:0]\n-A OUTPUT -j DOCKER\nCOMMIT\n"
	rs, err := ParseRestore(strings.NewReader(in))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	nat := rs.Table("nat")
	if c := nat.Chain("POSTROUTING"); !c.Builtin || c.Policy != "ACCEPT" || len(c.Rules) != 1 {
		t.Errorf("POSTROUTING = %+v, want built-in with its policy, keeping its rule", c)
	}
	if c := nat.Chain("OUTPUT"); !c.Builtin || c.Policy != "" {
		t.Errorf("OUTPUT = %+v, want built-in without a policy", c)
	}
	if r := nat.Chain("OUTPUT").Rules[0]; r.Target.Chain || !r.Opaque() {
		t.Errorf("a jump to a chain the input never names = %+v, want an opaque target", r)
	}
	flushed, err := ParseRestore(strings.NewReader("*filter\n:X - [0:0]\n-A X -j ACCEPT\n:X - [0:0]\n-A X -j DROP\nCOMMIT\n"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if r := flushed.Table("filter").Chain("X").Rules; len(r) != 1 || r[0].Target.Name != "DROP" {
		t.Errorf("a redeclared chain = %+v, want it flushed", r)
	}
}

func TestParseRestoreErrors(t *testing.T) {
	for name, tc := range map[string]struct{ in, want string }{
		"unknown table":       {"*broute\nCOMMIT\n", `line 1: unknown table "broute"`},
		"nested table":        {"*nat\n*raw\n", "line 2: table raw opened inside table nat"},
		"no commit":           {"*nat\n:X - [0:0]\n", "table nat has no COMMIT"},
		"stray commit":        {"COMMIT\n", "line 1: COMMIT outside a table"},
		"chain outside":       {":X - [0:0]\n", "line 1: chain declared outside a table"},
		"rule outside":        {"-A X -j ACCEPT\n", "line 1: rule outside a table"},
		"bad declaration":     {"*nat\n:X\n", `line 2: malformed chain declaration "X"`},
		"bad policy":          {"*filter\n:INPUT REJECT [0:0]\n", `line 2: chain INPUT has policy "REJECT"`},
		"user chain policy":   {"*filter\n:X DROP [0:0]\n", "line 2: chain X is not built-in, so it has no policy"},
		"no chain":            {"*filter\n-A\n", "line 2: -A without a chain"},
		"insert beyond":       {"*filter\n:X - [0:0]\n-I X 2 -j ACCEPT\n", "line 3: insert at 2 into chain X of 0 rules"},
		"insert at zero":      {"*filter\n:X - [0:0]\n-I X 0 -j ACCEPT\n", "line 3: insert at 0 into chain X of 0 rules"},
		"other command":       {"*filter\n-D X 1\n", `line 2: unexpected line "-D X 1"`},
		"unterminated":        {"*filter\n-A X -m comment --comment \"open\n", "line 2: unterminated quote"},
		"loose value":         {"*filter\n-A X extra\n", `line 2: value "extra" without an option`},
		"empty":               {"", "no tables in the input"},
		"comments only":       {"# nothing\n\n", "no tables in the input"},
		"incompatible note":   {"# Table `raw' is incompatible, use 'nft' tool.\n", "no tables in the input"},
		"undeclared one rule": {"*filter\n-A X -j\n", "line 2: -j needs one name"},
	} {
		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
			_, err := ParseRestore(strings.NewReader(tc.in))
			if err == nil || err.Error() != "netfilter: "+tc.want {
				t.Fatalf("err = %v, want netfilter: %s", err, tc.want)
			}
			if strings.HasSuffix(tc.want, "no tables in the input") && !errors.Is(err, ErrNoTables) {
				t.Fatalf("err = %v, want ErrNoTables", err)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestParseRestoreUFW parses every rules file UFW loads on each image, alone
// and as the whole load of its first start, which leaves no rule opaque.
func TestParseRestoreUFW(t *testing.T) {
	for _, image := range ufwImages {
		for _, ipv6 := range []bool{false, true} {
			typ := ""
			if ipv6 {
				typ = "6"
			}
			t.Run(image+"/v4"+typ, func(t *testing.T) {
				for _, file := range []string{"before", "after", "user"} {
					b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join("testdata", "ufw", image, file+typ+".rules")) //nolint:gosec // G304: a fixture under testdata/
					if err != nil {
						t.Fatal(err)
					}
					if _, err := ParseRestore(strings.NewReader(string(b))); err != nil {
						t.Errorf("%s%s.rules: %v", file, typ, err)
					}
				}
				rs, err := ParseRestore(strings.NewReader(ufwLoad(t, image, ipv6)))
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
				u := "ufw" + typ
				f := rs.Table("filter")
				for _, c := range f.Chains {
					for _, r := range c.Rules {
						if r.Opaque() {
							t.Errorf("chain %s line %d opaque: %q", c.Name, r.Line, r.Unsupported)
						}
					}
				}
				if in := f.Chain("INPUT"); in.Policy != "DROP" || len(in.Rules) != 6 {
					t.Errorf("INPUT = %s with %d rules, want DROP with UFW's six jumps", in.Policy, len(in.Rules))
				}
				deny := f.Chain(u + "-logging-deny").Rules
				if len(deny) != 2 || deny[0].Target.Name != "RETURN" || deny[1].Target.Name != "LOG" {
					t.Errorf("%s-logging-deny = %+v, want the inserted RETURN before the LOG", u, deny)
				}
				before := f.Chain(u + "-before-input").Rules
				if last := before[len(before)-1]; last.Target.Name != u+"-user-input" || !last.Target.Chain {
					t.Errorf("%s-before-input ends with %+v, want the jump to %s-user-input", u, last, u)
				}
				first := f.Chain(u + "-user-input").Rules[0]
				if first.Proto.Name != "tcp" || len(first.Matches) != 1 || first.Matches[0].Module != "tcp" {
					t.Errorf("%s-user-input's first rule = %+v, want an implicit tcp match", u, first)
				}
			})
		}
	}
}

// FuzzParseRestore feeds arbitrary input to ParseRestore: it must never
// panic, and a ruleset it accepts holds known tables once each, every jump
// to a chain names a chain of its table, and every other unknown target is
// opaque (spec 1.8, R74).
func FuzzParseRestore(f *testing.F) {
	seeds, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join("testdata", "ufw", "*", "*.rules"))
	if err != nil {
		f.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, name := range seeds {
		b, err := os.ReadFile(name) //nolint:gosec // G304: a fixture under testdata/
		if err != nil {
			f.Fatal(err)
		}
		f.Add(string(b))
	}
	f.Add(rsSample)
	f.Fuzz(func(t *testing.T, in string) {
		rs, err := ParseRestore(strings.NewReader(in))
		if err != nil {
			return
		}
		seen := map[string]bool{}
		for _, tb := range rs.Tables {
			if !slices.Contains(Tables(), tb.Name) || seen[tb.Name] {
				t.Fatalf("table %q unknown or repeated", tb.Name)
			}
			seen[tb.Name] = true
			for _, c := range tb.Chains {
				for _, r := range c.Rules {
					if r.Target.Chain && tb.Chain(r.Target.Name) == nil {
						t.Fatalf("jump to undeclared chain %q", r.Target.Name)
					}
					if _, ok := targets[r.Target.Name]; r.Target.Name != "" && !r.Target.Chain && !ok && !r.Opaque() {
						t.Fatalf("unknown target %q not opaque", r.Target.Name)
					}
				}
			}
		}
	})
}

```go
package netfilter

import (
	"bufio"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"slices"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

// builtinChains are each table's built-in chains.
var builtinChains = map[string][]string{
	"filter":   {"INPUT", "FORWARD", "OUTPUT"},
	"nat":      {"PREROUTING", "INPUT", "OUTPUT", "POSTROUTING"},
	"mangle":   {"PREROUTING", "INPUT", "FORWARD", "OUTPUT", "POSTROUTING"},
	"raw":      {"PREROUTING", "OUTPUT"},
	"security": {"INPUT", "FORWARD", "OUTPUT"},
}

// protoNames maps the protocol numbers and aliases iptables accepts for the
// protocols UFW, Docker and tailscaled use to the names iptables-save
// prints.
var protoNames = map[string]string{
	"1": "icmp", "2": "igmp", "6": "tcp", "17": "udp", "41": "ipv6", "47": "gre", "50": "esp", "51": "ah",
	"58": "ipv6-icmp", "icmpv6": "ipv6-icmp", "icmp6": "ipv6-icmp",
}

// canonicalProto is the protocol name iptables-save prints for p.
func canonicalProto(p string) string {
	p = strings.ToLower(p)
	if name, ok := protoNames[p]; ok {
		return name
	}
	return p
}

// implicitModules are the modules iptables loads by itself for an option of
// a rule's protocol given without -m, by canonical protocol name.
var implicitModules = map[string]string{"tcp": "tcp", "udp": "udp", "icmp": "icmp", "ipv6-icmp": "icmp6"}

// restoreOwner is the extension an option of a restore-syntax rule belongs
// to. iptables merges the options of every loaded extension, so the option
// goes to the current extension when it defines it, else to the latest
// loaded module or the target that does; failing those, an option of the
// rule's protocol module loads that module, as iptables does for -p tcp,
// udp, icmp and icmpv6 without -m. An option nothing defines stays with the
// current extension, for classify to report.
func (r *Rule) restoreOwner(cur int, name string) int {
	if r.defines(cur, name) {
		return cur
	}
	for i := len(r.Matches) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		if r.defines(i, name) {
			return i
		}
	}
	if r.defines(extTarget, name) {
		return extTarget
	}
	m := implicitModules[r.Proto.Name]
	if m == "" || r.Proto.Neg || slices.ContainsFunc(r.Matches, func(x Match) bool { return x.Module == m }) {
		return cur
	}
	if _, ok := modules[m][name]; !ok {
		return cur
	}
	r.Matches = append(r.Matches, Match{Module: m})
	return len(r.Matches) - 1
}

// defines reports whether the extension ext of r takes the option name in
// the contract.
func (r *Rule) defines(ext int, name string) bool {
	var known arity
	switch {
	case ext == extTarget && r.Target.Name != "":
		known = targets[r.Target.Name]
	case ext >= 0:
		known = modules[r.Matches[ext].Module]
	}
	_, ok := known[name]
	return ok
}

// ParseRestore reads iptables-restore input, as UFW's rules files and the
// firewall predictor's output are written, into the structure Parse gives
// save output: the ruleset `*-restore --noflush` would load into empty
// tables. A table may appear in several blocks, which continue it; a
// declared chain that exists already is flushed when it is a user chain and
// takes the declared policy when it is built-in; -A appends and -I inserts
// at its position (1 when none); a rule for a chain the input never
// declares creates that chain, built-in when the table has a built-in
// chain of that name, with Policy "". Rules are read as iptables-restore
// reads them (parseRule's restore syntax), and a jump resolves to a chain
// the input declares or appends to anywhere, so the files of one load are
// passed as one reader, in load order, each ending in a newline. Input
// without a table is ErrNoTables.
func ParseRestore(r io.Reader) (*Ruleset, error) {
	p := restoreParser{cur: -1}
	sc := bufio.NewScanner(r)
	sc.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, 64<<10), maxLine)
	for sc.Scan() {
		p.line++
		if err := p.parseLine(strings.TrimRight(sc.Text(), " \t\r")); err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("netfilter: line %d: %w", p.line, err)
		}
	}
	if err := sc.Err(); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("netfilter: %w", err)
	}
	if p.cur >= 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("netfilter: table %s has no COMMIT", p.rs.Tables[p.cur].Name)
	}
	if len(p.rs.Tables) == 0 {
		return nil, ErrNoTables
	}
	for ti := range p.rs.Tables {
		t := &p.rs.Tables[ti]
		for ci := range t.Chains {
			for ri := range t.Chains[ci].Rules {
				rule := &t.Chains[ci].Rules[ri]
				rule.Target.Chain = rule.Target.Name != "" && t.Chain(rule.Target.Name) != nil
				classify(rule)
			}
		}
	}
	return &p.rs, nil
}

type restoreParser struct {
	rs   Ruleset
	cur  int // index of the open table in rs.Tables; -1 outside a block
	line int
}

func (p *restoreParser) parseLine(line string) error {
	switch {
	case line == "" || strings.HasPrefix(line, "#"):
		return nil
	case strings.HasPrefix(line, "*"):
		return p.openTable(line[1:])
	case line == "COMMIT":
		if p.cur < 0 {
			return errors.New("COMMIT outside a table")
		}
		p.cur = -1
		return nil
	case strings.HasPrefix(line, ":"):
		return p.declareChain(line[1:])
	case line == "-A" || line == "-I" || strings.HasPrefix(line, "-A ") || strings.HasPrefix(line, "-I "):
		return p.addRule(line)
	}
	return fmt.Errorf("unexpected line %q", truncate(line))
}

func (p *restoreParser) openTable(name string) error {
	if p.cur >= 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("table %s opened inside table %s", name, p.rs.Tables[p.cur].Name)
	}
	if !slices.Contains(knownTables, name) {
		return fmt.Errorf("unknown table %q", truncate(name))
	}
	p.cur = slices.IndexFunc(p.rs.Tables, func(t Table) bool { return t.Name == name })
	if p.cur < 0 {
		p.rs.Tables = append(p.rs.Tables, Table{Name: name})
		p.cur = len(p.rs.Tables) - 1
	}
	return nil
}

// chain returns the open table's chain name, creating it when absent.
func (p *restoreParser) chain(name string) *Chain {
	t := &p.rs.Tables[p.cur]
	if c := t.Chain(name); c != nil {
		return c
	}
	t.Chains = append(t.Chains, Chain{Name: name, Builtin: slices.Contains(builtinChains[t.Name], name)})
	return &t.Chains[len(t.Chains)-1]
}

func (p *restoreParser) declareChain(decl string) error {
	if p.cur < 0 {
		return errors.New("chain declared outside a table")
	}
	f := strings.Fields(decl)
	if len(f) < 2 || len(f) > 3 {
		return fmt.Errorf("malformed chain declaration %q", truncate(decl))
	}
	if f[1] != "-" && f[1] != "ACCEPT" && f[1] != "DROP" {
		return fmt.Errorf("chain %s has policy %q", f[0], truncate(f[1]))
	}
	builtin := slices.Contains(builtinChains[p.rs.Tables[p.cur].Name], f[0])
	if f[1] != "-" && !builtin {
		return fmt.Errorf("chain %s is not built-in, so it has no policy", f[0])
	}
	c := p.chain(f[0])
	switch {
	case !builtin:
		c.Rules = nil
	case f[1] != "-":
		c.Policy = f[1]
	}
	return nil
}

func (p *restoreParser) addRule(line string) error {
	if p.cur < 0 {
		return errors.New("rule outside a table")
	}
	toks, err := tokenize(line)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	cmd := toks[0].text
	if len(toks) < 2 || toks[1].quoted {
		return fmt.Errorf("%s without a chain", cmd)
	}
	rest, pos := toks[2:], 1
	if cmd == "-I" && len(rest) > 0 && !rest[0].quoted {
		if n, err := strconv.Atoi(rest[0].text); err == nil {
			rest, pos = rest[1:], n
		}
	}
	rule, err := parseRule(rest, true)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	rule.Line, rule.Text = p.line, line
	c := p.chain(toks[1].text)
	if cmd == "-A" {
		c.Rules = append(c.Rules, rule)
		return nil
	}
	if pos < 1 || pos > len(c.Rules)+1 {
		return fmt.Errorf("insert at %d into chain %s of %d rules", pos, c.Name, len(c.Rules))
	}
	c.Rules = slices.Insert(c.Rules, pos-1, rule)
	return nil
}

// parseAddr reads an -s or -d value. Save output always prints a prefix;
// restore input may also give a bare address, a host prefix, or a prefix
// with host bits set, which iptables masks.
func parseAddr(v string, restore bool) (netip.Prefix, bool) {
	if pfx, err := netip.ParsePrefix(v); err == nil {
		if restore {
			return pfx.Masked(), true
		}
		return pfx, true
	}
	if !restore {
		return netip.Prefix{}, false
	}
	a, err := netip.ParseAddr(v)
	if err != nil || a.Zone() != "" {
		return netip.Prefix{}, false
	}
	return netip.PrefixFrom(a, a.BitLen()), true
}

### Task 12: CLI --confirm-timeout on change repair

**Files:**
- Modify: `internal/cli/change.go`
- Test: `internal/cli/change_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `addConfirmTimeoutFlag`, `confirmTimeout`, `planAndApply` (Task 6)
- Produces: `darkpanel change repair --confirm-timeout` (Part contracts, Task 12)

**Depends on:** Task 6

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-sonnet-medium
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 1 - risk 1 = 3

`darkpanel change repair` applies a repair plan, and a revertible repair action such as `firewall.state.repair` arms the revert timer too. The command gains the flag, range-checked before the repair request. The repairing action is known only from the answer, so a non-revertible plan given the flag is refused before it is applied. The test covers a revertible plan, a compensable plan and an out-of-range value.

// TestChangeRepairConfirmTimeout: change repair sends --confirm-timeout with
// the apply of a revertible repair plan, refuses it for any other plan
// before applying, and refuses a value out of range before the repair
// request.
func TestChangeRepairConfirmTimeout(t *testing.T) {
	base := newFakeAPI(t, testToken,
		exchange{method: "POST", path: "/api/v1/changes/c6/repair", body: `{}`,
			reply: `{"plan":` + planJSON("p6", "demo.rule.set", "h1", "", `[]`) + `}`},
		exchange{method: "POST", path: "/api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/demo.rule.set/v1/apply", body: `{"planId":"p6","confirmTimeoutSeconds":120}`,
			reply: changeJSON("c7", "demo.rule.set", "revertible", "pending",
				`"revertDeadline":"2026-10-18T12:02:00Z","output":null,"error":null,"compensatedBy":null`)},
		exchange{method: "POST", path: "/api/v1/changes/c8/repair", body: `{}`,
			reply: `{"plan":` + planJSON("p8", "demo.item.add", "h1", "", `[]`) + `}`},
	)
	cli := cliEnv{env: tokenEnv}
	out, errOut, code := cli.run(t, "change", "repair", "c6", "--yes", "--confirm-timeout", "120", "--url", base)
	if code != 0 || !strings.Contains(out, "Change c7: pending") || !strings.Contains(out, "Confirm it before 2026-10-18T12:02:00Z") {
		t.Errorf("revertible repair plan: exit %d, out %q, err %q", code, out, errOut)
	}
	if _, errOut, code := cli.run(t, "change", "repair", "c8", "--yes", "--confirm-timeout", "120", "--url", base); code != ExitUsage ||
		!strings.Contains(errOut, "--confirm-timeout applies only to a revertible repair action; demo.item.add/v1 is compensable") {
		t.Errorf("compensable repair plan: exit %d, err %q; want a usage error", code, errOut)
	}
	if _, errOut, code := cli.run(t, "change", "repair", "c9", "--confirm-timeout", "5", "--url", base); code != ExitUsage ||
		!strings.Contains(errOut, "--confirm-timeout must be 10 to 900 seconds, not 5") {
		t.Errorf("out of range: exit %d, err %q; want a usage error before the repair request", code, errOut)
	}
}

### Task 13: UFW rule tuples and merge

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/modules/firewall/model/tuple.go`
- Test: `internal/modules/firewall/model/tuple_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: Part contracts Task 10 (`Rule`, the enums, `Protos`, `Any`, `ParseTag`, `problems`, `maxPortSlots`; test helper `ruleTestID`).
- Produces: Part contracts Task 13 (`TuplePrefix`, `Tuple`, `ParseTuple`, `Tuple.Rule`, `Merge`; unexported `manualID`).

**Depends on:** Task 10

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-sonnet-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 2 - risk 2 = 5

Parses the `### tuple ###` lines of `user.rules` and `user6.rules` exactly as UFW 0.36 reads them, converts a tuple to a `Rule` (or marks it unrepresentable with its raw line), and merges the two files into one rule list where UFW's two halves of an any/any rule become one `both` rule. The expected manual ids in the tests were computed independently with `printf '%s%s' <family> <line> | sha256sum`. The fuzz target checks that every rule called representable passes the grammar.

	for _, c := range cases {
		tu, err := ParseTuple(c.line, c.v6)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("ParseTuple(%q): %v", c.line, err)
		}
		got, ok := tu.Rule()
		if ok != c.ok || !reflect.DeepEqual(got, c.want) {
			t.Errorf("Rule() of %q\n got %+v, %v\nwant %+v, %v", c.line, got, ok, c.want, c.ok)
		}
	}
}

func TestMerge(t *testing.T) {
	parse := func(lines []string, v6 bool) []Tuple {
		var out []Tuple
		for _, l := range lines {
			tu, err := ParseTuple(l, v6)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("ParseTuple(%q): %v", l, err)
			}
			out = append(out, tu)
		}
		return out
	}
	v4 := parse([]string{tupleTestSSH, tupleTestRoute, tupleTestLimit, tupleTestLog, tupleTestApp, tupleTestFwd}, false)
	v6 := parse([]string{tupleTestSSH6, tupleTestUDP6, tupleTestLimit6, tupleTestApp6, tupleTestFwd6, tupleTestHostBit}, true)
	want := []Rule{
		{ID: ruleTestID, Action: ActionAllow, Direction: DirIn, Proto: ProtoTCP, From: Any, To: Any, ToPort: "22",
			Family: FamilyBoth, Log: LogOff, Comment: "ssh", Origin: OriginDarkpanel},
		{ID: "manual-ef4bffdeac1f78d0", Action: ActionAllow, Direction: DirRoute, Proto: ProtoTCP, From: Any, To: "172.17.0.2",
			ToPort: "80", OutIface: "eth0", Family: FamilyV4, Log: LogOff, Origin: OriginManual},
		{ID: "manual-366f31a1f1903fdf", Action: ActionLimit, Direction: DirIn, Proto: ProtoTCP, From: Any, To: Any, ToPort: "2222",
			Family: FamilyBoth, Log: LogOff, Origin: OriginManual},
		{ID: "manual-fbec77a7f9553c86", Action: ActionAllow, Direction: DirIn, Proto: ProtoTCP, From: "10.0.0.0/8", To: Any,
			ToPort: "443,8000:8100", Family: FamilyV4, Log: LogOn, Origin: OriginManual},
		{ID: "manual-d1b2d8ed16e39ee8", Action: ActionAllow, Direction: DirIn, Family: FamilyBoth, Log: LogOff,
			Origin: OriginManual, Raw: tupleTestApp},
		{ID: "manual-83c8e87200530bb0", Action: ActionDeny, Direction: DirRoute, Proto: ProtoAny, From: Any, To: Any,
			InIface: "eth0", OutIface: "docker0", Family: FamilyBoth, Log: LogAll, Comment: "hand", Origin: OriginManual},
		{ID: "manual-10082ef169e6cca9", Action: ActionDeny, Direction: DirIn, Proto: ProtoUDP, From: "2001:db8::/32", To: Any,
			ToPort: "5000:5100", Family: FamilyV6, Log: LogOff, Origin: OriginManual},
		{ID: "manual-886f40953635d33b", Action: ActionDeny, Direction: DirIn, Family: FamilyV6, Log: LogOff,
			Origin: OriginManual, Raw: tupleTestHostBit},
	}
	got := Merge(v4, v6)
	if len(got) != len(want) {
		t.Fatalf("Merge returned %d rules, want %d: %+v", len(got), len(want), got)
	}
	for i := range want {
		if !reflect.DeepEqual(got[i], want[i]) {
			t.Errorf("rule %d\n got %+v\nwant %+v", i, got[i], want[i])
		}
	}
	if again := Merge(v4, v6); !reflect.DeepEqual(again, got) {
		t.Error("Merge is not stable across calls")
	}
	// Equal tuples whose comments differ stay apart, and a v6 tuple pairs
	// with at most one v4 tuple.
	split := Merge(parse([]string{tupleTestLimit, tupleTestLimit}, false), parse([]string{
		strings.Replace(tupleTestLimit6, " in", " in comment=78", 1), tupleTestLimit6}, true))
	fams := []Family{}
	for _, r := range split {
		fams = append(fams, r.Family)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(fams, []Family{FamilyBoth, FamilyV4, FamilyV6}) {
		t.Errorf("families = %v, want [both v4 v6]", fams)
	}
}

// FuzzParseTuple checks that no line panics the parser and that every rule
// it calls representable passes the grammar.
func FuzzParseTuple(f *testing.F) {
	for _, l := range []string{tupleTestSSH, tupleTestRoute, tupleTestLog, tupleTestApp, tupleTestFwd, tupleTestUDP6, tupleTestHostBit} {
		f.Add(l, false)
		f.Add(l, true)
	}
	f.Fuzz(func(t *testing.T, line string, v6 bool) {
		tu, err := ParseTuple(line, v6)
		if err != nil {
			return
		}
		r, ok := tu.Rule()
		if ok && len(r.problems(false)) > 0 {
			t.Fatalf("representable rule %+v has problems %v", r, r.problems(false))
		}
		if !ok && r.Raw == "" {
			t.Fatalf("unrepresentable rule %+v has no Raw", r)
		}
	})
}

Create `internal/modules/firewall/model/tuple.go`:

```go
package model

import (
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/hex"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net/netip"
	"regexp"
	"slices"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"unicode/utf8"
)

// TuplePrefix starts every rule line UFW writes in user.rules and
// user6.rules.
const TuplePrefix = "### tuple ###"

// Tuple is one "### tuple ###" line of user.rules or user6.rules, parsed as
// UFW 0.36 reads it (backend_iptables.py _read_rules). Addresses keep UFW's
// form: "0.0.0.0/0" or "::/0" for any, as the file's family requires.
type Tuple struct {
	Action    Action
	Log       Log // LogOff when the action has no _log or _log-all suffix
	Route     bool
	Proto     Proto
	DPort     string // "any" or a port list
	Dst       string
	SPort     string
	Src       string
	DApp      string // application profile names, "" for none
	SApp      string
	Direction Direction // DirIn or DirOut
	InIface   string
	OutIface  string
	Comment   string // decoded from the comment=<hex> field
	Family    Family // FamilyV4 for user.rules, FamilyV6 for user6.rules
	Raw       string // the line as read, trailing white space removed
}

var (
	tupleIfaceRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-zA-Z0-9_.+,=%@-]{1,15}$`)
	ifaceInRe    = regexp.MustCompile(`in_\w+`)
	ifaceOutRe   = regexp.MustCompile(`out_\w+`)
	tuplePortRe  = regexp.MustCompile(`^[0-9]+(:[0-9]+)?$`)
)

// ParseTuple parses one tuple line; v6 says it comes from user6.rules. It
// refuses what UFW would skip as malformed, and also an action, address or
// port UFW would silently reinterpret, so a hand-edited file is reported
// rather than guessed at.
func ParseTuple(line string, v6 bool) (Tuple, error) {
	raw := strings.TrimRight(line, " \t\r\n")
	rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(raw, TuplePrefix)
	if !ok {
		return Tuple{}, errors.New("model: not a tuple line")
	}
	t := Tuple{Raw: raw, Family: FamilyV4, Log: LogOff, Direction: DirIn}
	if v6 {
		t.Family = FamilyV6
	}
	if strings.Count(rest, " comment=") > 1 {
		return Tuple{}, errors.New("model: tuple has more than one comment")
	}
	body, hexComment, found := strings.Cut(rest, " comment=")
	if found {
		b, err := hex.DecodeString(strings.TrimSpace(hexComment))
		if err != nil || !utf8.Valid(b) {
			return Tuple{}, errors.New("model: tuple comment is not hex-encoded UTF-8")
		}
		t.Comment = string(b)
	}
	f := strings.Fields(body)
	if len(f) < 6 || len(f) > 9 {
		return Tuple{}, fmt.Errorf("model: tuple has %d fields, want 6 to 9", len(f))
	}
	if len(f) == 7 || len(f) == 9 {
		if err := t.parseIfaces(f[len(f)-1]); err != nil {
			return Tuple{}, err
		}
	}
	if err := t.parseAction(f[0]); err != nil {
		return Tuple{}, err
	}
	t.Proto = Proto(f[1])
	if !slices.Contains(Protos(), t.Proto) {
		return Tuple{}, fmt.Errorf("model: tuple protocol %q is not supported", f[1])
	}
	var err error
	if t.DPort, err = tuplePort(f[2]); err != nil {
		return Tuple{}, err
	}
	if t.Dst, err = tupleAddr(f[3], v6); err != nil {
		return Tuple{}, err
	}
	if t.SPort, err = tuplePort(f[4]); err != nil {
		return Tuple{}, err
	}
	if t.Src, err = tupleAddr(f[5], v6); err != nil {
		return Tuple{}, err
	}
	if len(f) >= 8 {
		t.DApp, t.SApp = tupleApp(f[6]), tupleApp(f[7])
	}
	return t, nil
}

// parseIfaces reads the last field of a 7- or 9-field tuple: "in", "out",
// "in_<if>", "out_<if>" or "in_<if>!out_<if>".
func (t *Tuple) parseIfaces(s string) error {
	dir, _, _ := strings.Cut(s, "_")
	if strings.Contains(s, "_") {
		switch {
		case strings.Contains(s, "!") && ifaceInRe.MatchString(s) && ifaceOutRe.MatchString(s):
			in, out, _ := strings.Cut(s, "!")
			_, t.InIface, _ = strings.Cut(in, "_")
			_, t.OutIface, _ = strings.Cut(out, "_")
		case strings.HasPrefix(s, "in_"):
			t.InIface = s[len("in_"):]
		case strings.HasPrefix(s, "out_"):
			t.OutIface = s[len("out_"):]
		default:
			return fmt.Errorf("model: tuple interfaces %q are malformed", s)
		}
	}
	for _, name := range []string{t.InIface, t.OutIface} {
		if name != "" && (!tupleIfaceRe.MatchString(name) || name == "." || name == "..") {
			return fmt.Errorf("model: tuple interface %q is not valid", name)
		}
	}
	switch Direction(dir) {
	case DirIn, DirOut:
		t.Direction = Direction(dir)
		return nil
	}
	return fmt.Errorf("model: tuple direction %q is not in or out", dir)
}

// parseAction reads "[route:]<action>[_log|_log-all]".
func (t *Tuple) parseAction(s string) error {
	if rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(s, "route:"); ok {
		t.Route, s = true, rest
	}
	act, logType, hasLog := strings.Cut(s, "_")
	t.Action = Action(act)
	if !slices.Contains([]Action{ActionAllow, ActionDeny, ActionLimit, ActionReject}, t.Action) {
		return fmt.Errorf("model: tuple action %q is not supported", act)
	}
	if hasLog {
		t.Log = Log(logType)
		if t.Log != LogOn && t.Log != LogAll {
			return fmt.Errorf("model: tuple log type %q is not supported", logType)
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// tuplePort checks a port field as UFW's set_port does once service names
// are resolved, which UFW does before it writes a tuple.
func tuplePort(s string) (string, error) {
	if s == Any {
		return s, nil
	}
	bad := fmt.Errorf("model: tuple port %q is not valid", s)
	if strings.Count(s, ",")+strings.Count(s, ":") > maxPortSlots-1 {
		return "", bad
	}
	for _, e := range strings.Split(s, ",") {
		if !tuplePortRe.MatchString(e) {
			return "", bad
		}
		lo, hi, isRange := strings.Cut(e, ":")
		a, _ := strconv.Atoi(lo)
		if a < 1 || a > 65535 {
			return "", bad
		}
		if isRange {
			if b, _ := strconv.Atoi(hi); b > 65535 || a >= b {
				return "", bad
			}
		}
	}
	return s, nil
}

// tupleAddr checks an address field and writes any in the file's family,
// as UFW's _fix_anywhere does. An IPv4 netmask in dotted form, which UFW
// keeps when it is not a prefix, is accepted.
func tupleAddr(s string, v6 bool) (string, error) {
	s = strings.ToLower(s)
	if v6 && (s == Any || s == "0.0.0.0/0") {
		return "::/0", nil
	}
	if !v6 && (s == Any || s == "::/0") {
		return "0.0.0.0/0", nil
	}
	bad := fmt.Errorf("model: tuple address %q is not valid in this file", s)
	addr, mask, hasMask := strings.Cut(s, "/")
	a, err := netip.ParseAddr(addr)
	if err != nil || a.Zone() != "" || a.Is4() == v6 {
		return "", bad
	}
	if !hasMask {
		return s, nil
	}
	if !v6 && strings.Contains(mask, ".") {
		if m, err := netip.ParseAddr(mask); err != nil || !m.Is4() {
			return "", bad
		}
		return s, nil
	}
	if _, err := netip.ParsePrefix(s); err != nil {
		return "", bad
	}
	return s, nil
}

func tupleApp(s string) string {
	if s == "-" {
		return ""
	}
	return strings.ReplaceAll(s, "%20", " ")
}

// manualID derives a manual rule's id from its family and tuple line, so it
// is stable across reads while the line is unchanged.
func manualID(fam Family, raw string) string {
	sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(string(fam) + raw))
	return "manual-" + hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])[:16]
}

// Rule converts t into the model. ID, Origin and Comment come from the tag,
// or for a manual rule the derived id and the comment as written. ok is
// false when the model cannot express t (an application rule, a route rule
// with a bare out direction, or any value outside the grammar of 2.2
// except the comment); the Rule then carries only ID, Action, Direction,
// Log, Family, Comment, Origin and Raw.
func (t Tuple) Rule() (Rule, bool) {
	r := Rule{Action: t.Action, Direction: t.Direction, Log: t.Log, Family: t.Family}
	if t.Route {
		r.Direction = DirRoute
	}
	if id, label, ok := ParseTag(t.Comment); ok {
		r.ID, r.Comment, r.Origin = id, label, OriginDarkpanel
	} else {
		r.ID, r.Comment, r.Origin = manualID(t.Family, t.Raw), t.Comment, OriginManual
	}
	full := r
	full.Proto, full.InIface, full.OutIface = t.Proto, t.InIface, t.OutIface
	full.From, full.To = ruleAddr(t.Src), ruleAddr(t.Dst)
	full.FromPort, full.ToPort = rulePort(t.SPort), rulePort(t.DPort)
	bareOut := t.Route && t.InIface == "" && t.OutIface == "" && t.Direction == DirOut
	if t.DApp != "" || t.SApp != "" || bareOut || len(full.problems(false)) > 0 {
		r.Raw = t.Raw
		return r, false
	}
	return full, true
}

func ruleAddr(s string) string {
	if s == "0.0.0.0/0" || s == "::/0" {
		return Any
	}
	return s
}

func rulePort(s string) string {
	if s == Any {
		return ""
	}
	return s
}

// Merge turns the tuples of user.rules (v4) and user6.rules (v6) into rules.
// A v4 tuple whose addresses are both any and an otherwise identical v6
// tuple, which is how UFW writes one rule for both families, become one
// rule with Family both, at the v4 tuple's position; each v6 tuple pairs at
// most once. The result lists the v4 file's rules in order, then the
// unpaired v6 rules in order. A merged manual rule's id is derived from
// "both" and the v4 line, and a merged unrepresentable rule's Raw is the v4
// line. Ids repeat only when the files carry the same tag twice.
func Merge(v4, v6 []Tuple) []Rule {
	out := make([]Rule, 0, len(v4)+len(v6))
	paired := make([]bool, len(v6))
	for _, a := range v4 {
		r, _ := a.Rule()
		for j, b := range v6 {
			if paired[j] || !mergeable(a, b) {
				continue
			}
			paired[j] = true
			r.Family = FamilyBoth
			if r.Origin == OriginManual {
				r.ID = manualID(FamilyBoth, a.Raw)
			}
			break
		}
		out = append(out, r)
	}
	for j, b := range v6 {
		if !paired[j] {
			r, _ := b.Rule()
			out = append(out, r)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// mergeable reports whether a (from user.rules) and b (from user6.rules)
// are the two halves UFW writes for one rule of both families.
func mergeable(a, b Tuple) bool {
	if a.Family != FamilyV4 || b.Family != FamilyV6 || a.Proto == ProtoIPv6 || a.Proto == ProtoIGMP {
		return false
	}
	if a.Src != "0.0.0.0/0" || a.Dst != "0.0.0.0/0" || b.Src != "::/0" || b.Dst != "::/0" {
		return false
	}
	return a.Action == b.Action && a.Log == b.Log && a.Route == b.Route && a.Proto == b.Proto &&
		a.DPort == b.DPort && a.SPort == b.SPort && a.DApp == b.DApp && a.SApp == b.SApp &&
		a.Direction == b.Direction && a.InIface == b.InIface && a.OutIface == b.OutIface && a.Comment == b.Comment
}

import { screen, within } from "@testing-library/react"
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event"
import { expect, test } from "vitest"
import { axe } from "vitest-axe"
import { renderWithProviders, stubFetch } from "@/test/utils"
import { fwStatus } from "./fixtures"
import { StatusBanners, StatusSummary } from "./status-panel"

function spValue(list: HTMLElement, label: string): string | null | undefined {
  return within(list).getByText(label, { selector: "dt" }).nextElementSibling?.textContent
}

test("shows the configured and the loaded state side by side", () => {
  renderWithProviders(<StatusSummary status={fwStatus()} />)
  const configured = screen.getByLabelText("Configured state")
  expect(spValue(configured, "Enabled at boot")).toBe("Yes")
  expect(spValue(configured, "Incoming")).toBe("deny")
  expect(spValue(configured, "Outgoing")).toBe("allow")
  expect(spValue(configured, "Routed")).toBe("deny")
  expect(spValue(configured, "Logging")).toBe("low")
  expect(spValue(configured, "IPv6")).toBe("Yes")
  const loaded = screen.getByLabelText("Loaded state")
  expect(spValue(loaded, "iptables variant")).toBe("nft")
  expect(spValue(loaded, "IPv6 rules")).toBe("Read")
  expect(spValue(loaded, "Chains loaded")).toBe("2")
  expect(spValue(loaded, "In sync")).toBe("Yes")
  expect(spValue(loaded, "net/ipv4/ip_forward")).toBe("0")
  expect(spValue(loaded, "net/ipv4/conf/all/rp_filter")).toBe("2")
  expect(screen.getByText("Active").textContent).toBe("Active")
})

test("an inactive firewall says so", () => {
  renderWithProviders(<StatusSummary status={fwStatus({ active: false })} />)

```ts
import type { DiffLine } from "@/api/types"

// The firewall module's id and the version of every firewall action.
export const FIREWALL_MODULE = "firewall"
export const FIREWALL_ACTION_VERSION = 1

// A rule of the firewall's model, as model.Rule encodes it (spec 2.2).
export type RuleAction = "allow" | "deny" | "limit" | "reject"
export type RuleDirection = "in" | "out" | "route"
export type RuleProto = "tcp" | "udp" | "any" | "ah" | "esp" | "gre" | "ipv6" | "igmp"
export type RuleFamily = "v4" | "v6" | "both"
export type RuleLog = "off" | "log" | "log-all"
export type RuleOrigin = "darkpanel" | "manual"

export interface Rule {
  id?: string
  action: RuleAction
  direction: RuleDirection
  proto: RuleProto
  from: string
  fromPort?: string
  to: string
  toPort?: string
  inIface?: string
  outIface?: string
  family: RuleFamily
  log?: RuleLog
  comment?: string
  origin?: RuleOrigin // darkpanel when omitted
  raw?: string // the tuple of a manual rule the model cannot express
}

export type Policy = "ACCEPT" | "DROP" | "REJECT"

// UFW's configured state, read from its files (spec 2.1).
export interface FirewallConfigured {
  enabled: boolean
  logLevel: string
  ipv6: boolean
  defaults: { incoming: Policy; outgoing: Policy; routed: Policy }
  sysctlFile?: string
}

// One chain of the loaded state.
export interface LoadedChain {
  family: "v4" | "v6"
  table: string
  chain: string
  policy?: string // built-in chains only
  rules: number
}

// The loaded state the kernel holds, in summary (spec 2.1).
export interface FirewallLoaded {
  variant: string
  ipv6: boolean // ip6tables is present
  sysctl: Record<string, string>
  chains: LoadedChain[]
}

// One chain whose loaded rules differ from what UFW's files predict.
export interface ChainDifference {
  family: "v4" | "v6"
  table: string
  chain: string
  policyPredicted?: string
  policyLoaded?: string
  onlyPredicted?: string[]
  onlyLoaded?: string[]
  orderDiffers?: boolean
}

// The firewall.status resource (spec 2.2).
export interface FirewallStatus {
  supported: boolean
  unsupported: string[] // why the configuration is unsupported
  active: boolean
  inSync: boolean
  outOfSync: ChainDifference[]
  syncError?: string // why sync could not be checked
  configured: FirewallConfigured
  loaded: FirewallLoaded
  rules: Rule[]
}

// One row of the firewall.snapshots resource (spec 2.5).
export interface SnapshotInfo {
  id: string
  createdAt: string
  changeId?: string // the change it was taken before; absent until that change applied
  actor: string
  system: boolean
  pinned: boolean
  baseline: boolean
  enabled: boolean // UFW's ENABLED in the snapshot
}

export interface SnapshotList {
  snapshots: SnapshotInfo[]
}

// One state file whose content differs between two states.
export interface FileChange {
  path: string
  from: string // "sha256:<hex>" or "absent"
  to: string
}

// The output of firewall.snapshot.compare.
export interface SnapshotComparison {
  from: string
  to: string // a snapshot id, or "now"
  diff: DiffLine[]
  files: FileChange[]
}

// The query keys of the firewall's resources; a module event refetches
// every ["resource", hostId] query.
export const statusQueryKey = (hostId: string) => ["resource", hostId, "firewall.status"] as const
export const snapshotsQueryKey = (hostId: string) => ["resource", hostId, "firewall.snapshots"] as const
```

Create `web/src/modules/firewall/firewall-change.tsx`:

```tsx
import { useQueryClient } from "@tanstack/react-query"
import { ChangeDialog } from "@/components/change-dialog"
import { FIREWALL_ACTION_VERSION, FIREWALL_MODULE } from "./types"

export interface FirewallChangeProps {
  hostId: string
  action: string // a mutating firewall action, such as "firewall.rule.add"
  title: string
  input: Record<string, unknown> | null // null keeps the dialog closed
  onClose: () => void
}

// FirewallChange plans and applies one firewall action through the change
// dialog. Every mutating firewall action is revertible, so the dialog asks
// for the revert timeout. The host's resources are read again once the
// change applies and when the dialog closes, since a revert by the timer
// raises no event that names them.
export function FirewallChange({ hostId, action, title, input, onClose }: FirewallChangeProps) {
  const client = useQueryClient()
  const refresh = () => void client.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ["resource", hostId] })
  return (
    <ChangeDialog
      open={input !== null}
      onOpenChange={(open) => {
        if (open) return
        onClose()
        refresh()
      }}
      title={title}
      target={{ name: action, version: FIREWALL_ACTION_VERSION, hostId, module: FIREWALL_MODULE, revertible: true }}
      input={input ?? undefined}
      onApplied={refresh}
    />
  )
}

Create `web/src/modules/firewall/status-panel.tsx`:

```tsx
import { useState } from "react"
import { Alert, AlertDescription, AlertTitle } from "darkraise-ui/components/alert"
import { Badge } from "darkraise-ui/components/badge"
import { Button } from "darkraise-ui/components/button"
import { Card, CardContent, CardHeader, CardTitle } from "darkraise-ui/components/card"
import { FirewallChange } from "./firewall-change"
import type { ChainDifference, FirewallStatus, Policy } from "./types"

const POLICY_WORDS: Record<Policy, string> = { ACCEPT: "allow", DROP: "deny", REJECT: "reject" }

function policyText(p: Policy): string {
  return POLICY_WORDS[p] ?? p
}

function yesNo(v: boolean): string {
  return v ? "Yes" : "No"
}

function chainName(d: ChainDifference): string {
  return `${d.family} ${d.table} ${d.chain}`
}

// StatusBanners says why changes are refused: an unsupported configuration
// refuses every change; a host out of sync refuses every change but a
// repair, which it offers.
export function StatusBanners({ hostId, status }: { hostId: string; status: FirewallStatus }) {
  const [repairing, setRepairing] = useState(false)
  return (
    <>
      {!status.supported && (
        <Alert variant="destructive" role="alert">
          <AlertTitle>Unsupported configuration</AlertTitle>
          <AlertDescription>
            <p>Darkpanel cannot predict what UFW will load on this host, so it refuses every firewall change until this is fixed:</p>
            <ul aria-label="Unsupported configuration reasons" className="mt-1 list-disc pl-5">
              {status.unsupported.map((reason) => (
                <li key={reason}>{reason}</li>
              ))}
            </ul>
          </AlertDescription>
        </Alert>
      )}
      {status.supported && !status.inSync && (
        <Alert variant="warning" role="status">
          <AlertTitle>Out of sync</AlertTitle>
          <AlertDescription>
            {status.syncError !== undefined && status.syncError !== "" ? (
              <p>{`Whether the loaded rules match UFW's files could not be checked, so every change except a repair is refused: ${status.syncError}`}</p>
            ) : (
              <>
                <p>The loaded rules differ from what UFW&apos;s files describe, so every change except a repair is refused. Differing chains:</p>
                <ul aria-label="Differing chains" className="mt-1 list-disc pl-5 font-mono text-xs">
                  {status.outOfSync.map((d) => (
                    <li key={chainName(d)}>{chainName(d)}</li>
                  ))}
                </ul>
              </>
            )}
            <Button className="mt-2" size="sm" variant="outline" onClick={() => setRepairing(true)}>
              Repair
            </Button>
          </AlertDescription>
        </Alert>
      )}
      <FirewallChange
        hostId={hostId}
        action="firewall.state.repair"
        title="Repair the firewall"
        input={repairing ? {} : null}
        onClose={() => setRepairing(false)}
      />
    </>
  )
}

interface Row {
  label: string
  value: string
  mono?: boolean
}

function configuredRows(s: FirewallStatus): Row[] {
  const c = s.configured
  return [
    { label: "Enabled at boot", value: yesNo(c.enabled) },
    { label: "Incoming", value: policyText(c.defaults.incoming) },
    { label: "Outgoing", value: policyText(c.defaults.outgoing) },
    { label: "Routed", value: policyText(c.defaults.routed) },
    { label: "Logging", value: c.logLevel },
    { label: "IPv6", value: yesNo(c.ipv6) },
  ]
}

function loadedRows(s: FirewallStatus): Row[] {
  const rows: Row[] = [
    { label: "iptables variant", value: s.loaded.variant, mono: true },
    { label: "IPv6 rules", value: s.loaded.ipv6 ? "Read" : "No ip6tables" },
    { label: "Chains loaded", value: String(s.loaded.chains.length) },
    { label: "In sync", value: yesNo(s.inSync) },
  ]
  for (const key of Object.keys(s.loaded.sysctl).sort()) {
    rows.push({ label: key, value: s.loaded.sysctl[key] ?? "", mono: true })
  }
  return rows
}

function Rows({ label, rows }: { label: string; rows: Row[] }) {
  return (
    <dl aria-label={label} className="grid grid-cols-1 gap-x-8 gap-y-2 sm:grid-cols-[max-content_1fr]">
      {rows.map((row) => (
        <div key={row.label} className="contents">
          <dt className={row.mono === true ? "font-mono text-sm text-muted-foreground" : "text-muted-foreground"}>{row.label}</dt>
          <dd className={row.mono === true ? "font-mono" : undefined}>{row.value}</dd>
        </div>
      ))}
    </dl>
  )
}

// StatusSummary shows the configured state from UFW's files beside the
// loaded state the kernel holds.
export function StatusSummary({ status }: { status: FirewallStatus }) {
  return (
    <div className="grid grid-cols-1 gap-4 lg:grid-cols-2">
      <Card>
        <CardHeader>
          <CardTitle>Configured</CardTitle>
        </CardHeader>
        <CardContent>
          <Rows label="Configured state" rows={configuredRows(status)} />
        </CardContent>
      </Card>
      <Card>
        <CardHeader>
          <CardTitle className="flex items-center gap-2">
            Loaded
            <Badge variant={status.active ? "default" : "secondary"} size="sm">
              {status.active ? "Active" : "Inactive"}
            </Badge>
          </CardTitle>
        </CardHeader>
        <CardContent>
          <Rows label="Loaded state" rows={loadedRows(status)} />
        </CardContent>
      </Card>
    </div>
  )
}
```

**Files:**
- Modify: `internal/controller/dispatch/guard.go`
- Test: `internal/controller/dispatch/guard_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `core.GuardContext.Complete` (Task 1)
- Produces: `dispatch.Topology.Complete`, `dispatch.Topology.Dropped` and the fill rule (Part contracts, Task 15)

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-opus-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 2 - risk 3 = 6
**Lenses:** security

The dispatcher builds every guard context and guard refresh from the server's topology. `Topology` gains `Complete` (every source registered) and `Dropped` (addresses that could not be read). The dispatcher copies `Complete` into the guard context only when nothing was dropped, and logs each dropped address at Warn with its value, so a partial topology can never pass as complete. The test plans a guarded agent action under four topologies (complete, not every source registered, an address dropped, no topology) and checks the handler's `Complete` and the Warn lines.

// TestGuardContextComplete: the guard context is complete only when the
// topology says every source registered and no address was dropped; each
// dropped address is logged at Warn with its value.
func TestGuardContextComplete(t *testing.T) {
	full := dgTopology
	full.Complete = true
	dropped := full
	dropped.Dropped = []string{"@agent-abstract", "fleet:7"}
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name     string
		topo     func() Topology
		complete bool
		warns    int
	}{
		{"complete", func() Topology { return full }, true, 0},
		{"not every source registered", func() Topology { return dgTopology }, false, 0},
		{"an address dropped", func() Topology { return dropped }, false, 2},
		{"no topology", nil, false, 0},

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the implementation**

Replace the whole of `internal/controller/dispatch/guard.go` with:

```go
package dispatch

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"net/netip"
	"strings"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
)

// Topology is the controller's side of a guard context (spec 1.5): its web
// and agent listeners and its live agents' addresses.
type Topology struct {
	PanelListen []netip.AddrPort
	AgentListen []netip.AddrPort
	AgentPeers  []netip.Addr
	// Complete is set when every source of the three lists has registered.
	Complete bool
	// Dropped holds each listener or peer address that could not be read as
	// an IP address and so is missing from the lists.
	Dropped []string
}

// guardContext is the guard context of a call now: the client peer the API
// stored in ctx, the exposure path of a request that came through a runtime
// listener, and the configured topology. A composite's children run on the
// engine's context and so carry neither. Every address loses its
// IPv6 zone: a zone names an interface of the controller, so it means nothing
// on the agent's host and two addresses that differ only by zone must compare
// equal. The topology's slices are copied, never changed. The context is
// complete only when the topology is and dropped no address, because a guard
// that saw a partial topology would protect too few flows.
func (d *Dispatcher) guardContext(ctx context.Context) core.GuardContext {
	var g core.GuardContext
	if d.cfg.Topology != nil {
		t := d.cfg.Topology()
		g.PanelListen = withoutPortZones(t.PanelListen)
		g.AgentListen = withoutPortZones(t.AgentListen)
		g.AgentPeers = withoutZones(t.AgentPeers)
		for _, addr := range t.Dropped {
			d.cfg.Log.Warn("dispatch: a guard topology address is not an IP address", "addr", addr)
		}
		g.Complete = t.Complete && len(t.Dropped) == 0
	}
	if p, ok := core.ClientPeer(ctx); ok {
		p.Addr = p.Addr.WithZone("")
		g.Client = &p
	}
	if px, ok := core.ProxiedFrom(ctx); ok {
		path := px.Path
		path.ProxyAddr = path.ProxyAddr.WithZone("")
		path.ListenerAddr = netip.AddrPortFrom(path.ListenerAddr.Addr().WithZone(""), path.ListenerAddr.Port())
		path.Public = withoutPortZones(path.Public)
		g.Via = &path
	}
	return g
}

func withoutZones(addrs []netip.Addr) []netip.Addr {
	if addrs == nil {
		return nil
	}
	out := make([]netip.Addr, len(addrs))
	for i, a := range addrs {
		out[i] = a.WithZone("")
	}
	return out
}

func withoutPortZones(addrs []netip.AddrPort) []netip.AddrPort {
	if addrs == nil {
		return nil
	}
	out := make([]netip.AddrPort, len(addrs))
	for i, a := range addrs {
		out[i] = netip.AddrPortFrom(a.Addr().WithZone(""), a.Port())
	}
	return out
}

// withGuard returns input with its top-level guard member set to g. Members
// whose name matches guard ignoring case are dropped first, because
// encoding/json would decode any of them as the guard. An input that is not
// a JSON object is returned as it is, for the validator to refuse.
func withGuard(input json.RawMessage, g core.GuardContext) (json.RawMessage, error) {
	var obj map[string]json.RawMessage
	if err := json.Unmarshal(input, &obj); err != nil || obj == nil {
		return input, nil
	}
	for key := range obj {
		if strings.EqualFold(key, "guard") {
			delete(obj, key)
		}
	}
	raw, err := json.Marshal(g)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("dispatch: encode the guard context: %w", err)
	}
	obj["guard"] = raw
	out, err := json.Marshal(obj)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("dispatch: encode the input: %w", err)
	}
	return out, nil
}

// withGuardRefresh returns opts whose call context carries the guard context
// now, on a copy, so the caller's call context is never changed.
func (d *Dispatcher) withGuardRefresh(ctx context.Context, opts core.ApplyOptions) core.ApplyOptions {
	var call core.CallContext
	if opts.Call != nil {
		call = *opts.Call
	}
	g := d.guardContext(ctx)
	call.GuardRefresh = &g
	opts.Call = &call
	return opts
}

### Task 16: Integrator: read the repair outcome of a revertible target

**Files:**
- Modify: `internal/core/lifecycle/repair.go`
- Test: `internal/core/lifecycle/repair_revertible_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: the registry rule of Task 9 (a revertible action may repair itself); `newRfx`, `rfxFixture`, `rfxHost`, `repairPlan`, `lockOwner`, `convergeTarget`, `setNeedsRepair`, `alice` (merged lifecycle test helpers)
- Produces: the repair outcome rule of Part contracts, Task 16

**Depends on:** Task 9

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-sonnet-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 2 - risk 2 = 5

Controller ruling on the lifecycle gap. When the target is revertible, its repair change ran the target's `RepairedBy` action, and that action may be the target's own action (`firewall.state.repair` repairing a `firewall.state.repair` change). The engine took any repair change with the target's action for a re-apply: it recorded `kept` and copied the repair's output into the target. Now the target's stored class decides. For a revertible target, `repairOutcomeOf` reads `repairOutcome` from the repair's output (a missing value keeps today's warning and NULL) and the target's output is never overwritten. A compensable target applied again keeps today's behaviour: `kept`, output copied. The tests come from the drafting scratch test. They cover a revertible target repaired by another revertible action, a self-repair reporting `restored`, `kept` and no outcome, a reverted repair handing the lock back, and the converging re-apply still kept with its output copied.

// srxTarget applies action, confirms it and leaves it in needs_repair

func (r *rfxFixture) srxTarget(action string) core.ChangeView {

// TestRevertibleRepairReportsItsOutcome: a revertible target is repaired by
// its RepairedBy action, also when that is the target's own action, so the
// outcome comes from the repair's output and the target keeps its own
// output.
func TestRevertibleRepairReportsItsOutcome(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		action, input, outcome string
	}{
		{"srx.rule.set", `{"outcome":"restore"}`, core.RepairRestored},
		{"srx.state.repair", `{"outcome":"restore"}`, core.RepairRestored},
		{"srx.state.repair", `{"outcome":"keep"}`, core.RepairKept},
		{"srx.state.repair", `{"outcome":"none"}`, ""},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.action+" "+tc.input, func(t *testing.T) {
			r, logs := newSrx(t)
			ctx := context.Background()
			target := r.srxTarget(tc.action)
			p := r.apply(alice, r.repairPlan(target.ID, tc.input).PlanID, core.ApplyOptions{})
			if p.State != core.StatePending || p.RevertDeadline == nil {
				t.Fatalf("repair change = %s, deadline %v; want pending with a revert deadline", p.State, p.RevertDeadline)
			}
			if _, err := r.eng.Confirm(ctx, alice, p.ID); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			v, err := r.eng.Change(ctx, target.ID)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if v.State != core.StateRepaired || v.RepairOutcome != tc.outcome || v.RepairedBy != p.ID {
				t.Errorf("target = %s, outcome %q, repaired by %q; want repaired, outcome %q, by %s",
					v.State, v.RepairOutcome, v.RepairedBy, tc.outcome, p.ID)
			}
			if string(v.Output) != `{"applied":"yes"}` {
				t.Errorf("target output = %s, want its own {\"applied\":\"yes\"}", v.Output)
			}
			if warned := strings.Contains(logs.String(), "reported no repairOutcome"); warned != (tc.outcome == "") {
				t.Errorf("warning logged %v, want %v:\n%s", warned, tc.outcome == "", logs)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestRevertibleRepairRevertedReturnsTheLocks: a reverted revertible repair
// change gives the srx lock back to its target, which stays in
// needs_repair.
func TestRevertibleRepairRevertedReturnsTheLocks(t *testing.T) {
	r, _ := newSrx(t)
	ctx := context.Background()
	target := r.srxTarget("srx.state.repair")
	p := r.apply(alice, r.repairPlan(target.ID, "").PlanID, core.ApplyOptions{})
	if _, err := r.eng.Revert(ctx, alice, p.ID); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	v, err := r.eng.Change(ctx, target.ID)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if v.State != core.StateNeedsRepair || v.Owner != "" || r.lockOwner("srx") != target.ID {
		t.Errorf("target = %s, owner %q, lock held by %q; want needs_repair, unowned, holding srx",
			v.State, v.Owner, r.lockOwner("srx"))
	}
}

// TestConvergingRepairKeepsAndCopiesTheOutput: a compensable target repaired
// by applying its own action again is kept, and takes the repair's output.
func TestConvergingRepairKeepsAndCopiesTheOutput(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRfx(t)
	ctx := context.Background()
	target := r.convergeTarget(`{"name":"a","value":"2"}`)
	p := r.apply(alice, r.repairPlan(target.ID, "").PlanID, core.ApplyOptions{})
	v, err := r.eng.Change(ctx, target.ID)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if v.RepairOutcome != core.RepairKept || string(v.Output) != string(p.Output) {
		t.Errorf("target outcome %q, output %s; want kept with the repair's output %s", v.RepairOutcome, v.Output, p.Output)
	}
}

Every read goes through `Host`, `env.Files` or `env.Units`, so tests use fakes; any failed read is an error, so a guard never passes on a fact it could not read. The tests prove the facts gathered, each controller-unit state, every error path including a proc root without socket tables read through the real `netstat.Table` (register row 259), and `LiveHost` against this host's `/proc` and loopback route (read-only).

```go
package guard

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"net/netip"
	"os"
	"reflect"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netstat"
)

// gHost is the fake Host every test of the package uses. routes maps a
// lookup to its answer; a lookup it does not hold fails with ErrNoRoute.
type gHost struct {
	sockets    []netstat.Socket
	socketsErr error
	ifaces     []netstat.Interface
	ifacesErr  error
	routes     map[netstat.RouteQuery]netstat.Route
	routeErrs  map[netstat.RouteQuery]error
	pid        int
	lookups    []netstat.RouteQuery
}

func (h *gHost) Sockets() ([]netstat.Socket, error) { return h.sockets, h.socketsErr }

func (h *gHost) Interfaces() ([]netstat.Interface, error) { return h.ifaces, h.ifacesErr }

func (h *gHost) RouteGet(q netstat.RouteQuery) (netstat.Route, error) {
	h.lookups = append(h.lookups, q)
	if err, ok := h.routeErrs[q]; ok {
		return netstat.Route{}, err
	}
	if r, ok := h.routes[q]; ok {
		return r, nil
	}
	return netstat.Route{}, netstat.ErrNoRoute
}

func (h *gHost) PID() int { return h.pid }

// gFiles is the fake FileWriter: it answers ReadSysctl from sysctl and
// panics on any other method.
type gFiles struct {
	core.FileWriter
	sysctl map[string]string
	err    error
	reads  []string
}

func (f *gFiles) ReadSysctl(_ context.Context, module, key string) (string, error) {
	f.reads = append(f.reads, module+" "+key)
	if f.err != nil {
		return "", f.err
	}
	v, ok := f.sysctl[key]
	if !ok {
		return "", errors.New("platform: no such key " + key)
	}
	return v, nil
}

// gUnits is the fake Units: it answers State from state and panics on any
// other method.
type gUnits struct {
	core.Units
	state core.UnitState
	err   error
	asked []string
}

func (u *gUnits) State(_ context.Context, unit string) (core.UnitState, error) {
	u.asked = append(u.asked, unit)
	return u.state, u.err
}

// gEnv is an Env with the fakes, the controller unit absent and rp_filter 0
// everywhere for the interfaces of gIfaces.
func gEnv() (core.Env, *gFiles, *gUnits) {
	files := &gFiles{sysctl: map[string]string{
		"net/ipv4/conf/all/rp_filter": "0", "net/ipv4/conf/eth0/rp_filter": "0", "net/ipv4/conf/eth1/rp_filter": "0",
	}}
	units := &gUnits{state: core.UnitState{LoadState: "not-found", ActiveState: "inactive", SubState: "dead"}}
	return core.Env{Files: files, Units: units}, files, units
}

// gIfaces are lo, two up interfaces and one down interface.
func gIfaces() []netstat.Interface {
	return []netstat.Interface{
		{Index: 1, Name: "lo", Up: true, Running: true, Loopback: true, Addrs: []netip.Prefix{netip.MustParsePrefix("127.0.0.1/8"), netip.MustParsePrefix("::1/128")}},
		{Index: 2, Name: "eth0", Up: true, Running: true, Addrs: []netip.Prefix{netip.MustParsePrefix("192.0.2.1/24"), netip.MustParsePrefix("2001:db8::1/64")}},
		{Index: 3, Name: "eth1", Up: true, Running: true, Addrs: []netip.Prefix{netip.MustParsePrefix("10.0.0.1/24")}},
		{Index: 4, Name: "eth2", Up: false, Addrs: []netip.Prefix{netip.MustParsePrefix("10.9.0.1/24")}},
	}
}

func TestGatherFacts(t *testing.T) {
	env, files, units := gEnv()
	files.sysctl["net/ipv4/conf/all/rp_filter"] = "1"
	files.sysctl["net/ipv4/conf/eth1/rp_filter"] = "2"
	units.state = core.UnitState{LoadState: "loaded", ActiveState: "active", SubState: "running", MainPID: 4242}
	socks := []netstat.Socket{{Proto: netstat.ProtoTCP, Family: netstat.IPv4, State: netstat.StateListen,
		Local: netip.MustParseAddrPort("0.0.0.0:22"), Processes: []netstat.Process{{PID: 7, Comm: "sshd"}}}}
	h := &gHost{sockets: socks, ifaces: gIfaces(), pid: 99}
	got, err := gatherFacts(context.Background(), env, h)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	want := facts{
		sockets: socks, ifaces: gIfaces(),
		rpFilter:   map[string]int{"all": 1, "eth0": 0, "eth1": 2},
		controller: 4242, pid: 99,
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("gatherFacts = %+v\nwant %+v", got, want)
	}
	wantReads := []string{
		"firewall net/ipv4/conf/all/rp_filter", "firewall net/ipv4/conf/eth0/rp_filter", "firewall net/ipv4/conf/eth1/rp_filter",
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(files.reads, wantReads) {
		t.Errorf("sysctl reads = %q, want %q", files.reads, wantReads)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(units.asked, []string{"darkpanel-controller.service"}) {
		t.Errorf("unit states asked = %q", units.asked)
	}
}

func TestGatherFactsController(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name  string
		state core.UnitState
		want  int
	}{
		{"unit absent", core.UnitState{LoadState: "not-found", ActiveState: "inactive"}, 0},
		{"unit inactive", core.UnitState{LoadState: "loaded", ActiveState: "inactive", SubState: "dead"}, 0},
		{"unit failed without a process", core.UnitState{LoadState: "loaded", ActiveState: "failed", SubState: "failed"}, 0},
		{"unit activating with a process", core.UnitState{LoadState: "loaded", ActiveState: "activating", SubState: "start", MainPID: 77}, 77},
		{"unit running", core.UnitState{LoadState: "loaded", ActiveState: "active", SubState: "running", MainPID: 88}, 88},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			env, _, units := gEnv()
			units.state = tc.state
			got, err := gatherFacts(context.Background(), env, &gHost{ifaces: gIfaces()})
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if got.controller != tc.want {
				t.Errorf("controller = %d, want %d", got.controller, tc.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestGatherFactsErrors(t *testing.T) {
	boom := errors.New("boom")
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name   string
		mutate func(h *gHost, env *core.Env, f *gFiles, u *gUnits)
		target error
	}{
		{"no socket tables", func(h *gHost, _ *core.Env, _ *gFiles, _ *gUnits) { h.socketsErr = netstat.ErrNoSocketTables }, netstat.ErrNoSocketTables},
		{"socket table unreadable", func(h *gHost, _ *core.Env, _ *gFiles, _ *gUnits) { h.socketsErr = boom }, boom},
		{"interfaces unreadable", func(h *gHost, _ *core.Env, _ *gFiles, _ *gUnits) { h.ifacesErr = boom }, boom},
		{"sysctl unreadable", func(_ *gHost, _ *core.Env, f *gFiles, _ *gUnits) { f.err = boom }, boom},
		{"unit state unreadable", func(_ *gHost, _ *core.Env, _ *gFiles, u *gUnits) { u.err = boom }, boom},
		{"no unit client", func(_ *gHost, env *core.Env, _ *gFiles, _ *gUnits) { env.Units = nil }, nil},
		{"no file writer", func(_ *gHost, env *core.Env, _ *gFiles, _ *gUnits) { env.Files = nil }, nil},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			env, files, units := gEnv()
			h := &gHost{ifaces: gIfaces()}
			tc.mutate(h, &env, files, units)
			_, err := gatherFacts(context.Background(), env, h)
			if err == nil {
				t.Fatal("gatherFacts succeeded")
			}
			if tc.target != nil && !errors.Is(err, tc.target) {
				t.Errorf("error %v does not wrap %v", err, tc.target)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestGatherFactsBadSysctl(t *testing.T) {
	env, files, _ := gEnv()
	files.sysctl["net/ipv4/conf/eth0/rp_filter"] = "strict"
	if _, err := gatherFacts(context.Background(), env, &gHost{ifaces: gIfaces()}); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("gatherFacts accepted a non-numeric rp_filter")
	}
}

func TestLiveHostNoSocketTables(t *testing.T) {
	env, _, _ := gEnv()
	_, err := gatherFacts(context.Background(), env, LiveHost{ProcRoot: t.TempDir()})
	if !errors.Is(err, netstat.ErrNoSocketTables) {
		t.Fatalf("gatherFacts on an empty proc root: %v, want ErrNoSocketTables", err)
	}
}

func TestLiveHost(t *testing.T) {
	h := LiveHost{}
	if h.PID() != os.Getpid() {
		t.Errorf("PID = %d, want %d", h.PID(), os.Getpid())
	}
	socks, err := h.Sockets()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(socks) == 0 {
		t.Error("the host has no sockets")
	}
	ifaces, err := h.Interfaces()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	loopback := false
	for _, i := range ifaces {
		loopback = loopback || i.Loopback
	}
	if !loopback {
		t.Error("no loopback interface")
	}
	r, err := h.RouteGet(netstat.RouteQuery{Dst: netip.MustParseAddr("127.0.0.1")})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if r.Type != "local" {
		t.Errorf("route to 127.0.0.1 has type %q, want local", r.Type)
	}
}

```go
// Package guard is the firewall's lockout guard (spec 2.3, 1.5): it
// gathers this host's live facts, builds every protected flow from them and
// from the controller's guard context, evaluates each flow on every
// eligible in-interface against a predicted or loaded state, and reports
// the firewall.lockout guard.
package guard

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"strconv"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netstat"
)

// moduleID is the module every env.Files call names.
const moduleID = "firewall"

// controllerUnit is the controller's systemd unit; the firewall's manifest
// declares it as an external unit with the state operation (owner ruling
// R3).
const controllerUnit = "darkpanel-controller.service"

// Host reads the live facts of the host the agent runs on. LiveHost is the
// production implementation.
type Host interface {
	Sockets() ([]netstat.Socket, error)
	Interfaces() ([]netstat.Interface, error)
	RouteGet(q netstat.RouteQuery) (netstat.Route, error)
	PID() int // the agent's own process id
}

// LiveHost reads this host through internal/platform/netstat.
type LiveHost struct {
	ProcRoot string // the proc root sockets are read from; "" is /proc
}

// Sockets reads the socket table under ProcRoot.
func (h LiveHost) Sockets() ([]netstat.Socket, error) {
	root := h.ProcRoot
	if root == "" {
		root = "/proc"
	}
	return netstat.Table{Root: root}.Sockets()
}

// Interfaces lists the host's interfaces.
func (LiveHost) Interfaces() ([]netstat.Interface, error) { return netstat.Interfaces() }

// RouteGet asks the kernel for the route of q.
func (LiveHost) RouteGet(q netstat.RouteQuery) (netstat.Route, error) { return netstat.RouteGet(q) }

// PID is os.Getpid.
func (LiveHost) PID() int { return os.Getpid() }

// facts are the live facts one guard check uses.
type facts struct {
	sockets    []netstat.Socket
	ifaces     []netstat.Interface
	rpFilter   map[string]int // live net/ipv4/conf/<name>/rp_filter for "all" and every up, non-loopback interface
	controller int            // MainPID of a running local darkpanel-controller.service; 0 when none
	pid        int            // the agent's own process id
}

// gatherFacts reads the socket table, the interfaces, the live rp_filter
// values and the local controller's main process. Any read that fails is an
// error, so a guard never passes on facts it could not read; in particular a
// proc root without socket tables (netstat.ErrNoSocketTables) is not a host
// without sessions.
func gatherFacts(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, h Host) (facts, error) {
	if env.Files == nil || env.Units == nil {
		return facts{}, errors.New("firewall: the guard needs the file writer and the unit client")
	}
	socks, err := h.Sockets()
	if err != nil {
		return facts{}, fmt.Errorf("firewall: read the socket table: %w", err)
	}
	ifaces, err := h.Interfaces()
	if err != nil {
		return facts{}, fmt.Errorf("firewall: read the interfaces: %w", err)
	}
	f := facts{sockets: socks, ifaces: ifaces, rpFilter: map[string]int{}, pid: h.PID()}
	names := []string{"all"}
	for _, i := range ifaces {
		if i.Up && !i.Loopback {
			names = append(names, i.Name)
		}
	}
	for _, name := range names {
		key := "net/ipv4/conf/" + name + "/rp_filter"
		v, err := env.Files.ReadSysctl(ctx, moduleID, key)
		if err != nil {
			return facts{}, fmt.Errorf("firewall: read %s: %w", key, err)
		}
		n, err := strconv.Atoi(v)
		if err != nil {
			return facts{}, fmt.Errorf("firewall: %s is %q, not a number", key, v)
		}
		f.rpFilter[name] = n
	}
	st, err := env.Units.State(ctx, controllerUnit)
	if err != nil {
		return facts{}, fmt.Errorf("firewall: state of %s: %w", controllerUnit, err)
	}
	if st.LoadState != "not-found" && st.ActiveState != "inactive" {
		f.controller = int(st.MainPID)
	}
	return f, nil
}
```

Create `internal/modules/firewall/fwstate/fwstate.go`:

```go
// Package fwstate holds the firewall's shared state types (spec 2.1-2.5):
// UFW's configured state, the loaded netfilter state, transitions, packets
// and verdicts. The configured-state reader, the loaded-state reader, the
// predictor, the evaluator, the guard and snapshots all exchange these.
package fwstate

import (
	"net/netip"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/model"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netfilter"
)

// Family is an IP family.
type Family string

// The families.
const (
	V4 Family = "v4"
	V6 Family = "v6"
)

// StateFiles are UFW's state files a snapshot holds (spec 2.5), in this order.
var StateFiles = []string{
	"/etc/ufw/user.rules", "/etc/ufw/user6.rules",
	"/etc/ufw/before.rules", "/etc/ufw/before6.rules",
	"/etc/ufw/after.rules", "/etc/ufw/after6.rules",
	"/etc/ufw/ufw.conf", "/etc/default/ufw",
}

// MaxFileSize is the largest state file a snapshot records (spec 2.5).
const MaxFileSize = 4 << 20

// Config is UFW's configured state (spec 2.1).
type Config struct {
	Enabled        bool   // ufw.conf ENABLED=yes
	LogLevel       string // ufw.conf LOGLEVEL: off, low, medium, high or full
	IPv6           bool   // /etc/default/ufw IPV6=yes
	ManageBuiltins bool   // MANAGE_BUILTINS=yes
	DefaultInput   string // DEFAULT_INPUT_POLICY: ACCEPT, DROP or REJECT
	DefaultOutput  string
	DefaultForward string
	SysctlFile     string                       // IPT_SYSCTL, absolute
	Rules4, Rules6 []model.Tuple                // the ### tuple ### lines of user.rules and user6.rules, in file order
	Files          map[string]core.RestoreEntry // StateFiles plus SysctlFile, by absolute path; Present false when absent
	Sysctl         []SysctlSetting              // SysctlFile's settings, in file order
	Unsupported    []string                     // why the configuration cannot be predicted (2.1); empty when supported
}

// SysctlSetting is one key = value line of UFW's sysctl file, the key in
// /proc/sys form ("net/ipv4/ip_forward").
type SysctlSetting struct{ Key, Value string }

// Loaded is the loaded state (spec 2.1): what the kernel holds now, or what
// a prediction says it will hold.
type Loaded struct {
	Variant     string             // "nft" or "legacy": the iptables variant UFW uses
	V4, V6      *netfilter.Ruleset // that variant's five tables; V6 nil when ip6tables is absent
	Sysctl      map[string]string  // supported keys in /proc/sys form to value, global and per present interface
	Unsupported []string           // foreign netfilter hooks found (2.1)
}

// Transition is what an action makes UFW do (spec 2.3).
type Transition string

// The transitions.
const (
	TransNone    Transition = "none"
	TransReload  Transition = "reload" // a rule change with reload, or a reload after a file change
	TransEnable  Transition = "enable"
	TransDisable Transition = "disable"
)

// Packet is one packet tuple the evaluator walks (spec 2.3).
type Packet struct {
	Family   Family
	Path     string // "input", "forward" or "output": the hook chain after routing
	InIface  string // input and forward
	OutIface string // forward and output
	Src, Dst netip.Addr
	SrcPort  uint16
	DstPort  uint16
	Proto    string // "tcp", "udp", "icmp", ...
	CtState  string // conntrack state: "NEW", "ESTABLISHED", ...
	Mark     uint32
}

// Verdict is what the evaluator decided.
type Verdict string

// The verdicts.
const (
	Accept  Verdict = "accept"
	Drop    Verdict = "drop"
	Reject  Verdict = "reject"
	Unknown Verdict = "unknown"
)

// Result is a verdict with the reason and the rules that decided it.
type Result struct {
	Verdict Verdict
	Reason  string   // why, for unknown and for a drop or reject: the deciding rule
	Trace   []string // "<table>/<chain>#<rule index>" in walk order
}

// Router says where a packet goes after nat PREROUTING rewrote its
// destination: the new path and out-interface.
type Router func(p Packet) (path, outIface string, err error)

// ChainDiff is one chain whose rules differ between two loaded states.
type ChainDiff struct {
	Family       Family
	Table, Chain string
	PolicyA      string // "" when equal or not a built-in chain
	PolicyB      string
	OnlyA, OnlyB []string // netfilter rule keys present on one side only, in order
	OrderDiffers bool     // same keys, different order
}
```

import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event"
import { expect, test } from "vitest"
import { axe } from "vitest-axe"
import type { Plan } from "@/api/types"
import { renderWithProviders, stubFetch, type StubHandler } from "@/test/utils"
import { fwRule, fwStatus } from "./fixtures"
import { RulesTable } from "./rules-table"

const RT_PLAN = "POST /api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/firewall.rule.delete/v1/plan"

function rtPlan(): Plan {
  return {
    planId: "p1", hostId: "h1", action: "firewall.rule.delete", version: 1, inputHash: "h",
    diff: [{ op: "-", text: "allow in tcp from any to any port 22 (manual)" }], guards: [], expiresAt: "2026-10-24T09:00:00Z", confirmation: null,
  }
}

function rtRender(routes: Record<string, StubHandler> = {}) {
  const calls = stubFetch({
    "GET /api/v1/hosts/h1/modules/firewall/availability": {
      body: { module: "firewall", available: true, reason: null, actions: [{ name: "firewall.rule.delete", available: true, reason: null }] },
    },
    [RT_PLAN]: { body: rtPlan() },
    ...routes,
  })
  renderWithProviders(<RulesTable hostId="h1" rules={fwStatus().rules} />)
  return calls
}

function rtRow(n: number): HTMLElement {
  const rows = within(screen.getByRole("table", { name: "Firewall rules" })).getAllByRole("row")
  const row = rows[n]
  if (row === undefined) throw new Error(`no row ${n}`)
  return row
}

  expect(cells(2)).toEqual(["2", "allow", "in", "tcp", "any", "any port 22", "", "both", "off", "", "manual", "Delete"])
  expect(cells(3)).toEqual(["3", "allow any 22 0.0.0.0/0 any 0.0.0.0/0 in_eth0 -m owner", "read-only", ""])

  )

  expect(cells.slice(1, 9)).toEqual(["allow", "route", "tcp", "10.0.0.0/8 port 1024:2048", "any port 443", "in on eth0, out on docker0", "v4", "log-all"])

  await within(dialog).findByLabelText("Planned changes")

test("a manual rule is deleted only after the operator agrees, with manual: true", async () => {
  const calls = rtRender()
  const user = userEvent.setup()
  await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Delete rule 2" }))
  const ask = await screen.findByRole("dialog")
  expect(within(ask).getByText("Delete a manual rule?").textContent).toBe("Delete a manual rule?")
  await user.click(within(ask).getByRole("button", { name: "Cancel" }))
  await waitFor(() => expect(screen.queryByRole("dialog")).toBeNull())
  expect(calls.some((c) => c.path.endsWith("/plan"))).toBe(false)

  expect(calls.find((c) => c.path.endsWith("/plan"))?.body).toEqual({ input: { id: "manual-0123456789abcdef", manual: true } })
})
