```tsx
import { useState } from "react"
import { Badge } from "darkraise-ui/components/badge"
import { Button } from "darkraise-ui/components/button"
import { Dialog, DialogContent, DialogDescription, DialogFooter, DialogHeader, DialogTitle } from "darkraise-ui/components/dialog"
import { EmptyState } from "darkraise-ui/components/empty-state"
import { Table, TableBody, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow } from "darkraise-ui/components/table"
import { FirewallChange } from "./firewall-change"
import type { Rule } from "./types"

// endpoint is a rule's source or destination with its port, as UFW shows it.
function endpoint(addr: string, port: string | undefined): string {
  return port === undefined || port === "" ? addr : `${addr} port ${port}`
}

function iface(r: Rule): string {
  const parts: string[] = []
  if (r.inIface) parts.push(`in on ${r.inIface}`)
  if (r.outIface) parts.push(`out on ${r.outIface}`)
  return parts.join(", ")
}

// ruleSummary is one line naming what a rule does, for titles and labels.
function ruleSummary(r: Rule): string {
  return [r.action, r.direction, r.proto, "from", endpoint(r.from, r.fromPort), "to", endpoint(r.to, r.toPort), iface(r)]
    .filter((p) => p !== "")
    .join(" ")
}

function OriginBadge({ rule }: { rule: Rule }) {
  if (rule.raw !== undefined && rule.raw !== "") return <Badge variant="outline" size="sm">read-only</Badge>
  if (rule.origin === "manual") return <Badge variant="secondary" size="sm">manual</Badge>
  return <Badge size="sm">darkpanel</Badge>
}

// ManualConsent asks before a manual rule is changed: Darkpanel did not
// make it, and the action refuses it unless the input says manual: true.
function ManualConsent({ rule, onCancel, onConfirm }: { rule: Rule | null; onCancel: () => void; onConfirm: () => void }) {
  return (
    <Dialog open={rule !== null} onOpenChange={(open) => !open && onCancel()}>
      <DialogContent>
        <DialogHeader>
          <DialogTitle>Delete a manual rule?</DialogTitle>
          <DialogDescription>
            {`Darkpanel did not make the rule "${rule === null ? "" : ruleSummary(rule)}"; someone added it by hand. Deleting it may cut access that rule exists for.`}
          </DialogDescription>
        </DialogHeader>
        <DialogFooter>
          <Button variant="outline" onClick={onCancel}>
            Cancel
          </Button>
          <Button variant="destructive" onClick={onConfirm}>
            Delete it anyway
          </Button>
        </DialogFooter>
      </DialogContent>
    </Dialog>
  )
}

// RulesTable lists UFW's rules in file order with who made each. A rule
// the model cannot express is shown read-only with its raw tuple; every
// other rule can be deleted through the change dialog.
export function RulesTable({ hostId, rules }: { hostId: string; rules: Rule[] }) {
  const [asking, setAsking] = useState<Rule | null>(null)
  const [deleting, setDeleting] = useState<{ rule: Rule; manual: boolean } | null>(null)

  if (rules.length === 0) return <EmptyState title="No rules" description="UFW has no rules on this host." />

  function startDelete(rule: Rule) {
    if (rule.origin === "manual") setAsking(rule)
    else setDeleting({ rule, manual: false })
  }

  const input = deleting === null ? null : deleting.manual ? { id: deleting.rule.id, manual: true } : { id: deleting.rule.id }
  return (
    <>
      <Table aria-label="Firewall rules">
        <TableHeader>
          <TableRow>
            <TableHead>#</TableHead>
            <TableHead>Action</TableHead>
            <TableHead>Direction</TableHead>
            <TableHead>Protocol</TableHead>
            <TableHead>From</TableHead>
            <TableHead>To</TableHead>
            <TableHead>Interface</TableHead>
            <TableHead>Family</TableHead>
            <TableHead>Log</TableHead>
            <TableHead>Comment</TableHead>
            <TableHead>Origin</TableHead>
            <TableHead>
              <span className="sr-only">Actions</span>
            </TableHead>
          </TableRow>
        </TableHeader>
        <TableBody>
          {rules.map((r, i) => {
            const readOnly = r.raw !== undefined && r.raw !== ""
            return (
              <TableRow key={r.id ?? `row-${i}`}>
                <TableCell>{i + 1}</TableCell>
                {readOnly ? (
                  <TableCell colSpan={9}>
                    <code className="font-mono text-xs">{r.raw}</code>
                  </TableCell>
                ) : (
                  <>
                    <TableCell className="font-medium">{r.action}</TableCell>
                    <TableCell>{r.direction}</TableCell>
                    <TableCell>{r.proto}</TableCell>
                    <TableCell className="font-mono">{endpoint(r.from, r.fromPort)}</TableCell>
                    <TableCell className="font-mono">{endpoint(r.to, r.toPort)}</TableCell>
                    <TableCell className="font-mono">{iface(r)}</TableCell>
                    <TableCell>{r.family}</TableCell>
                    <TableCell>{r.log ?? "off"}</TableCell>
                    <TableCell>{r.comment ?? ""}</TableCell>
                  </>
                )}
                <TableCell>
                  <OriginBadge rule={r} />
                </TableCell>
                <TableCell>
                  {!readOnly && r.id !== undefined && (
                    <Button variant="outline" size="sm" aria-label={`Delete rule ${i + 1}`} onClick={() => startDelete(r)}>
                      Delete
                    </Button>
                  )}
                </TableCell>
              </TableRow>
            )
          })}
        </TableBody>
      </Table>
      <ManualConsent
        rule={asking}
        onCancel={() => setAsking(null)}
        onConfirm={() => {
          if (asking !== null) setDeleting({ rule: asking, manual: true })
          setAsking(null)
        }}
      />
      <FirewallChange
        hostId={hostId}
        action="firewall.rule.delete"
        title={deleting === null ? "Delete a rule" : `Delete rule: ${ruleSummary(deleting.rule)}`}
        input={input}
        onClose={() => setDeleting(null)}
      />
    </>
  )
}
```

```tsx
import { useState, type FormEvent } from "react"
import { Button } from "darkraise-ui/components/button"
import { Dialog, DialogContent, DialogDescription, DialogFooter, DialogHeader, DialogTitle, DialogTrigger } from "darkraise-ui/components/dialog"
import { Input } from "darkraise-ui/components/input"
import { Label } from "darkraise-ui/components/label"
import { RadioGroup, RadioGroupItem } from "darkraise-ui/components/radio-group"
import { FirewallChange } from "./firewall-change"
import type { Rule, RuleAction, RuleDirection, RuleFamily, RuleLog, RuleProto } from "./types"

const ACTIONS: RuleAction[] = ["allow", "deny", "limit", "reject"]
const DIRECTIONS: RuleDirection[] = ["in", "out", "route"]
const PROTOS: RuleProto[] = ["tcp", "udp", "any", "ah", "esp", "gre", "ipv6", "igmp"]
const FAMILIES: RuleFamily[] = ["both", "v4", "v6"]
const LOGS: RuleLog[] = ["off", "log", "log-all"]

// Choice is one enumeration of the rule model as a radio group.
function Choice<T extends string>({ name, label, options, value, disabled, onChange }: {
  name: string
  label: string
  options: T[]
  value: T
  disabled?: (option: T) => boolean
  onChange: (value: T) => void
}) {
  return (
    <fieldset className="flex flex-col gap-2">
      <legend className="text-sm font-medium">{label}</legend>
      <RadioGroup value={value} onValueChange={(v) => onChange(v as T)} aria-label={label} className="flex flex-wrap gap-4">
        {options.map((o) => (
          <div key={o} className="flex items-center gap-2">
            <RadioGroupItem id={`rule-${name}-${o}`} value={o} disabled={disabled?.(o) ?? false} />
            <Label htmlFor={`rule-${name}-${o}`}>{o}</Label>
          </div>
        ))}
      </RadioGroup>
    </fieldset>
  )
}

function Text({ id, label, value, placeholder, disabled, onChange }: {
  id: string
  label: string
  value: string
  placeholder?: string
  disabled?: boolean
  onChange: (value: string) => void
}) {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
      <Label htmlFor={id}>{label}</Label>
      <Input id={id} value={value} placeholder={placeholder} disabled={disabled} autoComplete="off" onChange={(e) => onChange(e.target.value)} />
    </div>
  )
}

interface Draft {
  action: RuleAction
  direction: RuleDirection
  proto: RuleProto
  from: string
  fromPort: string
  to: string
  toPort: string
  inIface: string
  outIface: string
  family: RuleFamily
  log: RuleLog
  comment: string
}

const EMPTY: Draft = {
  action: "allow", direction: "in", proto: "tcp", from: "any", fromPort: "", to: "any", toPort: "",
  inIface: "", outIface: "", family: "both", log: "off", comment: "",
}

const PORTLESS = new Set<RuleProto>(["ah", "esp", "gre", "ipv6", "igmp"])

// ruleOf is the rule a draft describes. A field that does not apply to the
// direction or protocol, and an empty optional field, is left out; the
// action checks everything else against UFW's grammar (spec 2.2).
function ruleOf(d: Draft): Rule {
  const rule: Rule = { action: d.action, direction: d.direction, proto: d.proto, from: d.from.trim(), to: d.to.trim(), family: d.family }
  if (!PORTLESS.has(d.proto)) {
    if (d.fromPort.trim() !== "") rule.fromPort = d.fromPort.trim()
    if (d.toPort.trim() !== "") rule.toPort = d.toPort.trim()
  }
  if (d.direction !== "out" && d.inIface.trim() !== "") rule.inIface = d.inIface.trim()
  if (d.direction !== "in" && d.outIface.trim() !== "") rule.outIface = d.outIface.trim()
  if (d.log !== "off") rule.log = d.log
  if (d.comment.trim() !== "") rule.comment = d.comment.trim()
  return rule
}

// AddRule collects one rule of the model and plans firewall.rule.add with
// it through the change dialog.
export function AddRule({ hostId }: { hostId: string }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState<Draft>(EMPTY)
  const [planned, setPlanned] = useState<Rule | null>(null)

  function set<K extends keyof Draft>(key: K, value: Draft[K]) {
    setDraft((d) => {
      const next = { ...d, [key]: value }
      if (next.action === "limit" && next.direction !== "in") next.action = "allow"
      return next
    })
  }

  function submit(event: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
    event.preventDefault()
    setPlanned(ruleOf(draft))
    setOpen(false)
  }

  const portless = PORTLESS.has(draft.proto)
  return (
    <>
      <Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
        <DialogTrigger asChild>
          <Button>Add rule</Button>
        </DialogTrigger>
        <DialogContent>
          <DialogHeader>
            <DialogTitle>Add a rule</DialogTitle>
            <DialogDescription>The rule is tagged as Darkpanel&apos;s. The next step shows what it changes before anything is applied.</DialogDescription>
          </DialogHeader>
          <form aria-label="Rule" className="flex flex-col gap-4" onSubmit={submit}>
            <Choice name="action" label="Action" options={ACTIONS} value={draft.action}
              disabled={(o) => o === "limit" && draft.direction !== "in"} onChange={(v) => set("action", v)} />
            <Choice name="direction" label="Direction" options={DIRECTIONS} value={draft.direction} onChange={(v) => set("direction", v)} />
            <Choice name="proto" label="Protocol" options={PROTOS} value={draft.proto} onChange={(v) => set("proto", v)} />
            <div className="grid grid-cols-1 gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2">
              <Text id="rule-from" label="From" value={draft.from} placeholder="any, an address or a CIDR" onChange={(v) => set("from", v)} />
              <Text id="rule-from-port" label="From port" value={draft.fromPort} placeholder="22, 1000:2000 or 80,443" disabled={portless} onChange={(v) => set("fromPort", v)} />
              <Text id="rule-to" label="To" value={draft.to} placeholder="any, an address or a CIDR" onChange={(v) => set("to", v)} />
              <Text id="rule-to-port" label="To port" value={draft.toPort} placeholder="22, 1000:2000 or 80,443" disabled={portless} onChange={(v) => set("toPort", v)} />
              <Text id="rule-in-iface" label="In on interface" value={draft.inIface} disabled={draft.direction === "out"} onChange={(v) => set("inIface", v)} />
              <Text id="rule-out-iface" label="Out on interface" value={draft.outIface} disabled={draft.direction === "in"} onChange={(v) => set("outIface", v)} />
            </div>
            <Choice name="family" label="Family" options={FAMILIES} value={draft.family} onChange={(v) => set("family", v)} />
            <Choice name="log" label="Logging" options={LOGS} value={draft.log} onChange={(v) => set("log", v)} />
            <Text id="rule-comment" label="Comment" value={draft.comment} onChange={(v) => set("comment", v)} />
            <DialogFooter>
              <Button type="submit">Plan</Button>
            </DialogFooter>
          </form>
        </DialogContent>
      </Dialog>
      <FirewallChange
        hostId={hostId}
        action="firewall.rule.add"
        title="Add a rule"
        input={planned === null ? null : { rule: planned }}
        onClose={() => {
          setPlanned(null)
          setDraft(EMPTY)
        }}
      />
    </>
  )
}
```

The settings card enables or disables UFW (`firewall.state.enable` / `disable`), sets one default policy per change (`firewall.defaults.set` with `{ incoming | outgoing | routed: ACCEPT | DROP | REJECT }`) starting from its current value, and sets the logging level (`firewall.logging.set`). Create `web/src/modules/firewall/state-controls.test.tsx`:

```tsx
import { screen, within } from "@testing-library/react"
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event"
import { expect, test } from "vitest"
import { axe } from "vitest-axe"
import { renderWithProviders, stubFetch, type FetchCall } from "@/test/utils"
import { fwStatus } from "./fixtures"
import { StateControls } from "./state-controls"
import type { FirewallStatus } from "./types"

function scRender(status: FirewallStatus): { calls: FetchCall[]; container: HTMLElement } {
  const plan = (call: FetchCall) => {
    const action = call.path.split("/")[6] ?? ""
    return { body: { planId: "p1", hostId: "h1", action, version: 1, inputHash: "h", diff: [{ op: "~", text: action }], guards: [], expiresAt: "2026-10-24T09:00:00Z", confirmation: null } }
  }
  const calls = stubFetch({
    "GET /api/v1/hosts/h1/modules/firewall/availability": { body: { module: "firewall", available: true, reason: null, actions: [] } },
    "POST /api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/firewall.state.enable/v1/plan": plan,
    "POST /api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/firewall.state.disable/v1/plan": plan,
    "POST /api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/firewall.defaults.set/v1/plan": plan,
    "POST /api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/firewall.logging.set/v1/plan": plan,
  })
  const { container } = renderWithProviders(<StateControls hostId="h1" status={status} />)
  return { calls, container }
}

async function scPlanned(calls: FetchCall[], title: string): Promise<{ path: string; body: unknown }> {
  const dialog = await screen.findByRole("dialog", { name: title })
  await within(dialog).findByLabelText("Planned changes")
  const call = calls.find((c) => c.path.endsWith("/plan"))
  return { path: call?.path ?? "", body: call?.body }
}

test("an active firewall offers Disable, which plans firewall.state.disable", async () => {

  expect(screen.getByText("UFW is active.").textContent).toBe("UFW is active.")
```

```tsx
import { useState, type FormEvent } from "react"
import { Button } from "darkraise-ui/components/button"
import { Card, CardContent, CardHeader, CardTitle } from "darkraise-ui/components/card"
import { Label } from "darkraise-ui/components/label"
import { RadioGroup, RadioGroupItem } from "darkraise-ui/components/radio-group"
import { FirewallChange } from "./firewall-change"
import type { FirewallStatus, Policy } from "./types"

type PolicyDirection = "incoming" | "outgoing" | "routed"
type PolicyWord = "allow" | "deny" | "reject"

const DIRECTIONS: PolicyDirection[] = ["incoming", "outgoing", "routed"]
const POLICIES: PolicyWord[] = ["allow", "deny", "reject"]
const LEVELS = ["off", "low", "medium", "high", "full"]
const WORD_OF: Record<Policy, PolicyWord> = { ACCEPT: "allow", DROP: "deny", REJECT: "reject" }
const POLICY_OF: Record<PolicyWord, Policy> = { allow: "ACCEPT", deny: "DROP", reject: "REJECT" }

function currentPolicy(s: FirewallStatus, d: PolicyDirection): PolicyWord {
  return WORD_OF[s.configured.defaults[d]] ?? "deny"
}

function Choice({ name, label, options, value, onChange }: {
  name: string
  label: string
  options: string[]
  value: string
  onChange: (value: string) => void
}) {
  return (
    <fieldset className="flex flex-col gap-2">
      <legend className="text-sm font-medium">{label}</legend>
      <RadioGroup value={value} onValueChange={onChange} aria-label={label} className="flex flex-wrap gap-4">
        {options.map((o) => (
          <div key={o} className="flex items-center gap-2">
            <RadioGroupItem id={`fw-${name}-${o}`} value={o} />
            <Label htmlFor={`fw-${name}-${o}`}>{o}</Label>
          </div>
        ))}
      </RadioGroup>
    </fieldset>
  )
}

interface Pending {
  action: string
  title: string
  input: Record<string, unknown>
}

// StateControls enables or disables UFW and sets its default policies and
// its logging level, each through the change dialog.
export function StateControls({ hostId, status }: { hostId: string; status: FirewallStatus }) {
  const [pending, setPending] = useState<Pending | null>(null)
  const [direction, setDirection] = useState<PolicyDirection>("incoming")
  const [policy, setPolicy] = useState<PolicyWord>(() => currentPolicy(status, "incoming"))
  const [level, setLevel] = useState(status.configured.logLevel)

  function chooseDirection(d: PolicyDirection) {
    setDirection(d)
    setPolicy(currentPolicy(status, d))
  }

  function setDefault(event: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
    event.preventDefault()
    setPending({ action: "firewall.defaults.set", title: `Set the default ${direction} policy to ${policy}`, input: { [direction]: POLICY_OF[policy] } })
  }

  function setLogging(event: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
    event.preventDefault()
    setPending({ action: "firewall.logging.set", title: `Set logging to ${level}`, input: { level } })
  }

  return (
    <Card>
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle>Settings</CardTitle>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent className="flex flex-col gap-6">
        <div className="flex items-center gap-4">
          <span>{status.active ? "UFW is active." : "UFW is inactive."}</span>
          {status.active ? (
            <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setPending({ action: "firewall.state.disable", title: "Disable the firewall", input: {} })}>
              Disable
            </Button>
          ) : (
            <Button onClick={() => setPending({ action: "firewall.state.enable", title: "Enable the firewall", input: {} })}>Enable</Button>
          )}
        </div>
        <form aria-label="Default policy" className="flex flex-col gap-3" onSubmit={setDefault}>
          <Choice name="direction" label="Default policy for" options={DIRECTIONS} value={direction} onChange={(v) => chooseDirection(v as PolicyDirection)} />
          <Choice name="policy" label="Policy" options={POLICIES} value={policy} onChange={(v) => setPolicy(v as PolicyWord)} />
          <div>
            <Button type="submit" variant="outline" disabled={policy === currentPolicy(status, direction)}>
              Set default policy
            </Button>
          </div>
        </form>
        <form aria-label="Logging" className="flex flex-col gap-3" onSubmit={setLogging}>
          <Choice name="level" label="Logging level" options={LEVELS} value={level} onChange={setLevel} />
          <div>
            <Button type="submit" variant="outline" disabled={level === status.configured.logLevel}>
              Set logging
            </Button>
          </div>
        </form>
      </CardContent>
      <FirewallChange
        hostId={hostId}
        action={pending?.action ?? "firewall.state.enable"}
        title={pending?.title ?? ""}
        input={pending?.input ?? null}
        onClose={() => setPending(null)}
      />
    </Card>
  )
}
```

Create `web/src/modules/firewall/snapshots-panel.tsx`:

```tsx
import { useState } from "react"
import { Link } from "react-router"
import { useQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query"
import { Alert, AlertDescription } from "darkraise-ui/components/alert"
import { Badge } from "darkraise-ui/components/badge"
import { Button } from "darkraise-ui/components/button"
import { Checkbox } from "darkraise-ui/components/checkbox"
import { Dialog, DialogContent, DialogDescription, DialogFooter, DialogHeader, DialogTitle } from "darkraise-ui/components/dialog"
import { EmptyState } from "darkraise-ui/components/empty-state"
import { Label } from "darkraise-ui/components/label"
import { Spinner } from "darkraise-ui/components/spinner"
import { Table, TableBody, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow } from "darkraise-ui/components/table"
import { errorMessage, readResource } from "@/api/client"
import { formatTime } from "@/lib/format"
import { FirewallChange } from "./firewall-change"
import { FIREWALL_MODULE, snapshotsQueryKey, type SnapshotInfo, type SnapshotList } from "./types"

function Flags({ s }: { s: SnapshotInfo }) {
  return (
    <span className="flex flex-wrap gap-1">
      {s.baseline && <Badge size="sm">baseline</Badge>}
      {s.pinned && <Badge variant="secondary" size="sm">pinned</Badge>}
      {s.system && <Badge variant="outline" size="sm">system</Badge>}
    </span>
  )
}

// RestoreConsent warns before a restore and asks whether it may add or
// remove manual rules: the restore puts UFW's files back as they were, and
// the action refuses to touch a manual rule unless the input says manual.
function RestoreConsent({ snapshot, onCancel, onPlan }: {
  snapshot: SnapshotInfo | null
  onCancel: () => void
  onPlan: (manual: boolean) => void
}) {
  const [manual, setManual] = useState(false)
  return (
    <Dialog
      open={snapshot !== null}
      onOpenChange={(open) => {
        if (open) return
        setManual(false)
        onCancel()
      }}
    >
      <DialogContent>
        <DialogHeader>
          <DialogTitle>Restore this snapshot?</DialogTitle>
          <DialogDescription>
            {`UFW's files, the loaded rules and the forwarding settings go back to how they were on ${snapshot === null ? "" : formatTime(snapshot.createdAt)}.`}
          </DialogDescription>
        </DialogHeader>
        <Alert variant="warning" role="status">
          <AlertDescription>
            Rules added by hand since then are removed, and rules deleted by hand are added back. The next step lists every manual rule the restore would add or remove.
          </AlertDescription>
        </Alert>
        <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
          <Checkbox id="restore-manual" checked={manual} onCheckedChange={(checked) => setManual(checked === true)} />
          <Label htmlFor="restore-manual">Allow the restore to add or remove manual rules</Label>
        </div>
        <DialogFooter>
          <Button variant="outline" onClick={onCancel}>
            Cancel
          </Button>
          <Button
            onClick={() => {
              onPlan(manual)
              setManual(false)
            }}
          >
            Plan the restore
          </Button>
        </DialogFooter>
      </DialogContent>
    </Dialog>
  )
}

// SnapshotsPanel lists the firewall's snapshots, newest first, and
// restores one through the change dialog.
export function SnapshotsPanel({ hostId }: { hostId: string }) {
  const snapshots = useQuery({
    queryKey: snapshotsQueryKey(hostId),
    queryFn: () => readResource<SnapshotList>(hostId, FIREWALL_MODULE, "snapshots"),
  })
  const [asking, setAsking] = useState<SnapshotInfo | null>(null)
  const [restoring, setRestoring] = useState<{ id: string; manual: boolean } | null>(null)

  if (snapshots.isPending) return <Spinner aria-label="Loading the snapshots" />
  if (snapshots.isError) {
    return (
      <Alert variant="destructive" role="alert">
        <AlertDescription>{errorMessage(snapshots.error)}</AlertDescription>
      </Alert>
    )
  }
  const list = [...snapshots.data.snapshots].sort((a, b) => b.createdAt.localeCompare(a.createdAt))
  if (list.length === 0) return <EmptyState title="No snapshots yet" description="The firewall takes a snapshot before every change." />
  return (
    <>
      <Table aria-label="Firewall snapshots">
        <TableHeader>
          <TableRow>
            <TableHead>Taken</TableHead>
            <TableHead>Before change</TableHead>
            <TableHead>Actor</TableHead>
            <TableHead>Kept</TableHead>
            <TableHead>
              <span className="sr-only">Actions</span>
            </TableHead>
          </TableRow>
        </TableHeader>
        <TableBody>
          {list.map((s) => (
            <TableRow key={s.id}>
              <TableCell>{formatTime(s.createdAt)}</TableCell>
              <TableCell>
                {s.changeId === undefined || s.changeId === "" ? (
                  "—"
                ) : (
                  <Link to={`/changes/${encodeURIComponent(s.changeId)}`} className="font-mono underline-offset-4 hover:underline">
                    {s.changeId}
                  </Link>
                )}
              </TableCell>
              <TableCell className="font-mono">{s.actor}</TableCell>
              <TableCell>
                <Flags s={s} />
              </TableCell>
              <TableCell>
                <Button variant="outline" size="sm" aria-label={`Restore the snapshot taken ${formatTime(s.createdAt)}`} onClick={() => setAsking(s)}>
                  Restore
                </Button>
              </TableCell>
            </TableRow>
          ))}
        </TableBody>
      </Table>
      <RestoreConsent
        snapshot={asking}
        onCancel={() => setAsking(null)}
        onPlan={(manual) => {
          if (asking !== null) setRestoring({ id: asking.id, manual })
          setAsking(null)
        }}
      />
      <FirewallChange
        hostId={hostId}
        action="firewall.snapshot.restore"
        title="Restore a snapshot"
        input={restoring === null ? null : restoring.manual ? { id: restoring.id, manual: true } : { id: restoring.id }}
        onClose={() => setRestoring(null)}
      />
    </>
  )
}
```

Register row 82, the frozen half. Before the listeners register, `topology.read` returned empty lists, and `boundAddrs` dropped unreadable addresses silently. An embedded-agent controller, which has no agent listener and no sessions, registers empty agent and peer sources with `setNoAgents`, one line in `services.go`. The tests cover the dropped addresses, the four registrations, the embedded case and a started embedded server.

```go
package server

import (
	"net/netip"
	"sync"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/controller/dispatch"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/controller/listen"
)

// topology is the dispatcher's Topology. The listeners start after the
// dispatcher exists, and startup recovery may already call the dispatcher, so
// each source is registered under mu once it exists; until then it adds
// nothing and the topology reads as incomplete.
type topology struct {
	mu      sync.Mutex
	web     func() []listen.Bound
	runtime func() []netip.AddrPort
	agent   func() []listen.Bound
	peers   func() []netip.Addr
}

func (t *topology) setWeb(f func() []listen.Bound) {
	t.mu.Lock()
	defer t.mu.Unlock()
	t.web = f
}

func (t *topology) setRuntime(f func() []netip.AddrPort) {
	t.mu.Lock()
	defer t.mu.Unlock()
	t.runtime = f
}

func (t *topology) setAgent(f func() []listen.Bound) {
	t.mu.Lock()
	defer t.mu.Unlock()
	t.agent = f
}

func (t *topology) setPeers(f func() []netip.Addr) {
	t.mu.Lock()
	defer t.mu.Unlock()
	t.peers = f
}

// setNoAgents registers empty agent listeners and peers, for a controller
// whose agent runs embedded: it serves no agent listener and has no agent
// sessions, so their lists are complete when empty.
func (t *topology) setNoAgents() {
	t.mu.Lock()
	defer t.mu.Unlock()
	t.agent = func() []listen.Bound { return nil }
	t.peers = func() []netip.Addr { return nil }
}

// read is the topology now. It is complete once all four sources have
// registered.
func (t *topology) read() dispatch.Topology {
	t.mu.Lock()
	web, runtime, agent, peers := t.web, t.runtime, t.agent, t.peers
	t.mu.Unlock()
	var webBound, agentBound []listen.Bound
	var runtimeAddrs []netip.AddrPort
	var agentPeers []netip.Addr
	if web != nil {
		webBound = web()
	}
	if runtime != nil {
		runtimeAddrs = runtime()
	}
	if agent != nil {
		agentBound = agent()
	}
	if peers != nil {
		agentPeers = peers()
	}
	out := topologyOf(webBound, runtimeAddrs, agentBound, agentPeers)
	out.Complete = web != nil && runtime != nil && agent != nil && peers != nil
	return out
}

// topologyOf is the topology of the bound web listeners, the runtime
// listeners, the bound agent listeners and the live agents' addresses. The
// panel is reached through the web and the runtime listeners alike (spec
// 1.5). A listener without an IP address, such as a Unix socket, is left
// out; any other address that cannot be read is listed in Dropped.
func topologyOf(web []listen.Bound, runtime []netip.AddrPort, agent []listen.Bound, peers []netip.Addr) dispatch.Topology {
	panel, dropped := boundAddrs(web)
	for _, ap := range runtime {
		panel = append(panel, netip.AddrPortFrom(ap.Addr().Unmap(), ap.Port()))
	}
	agentAddrs, agentDropped := boundAddrs(agent)
	return dispatch.Topology{PanelListen: panel, AgentListen: agentAddrs, AgentPeers: peers,
		Dropped: append(dropped, agentDropped...)}
}

// boundAddrs returns the IP addresses of bound and, as dropped, every
// address that is not one. A Unix socket is neither: no firewall rule can
// cut it, so it is left out without being dropped.
func boundAddrs(bound []listen.Bound) (out []netip.AddrPort, dropped []string) {
	for _, b := range bound {
		if b.Addr.Network() == "unix" {
			continue
		}
		ap, err := netip.ParseAddrPort(b.Addr.String())
		if err != nil {
			dropped = append(dropped, b.Addr.String())
			continue
		}
		out = append(out, netip.AddrPortFrom(ap.Addr().Unmap(), ap.Port()))
	}
	return out, dropped
}
```

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/platform/netfilter/key.go`
- Test: `internal/platform/netfilter/key_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `ParseRestore`, `parseAddr`, `canonicalProto`, `ufwImages`, `ufwLoad`, `chainNames` (Task 11)
- Produces: `Key` (Part contracts, Task 24)

**Depends on:** Task 11

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-opus-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 2 - risk 3 = 6
**Lenses:** security

Prediction, the in-sync check and verify compare the rules UFW will load with the rules iptables-save prints, and the two spell the same rule differently. `Key` renders a rule's meaning canonically in one family. A false match could hide an out-of-sync host from the lockout guard, so risk is 3. The acceptance test checks that, for every chain on every image and family, the saved rules and the loaded rules have equal keys in the same order (stronger than the multiset the brief asks for), with equal built-in policies. Table tests pin each normalization and the differences `Key` must keep.

```go
// kyRule is the one rule of chain X in input, read by ParseRestore when
// restore is set and by Parse otherwise.
func kyRule(t *testing.T, line string, restore bool) Rule {
	t.Helper()
	in := "*filter\n:X - [0:0]\n:Y - [0:0]\n" + line + "\nCOMMIT\n"

	if restore {

	if err != nil {

	return rs.Table("filter").Chain("X").Rules[0]
}

func TestKeyDistinguishes(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		a, b string
		ipv6 bool
	}{
		{"-A X -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT", "-A X -p tcp --dport 23 -j ACCEPT", false},
		{"-A X -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT", "-A X -p tcp ! --dport 22 -j ACCEPT", false},
		{"-A X -s 10.0.0.0/8 -j ACCEPT", "-A X ! -s 10.0.0.0/8 -j ACCEPT", false},
		{"-A X -s 10.0.0.0/8 -j ACCEPT", "-A X -d 10.0.0.0/8 -j ACCEPT", false},
		{"-A X -i eth0 -j ACCEPT", "-A X -o eth0 -j ACCEPT", false},
		{"-A X -p tcp --dport 3000 -j REJECT", "-A X -p tcp --dport 3000 -j REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset", false},
		{"-A X -m recent --set", "-A X -m recent --set --rdest", false},
		{"-A X -m recent --set", "-A X -m recent --set --name other", false},
		{"-A X -m limit --limit 3/min -j LOG", "-A X -m limit --limit 3/hour -j LOG", false},
		{"-A X -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m recent --set", "-A X -m recent --set -m conntrack --ctstate NEW", false},
		{"-A X -j Y", "-A X -j ACCEPT", false},
		{"-A X -m comment --comment \"a b\" -j ACCEPT", "-A X -m comment --comment a -m comment --comment b -j ACCEPT", false},
		{"-A X -m multiport --dports 80 --dports 90 -j ACCEPT", "-A X -m multiport --dports 90 -j ACCEPT", false},
	} {
		ka, kb := Key(kyRule(t, tc.a, true), tc.ipv6), Key(kyRule(t, tc.b, true), tc.ipv6)
		if ka == kb {
			t.Errorf("%s and %s share the key %s", tc.a, tc.b, ka)
		}
	}
	// A family default differs between the families.
	r := kyRule(t, "-A X -j REJECT", true)
	if Key(r, false) == Key(r, true) {
		t.Errorf("REJECT has the key %s in both families", Key(r, false))
	}
	// An opaque rule keys by its text, so it equals only a rule written the
	// same way.
	o1, o2 := kyRule(t, "-A X -m set --match-set a src -j ACCEPT", true), kyRule(t, "-A X -m set --match-set b src -j ACCEPT", true)
	if !o1.Opaque() || Key(o1, false) == Key(o2, false) {
		t.Errorf("opaque rules: %s and %s", Key(o1, false), Key(o2, false))
	}
}

// TestKeyMatchesUFW is the acceptance test of Key: on every captured image
// and family, each chain of the filter table iptables-save printed holds
// exactly the rules, by Key and in order, of the same chain of the files
// UFW loaded (ufwLoad), and the built-in chains have the same policies.
func TestKeyMatchesUFW(t *testing.T) {
	for _, image := range ufwImages {
		for _, ipv6 := range []bool{false, true} {
			save, family := "iptables.save", "v4"
			if ipv6 {
				save, family = "ip6tables.save", "v6"
			}
			t.Run(image+"/"+family, func(t *testing.T) {
				f, err := os.Open(filepath.Join("testdata", "ufw", image, save)) //nolint:gosec // G304: a fixture under testdata/
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
				defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
				saved, err := Parse(f)
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
				loaded, err := ParseRestore(strings.NewReader(ufwLoad(t, image, ipv6)))
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
				st, lt := saved.Table("filter"), loaded.Table("filter")
				names, loadedNames := chainNames(st), chainNames(lt)
				slices.Sort(names)
				slices.Sort(loadedNames)
				if !slices.Equal(names, loadedNames) {
					t.Fatalf("chains differ:\nsaved  %v\nloaded %v", names, loadedNames)
				}
				if len(names) < 30 {
					t.Fatalf("only %d chains: the capture is not UFW's", len(names))
				}
				rules := 0
				for _, name := range names {
					sc, lc := st.Chain(name), lt.Chain(name)
					if sc.Policy != lc.Policy {
						t.Errorf("chain %s: policy %q saved, %q loaded", name, sc.Policy, lc.Policy)
					}
					var sk, lk []string
					for _, r := range sc.Rules {
						sk = append(sk, Key(r, ipv6))
					}
					for _, r := range lc.Rules {
						lk = append(lk, Key(r, ipv6))
					}
					rules += len(sk)
					if !slices.Equal(sk, lk) {
						t.Errorf("chain %s:\nsaved\n  %s\nloaded\n  %s", name, strings.Join(sk, "\n  "), strings.Join(lk, "\n  "))
					}
				}
				if rules < 60 {
					t.Errorf("only %d rules compared", rules)
				}
			})
		}
	}
}
```

Create `internal/platform/netfilter/key.go`:

```go
package netfilter

import (
	"fmt"
	"slices"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

// Key is the canonical text of what r matches and does, in a family (ipv6
// false for iptables, true for ip6tables), for comparing a rule read from
// restore input with one read from save output: prediction, the in-sync
// check and verify compare rules by Key, never by text. It renders -s, -d,
// -i, -o and -p in that order, then each module in the rule's order with
// its options sorted, then the target, and it fills in what iptables-save
// prints although the input may omit it: the protocol's implicit module
// (ParseRestore adds it), REJECT's default --reject-with, recent's default
// --name, --mask and --rsource, limit's default --limit; it drops what
// iptables-save leaves out: a non-negated /0 address, -p all, limit's
// default --limit-burst, LOG's default --log-level; and it spells values as
// iptables-save does: masked prefixes, protocol names, ICMP types as
// numbers, limit units, conntrack states in the kernel's order, marks in
// hexadecimal. The key of an opaque rule is its text, so two opaque rules
// compare equal only when written alike.
func Key(r Rule, ipv6 bool) string {
	if r.Opaque() {
		return "opaque " + strings.Join(strings.Fields(r.Text), " ")
	}
	var b []string
	add := func(neg bool, opt string, vals ...string) {
		if neg {
			b = append(b, "!")
		}
		b = append(b, opt)
		for _, v := range vals {
			b = append(b, keyQuote(v))
		}
	}
	for _, a := range []struct {
		opt string
		m   AddrMatch
	}{{"-s", r.Source}, {"-d", r.Dest}} {
		if a.m.Prefix.IsValid() && (a.m.Neg || a.m.Prefix.Bits() != 0) {
			add(a.m.Neg, a.opt, a.m.Prefix.Masked().String())
		}
	}
	for _, n := range []struct {
		opt string
		m   NameMatch
	}{{"-i", r.In}, {"-o", r.Out}} {
		if n.m.Name != "" {
			add(n.m.Neg, n.opt, n.m.Name)
		}
	}
	if p := canonicalProto(r.Proto.Name); p != "" && (p != "all" || r.Proto.Neg) {
		add(r.Proto.Neg, "-p", p)
	}
	for _, m := range r.Matches {
		add(false, "-m", m.Module)
		for _, o := range keyOptions(m.Module, m.Options, ipv6, keyMatchDefaults) {
			add(o.Neg, "--"+o.Name, o.Values...)
		}
	}
	if r.Target.Name != "" {
		add(false, "-j", r.Target.Name)
		if !r.Target.Chain {
			for _, o := range keyOptions(r.Target.Name, r.Target.Options, ipv6, keyTargetDefaults) {
				add(o.Neg, "--"+o.Name, o.Values...)
			}
		}
	}
	return strings.Join(b, " ")
}

// keyQuote quotes a value that is empty or holds a space, a quote or a
// backslash, so a key splits back into its tokens unambiguously.
func keyQuote(v string) string {
	if v == "" || strings.ContainsAny(v, " \t\"'\\") {
		return strconv.Quote(v)
	}
	return v
}

// keyOptions returns an extension's options normalized and sorted by name:
// values spelled as iptables-save prints them, defaults iptables-save prints
// added, and defaults it omits dropped. A repeated option is kept, so two
// rules that differ only by it never share a key.
func keyOptions(ext string, opts []Option, ipv6 bool, defaults func(string, []Option, bool) []Option) []Option {
	out := make([]Option, 0, len(opts))
	for _, o := range opts {
		o.Values = slices.Clone(o.Values)
		for i, v := range o.Values {
			o.Values[i] = keyValue(ext, o.Name, v, ipv6)
		}
		out = append(out, o)
	}
	out = defaults(ext, out, ipv6)
	slices.SortStableFunc(out, func(a, b Option) int { return strings.Compare(a.Name, b.Name) })
	return out
}

func hasOption(opts []Option, name string) bool {
	return slices.ContainsFunc(opts, func(o Option) bool { return o.Name == name })
}

// keyMatchDefaults applies the defaults of module ext to its options.
func keyMatchDefaults(ext string, opts []Option, ipv6 bool) []Option {
	switch ext {
	case "recent":
		if !hasOption(opts, "name") {
			opts = append(opts, Option{Name: "name", Values: []string{"DEFAULT"}})
		}
		if !hasOption(opts, "mask") {
			mask := "255.255.255.255"
			if ipv6 {
				mask = "ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff"
			}
			opts = append(opts, Option{Name: "mask", Values: []string{mask}})
		}
		if !hasOption(opts, "rsource") && !hasOption(opts, "rdest") {
			opts = append(opts, Option{Name: "rsource"})
		}
	case "limit":
		if !hasOption(opts, "limit") {
			opts = append(opts, Option{Name: "limit", Values: []string{"3/hour"}})
		}
		opts = slices.DeleteFunc(opts, func(o Option) bool {
			return o.Name == "limit-burst" && !o.Neg && slices.Equal(o.Values, []string{"5"})
		})
	}
	return opts
}

// keyTargetDefaults applies the defaults of target ext to its options.
func keyTargetDefaults(ext string, opts []Option, ipv6 bool) []Option {
	switch ext {
	case "REJECT":
		if !hasOption(opts, "reject-with") {
			with := "icmp-port-unreachable"
			if ipv6 {
				with = "icmp6-port-unreachable"
			}
			opts = append(opts, Option{Name: "reject-with", Values: []string{with}})
		}
	case "LOG":
		opts = slices.DeleteFunc(opts, func(o Option) bool { return o.Name == "log-level" && slices.Equal(o.Values, []string{"4"}) })
	}
	return opts
}

// keyValue spells one option value as iptables-save prints it.
func keyValue(ext, opt, v string, ipv6 bool) string {
	switch {
	case ext == "icmp" && opt == "icmp-type":
		return icmpTypeNumber(icmpTypes, v)
	case ext == "icmp6" && opt == "icmpv6-type":
		return icmpTypeNumber(icmp6Types, v)
	case ext == "limit" && opt == "limit":
		return limitRate(v)
	case (ext == "conntrack" && opt == "ctstate") || (ext == "state" && opt == "state"):
		return ctStates(v)
	case (ext == "mark" || ext == "connmark") && opt == "mark", ext == "MARK" && opt == "set-xmark":
		return markValue(v, ext == "MARK")
	case ext == "REJECT" && opt == "reject-with":
		aliases := rejectAliases
		if ipv6 {
			aliases = reject6Aliases
		}
		if c, ok := aliases[v]; ok {
			return c
		}
	case ext == "LOG" && opt == "log-level":
		if n, ok := logLevels[strings.ToLower(v)]; ok {
			return n
		}
	case ext == "recent" && opt == "mask":
		return keyAddr(v)
	}
	return v
}

// icmpType is an ICMP type name of iptables (libxt_icmp.c, libip6t_icmp6.c)
// with the type and, for a name of one code, the code.
type icmpType struct {
	typ  int
	code int // -1 for every code
}

var icmpTypes = map[string]icmpType{
	"any": {-1, -1}, "echo-reply": {0, -1}, "pong": {0, -1}, "destination-unreachable": {3, -1},
	"network-unreachable": {3, 0}, "host-unreachable": {3, 1}, "protocol-unreachable": {3, 2},
	"port-unreachable": {3, 3}, "fragmentation-needed": {3, 4}, "source-route-failed": {3, 5},
	"network-unknown": {3, 6}, "host-unknown": {3, 7}, "network-prohibited": {3, 9}, "host-prohibited": {3, 10},
	"tos-network-unreachable": {3, 11}, "tos-host-unreachable": {3, 12}, "communication-prohibited": {3, 13},
	"host-precedence-violation": {3, 14}, "precedence-cutoff": {3, 15}, "source-quench": {4, -1},
	"redirect": {5, -1}, "network-redirect": {5, 0}, "host-redirect": {5, 1}, "tos-network-redirect": {5, 2},
	"tos-host-redirect": {5, 3}, "echo-request": {8, -1}, "ping": {8, -1}, "router-advertisement": {9, -1},
	"router-solicitation": {10, -1}, "time-exceeded": {11, -1}, "ttl-exceeded": {11, -1},
	"ttl-zero-during-transit": {11, 0}, "ttl-zero-during-reassembly": {11, 1}, "parameter-problem": {12, -1},
	"ip-header-bad": {12, 0}, "required-option-missing": {12, 1}, "timestamp-request": {13, -1},
	"timestamp-reply": {14, -1}, "address-mask-request": {17, -1}, "address-mask-reply": {18, -1},
}

var icmp6Types = map[string]icmpType{
	"destination-unreachable": {1, -1}, "no-route": {1, 0}, "communication-prohibited": {1, 1},
	"beyond-scope": {1, 2}, "address-unreachable": {1, 3}, "port-unreachable": {1, 4},
	"failed-policy": {1, 5}, "reject-route": {1, 6}, "packet-too-big": {2, -1}, "time-exceeded": {3, -1},
	"ttl-exceeded": {3, -1}, "ttl-zero-during-transit": {3, 0}, "ttl-zero-during-reassembly": {3, 1},
	"parameter-problem": {4, -1}, "bad-header": {4, 0}, "unknown-header-type": {4, 1}, "unknown-option": {4, 2},
	"echo-request": {128, -1}, "ping": {128, -1}, "echo-reply": {129, -1}, "pong": {129, -1},
	"router-solicitation": {133, -1}, "router-advertisement": {134, -1}, "neighbour-solicitation": {135, -1},
	"neighbor-solicitation": {135, -1}, "neighbour-advertisement": {136, -1}, "neighbor-advertisement": {136, -1},
	"redirect": {137, -1},
}

// icmpTypeNumber is an ICMP type as iptables-save prints it: "any", the type
// number, or type/code for a single code. An unknown spelling is kept.
func icmpTypeNumber(names map[string]icmpType, v string) string {
	t, ok := names[strings.ToLower(v)]
	switch {
	case !ok:
		return v
	case t.typ < 0:
		return "any"
	case t.code < 0:
		return strconv.Itoa(t.typ)
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("%d/%d", t.typ, t.code)
}

// limitUnits are the units of a limit rate, in the order iptables tries
// them, with the spelling iptables-save prints.
var limitUnits = []struct{ word, short string }{{"second", "sec"}, {"minute", "min"}, {"hour", "hour"}, {"day", "day"}}

// limitRate is a rate such as 3/minute as iptables-save prints it, 3/min.
// Like iptables (libxt_limit.c, parse_rate), it takes any prefix of a unit
// word and a rate without a unit as per second.
func limitRate(v string) string {
	n, unit, ok := strings.Cut(v, "/")
	if !ok {
		return n + "/sec"
	}
	for _, u := range limitUnits {
		if unit != "" && len(unit) <= len(u.word) && strings.EqualFold(unit, u.word[:len(unit)]) {
			return n + "/" + u.short
		}
	}
	return v
}

// ctStateOrder is the order iptables-save prints conntrack states in.
var ctStateOrder = []string{"INVALID", "NEW", "RELATED", "ESTABLISHED", "UNTRACKED", "SNAT", "DNAT"}

// ctStates sorts a comma list of states into ctStateOrder; an unknown state
// sorts last, in its own order.
func ctStates(v string) string {
	states := strings.Split(strings.ToUpper(v), ",")
	slices.SortStableFunc(states, func(a, b string) int {
		ia, ib := slices.Index(ctStateOrder, a), slices.Index(ctStateOrder, b)
		if ia < 0 {
			ia = len(ctStateOrder)
		}
		if ib < 0 {
			ib = len(ctStateOrder)
		}
		return ia - ib
	})
	return strings.Join(states, ",")
}

// markValue is a mark value[/mask] in hexadecimal as iptables-save prints
// it: the mask is omitted when it is all ones, except for MARK
// --set-xmark, which always prints it. A value that is not a number is
// kept.
func markValue(v string, alwaysMask bool) string {
	val, mask, hasMask := strings.Cut(v, "/")
	n, err := strconv.ParseUint(val, 0, 32)
	if err != nil {
		return v
	}
	m := uint64(0xffffffff)
	if hasMask {
		if m, err = strconv.ParseUint(mask, 0, 32); err != nil {
			return v
		}
	}
	if m == 0xffffffff && !alwaysMask {
		return fmt.Sprintf("0x%x", n)
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("0x%x/0x%x", n, m)
}

// keyAddr is an address in its canonical spelling; a value that is not an
// address is kept.
func keyAddr(v string) string {
	if pfx, ok := parseAddr(v, true); ok {
		return pfx.Addr().String()
	}
	return v
}

// rejectAliases map the --reject-with spellings iptables accepts to the one
// iptables-save prints (libipt_REJECT.c); reject6Aliases do the same for
// ip6tables (libip6t_REJECT.c).
var (
	rejectAliases = map[string]string{
		"net-unreach": "icmp-net-unreachable", "host-unreach": "icmp-host-unreachable",
		"proto-unreach": "icmp-proto-unreachable", "port-unreach": "icmp-port-unreachable",
		"net-prohib": "icmp-net-prohibited", "host-prohib": "icmp-host-prohibited",
		"admin-prohib": "icmp-admin-prohibited", "tcp-rst": "tcp-reset",
	}
	reject6Aliases = map[string]string{
		"no-route": "icmp6-no-route", "adm-prohibited": "icmp6-adm-prohibited",
		"addr-unreach": "icmp6-addr-unreachable", "port-unreach": "icmp6-port-unreachable",
		"tcp-rst": "tcp-reset", "policy-fail": "icmp6-policy-fail", "reject-route": "icmp6-reject-route",
	}
)

// logLevels map syslog level names to the numbers iptables-save prints.
var logLevels = map[string]string{
	"emerg": "0", "alert": "1", "crit": "2", "err": "3", "error": "3", "warning": "4", "warn": "4",
	"notice": "5", "info": "6", "debug": "7",
}
```

```go
func TestArgs(t *testing.T) {
	for _, c := range argsTestRules {
		if err := c.rule.Validate(); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("test rule %+v is invalid: %v", c.rule, err)
		}
		if got := strings.Join(AddArgs(c.rule), "|"); got != c.add {
			t.Errorf("AddArgs(%+v)\n got %s\nwant %s", c.rule, got, c.add)
		}
		if got := strings.Join(DeleteArgs(c.rule), "|"); got != c.delete {
			t.Errorf("DeleteArgs(%+v)\n got %s\nwant %s", c.rule, got, c.delete)
		}
		if got := strings.Join(InsertArgs(2, c.rule), "|"); got != c.insert {
			t.Errorf("InsertArgs(2, %+v)\n got %s\nwant %s", c.rule, got, c.insert)
		}
	}
}

func TestArgsNoOptionLikeValue(t *testing.T) {
	for _, c := range argsTestRules {
		for _, args := range [][]string{AddArgs(c.rule), DeleteArgs(c.rule), InsertArgs(1, c.rule)} {
			if i := slices.IndexFunc(args, func(a string) bool { return strings.HasPrefix(a, "-") || a == "" }); i >= 0 {
				t.Errorf("argument %d of %q is empty or starts with a dash", i, args)
			}
		}
	}
}

// TestArgsRoundTrip checks that the tuples ufw wrote for AddArgs parse back
// to the same rules: the v4 and both-family rules in order, then the
// v6-only ones. A manual rule's id is derived from its tuple.
func TestArgsRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	var v4, v6 []Tuple
	for _, l := range argsTestUserRules {
		tu, err := ParseTuple(l, false)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		v4 = append(v4, tu)
	}
	for _, l := range argsTestUser6Rules {
		tu, err := ParseTuple(l, true)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		v6 = append(v6, tu)
	}
	var want []Rule
	for _, only6 := range []bool{false, true} {
		for _, c := range argsTestRules {
			if (c.rule.Family == FamilyV6) == only6 {
				want = append(want, c.rule)
			}
		}
	}
	got := Merge(v4, v6)
	if len(got) != len(want) {
		t.Fatalf("Merge returned %d rules, want %d", len(got), len(want))
	}
	for i, w := range want {
		if w.Origin == OriginManual {
			if !strings.HasPrefix(got[i].ID, "manual-") {
				t.Errorf("rule %d id = %q, want a manual id", i, got[i].ID)
			}
			w.ID = got[i].ID
		}
		if got[i] != w {
			t.Errorf("rule %d\n got %+v\nwant %+v", i, got[i], w)
		}
	}
}
```

```go
package model

import "strconv"

// AddArgs is the argument vector after /usr/sbin/ufw that adds r. A
// Darkpanel rule ends with "comment" and its tag as one argument; a manual
// rule ends with its own comment, if any. r must be valid (Validate) and,
// for a Darkpanel rule, carry its id.
func AddArgs(r Rule) []string {
	return withComment(r, actionPrefix(r, nil))
}

// DeleteArgs is the argument vector that deletes r: "delete" and the rule
// specification without the comment, which ufw matches whatever comment
// the stored rule carries.
func DeleteArgs(r Rule) []string {
	return actionPrefix(r, []string{"delete"})
}

// InsertArgs is the argument vector that adds r at position pos (1-based,
// as ufw numbers its rules), for the inverse of a delete.
func InsertArgs(pos int, r Rule) []string {
	return withComment(r, actionPrefix(r, []string{"insert", strconv.Itoa(pos)}))
}

// actionPrefix renders "[route] <verb...> <action> <rule spec>".
func actionPrefix(r Rule, verb []string) []string {
	var args []string
	if r.Direction == DirRoute {
		args = append(args, "route")
	}
	args = append(args, verb...)
	args = append(args, string(r.Action))
	return append(args, spec(r)...)
}

// spec renders the rule specification in the order ufw's grammar requires:
// direction and interfaces, then the log type, then protocol, source and
// destination ("ufw allow log in" is refused as an invalid interface
// clause).
func spec(r Rule) []string {
	var args []string
	switch r.Direction {
	case DirRoute:
		if r.InIface != "" {
			args = append(args, "in", "on", r.InIface)
		}
		if r.OutIface != "" {
			args = append(args, "out", "on", r.OutIface)
		}
	case DirIn:
		args = append(args, "in")
		if r.InIface != "" {
			args = append(args, "on", r.InIface)
		}
	case DirOut:
		args = append(args, "out")
		if r.OutIface != "" {
			args = append(args, "on", r.OutIface)
		}
	}
	if r.Log == LogOn || r.Log == LogAll {
		args = append(args, string(r.Log))
	}
	if r.Proto != ProtoAny {
		args = append(args, "proto", string(r.Proto))
	}
	args = append(args, "from", argAddr(r.From, r.Family))
	if r.FromPort != "" {
		args = append(args, "port", r.FromPort)
	}
	args = append(args, "to", argAddr(r.To, r.Family))
	if r.ToPort != "" {
		args = append(args, "port", r.ToPort)
	}
	return args
}

// argAddr writes any as the family's zero prefix for a single-family rule:
// ufw writes a rule whose addresses are both "any" into both files.
func argAddr(addr string, fam Family) string {
	if addr != Any {
		return addr
	}
	switch fam {
	case FamilyV4:
		return "0.0.0.0/0"
	case FamilyV6:
		return "::/0"
	}
	return Any
}

func withComment(r Rule, args []string) []string {
	if r.Origin == OriginManual {
		if r.Comment == "" {
			return args
		}
		return append(args, "comment", r.Comment)
	}
	return append(args, "comment", Tag(r.ID, r.Comment))
}
```

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-sonnet-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 1 - risk 3 = 5
**Lenses:** security

`darkpanel firewall rollback --local [--change <id>]` reverts the newest firewall change made by a person, or the named one, through the agent socket while the controller may be unreachable: a pending change is reverted; a confirmed change is undone by restoring the snapshot its output names through `firewall.snapshot.restore`, confirmed as soon as it verifies. It replaces the wave 0 stub of `firewallCommands`. The tests run the real command tree against a fake agent on a Unix socket and prove the target choice (system changes, composite steps and other modules skipped, paging), the question before a revert, the restore's input with `--manual` and `--override`, `ConfirmNow`, every refusal, and that the generated `firewall snapshot restore` serves break-glass with `--local --confirm`.

```go
package cli

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/controller/coreactions"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/coretest"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
)

// fwrbRestoreInput is the input of the fixture's firewall.snapshot.restore.
type fwrbRestoreInput struct {
	core.Guarded
	ID     string `json:"id" jsonschema_description:"Snapshot id."`
	Manual bool   `json:"manual,omitempty" jsonschema_description:"Allow adding or removing manual rules."`
}

// fwrbModule declares the firewall names rollback uses: the revertible
// firewall.snapshot.restore with its overridable lockout guard and the
// repair action it names.
type fwrbModule struct{}

func (fwrbModule) Manifest() core.Manifest {
	return core.Manifest{
		ID: "firewall", Version: 1, DefaultEnabled: true,
		Actions: []core.ActionDef{
			core.DefineRevertible(core.ActionSpec{
				Name: firewallRestoreAction, Version: 1, Side: core.SideAgent, Summary: "Restore a firewall snapshot.",
				LockKeys: []string{"firewall"}, RepairedBy: "firewall.state.repair",
				Guards: []core.GuardSpec{{ID: "firewall.lockout", Overridable: true}},
			}, fixtureHandler[fwrbRestoreInput, demoRule]{}),
			core.DefineMutating(core.ActionSpec{
				Name: "firewall.state.repair", Version: 1, Class: core.ClassIrreversible, Side: core.SideAgent,
				Summary: "Repair the firewall.", LockKeys: []string{"firewall"},
			}, fixtureHandler[demoNoInput, demoRule]{}),
		},
	}
}

func fwrbRegistry(t *testing.T) *core.Registry {
	t.Helper()
	reg, err := core.NewRegistry(coreactions.Module(coreactions.Deps{}), fwrbModule{})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return reg
}

// fwrbView is a firewall change whose output names the snapshot s<id>
// taken before it, as every mutating firewall action's output does.
func fwrbView(id, action, actor, state string) core.ChangeView {
	return core.ChangeView{ID: id, HostID: "h1", Action: action, Actor: actor, Version: 1, Class: core.ClassRevertible, State: state,
		Output: json.RawMessage(`{"snapshot":"s` + strings.TrimPrefix(id, "c") + `"}`)}
}

// fwrbAgent is a fake agent holding changes, newest first; it records the
// listings and every call that changes something.
func fwrbAgent(rec *agentCalls, changes []core.ChangeView) *coretest.FakeAgent {
	return &coretest.FakeAgent{
		ChangesFunc: func(_ context.Context, f core.ChangeFilter) ([]core.ChangeView, error) {
			rec.add("changes before=%q limit=%d", f.Before, f.Limit)
			start := 0
			if f.Before != "" {
				start = slices.IndexFunc(changes, func(v core.ChangeView) bool { return v.ID == f.Before }) + 1
			}
			return slices.Clone(changes[start:min(start+f.Limit, len(changes))]), nil
		},
		ChangeFunc: func(_ context.Context, id string) (core.ChangeView, error) {
			for _, v := range changes {
				if v.ID == id {
					return v, nil
				}
			}
			return core.ChangeView{}, errcode.New(errcode.ChangeNotFound, "no change "+id)
		},
		RevertFunc: func(_ context.Context, _ core.Principal, id string) (core.ChangeView, error) {
			rec.add("revert %s", id)
			return fwrbView(id, "firewall.rule.add", "user:u1", core.StateReverted), nil
		},
		PlanFunc: func(_ context.Context, _ core.Principal, a core.ActionRef, input json.RawMessage, _ core.PlanOptions) (core.PlanView, error) {
			rec.add("plan %s/v%d %s", a.Name, a.Version, input)
			var in fwrbRestoreInput
			_ = json.Unmarshal(input, &in)
			guard := core.Guard{ID: "firewall.lockout", OK: true, Message: "every protected flow passes", Overridable: true}
			if in.ID == "s3" && len(in.Overrides) == 0 {
				guard.OK, guard.Message = false, "ssh from 203.0.113.7 to 192.0.2.1:22 on eth0 is dropped"
			}
			return core.PlanView{PlanID: "p1", HostID: "h1", Action: a.Name, Version: a.Version,
				Diff: []core.DiffLine{{Op: "-", Text: "allow in tcp 8080"}}, Guards: []core.Guard{guard}}, nil
		},
		ApplyFunc: func(_ context.Context, _ core.Principal, planID string, opts core.ApplyOptions) (core.ChangeView, error) {
			rec.add("apply %s confirmNow=%t", planID, opts.ConfirmNow)
			return fwrbView("c9", firewallRestoreAction, "user:u1", core.StateConfirmed), nil
		},
	}
}

func TestFirewallRollbackRevertsTheNewestPendingChange(t *testing.T) {
	changes := []core.ChangeView{
		fwrbView("c5", "firewall.containers.apply", "system:firewall.reconcile", core.StatePending),
		fwrbView("c4", "docker.container.stop", "user:u1", core.StateCompleted),
		{ID: "c3s", Action: "firewall.rules.apply", Actor: "user:u1", State: core.StatePending, ParentChangeID: "c3p"},
		fwrbView("c2", "firewall.rule.add", "user:u1", core.StatePending),
		fwrbView("c1", "firewall.rule.add", "user:u1", core.StateConfirmed),
	}
	rec := &agentCalls{}
	cli := cliEnv{reg: fwrbRegistry(t), agentSocket: agentSocket(t, fwrbAgent(rec, changes))}
	out, errOut, code := cli.run(t, "firewall", "rollback", "--local", "--yes")
	if code != ExitOK || !strings.Contains(out, "Change c2 (firewall.rule.add) is pending: it will be reverted now.\n") ||
		!strings.Contains(out, "Change c2: reverted\n") {
		t.Errorf("exit %d, out %q, err %q", code, out, errOut)
	}
	if got, want := rec.list(), []string{`changes before="" limit=100`, "revert c2"}; !slices.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("the agent saw %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}

func TestFirewallRollbackAsksBeforeReverting(t *testing.T) {
	rec := &agentCalls{}
	changes := []core.ChangeView{fwrbView("c2", "firewall.rule.add", "user:u1", core.StatePending)}
	cli := cliEnv{reg: fwrbRegistry(t), agentSocket: agentSocket(t, fwrbAgent(rec, changes))}
	_, errOut, code := cli.run(t, "firewall", "rollback", "--local")
	if code != ExitRefused || !strings.Contains(errOut, "pass --yes") {
		t.Errorf("exit %d, err %q; want a refusal asking for --yes", code, errOut)
	}
	cli.terminal, cli.stdin = true, "y\n"
	if _, errOut, code = cli.run(t, "firewall", "rollback", "--local"); code != ExitOK {
		t.Errorf("answered y: exit %d, err %q", code, errOut)
	}
	want := []string{`changes before="" limit=100`, `changes before="" limit=100`, "revert c2"}
	if got := rec.list(); !slices.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("the agent saw %q, want %q: one revert, after the answer", got, want)
	}
}

func TestFirewallRollbackRestoresAConfirmedChange(t *testing.T) {
	changes := []core.ChangeView{
		fwrbView("c2", "firewall.rule.add", "user:u1", core.StateReverted),
		fwrbView("c1", "firewall.rule.add", "user:u1", core.StateConfirmed),
	}
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name  string
		extra []string
		input string
	}{
		{"plain", nil, `{"id":"s1"}`},
		{"manual and an override", []string{"--manual", "--override", "firewall.lockout"},
			`{"id":"s1","manual":true,"overrides":["firewall.lockout"]}`},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			rec := &agentCalls{}
			cli := cliEnv{reg: fwrbRegistry(t), agentSocket: agentSocket(t, fwrbAgent(rec, changes))}
			out, errOut, code := cli.run(t, slices.Concat([]string{"firewall", "rollback", "--change", "c1", "--local", "--yes"}, tc.extra)...)
			if code != ExitOK || !strings.Contains(out, "snapshot s1, taken before it, will be restored and confirmed") ||
				!strings.Contains(out, "Plan for firewall.snapshot.restore/v1 on host h1:\n  - allow in tcp 8080\n") ||
				!strings.Contains(out, "Change c9: confirmed\n") {

			}
			want := []string{"plan firewall.snapshot.restore/v1 " + tc.input, "apply p1 confirmNow=true"}
			if got := rec.list(); !slices.Equal(got, want) {
				t.Errorf("the agent saw %q, want %q", got, want)
			}
		})
	}
}
```

```go
package cli

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/spf13/cobra"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/agent/api"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
)

// The firewall names the break-glass rollback uses (spec 2.5).
const (
	firewallRestoreAction = "firewall.snapshot.restore"
	firewallModulePrefix  = "firewall."
	systemActorPrefix     = "system:"
)

// firewallChangePage is how many changes one listing of the agent socket
// asks for while rollback looks for the newest firewall change. It is a
// variable so tests can shorten it.
var firewallChangePage = 100

// firewallCommands are the hand-written commands of the firewall module,
// added under "darkpanel firewall": the break-glass rollback (spec 2.5).
// The break-glass snapshot restore is the generated command of
// firewall.snapshot.restore, which --local already serves.
func firewallCommands(a *app) []*cobra.Command {
	return []*cobra.Command{a.firewallRollbackCommand()}
}

func (a *app) firewallRollbackCommand() *cobra.Command {
	cmd := &cobra.Command{
		Use:   "rollback",
		Short: "Roll back a firewall change through this host's agent socket (break-glass, needs --local)",
		Long: "Roll back the newest firewall change that no background task made, or the change --change names, " +
			"through this host's agent socket. A pending change is reverted; a confirmed change is undone by restoring " +
			"the snapshot taken before it, and the restore is confirmed as soon as it verifies. Run it as root with --local.",
		Args:        cobra.NoArgs,
		Annotations: map[string]string{annotationLocal: "true"},
		RunE:        func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error { return a.runFirewallRollback(cmd) },
	}
	cmd.Flags().String("change", "", "the firewall change to roll back (default: the newest one no background task made)")
	cmd.Flags().Bool("yes", false, "roll back without asking Apply? [y/N]")
	cmd.Flags().Bool("manual", false, "let the snapshot restore add or remove manual rules, which its plan lists")
	cmd.Flags().StringArray("override", nil, "plan the snapshot restore again with this failing guard overridden (repeatable); overridable: firewall.lockout")
	cmd.Flags().Bool("json", false, "print the raw JSON of the change")
	return cmd
}

// runFirewallRollback reverts a pending firewall change, or restores the
// snapshot of a confirmed one and confirms the restore in the same run.
func (a *app) runFirewallRollback(cmd *cobra.Command) error {
	if local, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("local"); !local {
		return usagef("%s is a break-glass command: run it as root on the host with --local", cmd.CommandPath())
	}
	id, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("change")
	return a.withAgent(cmd, nil, nil, nil, func(c *api.Client) error {
		ch, err := firewallTarget(cmd.Context(), c, id)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		switch ch.State {
		case core.StatePending:
			return a.firewallRevert(cmd, c, ch)
		case core.StateConfirmed:
			return a.firewallRestore(cmd, c, ch)
		default:
			return refusedf("change %s (%s) is %s: only a pending or a confirmed firewall change can be rolled back",
				sanitize(ch.ID), sanitize(ch.Action), sanitize(ch.State))
		}
	})
}

// firewallTarget returns the change id names, which must be a firewall
// change, or else the newest firewall change that is neither a background
// task's nor a step of a composite.
func firewallTarget(ctx context.Context, c *api.Client, id string) (core.ChangeView, error) {
	if id != "" {
		cctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, localTimeout)
		defer cancel()
		v, err := c.Change(cctx, id)
		if err != nil {
			return core.ChangeView{}, localError(err)
		}
		if !strings.HasPrefix(v.Action, firewallModulePrefix) {
			return core.ChangeView{}, refusedf("change %s is %s, not a firewall change", sanitize(v.ID), sanitize(v.Action))
		}
		return v, nil
	}
	before := ""
	for {
		cctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, localTimeout)
		page, err := c.Changes(cctx, core.ChangeFilter{Before: before, Limit: firewallChangePage})
		cancel()
		if err != nil {
			return core.ChangeView{}, localError(err)
		}
		for _, v := range page {
			if strings.HasPrefix(v.Action, firewallModulePrefix) && !strings.HasPrefix(v.Actor, systemActorPrefix) && v.ParentChangeID == "" {
				return v, nil
			}
		}
		if len(page) < firewallChangePage {
			return core.ChangeView{}, refusedf("this host has no firewall change to roll back")
		}
		before = page[len(page)-1].ID
	}
}

// firewallRevert reverts the pending change ch through the agent's revert
// route, after the Apply? [y/N] question.
func (a *app) firewallRevert(cmd *cobra.Command, c *api.Client, ch core.ChangeView) error {
	info := firewallInfo(cmd)
	_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(info, "Change %s (%s) is pending: it will be reverted now.\n", sanitize(ch.ID), sanitize(ch.Action))
	if err := a.askApply(cmd, false); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(cmd.Context(), localTimeout)
	defer cancel()
	v, err := c.Revert(ctx, core.Principal{}, ch.ID)
	if err != nil {
		return localError(err)
	}
	return firewallShow(cmd, localChange(v), core.StateReverted)
}

// firewallRestore plans firewall.snapshot.restore with the snapshot taken
// before the confirmed change ch, shows the plan, asks, applies it and
// confirms it as soon as it verifies.
func (a *app) firewallRestore(cmd *cobra.Command, c *api.Client, ch core.ChangeView) error {
	def, ok := latestAction(a.opts.Registry, firewallRestoreAction)
	if !ok {
		return fmt.Errorf("this darkpanel has no %s action, so it cannot restore a snapshot", firewallRestoreAction)
	}
	snap, err := firewallSnapshotOf(ch)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(firewallInfo(cmd), "Change %s (%s) is confirmed: snapshot %s, taken before it, will be restored and confirmed.\n",
		sanitize(ch.ID), sanitize(ch.Action), sanitize(snap))
	in := map[string]any{"id": snap}
	if manual, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("manual"); manual {
		in["manual"] = true
	}
	raw, err := json.Marshal(in)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	input, err := withOverrides(cmd, raw)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	calls := localCalls(c, def, a.opts.AgentSocket)
	apply := calls.apply
	calls.apply = func(ctx context.Context, planID, confirmation string, _ bool, timeout time.Duration) (changeWire, json.RawMessage, error) {
		return apply(ctx, planID, confirmation, true, timeout)
	}
	restored, rawChange, err := a.planAndApply(cmd, calls, input, false)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if asJSON, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("json"); asJSON {
		if _, err := fmt.Fprintf(cmd.OutOrStdout(), "%s\n", rawChange); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	} else if err := printChange(cmd.OutOrStdout(), restored, nil); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return firewallOutcome(restored, core.StateConfirmed)
}

// firewallSnapshotOf returns the id of the snapshot the firewall took
// before change ch, which every mutating firewall action's output names.
func firewallSnapshotOf(ch core.ChangeView) (string, error) {
	var out struct {
		Snapshot string `json:"snapshot"`
	}
	if len(ch.Output) > 0 {
		if err := json.Unmarshal(ch.Output, &out); err != nil {
			return "", fmt.Errorf("decode the output of change %s: %w", ch.ID, err)
		}
	}
	if out.Snapshot == "" {
		return "", refusedf("change %s names no snapshot taken before it, so it cannot be rolled back; "+
			"list the snapshots with darkpanel firewall snapshots get --local", sanitize(ch.ID))
	}
	return out.Snapshot, nil
}

// firewallInfo is where rollback writes what it is about to do: standard
// output, or standard error with --json.
func firewallInfo(cmd *cobra.Command) io.Writer {
	if asJSON, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("json"); asJSON {
		return cmd.ErrOrStderr()
	}
	return cmd.OutOrStdout()
}

// firewallShow prints a change as rollback ended it, and fails unless it
// is in state want.
func firewallShow(cmd *cobra.Command, ch changeWire, want string) error {
	if asJSON, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("json"); asJSON {
		raw, err := json.Marshal(ch)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if _, err := fmt.Fprintf(cmd.OutOrStdout(), "%s\n", raw); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	} else if err := printChange(cmd.OutOrStdout(), ch, nil); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return firewallOutcome(ch, want)
}

// firewallOutcome is the error of a rollback whose change did not end in
// state want.
func firewallOutcome(ch changeWire, want string) error {
	if ch.State == want {
		return nil
	}
	if ch.Error != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("change %s is %s, not %s: %s (%s)", ch.ID, ch.State, want, ch.Error.Message, ch.Error.Code)
	}
	return fmt.Errorf("change %s is %s, not %s", ch.ID, ch.State, want)
}
```

```tsx
import { useQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query"
import { Alert, AlertDescription } from "darkraise-ui/components/alert"
import { Dialog, DialogContent, DialogDescription, DialogHeader, DialogTitle } from "darkraise-ui/components/dialog"
import { Spinner } from "darkraise-ui/components/spinner"
import { errorMessage, readAction } from "@/api/client"
import { formatTime } from "@/lib/format"
import { FIREWALL_ACTION_VERSION, type SnapshotComparison, type SnapshotInfo } from "./types"

// ComparePair is what to compare: snapshot a against snapshot b, or against
// the host's current state when b is null.
export interface ComparePair {
  a: SnapshotInfo
  b: SnapshotInfo | null
}

function Comparison({ hostId, pair }: { hostId: string; pair: ComparePair }) {
  const input = pair.b === null ? { from: pair.a.id } : { from: pair.a.id, to: pair.b.id }
  const compared = useQuery({
    queryKey: ["firewall.snapshot.compare", hostId, pair.a.id, pair.b?.id ?? null],
    queryFn: () => readAction<SnapshotComparison>("firewall.snapshot.compare", FIREWALL_ACTION_VERSION, input, hostId),
    gcTime: 0,
  })
  if (compared.isPending) return <Spinner aria-label="Comparing" />
  if (compared.isError) {
    return (
      <Alert variant="destructive" role="alert">
        <AlertDescription>{errorMessage(compared.error)}</AlertDescription>
      </Alert>
    )
  }
  const { diff, files } = compared.data
  if (diff.length === 0 && files.length === 0) return <p>No differences.</p>
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
      {diff.length > 0 && (
        <pre aria-label="Differences" className="overflow-x-auto rounded-md bg-muted p-3 font-mono text-xs">
          {diff.map((d, i) => (
            <div key={i} className={d.op === "+" ? "text-success" : d.op === "-" ? "text-destructive" : undefined}>
              {`${d.op} ${d.text}`}
            </div>
          ))}
        </pre>
      )}
      {files.length > 0 && (
        <div className="flex flex-col gap-1">
          <span className="text-sm font-medium">Files that differ</span>
          <ul aria-label="Files that differ" className="list-disc pl-5 font-mono text-xs">
            {files.map((f) => (
              <li key={f.path}>{f.path}</li>
            ))}
          </ul>
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

// CompareDialog shows firewall.snapshot.compare's diff of two snapshots,
// or of one snapshot against now.
export function CompareDialog({ hostId, pair, onClose }: { hostId: string; pair: ComparePair | null; onClose: () => void }) {
  return (
    <Dialog open={pair !== null} onOpenChange={(open) => !open && onClose()}>
      <DialogContent>
        <DialogHeader>
          <DialogTitle>{pair?.b === null ? "Compare with now" : "Compare two snapshots"}</DialogTitle>
          <DialogDescription>
            {pair === null
              ? ""
              : pair.b === null
                ? `From the snapshot taken ${formatTime(pair.a.createdAt)} to the firewall as it is now.`
                : `From the snapshot taken ${formatTime(pair.a.createdAt)} to the one taken ${formatTime(pair.b.createdAt)}.`}
          </DialogDescription>
        </DialogHeader>
        {pair !== null && <Comparison hostId={hostId} pair={pair} />}
      </DialogContent>
    </Dialog>
  )
}
```
