```tsx
import { useState } from "react"
import { Link } from "react-router"
import { useQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query"
import { Alert, AlertDescription } from "darkraise-ui/components/alert"
import { Badge } from "darkraise-ui/components/badge"
import { Button } from "darkraise-ui/components/button"
import { Checkbox } from "darkraise-ui/components/checkbox"
import { Dialog, DialogContent, DialogDescription, DialogFooter, DialogHeader, DialogTitle } from "darkraise-ui/components/dialog"
import { EmptyState } from "darkraise-ui/components/empty-state"
import { Label } from "darkraise-ui/components/label"
import { Spinner } from "darkraise-ui/components/spinner"
import { Table, TableBody, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow } from "darkraise-ui/components/table"
import { errorMessage, readResource } from "@/api/client"
import { formatTime } from "@/lib/format"
import { FirewallChange } from "./firewall-change"
import { CompareDialog, type ComparePair } from "./snapshot-compare"
import { FIREWALL_MODULE, snapshotsQueryKey, type SnapshotInfo, type SnapshotList } from "./types"

function Flags({ s }: { s: SnapshotInfo }) {
  return (
    <span className="flex flex-wrap gap-1">
      {s.baseline && <Badge size="sm">baseline</Badge>}
      {s.pinned && <Badge variant="secondary" size="sm">pinned</Badge>}
      {s.system && <Badge variant="outline" size="sm">system</Badge>}
    </span>
  )
}

// RestoreConsent warns before a restore and asks whether it may add or
// remove manual rules: the restore puts UFW's files back as they were, and
// the action refuses to touch a manual rule unless the input says manual.
function RestoreConsent({ snapshot, onCancel, onPlan }: {
  snapshot: SnapshotInfo | null
  onCancel: () => void
  onPlan: (manual: boolean) => void
}) {
  const [manual, setManual] = useState(false)
  return (
    <Dialog
      open={snapshot !== null}
      onOpenChange={(open) => {
        if (open) return
        setManual(false)
        onCancel()
      }}
    >
      <DialogContent>
        <DialogHeader>
          <DialogTitle>Restore this snapshot?</DialogTitle>
          <DialogDescription>
            {`UFW's files, the loaded rules and the forwarding settings go back to how they were on ${snapshot === null ? "" : formatTime(snapshot.createdAt)}.`}
          </DialogDescription>
        </DialogHeader>
        <Alert variant="warning" role="status">
          <AlertDescription>
            Rules added by hand since then are removed, and rules deleted by hand are added back. The next step lists every manual rule the restore would add or remove.
          </AlertDescription>
        </Alert>
        <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
          <Checkbox id="restore-manual" checked={manual} onCheckedChange={(checked) => setManual(checked === true)} />
          <Label htmlFor="restore-manual">Allow the restore to add or remove manual rules</Label>
        </div>
        <DialogFooter>
          <Button variant="outline" onClick={onCancel}>
            Cancel
          </Button>
          <Button
            onClick={() => {
              onPlan(manual)
              setManual(false)
            }}
          >
            Plan the restore
          </Button>
        </DialogFooter>
      </DialogContent>
    </Dialog>
  )
}

// SnapshotsPanel lists the firewall's snapshots, newest first, and
// restores one through the change dialog.
export function SnapshotsPanel({ hostId }: { hostId: string }) {
  const snapshots = useQuery({
    queryKey: snapshotsQueryKey(hostId),
    queryFn: () => readResource<SnapshotList>(hostId, FIREWALL_MODULE, "snapshots"),
  })
  const [asking, setAsking] = useState<SnapshotInfo | null>(null)
  const [restoring, setRestoring] = useState<{ id: string; manual: boolean } | null>(null)
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<string[]>([])
  const [comparing, setComparing] = useState<ComparePair | null>(null)

  if (snapshots.isPending) return <Spinner aria-label="Loading the snapshots" />
  if (snapshots.isError) {
    return (
      <Alert variant="destructive" role="alert">
        <AlertDescription>{errorMessage(snapshots.error)}</AlertDescription>
      </Alert>
    )
  }
  const list = [...snapshots.data.snapshots].sort((a, b) => b.createdAt.localeCompare(a.createdAt))
  if (list.length === 0) return <EmptyState title="No snapshots yet" description="The firewall takes a snapshot before every change." />

  // At most two snapshots are selected; selecting a third drops the first.
  function select(id: string, on: boolean) {
    setSelected((cur) => (on ? [...cur.filter((x) => x !== id), id].slice(-2) : cur.filter((x) => x !== id)))
  }

  function compare() {
    const chosen = list.filter((s) => selected.includes(s.id)).sort((x, y) => x.createdAt.localeCompare(y.createdAt))
    const [a, b] = chosen
    if (a !== undefined) setComparing({ a, b: b ?? null })
  }

  return (
    <>
      <div className="mb-2 flex items-center gap-2">
        <Button variant="outline" size="sm" disabled={selected.length === 0} onClick={compare}>
          {selected.length === 2 ? "Compare the two" : "Compare with now"}
        </Button>
        <span className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Select one snapshot to compare with now, or two to compare with each other.</span>
      </div>
      <Table aria-label="Firewall snapshots">
        <TableHeader>
          <TableRow>
            <TableHead>
              <span className="sr-only">Select</span>
            </TableHead>
            <TableHead>Taken</TableHead>
            <TableHead>Before change</TableHead>
            <TableHead>Actor</TableHead>
            <TableHead>Kept</TableHead>
            <TableHead>
              <span className="sr-only">Actions</span>
            </TableHead>
          </TableRow>
        </TableHeader>
        <TableBody>
          {list.map((s) => (
            <TableRow key={s.id}>
              <TableCell>
                <Checkbox
                  aria-label={`Select the snapshot taken ${formatTime(s.createdAt)}`}
                  checked={selected.includes(s.id)}
                  onCheckedChange={(checked) => select(s.id, checked === true)}
                />
              </TableCell>
              <TableCell>{formatTime(s.createdAt)}</TableCell>
              <TableCell>
                {s.changeId === undefined || s.changeId === "" ? (
                  "—"
                ) : (
                  <Link to={`/changes/${encodeURIComponent(s.changeId)}`} className="font-mono underline-offset-4 hover:underline">
                    {s.changeId}
                  </Link>
                )}
              </TableCell>
              <TableCell className="font-mono">{s.actor}</TableCell>
              <TableCell>
                <Flags s={s} />
              </TableCell>
              <TableCell>
                <Button variant="outline" size="sm" aria-label={`Restore the snapshot taken ${formatTime(s.createdAt)}`} onClick={() => setAsking(s)}>
                  Restore
                </Button>
              </TableCell>
            </TableRow>
          ))}
        </TableBody>
      </Table>
      <RestoreConsent
        snapshot={asking}
        onCancel={() => setAsking(null)}
        onPlan={(manual) => {
          if (asking !== null) setRestoring({ id: asking.id, manual })
          setAsking(null)
        }}
      />
      <FirewallChange
        hostId={hostId}
        action="firewall.snapshot.restore"
        title="Restore a snapshot"
        input={restoring === null ? null : restoring.manual ? { id: restoring.id, manual: true } : { id: restoring.id }}
        onClose={() => setRestoring(null)}
      />
      <CompareDialog hostId={hostId} pair={comparing} onClose={() => setComparing(null)} />
    </>
  )
}
```

Controller ruling on row 82's remaining silent drops. `fleet.Registry.Peers` and `listen.Runtime.Addrs` silently dropped an address that does not parse as an IP address and port. Each now returns those addresses by value as a second result and logs each at Warn. Their only non-test callers are the server topology's `setPeers` and `setRuntime`, which take the two-result functions and add the values to `Topology.Dropped`. The dispatcher then marks the guard context incomplete (Task 15). `services.go` passes the method values unchanged, so it needs no edit. The tests build a pipe session (remote `pipe`), a runtime listener whose address is a Unix address, and a topology fed dropped values; the existing call sites take the new second result.

```go
// peersLog is a slog handler's output, safe for the registry's goroutines.
type peersLog struct {
	mu sync.Mutex
	b  []byte
}

func (l *peersLog) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
	l.mu.Lock()
	defer l.mu.Unlock()
	l.b = append(l.b, p...)
	return len(p), nil
}

func (l *peersLog) String() string {
	l.mu.Lock()
	defer l.mu.Unlock()
	return string(l.b)
}

// TestRegistryPeers: the TCP sessions' addresses come once each; the pipe
// session, which has no IP address, is dropped by value and logged at Warn,
// so the guard topology can mark itself incomplete.

	e := newRegistry(t, transport.HeartbeatConfig{Interval: time.Hour})
```

```go
// rtOddListener is a listener whose address is not an IP address and port,
// as a custom BindFunc may return.
type rtOddListener struct{ net.Listener }

func (rtOddListener) Addr() net.Addr { return &net.UnixAddr{Name: "@runtime", Net: "unixpacket"} }

// TestRuntimeAddrsDropsUnreadableAddresses: a bound listener whose address
// cannot be read as an IP address and port is returned in dropped, by
// value, and logged at Warn, so the guard topology can mark itself
// incomplete.
func TestRuntimeAddrsDropsUnreadableAddresses(t *testing.T) {
	f := newRtFixture(t)
	log := &logBuffer{}
	f.rt = NewRuntime(RuntimeConfig{DB: f.db, Clock: f.clock, Log: slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(log, nil)),
		Bind: func(ctx context.Context, e Endpoint) (net.Listener, error) {
			ln, err := f.binder.bind(ctx, e)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			return rtOddListener{ln}, nil
		}})
	f.start(t)
	if _, err := f.rt.Open(context.Background(), rtSpec); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	addrs, dropped := f.rt.Addrs()
	if len(addrs) != 0 || !slices.Equal(dropped, []string{"@runtime"}) {
		t.Fatalf("Addrs = %v, dropped %v; want none and [@runtime]", addrs, dropped)
	}
	if out := log.String(); !strings.Contains(out, "level=WARN") || !strings.Contains(out, "addr=@runtime") {
		t.Errorf("logs %q, want a warning naming addr=@runtime", out)
	}
}
```

```go
// asDeps is a contribution that only keeps the deps it was given.
type asDeps struct{ deps ext.Deps }

func (c *asDeps) Controller(deps ext.Deps) ([]ext.Route, []ext.Service, error) {
	c.deps = deps
	return nil, nil, nil
}

// asAdminToken creates an active user with an admin token.
func asAdminToken(t *testing.T, s *Server, clock *coretest.FakeClock) string {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	_, secret, err := s.authService.CreateUser(ctx, "proxy-admin", "correct horse battery")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	code, err := auth.TOTPCode(secret, clock.Now())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	u, err := s.authService.ActivateUser(ctx, "proxy-admin", code)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	_, token, err := s.authService.CreateToken(ctx, u.ID, "proxy", core.ScopeAdmin, 0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return token
}

// asWebCAClient is an HTTPS client that trusts the controller's web
// authority and names localhost, a name every web leaf carries.
func asWebCAClient(t *testing.T, s *Server) *http.Client {
	t.Helper()
	code, body := get(t, socketClient(s.SocketPath()), "http://controller/api/v1/controller/web-ca", "")
	var ca struct{ PEM string }
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(body), &ca); err != nil || code != http.StatusOK {
		t.Fatalf("web CA = %d %s", code, body)
	}
	pool := x509.NewCertPool()
	if !pool.AppendCertsFromPEM([]byte(ca.PEM)) {
		t.Fatal("the web CA does not parse")
	}
	return &http.Client{Timeout: 10 * time.Second, Transport: &http.Transport{
		TLSClientConfig: &tls.Config{RootCAs: pool, ServerName: "localhost", MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS12},
	}}
}

// asPost posts body to the runtime listener at addr as the proxy would,
// naming client in X-Darkpanel-Client; an empty client sends no header.
func asPost(t *testing.T, c *http.Client, addr netip.AddrPort, path, token, client string, body any) (int, []byte, error) {
	t.Helper()
	b, err := json.Marshal(body)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(context.Background(), http.MethodPost, "https://"+addr.String()+path, bytes.NewReader(b))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)
	req.Header.Set("X-Forwarded-Proto", "https")
	if client != "" {
		req.Header.Set(core.ClientHeaderNPM, client)
	}
	resp, err := c.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, nil, err
	}
	defer func() { _ = resp.Body.Close() }()
	out, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
	return resp.StatusCode, out, err
}

// TestRuntimeListenerReachesTheAPI: a runtime listener opened through the
// contributions' Listeners serves the API over the web certificate, records
// the proxied client with the proxy's address in the audit log, counts as a
// panel address in the guard topology, and stops serving once revoked.
func TestRuntimeListenerReachesTheAPI(t *testing.T) {
	opts := testOptions(t)
	clock := opts.Clock.(*coretest.FakeClock)
	c := &asDeps{}
	opts.Contributors = []ext.Controller{c}
	s := start(t, opts)
	ctx := context.Background()
	if c.deps.Listeners != core.Listeners(s.runtimeListeners) || c.deps.Listeners == nil {
		t.Fatalf("deps.Listeners = %v, want the server's runtime listeners", c.deps.Listeners)
	}
	if got := s.engineConfig(s.registry).Base.Listeners; got != core.Listeners(s.runtimeListeners) {
		t.Errorf("the controller engine's Env.Listeners = %v, want the server's runtime listeners", got)
	}

	id, err := c.deps.Listeners.Open(ctx, core.ListenerSpec{
		Addr: netip.MustParseAddrPort("127.0.0.1:9443"), AllowedPeer: netip.MustParseAddr("127.0.0.1"),
		ClientHeader: core.ClientHeaderNPM, PublicHost: "panel.example.com", ChangeID: "01ASSEMBLYCHANGE0000000000",
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Open: %v", err)
	}
	addrs, _ := s.runtimeListeners.Addrs()
	if len(addrs) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("runtime listener addresses %v, want one", addrs)
	}
	addr := addrs[0]
	if !slices.Contains(s.topo.read().PanelListen, addr) {
		t.Errorf("topology %v does not list the runtime listener %s", s.topo.read().PanelListen, addr)
	}

	hc := asWebCAClient(t, s)
	token := asAdminToken(t, s, clock)
	in := map[string]any{"input": map[string]any{"name": "via-proxy", "scope": "read", "expiresInDays": 1}}
	code, body, err := asPost(t, hc, addr, "/api/v1/actions/core.token.create/v1/plan", token, "203.0.113.9", in)
	if err != nil || code != http.StatusOK {
		t.Fatalf("plan through the runtime listener = %d %s, %v", code, body, err)
	}
	var plan struct {
		PlanID string `json:"planId"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &plan); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	code, body, err = asPost(t, hc, addr, "/api/v1/actions/core.token.create/v1/apply", token, "203.0.113.9",
		map[string]any{"planId": plan.PlanID})
	if err != nil || code != http.StatusOK {
		t.Fatalf("apply through the runtime listener = %d %s, %v", code, body, err)
	}
	var source string
	if err := s.controllerDB.Read().QueryRowContext(ctx,
		`SELECT source FROM core_audit WHERE action = 'core.token.create' AND phase = 'apply' ORDER BY seq DESC, at DESC LIMIT 1`).
		Scan(&source); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if source != "203.0.113.9 via 127.0.0.1" {
		t.Errorf("audit source %q, want the client and the proxy's address", source)
	}
	if code, body, err := asPost(t, hc, addr, "/api/v1/actions/core.token.create/v1/plan", token, "", in); err == nil && code < 400 {
		t.Errorf("a request without the client header = %d %s, want a refusal", code, body)
	}

	if err := c.deps.Listeners.Revoke(ctx, id); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Revoke: %v", err)
	}
	if slices.Contains(s.topo.read().PanelListen, addr) {
		t.Errorf("topology %v still lists the revoked listener %s", s.topo.read().PanelListen, addr)
	}
	if code, _, err := asPost(t, hc, addr, "/api/v1/actions/core.token.create/v1/plan", token, "203.0.113.9", in); err == nil && code < 400 {
		t.Errorf("a request after Revoke = %d, want a refusal or no connection", code)
	}
}
```

Replace the whole of `internal/controller/server/topology.go` with:

```go
package server

import (
	"net/netip"
	"sync"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/controller/dispatch"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/controller/listen"
)

// topology is the dispatcher's Topology. The listeners start after the
// dispatcher exists, and startup recovery may already call the dispatcher, so
// each source is registered under mu once it exists; until then it adds
// nothing and the topology reads as incomplete.
type topology struct {
	mu      sync.Mutex
	web     func() []listen.Bound
	runtime func() ([]netip.AddrPort, []string)
	agent   func() []listen.Bound
	peers   func() ([]netip.Addr, []string)
}

func (t *topology) setWeb(f func() []listen.Bound) {
	t.mu.Lock()
	defer t.mu.Unlock()
	t.web = f
}

func (t *topology) setRuntime(f func() ([]netip.AddrPort, []string)) {
	t.mu.Lock()
	defer t.mu.Unlock()
	t.runtime = f
}

func (t *topology) setAgent(f func() []listen.Bound) {
	t.mu.Lock()
	defer t.mu.Unlock()
	t.agent = f
}

func (t *topology) setPeers(f func() ([]netip.Addr, []string)) {
	t.mu.Lock()
	defer t.mu.Unlock()
	t.peers = f
}

// setNoAgents registers empty agent listeners and peers, for a controller
// whose agent runs embedded: it serves no agent listener and has no agent
// sessions, so their lists are complete when empty.
func (t *topology) setNoAgents() {
	t.mu.Lock()
	defer t.mu.Unlock()
	t.agent = func() []listen.Bound { return nil }
	t.peers = func() ([]netip.Addr, []string) { return nil, nil }
}

// read is the topology now. It is complete once all four sources have
// registered; what the runtime listeners and the session registry could not
// read is dropped from it after what the bound listeners drop.
func (t *topology) read() dispatch.Topology {
	t.mu.Lock()
	web, runtime, agent, peers := t.web, t.runtime, t.agent, t.peers
	t.mu.Unlock()
	var webBound, agentBound []listen.Bound
	var runtimeAddrs []netip.AddrPort
	var agentPeers []netip.Addr
	var runtimeDropped, peersDropped []string
	if web != nil {
		webBound = web()
	}
	if runtime != nil {
		runtimeAddrs, runtimeDropped = runtime()
	}
	if agent != nil {
		agentBound = agent()
	}
	if peers != nil {
		agentPeers, peersDropped = peers()
	}
	out := topologyOf(webBound, runtimeAddrs, agentBound, agentPeers)
	out.Dropped = append(append(out.Dropped, runtimeDropped...), peersDropped...)
	out.Complete = web != nil && runtime != nil && agent != nil && peers != nil
	return out
}

// topologyOf is the topology of the bound web listeners, the runtime
// listeners, the bound agent listeners and the live agents' addresses. The
// panel is reached through the web and the runtime listeners alike (spec
// 1.5). A listener without an IP address, such as a Unix socket, is left
// out; any other address that cannot be read is listed in Dropped.
func topologyOf(web []listen.Bound, runtime []netip.AddrPort, agent []listen.Bound, peers []netip.Addr) dispatch.Topology {
	panel, dropped := boundAddrs(web)
	for _, ap := range runtime {
		panel = append(panel, netip.AddrPortFrom(ap.Addr().Unmap(), ap.Port()))
	}
	agentAddrs, agentDropped := boundAddrs(agent)
	return dispatch.Topology{PanelListen: panel, AgentListen: agentAddrs, AgentPeers: peers,
		Dropped: append(dropped, agentDropped...)}
}

// boundAddrs returns the IP addresses of bound and, as dropped, every
// address that is not one. A Unix socket is neither: no firewall rule can
// cut it, so it is left out without being dropped.
func boundAddrs(bound []listen.Bound) (out []netip.AddrPort, dropped []string) {
	for _, b := range bound {
		if b.Addr.Network() == "unix" {
			continue
		}
		ap, err := netip.ParseAddrPort(b.Addr.String())
		if err != nil {
			dropped = append(dropped, b.Addr.String())
			continue
		}
		out = append(out, netip.AddrPortFrom(ap.Addr().Unmap(), ap.Port()))
	}
	return out, dropped
}
```

**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 2 - risk 3 = 6
**Lenses:** security

Reads UFW's configured state from the files under a root directory (production `/`, tests a `t.TempDir()` tree) and lists every reason the configuration cannot be predicted (spec 2.1): executable init scripts, `MANAGE_BUILTINS=yes`, sysctl keys that change forwarding or filtering, and values UFW's Python and shell halves would read differently. A missed reason would let the guard trust a prediction that is wrong, which is why this is lockout-safety code. The tests build a stock tree, then edit it once per reason and per error; the fuzz target feeds arbitrary `ufw.conf`, `/etc/default/ufw` and sysctl contents.

```go
package conf

import (

	"path/filepath"
	"reflect"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/model"
)

const (
	confTestUFWConf = "# /etc/ufw/ufw.conf\n#\n\n# Set to yes to start on boot.\nENABLED=yes\n\n# Please use the 'ufw' command to set the loglevel.\nLOGLEVEL=low\n"
	confTestDefault = "# /etc/default/ufw\n#\n\nIPV6=yes\n\nDEFAULT_INPUT_POLICY=\"DROP\"\nDEFAULT_OUTPUT_POLICY=\"ACCEPT\"\n" +
		"DEFAULT_FORWARD_POLICY=\"DROP\"\nDEFAULT_APPLICATION_POLICY=\"SKIP\"\nMANAGE_BUILTINS=no\n\n" +
		"# Location of the sysctl file\nIPT_SYSCTL=/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf\n\nIPT_MODULES=\"\"\n"
	confTestSysctl = "#\n# Configuration file for setting network variables.\n#\n\n" +
		"net/ipv4/conf/all/accept_redirects=0\n#net/ipv4/ip_forward=1\n  net.ipv4.ip_forward = 1 \n" +
		"; a comment\n-net/ipv6/conf/default/forwarding=1\nnet.ipv4.conf.eth0/100.rp_filter=2\nnot a setting\n"
	confTestUser = "*filter\n:ufw-user-input - [0:0]\n### RULES ###\n\n" +
		"### tuple ### allow tcp 22 0.0.0.0/0 any 0.0.0.0/0 in comment=6461726b70616e656c3a30314a303030303030303030303030303030303030303030303020737368\n" +
		"-A ufw-user-input -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT\n\n" +
		"### tuple ### deny any any 0.0.0.0/0 any 10.0.0.0/8 in\n-A ufw-user-input -s 10.0.0.0/8 -j DROP\n\n### END RULES ###\nCOMMIT\n"
	confTestUser6 = "*filter\n:ufw6-user-input - [0:0]\n### RULES ###\n\n" +
		"### tuple ### allow tcp 22 ::/0 any ::/0 in comment=6461726b70616e656c3a30314a303030303030303030303030303030303030303030303020737368\n" +
		"-A ufw6-user-input -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT\n\n### END RULES ###\nCOMMIT\n"

// confTestFiles is a stock tree: every state file, the sysctl file and
// non-executable init scripts, keyed by path relative to the root.
func confTestFiles() map[string]string {
	return map[string]string{
		"etc/ufw/ufw.conf": confTestUFWConf, "etc/default/ufw": confTestDefault, "etc/ufw/sysctl.conf": confTestSysctl,
		"etc/ufw/user.rules": confTestUser, "etc/ufw/user6.rules": confTestUser6,
		"etc/ufw/before.rules": "*filter\nCOMMIT\n", "etc/ufw/before6.rules": "*filter\nCOMMIT\n",
		"etc/ufw/after.rules": "*filter\nCOMMIT\n", "etc/ufw/after6.rules": "*filter\nCOMMIT\n",
		"etc/ufw/before.init": "#!/bin/sh\n", "etc/ufw/after.init": "#!/bin/sh\n",
	}
}

// confTestTree writes files under a new temporary root; a "" content
// leaves the file out.
func confTestTree(t *testing.T, files map[string]string) string {
	t.Helper()
	root := t.TempDir()
	for rel, content := range files {
		if content == "" {
			continue
		}
		p := filepath.Join(root, rel)
		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(p), 0o750); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if err := os.WriteFile(p, []byte(content), 0o600); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	return root
}

func TestRead(t *testing.T) {
	root := confTestTree(t, confTestFiles())
	c, err := Read(root)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !c.Enabled || c.LogLevel != "low" || !c.IPv6 || c.ManageBuiltins || c.DefaultInput != "DROP" ||
		c.DefaultOutput != "ACCEPT" || c.DefaultForward != "DROP" || c.SysctlFile != "/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf" {
		t.Errorf("settings = %+v", c)
	}
	if len(c.Unsupported) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("Unsupported = %q, want none", c.Unsupported)
	}
	wantSysctl := []fwstate.SysctlSetting{{Key: "net/ipv4/conf/all/accept_redirects", Value: "0"},
		{Key: "net/ipv4/ip_forward", Value: "1"}, {Key: "net/ipv6/conf/default/forwarding", Value: "1"},
		{Key: "net/ipv4/conf/eth0.100/rp_filter", Value: "2"}}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(c.Sysctl, wantSysctl) {
		t.Errorf("Sysctl = %q, want %q", c.Sysctl, wantSysctl)
	}
	if len(c.Rules4) != 2 || len(c.Rules6) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("rules = %d v4, %d v6; want 2, 1", len(c.Rules4), len(c.Rules6))
	}
	if c.Rules4[1].Src != "10.0.0.0/8" || c.Rules4[1].Action != model.ActionDeny || c.Rules6[0].Family != model.FamilyV6 {
		t.Errorf("rules = %+v %+v", c.Rules4, c.Rules6)
	}
	if rules := model.Merge(c.Rules4, c.Rules6); len(rules) != 2 || rules[0].Family != model.FamilyBoth {
		t.Errorf("merged rules = %+v", rules)
	}
	wantPaths := append(slices.Clone(fwstate.StateFiles), "/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf")
	gotPaths := make([]string, 0, len(c.Files))
	for p, e := range c.Files {
		gotPaths = append(gotPaths, p)
		if e.Path != p || !e.Present || e.Mode != 0o600 || e.UID != os.Getuid() || e.GID != os.Getgid() {
			t.Errorf("Files[%s] = %+v", p, e)
		}
	}
	slices.Sort(gotPaths)
	slices.Sort(wantPaths)
	if !slices.Equal(gotPaths, wantPaths) {
		t.Errorf("Files paths = %q, want %q", gotPaths, wantPaths)
	}
	if string(c.Files["/etc/default/ufw"].Data) != confTestDefault {
		t.Error("Files[/etc/default/ufw] does not hold the file's bytes")
	}
}

func TestReadUnsupported(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name string
		edit func(t *testing.T, root string, files map[string]string)
		want string
	}{
		{"before.init executable", func(t *testing.T, root string, _ map[string]string) {
			confTestChmod(t, filepath.Join(root, "etc/ufw/before.init"), 0o750)
		}, "before.init"},
		{"after.init executable", func(t *testing.T, root string, _ map[string]string) {
			confTestChmod(t, filepath.Join(root, "etc/ufw/after.init"), 0o700)
		}, "after.init"},
		{"manage builtins", confTestSet("etc/default/ufw", "MANAGE_BUILTINS=no", "MANAGE_BUILTINS=yes"), "MANAGE_BUILTINS"},
		{"ipv4 conf forwarding", confTestSet("etc/ufw/sysctl.conf", "#net/ipv4/ip_forward=1", "net.ipv4.conf.all.forwarding=1"), "net/ipv4/conf/all/forwarding"},
		{"route_localnet", confTestSet("etc/ufw/sysctl.conf", "#net/ipv4/ip_forward=1", "net/ipv4/conf/eth0/route_localnet=1"), "route_localnet"},
		{"bridge netfilter", confTestSet("etc/ufw/sysctl.conf", "#net/ipv4/ip_forward=1", "net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables = 1"), "bridge-nf-call-iptables"},
		{"glob key", confTestSet("etc/ufw/sysctl.conf", "#net/ipv4/ip_forward=1", "net.ipv4.conf.*.rp_filter=1"), "glob"},
		{"enabled neither yes nor no", confTestSet("etc/ufw/ufw.conf", "ENABLED=yes", "ENABLED=Yes"), "ENABLED"},
		{"ipv6 neither yes nor no", confTestSet("etc/default/ufw", "IPV6=yes", "IPV6=true"), "IPV6"},
		{"bad loglevel", confTestSet("etc/ufw/ufw.conf", "LOGLEVEL=low", "LOGLEVEL=loud"), "LOGLEVEL"},
		{"missing loglevel", confTestSet("etc/ufw/ufw.conf", "LOGLEVEL=low", ""), "LOGLEVEL"},
		{"lower-case policy", confTestSet("etc/default/ufw", `DEFAULT_INPUT_POLICY="DROP"`, "DEFAULT_INPUT_POLICY=drop"), "DEFAULT_INPUT_POLICY"},
		{"missing policy", confTestSet("etc/default/ufw", `DEFAULT_FORWARD_POLICY="DROP"`, ""), "DEFAULT_FORWARD_POLICY"},
		{"relative sysctl file", confTestSet("etc/default/ufw", "IPT_SYSCTL=/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf", "IPT_SYSCTL=sysctl.conf"), `IPT_SYSCTL names "sysctl.conf"`},
		{"malformed tuple", confTestSet("etc/ufw/user.rules", "### tuple ### deny any any 0.0.0.0/0 any 10.0.0.0/8 in",
			"### tuple ### drop any any 0.0.0.0/0 any 10.0.0.0/8 in"), "user.rules line 8"},
		{"missing user.rules", func(t *testing.T, root string, _ map[string]string) {
			confTestRemove(t, filepath.Join(root, "etc/ufw/user.rules"))
		}, "/etc/ufw/user.rules is missing"},
		{"missing after6.rules", func(t *testing.T, root string, _ map[string]string) {
			confTestRemove(t, filepath.Join(root, "etc/ufw/after6.rules"))
		}, "/etc/ufw/after6.rules is missing"},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			files := confTestFiles()
			root := confTestTree(t, files)
			c.edit(t, root, files)
			got, err := Read(root)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if len(got.Unsupported) != 1 || !strings.Contains(got.Unsupported[0], c.want) {
				t.Fatalf("Unsupported = %q, want one reason naming %q", got.Unsupported, c.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

// confTestSet returns an edit that replaces old with replacement in one
// file of the tree.
func confTestSet(rel, old, replacement string) func(t *testing.T, root string, files map[string]string) {
	return func(t *testing.T, root string, files map[string]string) {
		t.Helper()
		if !strings.Contains(files[rel], old) {
			t.Fatalf("%s does not contain %q", rel, old)
		}
		data := strings.Replace(files[rel], old, replacement, 1)
		if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(root, rel), []byte(data), 0o600); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
}

func confTestChmod(t *testing.T, path string, mode os.FileMode) {
	t.Helper()
	if err := os.Chmod(path, mode); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}

func confTestRemove(t *testing.T, path string) {
	t.Helper()
	if err := os.Remove(path); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}

// TestReadOtherSysctlFile checks that a sysctl file other than UFW's default
// is unsupported and never read, while Files still records the default one.
func TestReadOtherSysctlFile(t *testing.T) {
	files := confTestFiles()
	files["etc/default/ufw"] = strings.Replace(confTestDefault, "IPT_SYSCTL=/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf", "IPT_SYSCTL=/etc/sysctl.d/99-ufw.conf", 1)
	files["etc/sysctl.d/99-ufw.conf"] = "net.ipv4.conf.all.forwarding=1\n"
	c, err := Read(confTestTree(t, files))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(c.Unsupported) != 1 || !strings.Contains(c.Unsupported[0], `IPT_SYSCTL names "/etc/sysctl.d/99-ufw.conf"`) {
		t.Errorf("Unsupported = %q, want one reason naming the path", c.Unsupported)
	}
	if c.SysctlFile != "/etc/sysctl.d/99-ufw.conf" || len(c.Sysctl) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("SysctlFile = %q, Sysctl = %q; want the named path and no settings", c.SysctlFile, c.Sysctl)
	}
	if _, ok := c.Files["/etc/sysctl.d/99-ufw.conf"]; ok {
		t.Error("Files records the unsupported sysctl file")
	}
	if e := c.Files["/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf"]; !e.Present || string(e.Data) != confTestSysctl {
		t.Errorf("Files[/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf] = %+v, want the default file", e)
	}

	files["etc/default/ufw"] = strings.Replace(confTestDefault, "IPT_SYSCTL=/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf", "IPT_SYSCTL=/etc/ufw/./sysctl.conf", 1)
	c, err = Read(confTestTree(t, files))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(c.Unsupported) != 0 || c.SysctlFile != "/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf" || len(c.Sysctl) != 4 {
		t.Errorf("default file through a dot path: Unsupported %q, SysctlFile %q, %d settings", c.Unsupported, c.SysctlFile, len(c.Sysctl))
	}
}

func TestReadErrors(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name string
		edit func(t *testing.T, root string)
	}{
		{"missing ufw.conf", func(t *testing.T, root string) { confTestRemove(t, filepath.Join(root, "etc/ufw/ufw.conf")) }},
		{"missing default", func(t *testing.T, root string) { confTestRemove(t, filepath.Join(root, "etc/default/ufw")) }},
		{"oversize", func(t *testing.T, root string) {

			}

			big := make([]byte, fwstate.MaxFileSize+1)
			if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(root, "etc/ufw/sysctl.conf"), big, 0o600); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
		}},

func TestSysctlKeys(t *testing.T) {
	keys := map[string]string{

}
```

```go
// Package conf reads UFW's configured state (spec 2.1) from its files:
// ufw.conf, /etc/default/ufw, the rule tuples of user.rules and
// user6.rules, the framework files and the sysctl file IPT_SYSCTL names. It
// also says which parts of a configuration Darkpanel cannot predict.
package conf

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"io/fs"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"regexp"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"syscall"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/model"
)

// The files Read parses itself, besides the rule files.
const (
	ufwConf     = "/etc/ufw/ufw.conf"
	defaultsUFW = "/etc/default/ufw"
	userRules   = "/etc/ufw/user.rules"
	userRules6  = "/etc/ufw/user6.rules"
)

// LogLevels are the values of ufw.conf's LOGLEVEL, lowest first.
var LogLevels = []string{"off", "low", "medium", "high", "full"}

var policies = []string{"ACCEPT", "DROP", "REJECT"}

// Read reads the configured state from the files under root: production
// passes "/", tests a temporary tree. Every state file and, when
// IPT_SYSCTL is set, /etc/ufw/sysctl.conf is recorded in Files, absent ones
// with Present false; IPT_SYSCTL naming any other file is unsupported. A state file that
// is not a regular file or exceeds fwstate.MaxFileSize, and a missing
// ufw.conf or /etc/default/ufw, are errors; anything Darkpanel cannot
// predict is a reason in Unsupported.
func Read(root string) (fwstate.Config, error) {
	c := fwstate.Config{Files: map[string]core.RestoreEntry{}}
	for _, p := range fwstate.StateFiles {
		e, err := readEntry(root, p)
		if err != nil {
			return fwstate.Config{}, err
		}
		c.Files[p] = e
	}
	for _, p := range []string{ufwConf, defaultsUFW} {
		if !c.Files[p].Present {
			return fwstate.Config{}, fmt.Errorf("conf: %s is missing", p)
		}
	}
	r := reader{c: &c}
	cv, dv := parseShell(c.Files[ufwConf].Data), parseShell(c.Files[defaultsUFW].Data)
	c.Enabled = r.yesNo(ufwConf, cv, "ENABLED")
	c.LogLevel = strings.ToLower(cv["LOGLEVEL"])
	if !slices.Contains(LogLevels, c.LogLevel) {
		r.unsupported("%s: LOGLEVEL is missing or not one of %s", ufwConf, strings.Join(LogLevels, ", "))
	}
	c.IPv6 = r.yesNo(defaultsUFW, dv, "IPV6")
	c.ManageBuiltins = r.yesNo(defaultsUFW, dv, "MANAGE_BUILTINS")
	if c.ManageBuiltins {
		r.unsupported("%s: MANAGE_BUILTINS=yes makes UFW flush the built-in chains, which Darkpanel cannot predict", defaultsUFW)
	}
	c.DefaultInput = r.policy(dv, "DEFAULT_INPUT_POLICY")
	c.DefaultOutput = r.policy(dv, "DEFAULT_OUTPUT_POLICY")
	c.DefaultForward = r.policy(dv, "DEFAULT_FORWARD_POLICY")

	required := []string{userRules, "/etc/ufw/before.rules", "/etc/ufw/after.rules"}
	if c.IPv6 {
		required = append(required, userRules6, "/etc/ufw/before6.rules", "/etc/ufw/after6.rules")
	}
	for _, p := range required {
		if !c.Files[p].Present {
			r.unsupported("%s is missing", p)
		}
	}
	c.Rules4 = r.tuples(userRules, false)
	c.Rules6 = r.tuples(userRules6, true)
	for _, name := range []string{"before.init", "after.init"} {
		if fi, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(root, "etc/ufw", name)); err == nil && fi.Mode().IsRegular() && fi.Mode()&0o111 != 0 {
			r.unsupported("/etc/ufw/%s is executable: UFW runs it at start, which Darkpanel cannot predict", name)
		}
	}
	if err := r.sysctl(root, dv["IPT_SYSCTL"]); err != nil {
		return fwstate.Config{}, err
	}
	return c, nil
}

// reader collects the unsupported reasons while Read fills the config.
type reader struct{ c *fwstate.Config }

func (r reader) unsupported(format string, args ...any) {
	r.c.Unsupported = append(r.c.Unsupported, fmt.Sprintf(format, args...))
}

// yesNo reads a yes/no key. UFW's Python code lower-cases the value and its
// init script accepts only yes and YES, so any other spelling would make
// the two disagree.
func (r reader) yesNo(file string, vars map[string]string, key string) bool {
	v, ok := vars[key]
	switch {
	case !ok:
		return false
	case v == "yes" || v == "YES":
		return true
	case v == "no" || v == "NO":
		return false
	}
	r.unsupported("%s: %s=%q is neither yes nor no", file, key, v)
	return false
}

// policy reads a default policy. The init script passes the value to
// iptables-restore as written, which accepts only upper case.
func (r reader) policy(vars map[string]string, key string) string {
	v := vars[key]
	if !slices.Contains(policies, v) {
		r.unsupported("%s: %s is missing or not ACCEPT, DROP or REJECT", defaultsUFW, key)
	}
	return v
}

// tuples parses the tuple lines of one rule file; a line UFW would skip or
// reinterpret is a reason, not an error.
func (r reader) tuples(path string, v6 bool) []model.Tuple {
	var out []model.Tuple
	for i, line := range strings.Split(string(r.c.Files[path].Data), "\n") {
		if !strings.HasPrefix(line, model.TuplePrefix) {
			continue
		}
		t, err := model.ParseTuple(line, v6)
		if err != nil {
			r.unsupported("%s line %d: %v", path, i+1, err)
			continue
		}
		out = append(out, t)
	}
	return out
}

// sysctlFile is the only sysctl file Darkpanel supports: snapshots restore
// it through an owned path the manifest declares, which cannot name a path
// read from the host.
const sysctlFile = "/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf"

// sysctl records the file IPT_SYSCTL names and its settings. Any other file
// than sysctlFile is unsupported and not read; Files then records
// sysctlFile, so a snapshot still holds UFW's default file.
func (r reader) sysctl(root, name string) error {
	if name == "" {
		return nil
	}
	r.c.SysctlFile = name
	supported := filepath.IsAbs(name) && filepath.Clean(name) == sysctlFile
	if !supported {
		r.unsupported("%s: IPT_SYSCTL names %q; only %s is supported", defaultsUFW, name, sysctlFile)
	}
	e, err := readEntry(root, sysctlFile)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	r.c.Files[sysctlFile] = e
	if !supported {
		return nil
	}
	r.c.SysctlFile = sysctlFile
	name = sysctlFile
	for _, s := range parseSysctl(e.Data) {
		r.c.Sysctl = append(r.c.Sysctl, s)
		switch {
		case strings.ContainsAny(s.Key, "*?["):
			r.unsupported("%s sets %s with a glob, which Darkpanel cannot predict", name, s.Key)
		case FilteringSysctl(s.Key):
			r.unsupported("%s sets %s, which changes forwarding or filtering in a way Darkpanel cannot predict", name, s.Key)
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// readEntry reads one file under root as a restore entry for its absolute
// path. Symbolic links are not followed.
func readEntry(root, path string) (core.RestoreEntry, error) {
	e := core.RestoreEntry{Path: path}
	f, err := os.OpenFile(filepath.Join(root, path), os.O_RDONLY|syscall.O_NOFOLLOW|syscall.O_NONBLOCK, 0) //nolint:gosec // G304: a UFW state file or the sysctl file UFW names, read-only
	if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
		return e, nil
	}
	if err != nil {
		return e, fmt.Errorf("conf: open %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
	fi, err := f.Stat()
	if err != nil {
		return e, fmt.Errorf("conf: stat %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	if !fi.Mode().IsRegular() {
		return e, fmt.Errorf("conf: %s is not a regular file", path)
	}
	data, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(f, fwstate.MaxFileSize+1))
	if err != nil {
		return e, fmt.Errorf("conf: read %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	if len(data) > fwstate.MaxFileSize {
		return e, fmt.Errorf("conf: %s is larger than %d bytes", path, fwstate.MaxFileSize)
	}
	e.Present, e.Mode, e.Data = true, fi.Mode().Perm(), data
	if st, ok := fi.Sys().(*syscall.Stat_t); ok {
		e.UID, e.GID = int(st.Uid), int(st.Gid)
	}
	return e, nil
}

var shellNameRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`)

// parseShell reads KEY=value lines as the init script's shell would for
// the forms UFW's files use: an optional pair of quotes, an unquoted value
// ending at white space, comments, the last assignment winning.
func parseShell(data []byte) map[string]string {
	vars := map[string]string{}
	for _, line := range strings.Split(string(data), "\n") {
		line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
		key, val, ok := strings.Cut(line, "=")
		if !ok || !shellNameRe.MatchString(key) {
			continue
		}
		if val != "" && (val[0] == '"' || val[0] == '\'') {
			if end := strings.IndexByte(val[1:], val[0]); end >= 0 {
				val = val[1 : 1+end]
			} else {
				val = val[1:]
			}
		} else if i := strings.IndexAny(val, " \t"); i >= 0 {
			val = val[:i]
		}
		vars[key] = val
	}
	return vars
}

// parseSysctl reads a sysctl file as "sysctl -p" does: comments start with
// # or ;, a leading - only suppresses errors, and a line without "=" is
// skipped.
func parseSysctl(data []byte) []fwstate.SysctlSetting {
	var out []fwstate.SysctlSetting
	for _, line := range strings.Split(string(data), "\n") {
		line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
		if line == "" || line[0] == '#' || line[0] == ';' {
			continue
		}
		key, val, ok := strings.Cut(strings.TrimPrefix(line, "-"), "=")
		key = strings.TrimSpace(key)
		if !ok || key == "" {
			continue
		}
		out = append(out, fwstate.SysctlSetting{Key: SysctlKey(key), Value: strings.TrimSpace(val)})
	}
	return out
}

// SysctlKey converts a sysctl name to its /proc/sys form as procps does:
// when the first separator is a dot, dots and slashes swap, so
// "net.ipv4.conf.eth0/100.rp_filter" names "net/ipv4/conf/eth0.100/rp_filter";
// a name that starts with a slash-separated component is already in that
// form.
func SysctlKey(name string) string {
	i := strings.IndexAny(name, "./")
	if i < 0 || name[i] == '/' {
		return name
	}
	b := []byte(name)
	for j := i; j < len(b); j++ {
		switch b[j] {
		case '.':
			b[j] = '/'
		case '/':
			b[j] = '.'
		}
	}
	return string(b)
}

var (
	supportedSysctlRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^(net/ipv4/ip_forward|net/ipv6/conf/[^/]+/(forwarding|accept_ra)|net/ipv4/conf/[^/]+/(rp_filter|accept_source_route))$`)
	filteringSysctlRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^(net/ipv4/conf/[^/]+/forwarding|.*/route_localnet|net/bridge/bridge-nf-call-.*)$`)
)

// SupportedSysctl reports whether key (in /proc/sys form) is one of the
// sysctl keys the firewall predicts, snapshots and restores (spec 2.1):
// net/ipv4/ip_forward and, for all, default or an interface,
// net/ipv6/conf/*/forwarding and accept_ra and net/ipv4/conf/*/rp_filter
// and accept_source_route.
func SupportedSysctl(key string) bool { return supportedSysctlRe.MatchString(key) }

// FilteringSysctl reports whether key (in /proc/sys form) changes
// forwarding or filtering outside the supported set, which makes a sysctl
// file that sets it unsupported: net/ipv4/conf/*/forwarding,
// */route_localnet and net/bridge/bridge-nf-call-*.
func FilteringSysctl(key string) bool { return filteringSysctlRe.MatchString(key) }
```

### Task 30: Chain walker and packet header matches

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/modules/firewall/eval/eval.go`
- Test: `internal/modules/firewall/eval/eval_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `netfilter.Ruleset`, `netfilter.Parse` (merged), `fwstate.Packet`, `fwstate.Result`, `fwstate.Router` (merged)
- Produces: `Evaluate` and the walker internals of Part contracts Task 30; the shared test helpers `evalRuleset`, `evalPacket`, `evalCheck`

**Depends on:** Task 18, Task 24

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-opus-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 2 - risk 3 = 6
**Lenses:** security

The evaluator's core: it validates the packet, walks the filter table's built-in chain for the packet's path with jumps, `RETURN`, `ACCEPT`, `DROP`, `REJECT`, `LOG`/`TCPMSS` (continue) and the chain policy, and evaluates the header options `-i`, `-o` (with `+` and `!`), `-s`, `-d` (with `!`) and `-p` (names and numbers). A rule the parser marked opaque is `unknown` once its header matches; a rule whose `-m` match cannot be decided is `unknown` only when its target can change the verdict. Every `-m` module except `comment` is undecidable in this task (Task 35 models them), and only the filter table is walked (Task 41 replaces `run`). The test proves the walk order, the trace, policies, the jump-depth bound, incompatible tables and packet validation; its expectations stay true after the later tasks.

```go
package eval

import (
	"net/netip"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netfilter"
)

// evalRuleset parses save output for the tests of this package.
func evalRuleset(t *testing.T, text string) *netfilter.Ruleset {
	t.Helper()
	rs, err := netfilter.Parse(strings.NewReader(text))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("parse: %v", err)
	}
	return rs
}

// evalPacket is the first packet of a new TCP connection from
// 203.0.113.7:40000 to this host's 192.0.2.1:22, arriving on eth0.
func evalPacket() fwstate.Packet {
	return fwstate.Packet{
		Family:  fwstate.V4,
		Path:    "input",
		InIface: "eth0",
		Src:     netip.MustParseAddr("203.0.113.7"),
		Dst:     netip.MustParseAddr("192.0.2.1"),
		SrcPort: 40000,
		DstPort: 22,
		Proto:   "tcp",
		CtState: "NEW",
	}
}

// evalCheck compares a result with the wanted verdict and trace, and checks
// that the reason contains the wanted fragment ("" checks nothing). A nil
// trace is not compared.
func evalCheck(t *testing.T, got fwstate.Result, verdict fwstate.Verdict, trace []string, reason string) {
	t.Helper()
	if got.Verdict != verdict {
		t.Errorf("verdict = %q (reason %q, trace %q), want %q", got.Verdict, got.Reason, got.Trace, verdict)
	}
	if trace != nil && !slices.Equal(got.Trace, trace) {
		t.Errorf("trace = %q, want %q", got.Trace, trace)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(got.Reason, reason) {
		t.Errorf("reason = %q, want it to contain %q", got.Reason, reason)
	}
}

const walkFilter = `*filter
:INPUT DROP [0:0]
:FORWARD DROP [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
:walk-user - [0:0]
:walk-return - [0:0]
:walk-loop - [0:0]
-A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -j walk-return
-A INPUT -p tcp -m comment --comment "the user chain" -j walk-user
-A INPUT -p udp -j REJECT --reject-with icmp-port-unreachable
-A INPUT -p esp -m limit --limit 3/min -j LOG --log-prefix "[ESP] "
-A INPUT -p esp -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p gre -m limit --limit 3/min -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p ah -m hashlimit --hashlimit-upto 1/sec -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p 132 -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p icmp -j walk-loop
-A FORWARD -i eth+ ! -o eth0 -j ACCEPT
-A FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/8 ! -d 10.1.0.0/16 -j ACCEPT
-A OUTPUT -i eth0 -j DROP
-A OUTPUT -o lo -j ACCEPT
-A OUTPUT -d 198.51.100.0/24 -j RETURN
-A OUTPUT -p tcp -j DROP
-A walk-return -s 203.0.113.0/24 -j RETURN
-A walk-return -s 198.51.100.0/24 -j DROP
-A walk-user -p tcp -m limit --limit 1/sec -j LOG --log-prefix "[SSH] "
-A walk-user ! -s 203.0.113.0/24 -p tcp -j ACCEPT
-A walk-loop -j walk-loop
COMMIT
`

func TestEvaluateWalk(t *testing.T) {
	rs := evalRuleset(t, walkFilter)
	tests := []struct {
		name    string
		edit    func(p *fwstate.Packet)
		verdict fwstate.Verdict
		trace   []string
		reason  string
	}{
		{
			name:    "loopback accepted by the first rule",
			edit:    func(p *fwstate.Packet) { p.InIface = "lo" },
			verdict: fwstate.Accept,
			trace:   []string{"filter/INPUT#1"},
		},
		{
			name: "a user chain returns and the built-in policy drops",
			edit: func(*fwstate.Packet) {},
			// walk-return returns for 203.0.113.0/24; walk-user's rate-limited
			// LOG rule may or may not match, which cannot change the verdict,
			// and its ACCEPT excludes the source.
			verdict: fwstate.Drop,
			trace:   []string{"filter/INPUT#2", "filter/walk-return#1", "filter/INPUT#3"},
			reason:  "filter/INPUT policy DROP",
		},
		{
			name:    "a user chain accepts",
			edit:    func(p *fwstate.Packet) { p.Src = netip.MustParseAddr("192.0.2.77") },
			verdict: fwstate.Accept,
			trace:   []string{"filter/INPUT#2", "filter/INPUT#3", "filter/walk-user#2"},
		},
		{
			name:    "a user chain drops",
			edit:    func(p *fwstate.Packet) { p.Src = netip.MustParseAddr("198.51.100.9") },
			verdict: fwstate.Drop,
			trace:   []string{"filter/INPUT#2", "filter/walk-return#2"},
			reason:  "filter/walk-return#2 drops",
		},
		{
			name:    "reject",
			edit:    func(p *fwstate.Packet) { p.Proto = "udp" },
			verdict: fwstate.Reject,
			trace:   []string{"filter/INPUT#2", "filter/walk-return#1", "filter/INPUT#4"},
			reason:  "filter/INPUT#4 rejects",
		},
		{
			name: "a rate-limited LOG continues and the next rule accepts",
			edit: func(p *fwstate.Packet) { p.Proto = "esp" },
			// The LOG rule's limit makes its match uncertain, so it is not
			// traced, but LOG never decides.
			verdict: fwstate.Accept,
			trace:   []string{"filter/INPUT#2", "filter/walk-return#1", "filter/INPUT#6"},
		},
		{
			name:    "a rate-limited ACCEPT is unknown",
			edit:    func(p *fwstate.Packet) { p.Proto = "gre" },
			verdict: fwstate.Unknown,
			reason:  "filter/INPUT#7: ",
		},
		{
			name:    "an opaque rule whose header matches is unknown",
			edit:    func(p *fwstate.Packet) { p.Proto = "ah" },
			verdict: fwstate.Unknown,
			reason:  "filter/INPUT#8: match hashlimit",
		},
		{
			name:    "a protocol number matches its name",
			edit:    func(p *fwstate.Packet) { p.Proto = "SCTP" },
			verdict: fwstate.Accept,
			trace:   []string{"filter/INPUT#2", "filter/walk-return#1", "filter/INPUT#9"},
		},
		{
			name:    "a jump loop is unknown",
			edit:    func(p *fwstate.Packet) { p.Proto = "icmp" },
			verdict: fwstate.Unknown,
			reason:  "jumps nest deeper than 64",
		},
		{
			name: "forward: wildcard in-interface and negated out-interface",
			edit: func(p *fwstate.Packet) {
				p.Path, p.InIface, p.OutIface = "forward", "eth1", "eth2"
			},
			verdict: fwstate.Accept,
			trace:   []string{"filter/FORWARD#1"},
		},
		{
			name: "forward: negated destination",
			edit: func(p *fwstate.Packet) {
				p.Path, p.InIface, p.OutIface = "forward", "wg0", "eth0"
				p.Src, p.Dst = netip.MustParseAddr("10.2.3.4"), netip.MustParseAddr("10.2.0.1")
			},
			verdict: fwstate.Accept,
			trace:   []string{"filter/FORWARD#2"},
		},
		{
			name: "forward: nothing matches and the policy drops",
			edit: func(p *fwstate.Packet) {
				p.Path, p.InIface, p.OutIface = "forward", "wg0", "eth0"
				p.Src, p.Dst = netip.MustParseAddr("10.2.3.4"), netip.MustParseAddr("10.1.0.1")
			},
			verdict: fwstate.Drop,
			trace:   []string{},
			reason:  "filter/FORWARD policy DROP",
		},
		{
			name: "output: no in-interface, RETURN in a built-in chain applies the policy",
			edit: func(p *fwstate.Packet) {
				p.Path, p.InIface, p.OutIface = "output", "", "eth0"
				p.Src, p.Dst = netip.MustParseAddr("192.0.2.1"), netip.MustParseAddr("198.51.100.4")
			},
			verdict: fwstate.Accept,
			trace:   []string{"filter/OUTPUT#3"},
		},
		{
			name: "output: drop",
			edit: func(p *fwstate.Packet) {
				p.Path, p.InIface, p.OutIface = "output", "", "eth0"
				p.Src, p.Dst = netip.MustParseAddr("192.0.2.1"), netip.MustParseAddr("192.0.2.200")
			},
			verdict: fwstate.Drop,
			trace:   []string{"filter/OUTPUT#4"},
		},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			p := evalPacket()
			tt.edit(&p)
			evalCheck(t, Evaluate(rs, p, nil), tt.verdict, tt.trace, tt.reason)
		})
	}
}

func TestEvaluateTables(t *testing.T) {
	p := evalPacket()
	t.Run("an absent table decides nothing", func(t *testing.T) {
		rs := evalRuleset(t, "*raw\n:PREROUTING ACCEPT [0:0]\n:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]\nCOMMIT\n")
		evalCheck(t, Evaluate(rs, p, nil), fwstate.Accept, []string{}, "")
	})
	t.Run("an incompatible table is unknown", func(t *testing.T) {
		rs := evalRuleset(t, "# Table `filter' is incompatible, use 'nft' tool.\n")
		evalCheck(t, Evaluate(rs, p, nil), fwstate.Unknown, nil, "filter: Table `filter' is incompatible")
	})
	t.Run("no ruleset is unknown", func(t *testing.T) {
		evalCheck(t, Evaluate(nil, p, nil), fwstate.Unknown, nil, "eval: no ruleset")
	})
}

func TestEvaluateInvalidPacket(t *testing.T) {
	rs := evalRuleset(t, walkFilter)
	tests := []struct {
		name   string
		edit   func(p *fwstate.Packet)
		reason string
	}{
		{"family", func(p *fwstate.Packet) { p.Family = "v5" }, `eval: family "v5"`},
		{"address family", func(p *fwstate.Packet) { p.Src = netip.MustParseAddr("2001:db8::1") }, "eval: source 2001:db8::1 is not a v4 address"},
		{"v6 destination", func(p *fwstate.Packet) {
			p.Family, p.Src = fwstate.V6, netip.MustParseAddr("2001:db8::1")
		}, "eval: destination 192.0.2.1 is not a v6 address"},
		{"path", func(p *fwstate.Packet) { p.Path = "prerouting" }, `eval: path "prerouting"`},
		{"input without in-interface", func(p *fwstate.Packet) { p.InIface = "" }, "eval: path input needs an in-interface"},
		{"forward without out-interface", func(p *fwstate.Packet) { p.Path = "forward" }, "eval: path forward needs an out-interface"},
		{"output without out-interface", func(p *fwstate.Packet) { p.Path, p.InIface = "output", "" }, "eval: path output needs an out-interface"},
		{"conntrack state", func(p *fwstate.Packet) { p.CtState = "new" }, `eval: conntrack state "new"`},
		{"protocol", func(p *fwstate.Packet) { p.Proto = "" }, "eval: no protocol"},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			p := evalPacket()
			tt.edit(&p)
			evalCheck(t, Evaluate(rs, p, nil), fwstate.Unknown, []string{}, tt.reason)
		})
	}
}
```

Create `internal/modules/firewall/eval/eval.go`:

```go
// Package eval walks a loaded or predicted netfilter state for one packet
// and decides whether the kernel would accept, drop or reject it (spec
// 2.3). It is pure: it reads only the ruleset, the packet and the router it
// is given. Whatever it cannot model makes the verdict unknown, which every
// caller treats as a failure, so a gap in the model is never a false accept.
package eval

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net/netip"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netfilter"
)

// maxDepth bounds nested jumps. The kernel refuses jump loops, but a
// predicted or hand-written ruleset has not been through the kernel.
const maxDepth = 64

// Evaluate walks rs, one family's tables, for packet p and returns the
// verdict, the reason for anything but an accept, and the trace of every
// rule that matched. route says where the packet goes once its destination
// has been rewritten; it may be nil when nothing rewrites it.
func Evaluate(rs *netfilter.Ruleset, p fwstate.Packet, route fwstate.Router) fwstate.Result {
	w, err := newWalker(rs, p, route)
	if err != nil {
		return fwstate.Result{Verdict: fwstate.Unknown, Reason: err.Error()}
	}
	return w.run()
}

// tri is the outcome of a match the walk may not be able to decide.
type tri int

const (
	no tri = iota
	yes
	maybe
)

// outcome is how a rule, a chain or a table's hook ended.
type outcome int

const (
	next   outcome = iota // fall through to the next rule, or back to the calling chain
	ret                   // RETURN: leave the current chain
	accept                // ACCEPT or a NAT target: this table's hook is done
	final                 // a drop, reject or unknown verdict
)

var ctStates = map[string]bool{"NEW": true, "ESTABLISHED": true, "RELATED": true, "INVALID": true, "UNTRACKED": true}

type walker struct {
	rs    *netfilter.Ruleset
	route fwstate.Router
	pkt   fwstate.Packet // the packet as the current hook sees it
	in    string         // the in-interface the current hook sees, "" for none
	out   string         // the out-interface the current hook sees, "" for none
	res   fwstate.Result
}

func newWalker(rs *netfilter.Ruleset, p fwstate.Packet, route fwstate.Router) (*walker, error) {
	if rs == nil {
		return nil, errors.New("eval: no ruleset for the packet's family")
	}
	var ok func(netip.Addr) bool
	switch p.Family {
	case fwstate.V4:
		ok = netip.Addr.Is4
	case fwstate.V6:
		ok = func(a netip.Addr) bool { return a.Is6() && !a.Is4In6() }
	default:
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("eval: family %q", p.Family)
	}
	if !ok(p.Src) {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("eval: source %s is not a %s address", p.Src, p.Family)
	}
	if !ok(p.Dst) {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("eval: destination %s is not a %s address", p.Dst, p.Family)
	}
	switch {
	case p.Path != "input" && p.Path != "forward" && p.Path != "output":
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("eval: path %q", p.Path)
	case p.Path != "output" && p.InIface == "":
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("eval: path %s needs an in-interface", p.Path)
	case p.Path != "input" && p.OutIface == "":
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("eval: path %s needs an out-interface", p.Path)
	case !ctStates[p.CtState]:
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("eval: conntrack state %q", p.CtState)
	case p.Proto == "":
		return nil, errors.New("eval: no protocol")
	}
	p.Proto = strings.ToLower(p.Proto)
	if p.Path == "output" {
		p.InIface = ""
	}
	return &walker{rs: rs, route: route, pkt: p, res: fwstate.Result{Trace: []string{}}}, nil
}

// run walks the hooks the packet traverses.
func (w *walker) run() fwstate.Result {
	chain := map[string]string{"input": "INPUT", "forward": "FORWARD", "output": "OUTPUT"}[w.pkt.Path]
	if w.hook("filter", chain) == final {
		return w.res
	}
	w.res.Verdict = fwstate.Accept
	return w.res
}

func (w *walker) stop(v fwstate.Verdict, reason string) outcome {
	w.res.Verdict, w.res.Reason = v, reason
	return final
}

// hook walks one built-in chain of one table. An absent table or chain
// registers no hook in the kernel, so it lets the packet through.
func (w *walker) hook(table, chain string) outcome {
	t := w.rs.Table(table)
	if t == nil {
		return accept
	}
	if t.Incompatible != "" {
		return w.stop(fwstate.Unknown, table+": "+t.Incompatible)
	}
	c := t.Chain(chain)
	if c == nil {
		return accept
	}
	// The kernel gives PREROUTING and INPUT no out-interface, and OUTPUT
	// and POSTROUTING no in-interface, whatever the packet's path.
	w.in, w.out = w.pkt.InIface, w.pkt.OutIface
	switch chain {
	case "PREROUTING", "INPUT":
		w.out = ""
	case "OUTPUT", "POSTROUTING":
		w.in = ""
	}
	if o := w.walkChain(t, c, 0); o == accept || o == final {
		return o
	}
	ref := table + "/" + chain
	switch c.Policy {
	case "ACCEPT":
		return accept
	case "DROP":
		return w.stop(fwstate.Drop, ref+" policy DROP")
	}
	return w.stop(fwstate.Unknown, ref+" has no policy")
}

func (w *walker) walkChain(t *netfilter.Table, c *netfilter.Chain, depth int) outcome {
	for i := range c.Rules {
		r := &c.Rules[i]
		ref := t.Name + "/" + c.Name + "#" + strconv.Itoa(i+1)
		if !w.header(r) {
			continue
		}
		if r.Opaque() {
			return w.stop(fwstate.Unknown, ref+": "+strings.Join(r.Unsupported, ", "))
		}
		m, why := w.modules(t, r)
		if m == no {
			continue
		}
		if m == maybe {
			if decides(r.Target) {
				return w.stop(fwstate.Unknown, ref+": "+why)
			}
			continue
		}
		w.res.Trace = append(w.res.Trace, ref)
		switch o := w.target(t, r, ref, depth); o {
		case next:
		case ret:
			return next
		default:
			return o
		}
	}
	return next
}

// decides reports whether a rule's target can change the verdict when the
// rule matches; a rule whose match the walk cannot decide is harmless only
// when it cannot.
func decides(tg netfilter.Target) bool {
	if tg.Chain {
		return true
	}
	switch tg.Name {
	case "", "LOG", "TCPMSS":
		return false
	}
	return true
}

func (w *walker) target(t *netfilter.Table, r *netfilter.Rule, ref string, depth int) outcome {
	tg := r.Target
	if tg.Chain {
		c := t.Chain(tg.Name)
		if c == nil {
			return w.stop(fwstate.Unknown, ref+": no chain "+tg.Name)
		}
		if depth >= maxDepth {
			return w.stop(fwstate.Unknown, fmt.Sprintf("%s: jumps nest deeper than %d", ref, maxDepth))
		}
		return w.walkChain(t, c, depth+1)
	}
	switch tg.Name {
	case "", "LOG", "TCPMSS":
		return next
	case "ACCEPT":
		return accept
	case "DROP":
		return w.stop(fwstate.Drop, ref+" drops")
	case "REJECT":
		return w.stop(fwstate.Reject, ref+" rejects")
	case "RETURN":
		return ret
	}
	return w.stop(fwstate.Unknown, ref+": target "+tg.Name+" is not modelled")
}

// header evaluates the options outside any -m module.
func (w *walker) header(r *netfilter.Rule) bool {
	return ifaceMatch(r.In, w.in) && ifaceMatch(r.Out, w.out) &&
		addrMatch(r.Source, w.pkt.Src) && addrMatch(r.Dest, w.pkt.Dst) &&
		protoMatch(r.Proto, w.pkt.Proto)
}

// ifaceMatch applies -i or -o; a trailing "+" matches every name with that
// prefix, and no interface at all is the empty name, as in the kernel.
func ifaceMatch(m netfilter.NameMatch, name string) bool {
	if m.Name == "" {
		return true
	}
	var ok bool
	if prefix, wild := strings.CutSuffix(m.Name, "+"); wild {
		ok = strings.HasPrefix(name, prefix)
	} else {
		ok = name == m.Name
	}
	return ok != m.Neg
}

func addrMatch(m netfilter.AddrMatch, a netip.Addr) bool {
	if !m.Prefix.IsValid() {
		return true
	}
	return m.Prefix.Contains(a) != m.Neg
}

var protoNumbers = map[string]int{
	"icmp": 1, "igmp": 2, "tcp": 6, "dccp": 33, "udp": 17, "ipv6": 41, "gre": 47,
	"esp": 50, "ah": 51, "ipv6-icmp": 58, "icmpv6": 58, "sctp": 132, "udplite": 136,
}

// protoNumber returns a protocol's number from its name as iptables-save or
// a caller spells it, or from its decimal number.
func protoNumber(name string) (int, bool) {
	name = strings.ToLower(name)
	if n, ok := protoNumbers[name]; ok {
		return n, true
	}
	n, err := strconv.Atoi(name)
	return n, err == nil && n >= 0 && n <= 255
}

func sameProto(a, b string) bool {
	na, oka := protoNumber(a)
	nb, okb := protoNumber(b)
	if oka && okb {
		return na == nb
	}
	return strings.EqualFold(a, b)
}

func protoMatch(m netfilter.NameMatch, proto string) bool {
	if m.Name == "" {
		return true
	}
	return (m.Name == "all" || sameProto(m.Name, proto)) != m.Neg
}

// modules evaluates the rule's -m matches.
func (w *walker) modules(_ *netfilter.Table, r *netfilter.Rule) (tri, string) {
	for _, m := range r.Matches {
		if m.Module != "comment" {
			return maybe, "match " + m.Module + " is not modelled"
		}
	}
	return yes, ""
}
```

```go
package guard

import (
	"net/netip"
	"reflect"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netstat"
)

// flPkt is the expected packet of a new connection.
func flPkt(path, src string, sport uint16, dst string, dport uint16, proto string) fwstate.Packet {
	s, d := netip.MustParseAddr(src), netip.MustParseAddr(dst)
	fam := fwstate.V4
	if s.Is6() {
		fam = fwstate.V6
	}
	return fwstate.Packet{Family: fam, Path: path, Src: s, SrcPort: sport, Dst: d, DstPort: dport, Proto: proto, CtState: "NEW"}
}

// flOn is flPkt with a fixed in-interface.
func flOn(iface string, p fwstate.Packet) fwstate.Packet {
	p.InIface = iface
	return p
}

// flSock is a socket of the table held by one process.
func flSock(proto netstat.Proto, state netstat.State, local, remote, comm string, pid int) netstat.Socket {
	s := netstat.Socket{Proto: proto, Family: netstat.IPv4, State: state, Local: netip.MustParseAddrPort(local)}
	if remote != "" {
		s.Remote = netip.MustParseAddrPort(remote)
	}
	if s.Local.Addr().Is6() {
		s.Family = netstat.IPv6
	}
	if comm != "" {
		s.Processes = []netstat.Process{{PID: pid, Comm: comm}}
	}
	return s
}

func flAddrPorts(s ...string) []netip.AddrPort {
	out := make([]netip.AddrPort, len(s))
	for i, a := range s {
		out[i] = netip.MustParseAddrPort(a)
	}
	return out
}
```

```go
package guard

import (
	"net/netip"
	"slices"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netfilter"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netstat"
)

// Input is what a guard check protects besides the host's live facts.
type Input struct {
	Plan    *core.GuardContext // the plan input's guard (nil for break-glass and system plans)
	Refresh *core.GuardContext // env.Call.GuardRefresh at apply; nil at plan
	Retired []string           // env.Call.Retired
	Eval    func(rs *netfilter.Ruleset, p fwstate.Packet, route fwstate.Router) fwstate.Result
}

// panelBridge is the Docker bridge of the panel network (spec 8).
const panelBridge = "dp-panel"

// ephemeralPort stands in for the source port of a connection that does
// not exist yet; it lies inside every Linux ephemeral port range.
const ephemeralPort uint16 = 49152

// The documentation addresses that stand in for "any internet address".
var (
	internet4 = netip.MustParseAddr("198.51.100.1")
	internet6 = netip.MustParseAddr("2001:db8:ffff::1")
)

// sshComms are the process names that hold an OpenSSH session's socket:
// OpenSSH before 9.8 keeps it in sshd, later releases in sshd-session, and
// 10.0 authenticates in sshd-auth.
var sshComms = []string{"sshd", "sshd-session", "sshd-auth"}

// tailscaled is the process name of the Tailscale daemon.
const tailscaled = "tailscaled"

// flow is one protected flow before routing: pkt has no in- or
// out-interface yet unless the flow fixes its in-interface. A flow with a
// non-empty unknown is not evaluated and fails with that reason.
type flow struct {
	label   string
	pkt     fwstate.Packet
	standIn bool // pkt.Dst stands in for any destination: with no route of its family there is nothing to protect
	unknown string
}

// flowSet collects flows in order without duplicates. Two flows with the
// same packet are one flow, whichever label came first.
type flowSet struct {
	flows []flow
	seen  map[flowKey]bool
}

type flowKey struct {
	pkt            fwstate.Packet
	label, unknown string // set only for a flow that is not evaluated
}

func (s *flowSet) add(f flow) {
	k := flowKey{pkt: f.pkt}
	if f.unknown != "" {
		k = flowKey{label: f.label, unknown: f.unknown}
	}
	if s.seen[k] {
		return
	}
	s.seen[k] = true
	s.flows = append(s.flows, f)
}

// buildFlows returns every protected flow of spec 2.3 for in and f, in the
// spec's order, with Plan and Refresh merged.
func buildFlows(in Input, f facts) []flow {
	s := &flowSet{seen: map[flowKey]bool{}}
	local := localAddrs(f.ifaces)
	var ctxs []*core.GuardContext
	for _, g := range []*core.GuardContext{in.Plan, in.Refresh} {
		if g != nil {
			ctxs = append(ctxs, g)
			if !g.Complete {
				s.add(flow{label: "controller topology", unknown: "the controller's topology is incomplete"})
			}
		}
	}
	sshFlows(s, f, local)
	if f.controller != 0 || listensHere(ctxs, local) {
		panelFlows(s, ctxs, local)
		viaFlows(s, ctxs, in.Retired)
		agentLinkFlows(s, ctxs, local)
	}
	controllerSessionFlows(s, f, local)
	agentOutboundFlows(s, f, local)
	tailscaleFlows(s, f)
	return s.flows
}

// localAddrs are the addresses of every interface of the host.
func localAddrs(ifaces []netstat.Interface) map[netip.Addr]bool {
	out := map[netip.Addr]bool{}
	for _, i := range ifaces {
		for _, p := range i.Addrs {
			out[p.Addr().Unmap()] = true
		}
	}
	return out
}

// fromHere reports whether a packet from a reaches this host only through
// the loopback interface, which no flow is checked on.
func fromHere(a netip.Addr, local map[netip.Addr]bool) bool {
	a = a.Unmap()
	return a.IsLoopback() || local[a]
}

// listensHere reports whether a guard context names a listener on one of
// this host's addresses, so the controller runs here.
func listensHere(ctxs []*core.GuardContext, local map[netip.Addr]bool) bool {
	for _, g := range ctxs {
		for _, l := range slices.Concat(g.PanelListen, g.AgentListen) {
			if local[l.Addr().Unmap()] {
				return true
			}
		}
	}
	return false
}

// newPacket is a new TCP or UDP connection from src to dst on path.
func newPacket(path string, src netip.Addr, sport uint16, dst netip.Addr, dport uint16, proto string) fwstate.Packet {
	src, dst = src.Unmap(), dst.Unmap()
	fam := fwstate.V6
	if src.Is4() {
		fam = fwstate.V4
	}
	return fwstate.Packet{Family: fam, Path: path, Src: src, SrcPort: sport, Dst: dst, DstPort: dport, Proto: proto, CtState: "NEW"}
}

// listenFor is the destination a client at src reaches a listener on l
// through, or false when the listener does not take src's family. An
// unspecified IPv6 listener is dual-stack, as Go's listeners are; the
// unspecified destination stays for routing to resolve.
func listenFor(src, l netip.Addr) (netip.Addr, bool) {
	src, l = src.Unmap(), l.Unmap()
	switch {
	case l.IsUnspecified() && l.Is6() && src.Is4():
		return netip.IPv4Unspecified(), true
	case l.Is4() == src.Is4():
		return l, true
	}
	return netip.Addr{}, false
}

// heldBy reports whether a process named one of comms, or with pid, holds s.
func heldBy(s netstat.Socket, pid int, comms ...string) bool {
	for _, p := range s.Processes {
		if (pid != 0 && p.PID == pid) || slices.Contains(comms, p.Comm) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// inbound reports whether the established TCP socket s was accepted on a
// listening socket of this host, whichever process holds that listener
// (systemd holds sshd's under socket activation).
func inbound(socks []netstat.Socket, s netstat.Socket) bool {
	for _, l := range socks {
		if l.Proto == netstat.ProtoTCP && l.State == netstat.StateListen && l.Local.Port() == s.Local.Port() &&
			(l.Local.Addr().IsUnspecified() || l.Local.Addr().Unmap() == s.Local.Addr().Unmap()) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// established lists the established TCP sockets of the table.
func established(socks []netstat.Socket) []netstat.Socket {
	var out []netstat.Socket
	for _, s := range socks {
		if s.Proto == netstat.ProtoTCP && s.State == netstat.StateEstablished {
			out = append(out, s)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// sshFlows is flow 1: a new connection from each SSH session's peer to its
// local address and port.
func sshFlows(s *flowSet, f facts, local map[netip.Addr]bool) {
	for _, so := range established(f.sockets) {
		if !heldBy(so, 0, sshComms...) || !inbound(f.sockets, so) || fromHere(so.Remote.Addr(), local) {
			continue
		}
		s.add(flow{label: "ssh", pkt: newPacket("input", so.Remote.Addr(), so.Remote.Port(), so.Local.Addr(), so.Local.Port(), "tcp")})
	}
}

// panelFlows is flow 2: each client that reached the controller directly,
// to every panel listener.
func panelFlows(s *flowSet, ctxs []*core.GuardContext, local map[netip.Addr]bool) {
	var listen []netip.AddrPort
	for _, g := range ctxs {
		listen = append(listen, g.PanelListen...)
	}
	for _, g := range ctxs {
		if g.Via != nil || g.Client == nil || !g.Client.Addr.IsValid() || fromHere(g.Client.Addr, local) {
			continue
		}
		for _, l := range listen {
			if dst, ok := listenFor(g.Client.Addr, l.Addr()); ok {
				s.add(flow{label: "panel", pkt: newPacket("input", g.Client.Addr, g.Client.Port, dst, l.Port(), "tcp")})
			}
		}
	}
}

// viaFlows is flow 3: the exposure a request came through, unless a
// composite has retired it.
func viaFlows(s *flowSet, ctxs []*core.GuardContext, retired []string) {
	for _, g := range ctxs {
		v := g.Via
		if v == nil || slices.Contains(retired, v.ExposureID) {
			continue
		}
		label := "exposure " + v.ExposureID
		if !v.ProxyAddr.IsValid() || !v.ListenerAddr.IsValid() {
			s.add(flow{label: label, unknown: "the exposure has no proxy or listener address"})
			continue
		}
		proxy := newPacket("input", v.ProxyAddr, ephemeralPort, v.ListenerAddr.Addr(), v.ListenerAddr.Port(), "tcp")
		proxy.InIface = panelBridge
		s.add(flow{label: label + " proxy", pkt: proxy})
		switch v.Kind {
		case "npm":
			for _, pub := range v.Public {
				s.add(flow{label: label + " public", pkt: newPacket("input", internetFor(pub.Addr()), ephemeralPort, pub.Addr(), pub.Port(), "tcp")})
			}
		case "tunnel":
			for _, out := range []struct {
				proto string
				port  uint16
			}{{"udp", 7844}, {"tcp", 7844}, {"tcp", 443}} {
				p := newPacket("forward", v.ProxyAddr, ephemeralPort, internetFor(v.ProxyAddr), out.port, out.proto)
				p.InIface = panelBridge
				s.add(flow{label: label + " tunnel", pkt: p, standIn: true})
			}
		default:
			s.add(flow{label: label, unknown: "the exposure kind " + v.Kind + " is not npm or tunnel"})
		}
	}
}

// internetFor is the stand-in internet address of a's family.
func internetFor(a netip.Addr) netip.Addr {
	if a.Unmap().Is4() {
		return internet4
	}
	return internet6
}

// agentLinkFlows is flow 4 from the guard context: every live agent's
// address to every agent listener.
func agentLinkFlows(s *flowSet, ctxs []*core.GuardContext, local map[netip.Addr]bool) {
	var peers []netip.Addr
	var listen []netip.AddrPort
	for _, g := range ctxs {
		peers = append(peers, g.AgentPeers...)
		listen = append(listen, g.AgentListen...)
	}
	for _, p := range peers {
		if !p.IsValid() || fromHere(p, local) {
			continue
		}
		for _, l := range listen {
			if dst, ok := listenFor(p, l.Addr()); ok {
				s.add(flow{label: "agent link", pkt: newPacket("input", p, ephemeralPort, dst, l.Port(), "tcp")})
			}
		}
	}
}

// controllerSessionFlows is flow 4 from live facts: each established
// session a local controller accepted, from its peer to its local address
// and port. Without a guard context these are the panel and agent links a
// --local change must keep.
func controllerSessionFlows(s *flowSet, f facts, local map[netip.Addr]bool) {
	if f.controller == 0 {
		return
	}
	for _, so := range established(f.sockets) {
		if !heldBy(so, f.controller) || !inbound(f.sockets, so) || fromHere(so.Remote.Addr(), local) {
			continue
		}
		s.add(flow{label: "controller session", pkt: newPacket("input", so.Remote.Addr(), so.Remote.Port(), so.Local.Addr(), so.Local.Port(), "tcp")})
	}
}

// agentOutboundFlows is flow 5: every outbound TCP session of the agent
// itself, which includes its link to the controller.
func agentOutboundFlows(s *flowSet, f facts, local map[netip.Addr]bool) {
	for _, so := range established(f.sockets) {
		if !heldBy(so, f.pid) || inbound(f.sockets, so) || fromHere(so.Remote.Addr(), local) {
			continue
		}
		s.add(flow{label: "controller link", pkt: newPacket("output", so.Local.Addr(), so.Local.Port(), so.Remote.Addr(), so.Remote.Port(), "tcp")})
	}
}

// tailscaleFlows is flow 6: when tailscaled runs, its WireGuard UDP port to
// any destination and TCP 443 to any destination (DERP and the control
// plane). The source address is left for routing to choose.
func tailscaleFlows(s *flowSet, f facts) {
	running := false
	var ports []uint16
	for _, so := range f.sockets {
		if !heldBy(so, 0, tailscaled) {
			continue
		}
		running = true
		if so.Proto == netstat.ProtoUDP && so.Listening() && so.Local.Port() != 0 && !so.Local.Addr().IsLoopback() && !slices.Contains(ports, so.Local.Port()) {
			ports = append(ports, so.Local.Port())
		}
	}
	if !running {
		return
	}
	slices.Sort(ports)
	for _, port := range ports {
		s.add(flow{label: "tailscale", pkt: newPacket("output", netip.IPv4Unspecified(), port, internet4, 41641, "udp"), standIn: true})
	}
	s.add(flow{label: "tailscale", pkt: newPacket("output", netip.IPv4Unspecified(), ephemeralPort, internet4, 443, "tcp"), standIn: true})
}
```

### Task 32: Repair before-images

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/modules/firewall/image.go`
- Test: `internal/modules/firewall/image_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `fwstate.Loaded`, `fwstate.Family`, `fwstate.V4`, `fwstate.V6` (Task 18); `netfilter.Ruleset`, `netfilter.Chain`, `netfilter.Parse` (merged), `netfilter.Key` (Task 24).
- Produces: `beforeImage`, `imageTable`, `imageChain`, `imageRule`, `chainRef`, `imagePlan`, `builtinChains`, `firewallChain`, `takeImage`, `planImage`, `imageMismatch`, `restoreProgram` (Part contracts, Task 32).

**Depends on:** Task 18, Task 24

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-opus-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 2 - risk 3 = 6
**Lenses:** security

A repair starts from the loaded state, not from the files, so its snapshot holds a loaded-state before-image (spec 2.3). The image covers UFW's and Darkpanel's chains and the filter table's built-in chains, and reverting the repair loads it with `*-restore -n`. This task takes the image from a loaded state and plans its load: a declaration flushes each user chain, and `-F` flushes each built-in chain. A built-in chain whose other programs' rules changed since the image is left as it is and reported. The task also lists the chains that differ from the image after a load. The tests prove which chains the image holds and their `Own` flags, the exact restore input, the exclusion of a built-in chain whose foreign rules were added, removed or doubled, the handling of a missing family, and the mismatch report. A container run confirmed the restore input on real iptables-nft (Assumptions).
