```go
package firewall

import (
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netfilter"
)

// imTestSave4 is IPv4 save output with UFW's chains, a foreign chain
// jumped to from INPUT, Docker's DOCKER-USER and a Darkpanel chain in nat.
const imTestSave4 = `*nat
:PREROUTING ACCEPT [0:0]
:INPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
:POSTROUTING ACCEPT [0:0]
:DOCKER - [0:0]
:darkpanel-nat - [0:0]
-A PREROUTING -j darkpanel-nat
-A darkpanel-nat -d 192.0.2.1/32 -j RETURN
COMMIT
*filter
:INPUT DROP [0:0]
:FORWARD DROP [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
:DOCKER-USER - [0:0]
:fw-foreign - [0:0]
:ufw-before-input - [0:0]
:ufw-user-input - [0:0]
-A INPUT -j fw-foreign
-A INPUT -j ufw-before-input
-A FORWARD -j DOCKER-USER
-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN
-A fw-foreign -s 198.51.100.7/32 -j ACCEPT
-A ufw-before-input -i lo -j ACCEPT
-A ufw-before-input -j ufw-user-input
-A ufw-user-input -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
COMMIT
`

const imTestSave6 = `*filter
:INPUT DROP [0:0]
:FORWARD DROP [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
:ufw6-user-input - [0:0]
-A INPUT -j ufw6-user-input
-A ufw6-user-input -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
COMMIT
`

func imTestParse(t *testing.T, text string) *netfilter.Ruleset {
	t.Helper()
	rs, err := netfilter.Parse(strings.NewReader(text))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return rs
}

func imTestLoaded(t *testing.T, v4, v6 string) fwstate.Loaded {
	t.Helper()
	st := fwstate.Loaded{Variant: "nft", V4: imTestParse(t, v4)}
	if v6 != "" {
		st.V6 = imTestParse(t, v6)
	}
	return st
}

func imTestNames(img []imageTable) []string {
	var out []string
	for _, t := range img {
		for _, c := range t.Chains {
			out = append(out, t.Name+"/"+c.Name)
		}
	}
	return out
}

func TestFirewallChain(t *testing.T) {
	for name, want := range map[string]bool{
		"ufw-user-input": true, "ufw6-before-input": true, "DOCKER-USER": true, "darkpanel-block": true,
		"dp-b-0a1b": true, "DOCKER": false, "ts-input": false, "INPUT": false, "ufwx": false, "": false,
	} {
		if got := firewallChain(name); got != want {
			t.Errorf("firewallChain(%q) = %v, want %v", name, got, want)
		}
	}
}

func TestTakeImage(t *testing.T) {
	img := takeImage(imTestLoaded(t, imTestSave4, imTestSave6))
	if got, want := imTestNames(img.V4), []string{
		"nat/darkpanel-nat", "filter/INPUT", "filter/FORWARD", "filter/OUTPUT", "filter/DOCKER-USER",
		"filter/ufw-before-input", "filter/ufw-user-input",
	}; !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("v4 chains = %v, want %v", got, want)
	}
	if got, want := imTestNames(img.V6), []string{"filter/INPUT", "filter/FORWARD", "filter/OUTPUT", "filter/ufw6-user-input"}; !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("v6 chains = %v, want %v", got, want)
	}
	input := img.V4[1].Chains[0]
	if !input.Builtin || input.Policy != "DROP" || len(input.Rules) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("INPUT = %+v", input)
	}
	if input.Rules[0].Own || !input.Rules[1].Own {
		t.Errorf("INPUT own flags = %v %v, want false true", input.Rules[0].Own, input.Rules[1].Own)
	}
	if input.Rules[0].Text != "-A INPUT -j fw-foreign" || input.Rules[0].Key == "" {
		t.Errorf("INPUT rule 1 = %+v", input.Rules[0])
	}
	if empty := img.V4[1].Chains[2]; empty.Rules == nil {
		t.Error("an empty chain's rules are nil, which encodes as null")
	}
	if got := takeImage(fwstate.Loaded{Variant: "nft", V4: imTestParse(t, imTestSave4)}); got.V6 != nil {
		t.Errorf("an image of a state without IPv6 has v6 chains %v", got.V6)
	}
}

func TestPlanImageRestoresEverything(t *testing.T) {
	img := takeImage(imTestLoaded(t, imTestSave4, imTestSave6))
	cur := strings.NewReplacer(":INPUT DROP", ":INPUT ACCEPT", "-A INPUT -j ufw-before-input\n", "",
		"--dport 22 -j ACCEPT", "--dport 2222 -j ACCEPT").Replace(imTestSave4)
	p := planImage(img, imTestLoaded(t, cur, imTestSave6))
	if len(p.Excluded) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("excluded %v, want none", p.Excluded)
	}
	want4 := `*nat
:darkpanel-nat - [0:0]
-A darkpanel-nat -d 192.0.2.1/32 -j RETURN
COMMIT
*filter
:INPUT DROP [0:0]
:FORWARD DROP [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
:DOCKER-USER - [0:0]
:ufw-before-input - [0:0]
:ufw-user-input - [0:0]
-F INPUT
-F FORWARD
-F OUTPUT
-A INPUT -j fw-foreign
-A INPUT -j ufw-before-input
-A FORWARD -j DOCKER-USER
-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN
-A ufw-before-input -i lo -j ACCEPT
-A ufw-before-input -j ufw-user-input
-A ufw-user-input -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
COMMIT
`
	if string(p.Restore4) != want4 {
		t.Errorf("v4 restore input =\n%s\nwant\n%s", p.Restore4, want4)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(string(p.Restore6), ":ufw6-user-input - [0:0]\n-F INPUT\n") {
		t.Errorf("v6 restore input =\n%s", p.Restore6)
	}
}

func TestPlanImageExcludesChangedBuiltin(t *testing.T) {
	img := takeImage(imTestLoaded(t, imTestSave4, imTestSave6))
	for name, cur := range map[string]string{
		"foreign rule added":   strings.Replace(imTestSave4, "-A INPUT -j ufw-before-input\n", "-A INPUT -j ufw-before-input\n-A INPUT -s 192.0.2.9/32 -j DROP\n", 1),
		"foreign rule removed": strings.Replace(imTestSave4, "-A INPUT -j fw-foreign\n", "", 1),
		"foreign rule doubled": strings.Replace(imTestSave4, "-A INPUT -j fw-foreign\n-A INPUT -j ufw-before-input\n", "-A INPUT -j fw-foreign\n-A INPUT -j fw-foreign\n", 1),
	} {
		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
			p := planImage(img, imTestLoaded(t, cur, imTestSave6))
			if want := []chainRef{{fwstate.V4, "filter", "INPUT"}}; !reflect.DeepEqual(p.Excluded, want) {
				t.Errorf("excluded %v, want %v", p.Excluded, want)
			}
			text := string(p.Restore4)
			if strings.Contains(text, ":INPUT") || strings.Contains(text, "-F INPUT") || strings.Contains(text, "-A INPUT ") {
				t.Errorf("restore input touches INPUT:\n%s", text)
			}
			if !strings.Contains(text, "-F FORWARD\n") || !strings.Contains(text, ":ufw-user-input - [0:0]") {
				t.Errorf("restore input lost the other chains:\n%s", text)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestPlanImageMissingFamily(t *testing.T) {
	img := takeImage(imTestLoaded(t, imTestSave4, imTestSave6))
	p := planImage(img, imTestLoaded(t, imTestSave4, ""))
	if p.Restore6 != nil {

func TestImageMismatch(t *testing.T) {
	img := takeImage(imTestLoaded(t, imTestSave4, imTestSave6))
	if got := imageMismatch(img, imTestLoaded(t, imTestSave4, imTestSave6), nil); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("mismatch against the imaged state: %v", got)
	}
	changed := strings.NewReplacer(":INPUT DROP", ":INPUT ACCEPT", "--dport 22 -j ACCEPT", "--dport 23 -j ACCEPT",
		":darkpanel-nat - [0:0]\n", "", "-A PREROUTING -j darkpanel-nat\n", "", "-A darkpanel-nat -d 192.0.2.1/32 -j RETURN\n", "").Replace(imTestSave4)
	want := []chainRef{{fwstate.V4, "nat", "darkpanel-nat"}, {fwstate.V4, "filter", "INPUT"}, {fwstate.V4, "filter", "ufw-user-input"}}
	if got := imageMismatch(img, imTestLoaded(t, changed, imTestSave6), nil); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("mismatch = %v, want %v", got, want)

	if got := imageMismatch(img, imTestLoaded(t, changed, imTestSave6), want[1:2]); len(got) != 2 {

	if got := imageMismatch(img, imTestLoaded(t, imTestSave4, extra), nil); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, []chainRef{{fwstate.V6, "filter", "ufw6-user-input"}}) {
		t.Errorf("mismatch with an extra v6 rule = %v", got)
	}
}

	for _, c := range []struct {

		variant string

		{fwstate.V6, "legacy", "/usr/sbin/ip6tables-legacy-restore"},

			t.Errorf("restoreProgram(%s, %s) = %s, want %s", c.fam, c.variant, got, c.want)
		}
	}
}
```

```go
package firewall

import (
	"bytes"
	"fmt"
	"slices"
	"strings"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netfilter"
)

// beforeImage is a repair snapshot's loaded-state before-image (spec 2.3):
// per family, every UFW and Darkpanel chain of every table and the
// built-in INPUT, FORWARD and OUTPUT chains of the filter table, with
// their policies and rules as *-save printed them.
type beforeImage struct {
	V4 []imageTable `json:"v4,omitempty"`
	V6 []imageTable `json:"v6,omitempty"`
}

// imageTable is one table's chains in a before-image.
type imageTable struct {
	Name   string       `json:"name"`
	Chains []imageChain `json:"chains"`
}

// imageChain is one chain in a before-image.
type imageChain struct {
	Name    string      `json:"name"`
	Builtin bool        `json:"builtin,omitempty"`
	Policy  string      `json:"policy,omitempty"`
	Rules   []imageRule `json:"rules"`
}

// imageRule is one rule of an imageChain. Key is taken when the image is,
// from the rule in its whole table, so a jump compares the same way it did
// in the loaded state.
type imageRule struct {
	Text string `json:"text"`          // the -A line as *-save printed it
	Key  string `json:"key"`           // netfilter.Key of the rule in its family
	Own  bool   `json:"own,omitempty"` // a jump to a UFW or Darkpanel chain
}

// chainRef names one chain of a loaded state.
type chainRef struct {
	Family fwstate.Family
	Table  string
	Chain  string
}

func (c chainRef) String() string { return fmt.Sprintf("%s %s/%s", c.Family, c.Table, c.Chain) }

// imagePlan is what loading a before-image does to the current loaded state.
type imagePlan struct {
	Restore4, Restore6 []byte     // *-restore -n input per family; nil when the family loads nothing
	Excluded           []chainRef // built-in chains left as they are, because their other rules changed
}

// builtinChains are the built-in chains a before-image holds, of the filter
// table only: UFW hooks its chains there, and other tables' built-in chains
// belong to Docker, tailscaled and other programs.
var builtinChains = []string{"INPUT", "FORWARD", "OUTPUT"}

// firewallChain reports whether a chain is UFW's or Darkpanel's (spec 2.3).
func firewallChain(name string) bool {
	return strings.HasPrefix(name, "ufw-") || strings.HasPrefix(name, "ufw6-") || name == "DOCKER-USER" ||
		strings.HasPrefix(name, "darkpanel-") || strings.HasPrefix(name, "dp-b-")
}

// imageHolds reports whether a before-image holds chain c of table.
func imageHolds(table string, c netfilter.Chain) bool {
	return firewallChain(c.Name) || (table == "filter" && c.Builtin && slices.Contains(builtinChains, c.Name))
}

// takeImage takes the before-image of st.
func takeImage(st fwstate.Loaded) *beforeImage {
	return &beforeImage{V4: imageTables(st.V4, false), V6: imageTables(st.V6, true)}
}

func imageTables(rs *netfilter.Ruleset, ipv6 bool) []imageTable {
	if rs == nil {
		return nil
	}
	var out []imageTable
	for _, t := range rs.Tables {
		it := imageTable{Name: t.Name}
		for _, c := range t.Chains {
			if !imageHolds(t.Name, c) {
				continue
			}
			ic := imageChain{Name: c.Name, Builtin: c.Builtin, Policy: c.Policy, Rules: []imageRule{}}
			for _, r := range c.Rules {
				ic.Rules = append(ic.Rules, imageRule{Text: r.Text, Key: netfilter.Key(r, ipv6), Own: firewallChain(r.Target.Name)})
			}
			it.Chains = append(it.Chains, ic)
		}
		if len(it.Chains) > 0 {
			out = append(out, it)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// planImage decides how to load img over the current loaded state st. A
// user chain is always loaded: *-restore -n flushes and refills a chain it
// declares. A built-in chain is not flushed by a declaration, so it is
// flushed explicitly, and only when its rules other than jumps to UFW and
// Darkpanel chains equal the image's; otherwise it is left as it is and
// listed in Excluded, so no other program's rule is overwritten. A family
// the current state lacks is left out with all its built-in chains
// excluded.
func planImage(img *beforeImage, st fwstate.Loaded) imagePlan {
	var p imagePlan
	p.Restore4 = planFamily(img.V4, st.V4, fwstate.V4, false, &p.Excluded)
	p.Restore6 = planFamily(img.V6, st.V6, fwstate.V6, true, &p.Excluded)
	return p
}

func planFamily(tables []imageTable, cur *netfilter.Ruleset, fam fwstate.Family, ipv6 bool, excluded *[]chainRef) []byte {
	if len(tables) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	if cur == nil {
		for _, t := range tables {
			for _, c := range t.Chains {
				*excluded = append(*excluded, chainRef{fam, t.Name, c.Name})
			}
		}
		return nil
	}
	var b bytes.Buffer
	for _, t := range tables {
		var decl, flush, rules []string
		for _, c := range t.Chains {
			if c.Builtin {
				if !foreignEqual(c, cur, t.Name, ipv6) {
					*excluded = append(*excluded, chainRef{fam, t.Name, c.Name})
					continue
				}
				decl = append(decl, fmt.Sprintf(":%s %s [0:0]", c.Name, c.Policy))
				flush = append(flush, "-F "+c.Name)
			} else {
				decl = append(decl, fmt.Sprintf(":%s - [0:0]", c.Name))
			}
			for _, r := range c.Rules {
				rules = append(rules, r.Text)
			}
		}
		if len(decl) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		b.WriteString("*" + t.Name + "\n")
		for _, l := range slices.Concat(decl, flush, rules) {
			b.WriteString(l + "\n")
		}
		b.WriteString("COMMIT\n")
	}
	if b.Len() == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	return b.Bytes()
}

// foreignEqual reports whether the current built-in chain's rules other
// than jumps to UFW and Darkpanel chains equal, in order, the image's.
func foreignEqual(c imageChain, cur *netfilter.Ruleset, table string, ipv6 bool) bool {
	var want []string
	for _, r := range c.Rules {
		if !r.Own {
			want = append(want, r.Key)
		}
	}
	var got []string
	if ch := chainOf(cur, table, c.Name); ch != nil {
		for _, r := range ch.Rules {
			if !firewallChain(r.Target.Name) {
				got = append(got, netfilter.Key(r, ipv6))
			}
		}
	}
	return slices.Equal(want, got)
}

func chainOf(rs *netfilter.Ruleset, table, chain string) *netfilter.Chain {
	if rs == nil {
		return nil
	}
	t := rs.Table(table)
	if t == nil {
		return nil
	}
	return t.Chain(chain)
}

// imageMismatch lists the chains of img, except those excluded, whose
// policy or rules in st differ from the image.
func imageMismatch(img *beforeImage, st fwstate.Loaded, excluded []chainRef) []chainRef {
	var out []chainRef
	check := func(tables []imageTable, cur *netfilter.Ruleset, fam fwstate.Family, ipv6 bool) {
		for _, t := range tables {
			for _, c := range t.Chains {
				ref := chainRef{fam, t.Name, c.Name}
				if slices.Contains(excluded, ref) {
					continue
				}
				ch := chainOf(cur, t.Name, c.Name)
				if ch == nil || (c.Builtin && ch.Policy != c.Policy) || len(ch.Rules) != len(c.Rules) {
					out = append(out, ref)
					continue
				}
				for i, r := range ch.Rules {
					if netfilter.Key(r, ipv6) != c.Rules[i].Key {
						out = append(out, ref)
						break
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}
	check(img.V4, st.V4, fwstate.V4, false)
	check(img.V6, st.V6, fwstate.V6, true)
	return out
}

// restoreProgram is the *-restore program of the iptables variant UFW uses
// for a family.
func restoreProgram(fam fwstate.Family, variant string) string {
	name := "iptables"
	if fam == fwstate.V6 {
		name = "ip6tables"
	}
	return "/usr/sbin/" + name + "-" + variant + "-restore"
}
```

```go
func TestGoldenLayout(t *testing.T) {

// goldenSameRules compares rules, ignoring manual rules' derived ids.
func goldenSameRules(t *testing.T, where string, got, want []model.Rule) {
	t.Helper()
	if len(got) < len(want) {
		t.Errorf("%s: %d rules, want at least %d", where, len(got), len(want))
		return
	}
	for i, w := range want {
		g := got[i]
		if w.Origin == model.OriginManual {
			if !strings.HasPrefix(g.ID, "manual-") {
				t.Errorf("%s: rule %d id = %q", where, i, g.ID)
			}
			g.ID = ""
		}
		if g != w {
			t.Errorf("%s: rule %d\n got %+v\nwant %+v", where, i, g, w)
		}
	}
}

func TestGoldenRead(t *testing.T) {
	for _, img := range goldenImages {
		for _, sc := range goldenScenarios {
			where := img + "/" + sc
			c, err := Read(filepath.Join(goldenDir, img, sc, "files"))
			if err != nil {
				t.Errorf("%s: %v", where, err)
				continue
			}
			if len(c.Unsupported) != 0 {
				t.Errorf("%s: Unsupported = %q", where, c.Unsupported)
			}
			for p, e := range c.Files {
				if !e.Present {
					t.Errorf("%s: %s is absent", where, p)
				}
			}
			rules := model.Merge(c.Rules4, c.Rules6)
			wantEnabled := sc != "fresh" && sc != "disabled"
			if c.Enabled != wantEnabled || c.IPv6 != (sc != "ipv6no") || c.SysctlFile != "/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf" ||
				c.DefaultInput != "DROP" || c.DefaultOutput != "ACCEPT" || c.DefaultForward != "DROP" {
				t.Errorf("%s: settings = enabled %v, ipv6 %v, sysctl %q, policies %s/%s/%s", where, c.Enabled, c.IPv6,
					c.SysctlFile, c.DefaultInput, c.DefaultOutput, c.DefaultForward)
			}
			wantLog := "low"
			if sc == "logging" {
				wantLog = "high"
			}
			if c.LogLevel != wantLog {
				t.Errorf("%s: LogLevel = %q, want %q", where, c.LogLevel, wantLog)
			}
			switch sc {
			case "fresh", "enabled":
				if len(rules) != 0 {
					t.Errorf("%s: %d rules, want none", where, len(rules))
				}
			case "rules", "disabled", "logging", "sysctl":
				if len(rules) != len(goldenRulesScenario) {
					t.Errorf("%s: %d rules, want %d", where, len(rules), len(goldenRulesScenario))
				}
				goldenSameRules(t, where, rules, goldenRulesScenario)
			case "ipv6no":
				if len(rules) != 1 || len(c.Rules6) != 0 || rules[0].Family != model.FamilyV4 || rules[0].ToPort != "22" {
					t.Errorf("%s: rules = %+v", where, rules)
				}
			case "manual":
				goldenManual(t, where, rules)
			}
			if sc == "sysctl" {
				want := []fwstate.SysctlSetting{{Key: "net/ipv4/ip_forward", Value: "1"}, {Key: "net/ipv6/conf/default/forwarding", Value: "1"}}
				if len(c.Sysctl) < 2 || !slices.Equal(c.Sysctl[len(c.Sysctl)-2:], want) {
					t.Errorf("%s: Sysctl = %q, want it to end with %q", where, c.Sysctl, want)
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

// goldenManual checks the "manual" scenario: the rule set, then an
// application rule and a manual comment rule in both files, then the IPv6
// rule with host bits UFW keeps as written.
func goldenManual(t *testing.T, where string, rules []model.Rule) {
	t.Helper()
	if len(rules) != 11 {
		t.Errorf("%s: %d rules, want 11", where, len(rules))
		return
	}
	goldenSameRules(t, where, rules[:7], goldenRulesScenario[:7])
	if app := rules[7]; app.Raw == "" || app.Family != model.FamilyBoth || !strings.Contains(app.Raw, "DP%20Web") {
		t.Errorf("%s: application rule = %+v", where, app)
	}
	if hand := rules[8]; hand.Raw != "" || hand.Comment != "hand rule" || hand.Origin != model.OriginManual ||
		hand.Family != model.FamilyBoth || hand.ToPort != "8080" {
		t.Errorf("%s: hand rule = %+v", where, hand)
	}
	goldenSameRules(t, where, rules[9:10], goldenRulesScenario[7:])
	if host := rules[10]; host.Raw == "" || host.Family != model.FamilyV6 || !strings.Contains(host.Raw, "2001:db8::1/32") {
		t.Errorf("%s: host-bits rule = %+v", where, host)
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the capture script and run it**

Create `internal/modules/firewall/testdata/capture.sh`:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Captures UFW's state files and the loaded netfilter state for each
# firewall scenario on one OS image, as golden files for the firewall's
# readers, predictor and evaluator.
#
# Usage: capture.sh <image> <outdir>
#   for example: capture.sh ubuntu:24.04 internal/modules/firewall/testdata/golden
# Writes <outdir>/<image-slug>/<scenario>/. Runs everything inside a
# privileged container in its own network namespace, which it removes on
# exit; it never touches the host's firewall.
#
# For stable output the "# Generated by" and "# Completed on" lines of the
# save output are dropped and chain counters are written as [0:0]. A legacy
# table is captured only when it already exists in the container's network
# namespace (/proc/net/ip*_tables_names): asking for another one would make
# the host kernel load its module.
#
# The single-quoted scripts and the echoed commands run inside the
# container, so their expansions and escapes are meant to happen there.
# shellcheck disable=SC2016,SC2028
set -euo pipefail

if [ $# -ne 2 ]; then
	echo "usage: $0 <image> <outdir>" >&2
	exit 2
fi
image=$1
slug=$(printf '%s' "$image" | tr ':/' '--')
out=$2/$slug
name=dp-w1-cap-$slug

docker rm -f "$name" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
trap 'docker rm -f "$name" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT
docker run -d --privileged --name "$name" "$image" sleep infinity >/dev/null

dx() { docker exec -i "$name" bash -euo pipefail -c "$1"; }

dx 'apt-get update -qq >/dev/null && DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -qq ufw iptables nftables procps iproute2 >/dev/null 2>&1'

# The pristine files and sysctl values every scenario starts from.
dx 'mkdir -p /root/pristine && cp -a /etc/ufw /root/pristine/ufw && cp -a /etc/default/ufw /root/pristine/default-ufw
keys() {
	echo net/ipv4/ip_forward
	for d in all default $(ls /sys/class/net); do
		for k in net/ipv6/conf/$d/forwarding net/ipv6/conf/$d/accept_ra net/ipv4/conf/$d/rp_filter net/ipv4/conf/$d/accept_source_route; do
			[ -e /proc/sys/$k ] && echo $k
		done
	done
}
for k in $(keys); do echo "$k=$(cat /proc/sys/$k)"; done | sort > /root/pristine/sysctl.txt'

reset_state() {
	dx 'ufw --force reset >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
rm -rf /etc/ufw && cp -a /root/pristine/ufw /etc/ufw && cp -a /root/pristine/default-ufw /etc/default/ufw
nft flush ruleset
while IFS== read -r k v; do echo "$v" > /proc/sys/$k; done < /root/pristine/sysctl.txt'
}

# The rule set of the "rules" scenario.
rules_cmds="ufw allow in proto tcp to any port 22 comment 'darkpanel:01J00000000000000000000000 ssh'
ufw deny in proto udp from 2001:db8::/32 to any port 5000:5100
ufw route allow out on eth0 proto tcp to 172.17.0.2 port 80
ufw limit in proto tcp to any port 2222
ufw reject in to any port 3000
ufw allow in log proto tcp from 10.0.0.0/8 to any port 443,8000:8100
ufw allow out on eth0 to any port 53
ufw allow in on eth0 proto esp"

scenario_cmds() {
	case $1 in
	fresh) ;;
	enabled) echo "ufw --force enable" ;;
	rules) printf '%s\nufw --force enable\n' "$rules_cmds" ;;
	disabled) printf '%s\nufw --force enable\nufw disable\n' "$rules_cmds" ;;
	ipv6no)
		echo "sed -i 's/^IPV6=.*/IPV6=no/' /etc/default/ufw"
		echo "ufw allow in proto tcp to any port 22"
		echo "ufw --force enable"
		;;
	logging)
		printf '%s\nufw --force enable\n' "$rules_cmds"
		echo "ufw logging high"
		echo "ufw default allow outgoing"
		echo "ufw default deny routed"
		;;
	manual)
		printf '%s\nufw --force enable\n' "$rules_cmds"
		echo "printf '[DP Web]\\ntitle=Darkpanel test\\ndescription=Darkpanel test profile\\nports=8443,9443/tcp\\n' > /etc/ufw/applications.d/dp-test"
		echo "ufw allow 'DP Web'"
		echo "ufw deny from 2001:db8::1/32"
		echo "ufw allow 8080/tcp comment 'hand rule'"
		;;
	sysctl)
		echo "printf 'net/ipv4/ip_forward=1\nnet/ipv6/conf/default/forwarding=1\n' >> /etc/ufw/sysctl.conf"
		printf '%s\nufw --force enable\n' "$rules_cmds"
		;;
	esac
}

capture() {
	local dir=$out/$1
	rm -rf "$dir"
	mkdir -p "$dir/files/etc/ufw" "$dir/files/etc/default" "$dir/save"
	for f in user.rules user6.rules before.rules before6.rules after.rules after6.rules ufw.conf sysctl.conf; do
		docker exec "$name" cat "/etc/ufw/$f" > "$dir/files/etc/ufw/$f"
	done
	docker exec "$name" cat /etc/default/ufw > "$dir/files/etc/default/ufw"
	dx 'iptables --version; printf "ufw %s\n" "$(awk "/^Package: ufw\$/{p=1} p&&/^Version:/{print \$2; exit}" /var/lib/dpkg/status)"' > "$dir/version.txt"
	dx 'nft list tables' > "$dir/nft-tables.txt"
	local fam bin names t
	for fam in v4 v6; do
		bin=iptables names=ip_tables_names
		[ $fam = v6 ] && bin=ip6tables names=ip6_tables_names
		for t in filter nat raw mangle security; do
			dx "$bin-nft-save -t $t" | sed -e '/^# Generated by /d' -e '/^# Completed on /d' -e 's/^\(:.*\) \[[0-9]*:[0-9]*\]$/\1 [0:0]/' > "$dir/save/nft-$fam-$t.txt"
		done
		for t in $(dx "cat /proc/net/$names 2>/dev/null || true"); do
			dx "$bin-legacy-save -t $t" | sed -e '/^# Generated by /d' -e '/^# Completed on /d' -e 's/^\(:.*\) \[[0-9]*:[0-9]*\]$/\1 [0:0]/' > "$dir/save/legacy-$fam-$t.txt"
		done
	done
	dx 'for d in all default $(ls /sys/class/net); do
	for k in net/ipv6/conf/$d/forwarding net/ipv6/conf/$d/accept_ra net/ipv4/conf/$d/rp_filter net/ipv4/conf/$d/accept_source_route; do
		[ -e /proc/sys/$k ] && echo "$k=$(cat /proc/sys/$k)"
	done
done; echo "net/ipv4/ip_forward=$(cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward)"' | sort > "$dir/sysctl.txt"
}

for s in fresh enabled rules disabled ipv6no logging manual sysctl; do
	reset_state
	cmds=$(scenario_cmds $s)
	if [ -n "$cmds" ]; then
		dx "$cmds" >/dev/null
	fi
	capture $s
	printf '%s\n' "$cmds" | sed '/^$/d' > "$out/$s/commands.txt"
	echo "captured $slug/$s"
done
```

Then run from the repository root (the four images run in parallel; each uses its own container `dp-w1-cap-<slug>`):

```tsx
import { Link } from "react-router"
import { useQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query"
import { Alert, AlertDescription } from "darkraise-ui/components/alert"
import { Card, CardContent, CardHeader, CardTitle } from "darkraise-ui/components/card"
import { Spinner } from "darkraise-ui/components/spinner"
import { errorMessage, readResource } from "@/api/client"
import { AddRule } from "./rule-form"
import { RulesTable } from "./rules-table"
import { SnapshotsPanel } from "./snapshots-panel"
import { StateControls } from "./state-controls"
import { StatusBanners, StatusSummary } from "./status-panel"
import { FIREWALL_MODULE, statusQueryKey, type FirewallStatus } from "./types"

// FirewallPage is /hosts/:hostId/firewall: the configured and loaded
// state with its banners, the settings, and the rules.
export function FirewallPage({ hostId }: { hostId: string }) {
  const status = useQuery({
    queryKey: statusQueryKey(hostId),
    queryFn: () => readResource<FirewallStatus>(hostId, FIREWALL_MODULE, "status"),
  })
  if (status.isPending) return <Spinner aria-label="Loading the firewall" />
  if (status.isError) {
    return (
      <Alert variant="destructive" role="alert">
        <AlertDescription>{errorMessage(status.error)}</AlertDescription>
      </Alert>
    )
  }
  const s = status.data
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
      <StatusBanners hostId={hostId} status={s} />
      <StatusSummary status={s} />
      <StateControls key={JSON.stringify(s.configured) + String(s.active)} hostId={hostId} status={s} />
      <Card>
        <CardHeader>
          <CardTitle className="flex items-center justify-between gap-4">
            Rules
            <AddRule hostId={hostId} />
          </CardTitle>
        </CardHeader>
        <CardContent>
          <RulesTable hostId={hostId} rules={s.rules} />
        </CardContent>
      </Card>
      <Link to="snapshots" className="text-sm underline-offset-4 hover:underline">
        Snapshots
      </Link>
    </div>
  )
}

// SnapshotsPage is /hosts/:hostId/firewall/snapshots.
export function SnapshotsPage({ hostId }: { hostId: string }) {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
      <Link to=".." relative="path" className="text-sm underline-offset-4 hover:underline">
        Back to the firewall
      </Link>
      <Card>
        <CardHeader>
          <CardTitle>Snapshots</CardTitle>
        </CardHeader>
        <CardContent>
          <SnapshotsPanel hostId={hostId} />
        </CardContent>
      </Card>
    </div>
  )
}
```

**Interfaces:**

- Produces: `modules`, `module`, `options`, `portIn`, `toTri` and the conntrack fields of Part contracts Task 35

**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 1 - risk 3 = 5
**Lenses:** security

Models the `-m` matches spec 2.3 lists: `tcp`/`udp` ports and `--tcp-flags` (a new connection's first packet is SYN alone), `multiport`, `conntrack --ctstate` (with `DNAT`/`SNAT`), `--ctorigdst`, `--ctorigdstport`, `state`, `addrtype` (address types inferred from the routing path, Part constraints), `comment`; `rt` never matches; `icmp`/`icmp6` types, `hl`, `limit`, `recent` and `statistic` are undecidable. One false match makes a rule miss whatever the others say. The walker gains the original destination, port and DNAT flag that the conntrack matches read (Task 41 sets them). The test drives each match through `Evaluate` on a one-rule table, and checks that conntrack matches in the raw table are undecidable.

```go
// matchFilter is a filter table whose built-in chains drop by policy and
// accept what the one rule spec matches.
func matchFilter(spec string) string {
	return "*filter\n:INPUT DROP [0:0]\n:FORWARD DROP [0:0]\n:OUTPUT DROP [0:0]\n" +
		"-A INPUT " + spec + " -j ACCEPT\n" +
		"-A FORWARD " + spec + " -j ACCEPT\n" +
		"-A OUTPUT " + spec + " -j ACCEPT\n" +
		"COMMIT\n"
}

func matchForward(p *fwstate.Packet) {
	p.Path, p.OutIface, p.Dst = "forward", "eth1", netip.MustParseAddr("198.51.100.2")
}

func matchOutput(out string) func(p *fwstate.Packet) {
	return func(p *fwstate.Packet) {
		p.Path, p.InIface, p.OutIface = "output", "", out
		p.Src, p.Dst = netip.MustParseAddr("192.0.2.1"), netip.MustParseAddr("198.51.100.2")
	}
}

	p.Family = fwstate.V6
	p.Src, p.Dst = netip.MustParseAddr("2001:db8:1::7"), netip.MustParseAddr("2001:db8::1")
}

func TestMatchConntrackInRaw(t *testing.T) {
	w, err := newWalker(evalRuleset(t, matchFilter("-p tcp")), evalPacket(), nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	r := &netfilter.Rule{Matches: []netfilter.Match{{
		Module:  "conntrack",
		Options: []netfilter.Option{{Name: "ctstate", Values: []string{"NEW"}}},
	}}}
	if got, why := w.modules(&netfilter.Table{Name: "raw"}, r); got != maybe || why == "" {
		t.Fatalf("conntrack in raw = %v %q, want maybe with a reason", got, why)
	}
	if got, _ := w.modules(&netfilter.Table{Name: "filter"}, r); got != yes {
		t.Fatalf("conntrack in filter = %v, want yes", got)
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the implementation**

Create `internal/modules/firewall/eval/match.go`:

```go
package eval

import (
	"net/netip"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netfilter"
)

// modules evaluates the rule's -m matches. One false match makes the rule
// miss whatever the others say; otherwise the first undecidable match makes
// the rule undecidable.
func (w *walker) modules(t *netfilter.Table, r *netfilter.Rule) (tri, string) {
	res, why := yes, ""
	for _, m := range r.Matches {
		v, reason := w.module(t, m)
		switch {
		case v == no:
			return no, ""
		case v == maybe && res == yes:
			res, why = maybe, reason
		}
	}
	return res, why
}

func (w *walker) module(t *netfilter.Table, m netfilter.Match) (tri, string) {
	switch m.Module {
	case "comment":
		return yes, ""
	case "tcp", "udp":
		if !sameProto(m.Module, w.pkt.Proto) {
			return no, ""
		}
		return w.options(m, w.portOption)
	case "multiport":
		if !hasPorts(w.pkt.Proto) {
			return no, ""
		}
		return w.options(m, w.portOption)
	case "icmp", "icmp6":
		proto := map[string]string{"icmp": "icmp", "icmp6": "ipv6-icmp"}[m.Module]
		if !sameProto(proto, w.pkt.Proto) {
			return no, ""
		}
		return maybe, "ICMP types are not modelled"
	case "conntrack", "state":
		// The raw table runs before connection tracking attaches a
		// connection to the packet.
		if t.Name == "raw" {
			return maybe, "the raw table runs before connection tracking"
		}
		return w.options(m, w.conntrackOption)
	case "addrtype":
		return w.options(m, w.addrtypeOption)
	case "rt":
		// The packets the guard evaluates carry no IPv6 extension headers,
		// and the kernel's rt match never matches a packet without a
		// routing header, negated or not.
		return no, ""
	case "hl":
		return maybe, "the hop limit is not modelled"
	case "limit", "recent", "statistic":
		return maybe, "match " + m.Module + " depends on rates or earlier packets"
	}
	return maybe, "match " + m.Module + " is not modelled"
}

// options combines a module's options, each decided by check; a negated
// option inverts a decided result.
func (w *walker) options(m netfilter.Match, check func(o netfilter.Option) (tri, string)) (tri, string) {
	res, why := yes, ""
	for _, o := range m.Options {
		v, reason := check(o)
		if o.Neg && v != maybe {
			v = toTri(v == no)
		}
		switch {
		case v == no:
			return no, ""
		case v == maybe && res == yes:
			res, why = maybe, reason
		}
	}
	return res, why
}

func hasPorts(proto string) bool {
	for _, p := range []string{"tcp", "udp", "sctp", "dccp", "udplite"} {
		if sameProto(p, proto) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

func (w *walker) portOption(o netfilter.Option) (tri, string) {
	switch o.Name {
	case "sport", "sports":
		return portIn(o.Values[0], w.pkt.SrcPort)
	case "dport", "dports":
		return portIn(o.Values[0], w.pkt.DstPort)
	case "tcp-flags":
		return w.tcpFlags(o.Values[0], o.Values[1])
	}
	return maybe, "option --" + o.Name + " is not modelled"
}

// portIn reports whether port is in a list of ports and ranges as
// iptables-save prints them ("22", "1000:2000", "443,8000:8100").
func portIn(list string, port uint16) (tri, string) {
	for item := range strings.SplitSeq(list, ",") {
		lo, hi, ok := portRange(item)
		if !ok {
			return maybe, "port " + strconv.Quote(item) + " is not a number"
		}
		if lo <= port && port <= hi {
			return yes, ""
		}
	}
	return no, ""
}

func portRange(s string) (lo, hi uint16, ok bool) {
	a, b, isRange := strings.Cut(s, ":")
	if !isRange {
		b = a
	}
	if a == "" {
		a = "0"
	}
	if b == "" {
		b = "65535"
	}
	l, err1 := strconv.ParseUint(a, 10, 16)
	h, err2 := strconv.ParseUint(b, 10, 16)
	return uint16(l), uint16(h), err1 == nil && err2 == nil
}

var tcpFlagBits = map[string]uint8{
	"FIN": 0x01, "SYN": 0x02, "RST": 0x04, "PSH": 0x08, "ACK": 0x10, "URG": 0x20, "ALL": 0x3f, "NONE": 0,
}

// tcpFlags applies --tcp-flags. Only a new connection's first packet has
// known flags: SYN alone.
func (w *walker) tcpFlags(maskList, setList string) (tri, string) {
	if w.pkt.CtState != "NEW" {
		return maybe, "TCP flags are known only for a new connection's first packet"
	}
	mask, ok1 := flagSet(maskList)
	set, ok2 := flagSet(setList)
	if !ok1 || !ok2 {
		return maybe, "TCP flags " + maskList + " " + setList + " are not modelled"
	}
	if 0x02&mask == set {
		return yes, ""
	}
	return no, ""
}

func flagSet(list string) (uint8, bool) {
	var bits uint8
	for name := range strings.SplitSeq(list, ",") {
		b, ok := tcpFlagBits[name]
		if !ok {
			return 0, false
		}
		bits |= b
	}
	return bits, true
}

func (w *walker) conntrackOption(o netfilter.Option) (tri, string) {
	isNew := w.pkt.CtState == "NEW"
	switch o.Name {
	case "ctstate", "state":
		return w.ctstate(o.Values[0])
	case "ctorigdst":
		if !isNew {
			return maybe, "the original destination is known only for a new connection"
		}
		pfx, err := netip.ParsePrefix(o.Values[0])
		if err != nil {
			a, err := netip.ParseAddr(o.Values[0])
			if err != nil {
				return maybe, "original destination " + strconv.Quote(o.Values[0]) + " is not an address"
			}
			pfx = netip.PrefixFrom(a, a.BitLen())
		}
		return toTri(pfx.Contains(w.origDst)), ""
	case "ctorigdstport":
		if !isNew {
			return maybe, "the original destination is known only for a new connection"
		}
		return portIn(o.Values[0], w.origPort)
	}
	return maybe, "option --" + o.Name + " is not modelled"
}

// ctstate matches a conntrack state list. The DNAT and SNAT states say
// whether the connection's destination or source was rewritten, which the
// walk knows only for a connection it sees start.
func (w *walker) ctstate(list string) (tri, string) {
	has := func(dnat, snat bool) bool {
		for s := range strings.SplitSeq(list, ",") {
			if s == w.pkt.CtState || s == "DNAT" && dnat || s == "SNAT" && snat {
				return true
			}
		}
		return false
	}
	if w.pkt.CtState == "NEW" {
		// SNAT is applied in nat POSTROUTING, after every filtering hook.
		return toTri(has(w.dnat, false)), ""
	}
	v := has(false, false)
	if v != has(true, false) || v != has(false, true) || v != has(true, true) {
		return maybe, "the connection's NAT state is known only for a new connection"
	}
	return toTri(v), ""
}

func (w *walker) addrtypeOption(o netfilter.Option) (tri, string) {
	var dst bool
	switch o.Name {
	case "src-type":
	case "dst-type":
		dst = true
	default:
		return maybe, "option --" + o.Name + " is not modelled"
	}
	res, why := no, ""
	for typ := range strings.SplitSeq(o.Values[0], ",") {
		switch v, reason := w.addrType(dst, typ); v {
		case yes:
			return yes, ""
		case maybe:
			res, why = maybe, reason
		}
	}
	return res, why
}

// addrType reports whether the packet's source or destination has an
// address type, as the routing decision implies: a packet on the input
// path is addressed to this host and one on the forward path is not; a
// locally generated packet is addressed to this host when it leaves
// through lo. Only a packet arriving on lo or generated here has a local
// source.
func (w *walker) addrType(dst bool, typ string) (tri, string) {
	a := w.pkt.Src
	local := w.pkt.Path == "output" || w.pkt.InIface == "lo"
	if dst {
		a = w.pkt.Dst
		local = w.pkt.Path == "input" || w.pkt.Path == "output" && w.pkt.OutIface == "lo"
	}
	switch {
	case a.IsMulticast():
		return toTri(typ == "MULTICAST"), ""
	case dst && a == netip.AddrFrom4([4]byte{255, 255, 255, 255}):
		return toTri(typ == "BROADCAST"), ""
	}
	switch typ {
	case "LOCAL":
		return toTri(local), ""
	case "BROADCAST", "MULTICAST":
		return no, ""
	case "UNICAST":
		if local || dst {
			return toTri(!local), ""
		}
		return maybe, "whether the kernel has a unicast route back to the source is not known"
	}
	return maybe, "address type " + typ + " is not modelled"
}

func toTri(b bool) tri {
	if b {
		return yes
	}
	return no
}
```

**Lenses:** security

Places each flow on the host (spec 2.3 "Protected flows"): an incoming flow on every eligible in-interface (up, non-loopback; for IPv4 strict `rp_filter` keeps only the interface of the route back), the out-interface of output and forwarded flows from route lookups, and the `fwstate.Router` the evaluator calls after nat `PREROUTING`. Every lookup that cannot be resolved makes the flow `unknown`, except that a stand-in destination without a route has nothing to protect. The tests cover strict, loose and predicted `rp_filter`, IPv6, unspecified addresses, fixed interfaces, failed and multipath lookups, forwarding off, and every Router branch.

```go
package guard

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net/netip"
	"os"

	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netstat"
)

// rtQuery is a route lookup; src and iif may be empty.
func rtQuery(dst, src, iif string) netstat.RouteQuery {
	q := netstat.RouteQuery{Dst: netip.MustParseAddr(dst), IIF: iif}
	if src != "" {
		q.Src = netip.MustParseAddr(src)
	}
	return q
}

// rtVia is a unicast route through iface with a preferred source.
func rtVia(iface, prefSrc string) netstat.Route {
	r := netstat.Route{Type: "unicast", OutIface: iface}
	if prefSrc != "" {
		r.PrefSrc = netip.MustParseAddr(prefSrc)
	}
	return r
}

// rtFacts are the facts of gIfaces with the given live rp_filter values for
// all, eth0 and eth1.
func rtFacts(all, eth0, eth1 int) facts {
	return facts{ifaces: gIfaces(), rpFilter: map[string]int{"all": all, "eth0": eth0, "eth1": eth1}}
}

// rtProbe is a probe of a packet that was evaluated.
func rtProbe(desc string, p fwstate.Packet, in, out string) probe {
	p.InIface, p.OutIface = in, out
	return probe{desc: desc, pkt: p}
}

func TestRouterRoute(t *testing.T) {
	fwd := flOn("eth0", flPkt("input", "198.51.100.1", 49152, "172.17.0.2", 80, "tcp"))
	out := flPkt("output", "192.0.2.1", 40100, "198.51.100.9", 7443, "tcp")
	toDocker := rtQuery("172.17.0.2", "198.51.100.1", "eth0")
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name      string
		p         fwstate.Packet
		sysctl    map[string]string
		routes    map[netstat.RouteQuery]netstat.Route
		routeErrs map[netstat.RouteQuery]error
		path, oif string
		err       string
	}{
		{name: "a host address", p: flOn("eth0", flPkt("input", "198.51.100.1", 49152, "10.0.0.1", 80, "tcp")), path: "input"},
		{name: "a loopback address", p: flOn("eth0", flPkt("input", "198.51.100.1", 49152, "127.0.0.2", 80, "tcp")), path: "input"},
		{name: "forwarded", p: fwd, routes: map[netstat.RouteQuery]netstat.Route{toDocker: rtVia("docker0", "")}, path: "forward", oif: "docker0"},
		{name: "a local route", p: fwd, routes: map[netstat.RouteQuery]netstat.Route{toDocker: {Type: "local", OutIface: "lo"}}, path: "input"},
		{name: "forwarding off", p: fwd, sysctl: map[string]string{"net/ipv4/ip_forward": "0"}, err: "firewall: forwarding is off (net/ipv4/ip_forward = 0)"},
		{name: "no route", p: fwd, err: "firewall: route to 172.17.0.2 from 198.51.100.1 on eth0: netstat: no route"},
		{name: "multipath", p: fwd, routes: map[netstat.RouteQuery]netstat.Route{toDocker: rtVia("", "")}, err: "firewall: the route to 172.17.0.2 has no single out-interface"},
		{name: "outbound", p: out, routes: map[netstat.RouteQuery]netstat.Route{rtQuery("198.51.100.9", "192.0.2.1", ""): rtVia("eth1", "")}, path: "output", oif: "eth1"},
		{name: "outbound without a route", p: out, err: "firewall: route to 198.51.100.9: netstat: no route"},
		{name: "outbound multipath", p: out, routes: map[netstat.RouteQuery]netstat.Route{rtQuery("198.51.100.9", "192.0.2.1", ""): rtVia("", "")},
			err: "firewall: the route to 198.51.100.9 has no single out-interface"},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			r := newRouter(&gHost{routes: tc.routes, routeErrs: tc.routeErrs}, rtFacts(0, 0, 0), fwstate.Loaded{Sysctl: tc.sysctl})
			path, oif, err := r.route(tc.p)
			if tc.err != "" {
				if err == nil || err.Error() != tc.err {
					t.Fatalf("route error = %v, want %q", err, tc.err)
				}
				if strings.Contains(tc.err, "no route") && !errors.Is(err, netstat.ErrNoRoute) {
					t.Errorf("error %v does not wrap ErrNoRoute", err)
				}
				return
			}
			if err != nil || path != tc.path || oif != tc.oif {
				t.Errorf("route = %q, %q, %v; want %q, %q", path, oif, err, tc.path, tc.oif)
			}
		})
	}
}
```

```go
package guard

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net/netip"
	"strconv"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netstat"
)

// probe is one packet the guard evaluates, or a flow it cannot evaluate.
type probe struct {
	desc    string         // FlowResult.Flow
	pkt     fwstate.Packet // with its in- and out-interface
	unknown string         // non-empty: not evaluated, and why
}

// router places flows on this host's interfaces and routes. Its route
// method is the fwstate.Router the evaluator calls.
type router struct {
	host  Host
	f     facts
	st    fwstate.Loaded
	local map[netip.Addr]bool
}

func newRouter(h Host, f facts, st fwstate.Loaded) *router {
	return &router{host: h, f: f, st: st, local: localAddrs(f.ifaces)}
}

// probes turns a flow into the packets to evaluate: an incoming flow
// without a fixed in-interface on every eligible in-interface, any other
// flow once with the out-interface its route gives. A route that cannot be
// resolved makes the flow unknown, except that a stand-in destination
// without a route of its family has nothing to protect.
func (r *router) probes(fl flow) []probe {
	if fl.unknown != "" {
		return []probe{{desc: fl.label, unknown: fl.unknown}}
	}
	p := fl.pkt
	fail := func(reason string) []probe { return []probe{{desc: describe(fl.label, p), unknown: reason}} }
	lookup := func(q netstat.RouteQuery) (netstat.Route, bool, []probe) {
		rt, err := r.host.RouteGet(q)
		switch {
		case err != nil && fl.standIn && errors.Is(err, netstat.ErrNoRoute):
			return rt, false, nil
		case err != nil:
			return rt, false, fail(fmt.Sprintf("the route to %s cannot be resolved: %v", q.Dst, err))
		case rt.Type != "local" && rt.OutIface == "":
			return rt, false, fail(fmt.Sprintf("the route to %s has no single out-interface", q.Dst))
		}
		return rt, true, nil
	}
	switch p.Path {
	case "output":
		q := netstat.RouteQuery{Dst: p.Dst}
		if !p.Src.IsUnspecified() {
			q.Src = p.Src
		}
		rt, ok, out := lookup(q)
		if !ok {
			return out
		}
		if p.Src.IsUnspecified() {
			if !rt.PrefSrc.IsValid() {
				return fail(fmt.Sprintf("the route to %s has no source address", p.Dst))
			}
			p.Src = rt.PrefSrc.Unmap()
		}
		p.OutIface = rt.OutIface
		return []probe{{desc: describe(fl.label, p), pkt: p}}
	case "forward":
		if off := r.forwardingOff(p.Family); off != "" {
			return fail(off)
		}
		rt, ok, out := lookup(netstat.RouteQuery{Dst: p.Dst, Src: p.Src, IIF: p.InIface})
		if !ok {
			return out
		}
		if rt.Type == "local" {
			p.Path = "input"
		} else {
			p.OutIface = rt.OutIface
		}
		return []probe{{desc: describe(fl.label, p), pkt: p}}
	}
	if p.Dst.IsUnspecified() {
		rt, err := r.host.RouteGet(netstat.RouteQuery{Dst: p.Src})
		if err != nil {
			return fail(fmt.Sprintf("the route back to %s cannot be resolved: %v", p.Src, err))
		}
		if !rt.PrefSrc.IsValid() {
			return fail(fmt.Sprintf("the route back to %s has no source address", p.Src))
		}
		p.Dst = rt.PrefSrc.Unmap()
	}
	if p.InIface != "" {
		return []probe{{desc: describe(fl.label, p), pkt: p}}
	}
	ifaces, err := r.eligible(p)
	if err != nil {
		return fail(err.Error())
	}
	if len(ifaces) == 0 {
		return fail("no interface can receive the flow")
	}
	out := make([]probe, 0, len(ifaces))
	for _, name := range ifaces {
		q := p
		q.InIface = name
		out = append(out, probe{desc: describe(fl.label, q), pkt: q})
	}
	return out
}

// eligible lists the in-interfaces an incoming packet may arrive on: every
// up, non-loopback interface, except that for IPv4 an interface under
// strict reverse-path filtering takes only packets whose route back to the
// source leaves through it.
func (r *router) eligible(p fwstate.Packet) ([]string, error) {
	var out []string
	back := ""
	looked := false
	for _, i := range r.f.ifaces {
		if !i.Up || i.Loopback {
			continue
		}
		if p.Family == fwstate.V4 {
			rp, err := r.rpFilter(i.Name)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			if rp == 1 {
				if !looked {
					q := netstat.RouteQuery{Dst: p.Src}
					if r.local[p.Dst] {
						q.Src = p.Dst
					}
					rt, err := r.host.RouteGet(q)
					if err != nil {
						return nil, fmt.Errorf("the route back to %s cannot be resolved: %w", p.Src, err)
					}
					back, looked = rt.OutIface, true
				}
				if back != i.Name {
					continue
				}
			}
		}
		out = append(out, i.Name)
	}
	return out, nil
}

// rpFilter is an interface's effective rp_filter: the larger of all's and
// the interface's value, each from the state being checked when it holds
// the key and from the live host otherwise.
func (r *router) rpFilter(name string) (int, error) {
	eff := 0
	for _, n := range []string{"all", name} {
		key := "net/ipv4/conf/" + n + "/rp_filter"
		v, ok := r.f.rpFilter[n]
		if s, has := r.st.Sysctl[key]; has {
			parsed, err := strconv.Atoi(s)
			if err != nil {
				return 0, fmt.Errorf("%s is %q in the checked state, not a number", key, s)
			}
			v, ok = parsed, true
		}
		if !ok {
			return 0, fmt.Errorf("%s was not read", key)
		}
		eff = max(eff, v)
	}
	return eff, nil
}

// forwardingOff says why the checked state forwards no packet of family
// fam, or "" when it does or does not say.
func (r *router) forwardingOff(fam fwstate.Family) string {
	key := "net/ipv4/ip_forward"
	if fam == fwstate.V6 {
		key = "net/ipv6/conf/all/forwarding"
	}
	if r.st.Sysctl[key] == "0" {
		return "forwarding is off (" + key + " = 0)"
	}
	return ""
}

// route is the evaluator's fwstate.Router: where a packet goes once nat
// PREROUTING has set its destination.
func (r *router) route(p fwstate.Packet) (string, string, error) {
	dst := p.Dst.Unmap()
	if dst.IsLoopback() || r.local[dst] {
		return "input", "", nil
	}
	if p.Path == "output" {
		rt, err := r.host.RouteGet(netstat.RouteQuery{Dst: dst, Src: p.Src})
		switch {
		case err != nil:
			return "", "", fmt.Errorf("firewall: route to %s: %w", dst, err)
		case rt.OutIface == "":
			return "", "", fmt.Errorf("firewall: the route to %s has no single out-interface", dst)
		}
		return "output", rt.OutIface, nil
	}
	if off := r.forwardingOff(p.Family); off != "" {
		return "", "", errors.New("firewall: " + off)
	}
	rt, err := r.host.RouteGet(netstat.RouteQuery{Dst: dst, Src: p.Src, IIF: p.InIface})
	switch {
	case err != nil:
		return "", "", fmt.Errorf("firewall: route to %s from %s on %s: %w", dst, p.Src, p.InIface, err)
	case rt.Type == "local":
		return "input", "", nil
	case rt.OutIface == "":
		return "", "", fmt.Errorf("firewall: the route to %s has no single out-interface", dst)
	}
	return "forward", rt.OutIface, nil
}

// describe names a flow for the guard's message: label, protocol when not
// TCP, addresses and the interfaces known so far.
func describe(label string, p fwstate.Packet) string {
	s := label
	if p.Proto != "tcp" {
		s += " " + p.Proto
	}
	s += " from " + p.Src.String() + " to " + netip.AddrPortFrom(p.Dst, p.DstPort).String()
	if p.InIface != "" {
		s += " on " + p.InIface
	}
	if p.OutIface != "" {
		s += " out " + p.OutIface
	}
	return s
}
```

The firewall's own migration and the store over `env.DB` (spec 2.5, store and retention). A snapshot row holds the state files as restore entries, the logical state, the hash of each file at capture and, once the change applied, right after it. The task covers inserting a row (the host's first row becomes the never-pruned baseline), reading it, listing newest first, attaching the change id (and the engine's system flag), recording the post-apply hashes, pinning and unpinning, and pruning by retention: 50 non-system and 10 system unpinned snapshots, plus those of unfinished changes, pinned ones, the baseline and the snapshot of a restore in progress. It also covers the one-row record of a restore in progress. The tests run on a temporary database with the core's and the firewall's migrations applied. They prove the round trip, including binary file data and the before-image, the order and filters of the list, attaching rules, pin and post-hash updates, every retention rule, and the restore record's replacement.

```go
func TestSnapshotRetention(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	db := fwTestDB(t)
	save := func(s snapshot) {
		t.Helper()
		if _, err := saveSnapshot(ctx, db, s); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	// n=1 becomes the baseline; 2 to 6 are old and each protected one way.
	save(stTestSnap(1, false))
	pinned := stTestSnap(2, false)
	pinned.Pinned = true
	save(pinned)
	for n, state := range map[int]string{3: "needs_repair", 4: "pending", 5: "applying", 6: "confirmed"} {
		s := stTestSnap(n, false)
		s.ChangeID = fmt.Sprintf("c-%d", n)
		stTestChange(t, db, s.ChangeID, state, false)
		save(s)
	}
	save(stTestSnap(7, false))
	if err := beginRestore(ctx, db, stTestSnap(7, false).ID, fwstate.TransReload, stTestT0); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	save(stTestSnap(8, true))
	for n := 100; n < 100+keepSnapshots; n++ {
		save(stTestSnap(n, false))
	}
	for n := 200; n < 200+keepSystemSnapshots; n++ {
		save(stTestSnap(n, true))
	}
	ids := stTestIDs(t, db)
	for n, want := range map[int]bool{1: true, 2: true, 3: true, 4: true, 5: true, 6: false, 7: true, 8: false, 100: true, 149: true, 200: true, 209: true} {
		if got := ids[stTestSnap(n, false).ID]; got != want {
			t.Errorf("snapshot %d kept = %v, want %v", n, got, want)
		}
	}
	if want := 6 + keepSnapshots + keepSystemSnapshots; len(ids) != want {
		t.Errorf("%d snapshots kept, want %d", len(ids), want)
	}
	// One more of each kind pushes out the oldest unprotected one of that kind only.
	save(stTestSnap(150, false))
	save(stTestSnap(210, true))
	ids = stTestIDs(t, db)
	if ids[stTestSnap(100, false).ID] || ids[stTestSnap(200, true).ID] {
		t.Error("the oldest unpinned snapshot of each kind was not pruned")
	}
	if !ids[stTestSnap(101, false).ID] || !ids[stTestSnap(201, true).ID] || !ids[stTestSnap(7, false).ID] {
		t.Error("retention pruned a snapshot it keeps")
	}
}

	}
	if err := beginRestore(ctx, db, b.ID, fwstate.TransEnable, stTestT0); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, ok, _ := restoreIntent(ctx, db, a.ID); ok {
		t.Error("a new restore kept the superseded restore's record")
	}
	if id, ok, err := pendingRestore(ctx, db); err != nil || !ok || id != b.ID {
		t.Errorf("pendingRestore = %s, %v, %v", id, ok, err)
	}
	if err := endRestore(ctx, db, b.ID); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, ok, _ := pendingRestore(ctx, db); ok {
		t.Error("endRestore left the record")
	}
}
```

Create `internal/modules/firewall/migrations/agent/0001_firewall.sql` (create the directory `internal/modules/firewall/migrations/agent/` first):

```sql
-- The firewall's logical snapshots (spec 2.5), read and written only
-- through internal/modules/firewall. Times are fixed-width RFC 3339 UTC
-- text, so they compare as text.
--
-- A snapshot is captured before its change exists, so change_id is NULL
-- until the change's Apply or Revert attaches it. entries holds UFW's state
-- files as core.RestoreEntry values (Data base64), state the logical state
-- (live sysctl values, the recorded guard context, a repair's loaded-state
-- before-image, the Docker integration flag), hashes each file's hash at
-- capture and post_hashes each file's hash right after the change applied.
CREATE TABLE firewall_snapshots (
    id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    created_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
    change_id   TEXT,
    actor       TEXT NOT NULL,
    system      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (system IN (0, 1)),
    pinned      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (pinned IN (0, 1)),
    baseline    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (baseline IN (0, 1)),
    entries     TEXT NOT NULL,
    state       TEXT NOT NULL,
    hashes      TEXT NOT NULL,
    post_hashes TEXT
) STRICT;
CREATE INDEX firewall_snapshots_retention ON firewall_snapshots (system, pinned, baseline, created_at);
CREATE INDEX firewall_snapshots_change ON firewall_snapshots (change_id);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX firewall_snapshots_baseline ON firewall_snapshots (baseline) WHERE baseline = 1;

-- A restore in progress: written before the first file and deleted after
-- the restore verified, so a restore cut off by a crash is finished by
-- restoring the same snapshot with the same UFW transition. At most one row
-- exists, because a new restore supersedes an unfinished one.
CREATE TABLE firewall_restores (
    snapshot_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES firewall_snapshots (id),
    transition  TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (transition IN ('none', 'reload', 'enable', 'disable')),
    started_at  TEXT NOT NULL
) STRICT;
```

Create `internal/modules/firewall/store.go`:

```go
package firewall

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"database/sql"
	"embed"
	"encoding/hex"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io/fs"
	"time"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/store"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
)

//go:embed migrations/agent/*.sql
var migrationsFS embed.FS

// agentMigrations returns the module's agent-side migrations, the value of
// Manifest.Migrations[core.SideAgent].
func agentMigrations() fs.FS {
	sub, err := fs.Sub(migrationsFS, "migrations/agent")
	if err != nil {
		// fs.Sub fails only for an invalid path, and this one is a constant.
		panic(err)
	}
	return sub
}

// snapshotTimeFormat is the fixed-width form of every stored time, so times
// compare as text.
const snapshotTimeFormat = "2006-01-02T15:04:05.000000000Z"

// Retention (spec 2.5): the newest unpinned snapshots kept per kind.
const (
	keepSnapshots       = 50
	keepSystemSnapshots = 10
)

// errSnapshotNotFound is wrapped by every store function that finds no
// snapshot to act on.
var errSnapshotNotFound = errors.New("firewall: snapshot not found")

// snapshot is one firewall_snapshots row.
type snapshot struct {
	ID         string
	CreatedAt  time.Time
	ChangeID   string // "" until a change attaches it
	Actor      string
	System     bool // the change is a background task's (core_changes.system)
	Pinned     bool // never pruned; set while the change needs repair
	Baseline   bool // the host's first snapshot, never pruned
	Entries    []core.RestoreEntry
	State      snapshotState
	Hashes     map[string]string // fileHash of every entry at capture, by path
	PostHashes map[string]string // fileHash of every entry right after the change applied; nil until recorded
}

// snapshotState is a snapshot's logical state, the state column (spec 2.1,
// 2.3, 2.5).
type snapshotState struct {
	Enabled bool               `json:"enabled"`               // ufw.conf ENABLED at capture
	Sysctl  map[string]string  `json:"sysctl"`                // every supported key's live value at capture, in /proc/sys form
	Guard   *core.GuardContext `json:"guard,omitempty"`       // the guard context of the change's plan, for the connectivity exception
	Image   *beforeImage       `json:"beforeImage,omitempty"` // a repair's loaded-state before-image
	Docker  bool               `json:"docker"`                // the Docker integration flag; false until the integration exists
}

// snapshotFilter narrows listSnapshots.
type snapshotFilter struct {
	System *bool // only system (true) or only non-system (false) snapshots; nil for both
	Limit  int   // at most this many rows; 0 for all
}

// fileHash is the comparable form of a state file: "sha256:<hex>" of its
// bytes, or "absent".
func fileHash(e core.RestoreEntry) string {
	if !e.Present {
		return "absent"
	}
	sum := sha256.Sum256(e.Data)
	return "sha256:" + hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
}

func formatSnapshotTime(t time.Time) string { return t.UTC().Format(snapshotTimeFormat) }

// saveSnapshot inserts s, makes it the baseline when the host has none yet,
// and prunes by retention, in one transaction. It returns s as stored.
func saveSnapshot(ctx context.Context, db *store.DB, s snapshot) (snapshot, error) {
	entries, err := json.Marshal(s.Entries)
	if err != nil {
		return s, fmt.Errorf("firewall: encode snapshot entries: %w", err)
	}
	state, err := json.Marshal(s.State)
	if err != nil {
		return s, fmt.Errorf("firewall: encode snapshot state: %w", err)
	}
	hashes, err := json.Marshal(s.Hashes)
	if err != nil {
		return s, fmt.Errorf("firewall: encode snapshot hashes: %w", err)
	}
	var post any
	if s.PostHashes != nil {
		b, err := json.Marshal(s.PostHashes)
		if err != nil {
			return s, fmt.Errorf("firewall: encode snapshot post hashes: %w", err)
		}
		post = string(b)
	}
	var change any
	if s.ChangeID != "" {
		change = s.ChangeID
	}
	err = db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error {
		var baselines int
		if err := tx.QueryRowContext(ctx, "SELECT count(*) FROM firewall_snapshots WHERE baseline = 1").Scan(&baselines); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		s.Baseline = baselines == 0
		if _, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx,
			`INSERT INTO firewall_snapshots (id, created_at, change_id, actor, system, pinned, baseline, entries, state,
			 hashes, post_hashes)
			 VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
			s.ID, formatSnapshotTime(s.CreatedAt), change, s.Actor, s.System, s.Pinned, s.Baseline, string(entries),
			string(state), string(hashes), post); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		_, err := pruneSnapshots(ctx, tx)
		return err
	})
	if err != nil {
		return s, fmt.Errorf("firewall: save snapshot %s: %w", s.ID, err)
	}
	return s, nil
}

// pruneSnapshots deletes the snapshots retention no longer keeps (spec 2.5)
// and returns how many. It keeps the newest keepSnapshots unpinned
// snapshots of non-system changes and the newest keepSystemSnapshots of
// system changes, every pinned or baseline snapshot, every snapshot whose
// change is pending, applying or needs_repair, and the snapshot of a
// restore in progress. An unattached snapshot counts as a non-system
// change's unless its actor made it system.
func pruneSnapshots(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx) (int64, error) {
	res, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx,
		`DELETE FROM firewall_snapshots
		 WHERE pinned = 0 AND baseline = 0
		   AND id NOT IN (SELECT snapshot_id FROM firewall_restores)
		   AND (change_id IS NULL OR change_id NOT IN
		        (SELECT id FROM core_changes WHERE state IN ('pending', 'applying', 'needs_repair')))
		   AND id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM firewall_snapshots WHERE pinned = 0 AND baseline = 0 AND system = 0
		                  ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT ?)
		   AND id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM firewall_snapshots WHERE pinned = 0 AND baseline = 0 AND system = 1
		                  ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT ?)`,
		keepSnapshots, keepSystemSnapshots)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("firewall: prune snapshots: %w", err)
	}
	return res.RowsAffected()
}

const snapshotColumns = "id, created_at, change_id, actor, system, pinned, baseline, state, hashes, post_hashes"

type rowScanner interface{ Scan(dest ...any) error }

// scanSnapshot reads snapshotColumns, then entries when withEntries.
func scanSnapshot(row rowScanner, withEntries bool) (snapshot, error) {
	var s snapshot
	var created, state, hashes string
	var change, post, entries sql.NullString
	dest := []any{&s.ID, &created, &change, &s.Actor, &s.System, &s.Pinned, &s.Baseline, &state, &hashes, &post}
	if withEntries {
		dest = append(dest, &entries)
	}
	if err := row.Scan(dest...); err != nil {
		return s, err
	}
	t, err := time.Parse(snapshotTimeFormat, created)
	if err != nil {
		return s, fmt.Errorf("firewall: snapshot %s: created_at %q: %w", s.ID, created, err)
	}
	s.CreatedAt, s.ChangeID = t, change.String
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(state), &s.State); err != nil {
		return s, fmt.Errorf("firewall: snapshot %s: state: %w", s.ID, err)
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(hashes), &s.Hashes); err != nil {
		return s, fmt.Errorf("firewall: snapshot %s: hashes: %w", s.ID, err)
	}
	if post.Valid {
		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(post.String), &s.PostHashes); err != nil {
			return s, fmt.Errorf("firewall: snapshot %s: post hashes: %w", s.ID, err)
		}
	}
	if withEntries {
		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(entries.String), &s.Entries); err != nil {
			return s, fmt.Errorf("firewall: snapshot %s: entries: %w", s.ID, err)
		}
	}
	return s, nil
}

// getSnapshot returns the snapshot id with its entries.
func getSnapshot(ctx context.Context, db *store.DB, id string) (snapshot, error) {
	s, err := scanSnapshot(db.Read().QueryRowContext(ctx,
		"SELECT "+snapshotColumns+", entries FROM firewall_snapshots WHERE id = ?", id), true)
	if errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows) {
		return s, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", errSnapshotNotFound, id)
	}
	if err != nil {
		return s, fmt.Errorf("firewall: read snapshot %s: %w", id, err)
	}
	return s, nil
}

// listSnapshots returns snapshots newest first, without their entries.
func listSnapshots(ctx context.Context, db *store.DB, f snapshotFilter) ([]snapshot, error) {
	q := "SELECT " + snapshotColumns + " FROM firewall_snapshots"
	var args []any
	if f.System != nil {
		q += " WHERE system = ?"
		args = append(args, *f.System)
	}
	q += " ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC"
	if f.Limit > 0 {
		q += " LIMIT ?"
		args = append(args, f.Limit)
	}
	rows, err := db.Read().QueryContext(ctx, q, args...)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("firewall: list snapshots: %w", err)
	}
	defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
	var out []snapshot
	for rows.Next() {
		s, err := scanSnapshot(rows, false)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("firewall: list snapshots: %w", err)
		}
		out = append(out, s)
	}
	if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("firewall: list snapshots: %w", err)
	}
	return out, nil
}

// attachTx records changeID on snapshot id and copies the change's system
// flag when the change row exists. Attaching the same change again is a
// no-op; a snapshot attached to another change is refused.
func attachTx(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx, id, changeID string) error {
	res, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx,
		`UPDATE firewall_snapshots
		 SET change_id = ?, system = coalesce((SELECT system FROM core_changes WHERE id = ?), system)
		 WHERE id = ? AND (change_id IS NULL OR change_id = ?)`,
		changeID, changeID, id, changeID)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if n, err := res.RowsAffected(); err != nil || n == 1 {
		return err
	}
	var other sql.NullString
	err = tx.QueryRowContext(ctx, "SELECT change_id FROM firewall_snapshots WHERE id = ?", id).Scan(&other)
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", errSnapshotNotFound, id)
	case err != nil:
		return err
	}
	return fmt.Errorf("firewall: snapshot %s belongs to change %s, not %s", id, other.String, changeID)
}

// attachSnapshot records changeID on snapshot id (attachTx).
func attachSnapshot(ctx context.Context, db *store.DB, id, changeID string) error {
	if err := db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error { return attachTx(ctx, tx, id, changeID) }); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("firewall: attach snapshot %s: %w", id, err)
	}
	return nil
}

// attachNewest attaches changeID to the snapshot captured for it and
// returns that snapshot's id: the one already attached to changeID, else
// the newest unattached one. The engine captures a revertible change's
// snapshot and persists the change under one lock, and the change holds the
// firewall lock from then on, so no other firewall snapshot can be captured
// between them; older unattached snapshots belong to applies that never
// started.
func attachNewest(ctx context.Context, db *store.DB, changeID string) (string, error) {
	var id string
	err := db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error {
		err := tx.QueryRowContext(ctx, "SELECT id FROM firewall_snapshots WHERE change_id = ?", changeID).Scan(&id)
		if !errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows) {
			return err
		}
		err = tx.QueryRowContext(ctx,
			"SELECT id FROM firewall_snapshots WHERE change_id IS NULL ORDER BY rowid DESC LIMIT 1").Scan(&id)
		if errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows) {
			return fmt.Errorf("%w: none is unattached", errSnapshotNotFound)
		}
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		return attachTx(ctx, tx, id, changeID)
	})
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("firewall: attach the snapshot of change %s: %w", changeID, err)
	}
	return id, nil
}

// snapshotOfChange returns the id of the snapshot attached to changeID.
func snapshotOfChange(ctx context.Context, db *store.DB, changeID string) (string, error) {
	var id string
	err := db.Read().QueryRowContext(ctx, "SELECT id FROM firewall_snapshots WHERE change_id = ?", changeID).Scan(&id)
	if errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows) {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: change %s has none", errSnapshotNotFound, changeID)
	}
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("firewall: read the snapshot of change %s: %w", changeID, err)
	}
	return id, nil
}

// updateSnapshot runs query, an UPDATE of one snapshot whose last
// parameter is the id, and fails when no row matched.
func updateSnapshot(ctx context.Context, db *store.DB, id, query string, args ...any) error {
	return db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error {
		res, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, query, append(args, id)...)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("firewall: update snapshot %s: %w", id, err)
		}
		if n, err := res.RowsAffected(); err != nil || n == 0 {
			return errors.Join(err, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", errSnapshotNotFound, id))
		}
		return nil
	})
}

// setPostHashes records the hash of every state file right after the
// change applied (spec 2.5).
func setPostHashes(ctx context.Context, db *store.DB, id string, hashes map[string]string) error {
	b, err := json.Marshal(hashes)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("firewall: encode post hashes: %w", err)
	}
	return updateSnapshot(ctx, db, id, "UPDATE firewall_snapshots SET post_hashes = ? WHERE id = ?", string(b))
}

// setPinned pins or unpins snapshot id. A pinned snapshot is never pruned;
// the baseline flag is separate, so unpinning never exposes the baseline.
func setPinned(ctx context.Context, db *store.DB, id string, pinned bool) error {
	return updateSnapshot(ctx, db, id, "UPDATE firewall_snapshots SET pinned = ? WHERE id = ?", pinned)
}

// beginRestore records a restore of snapshot id with transition tr, in place
// of any unfinished restore.
func beginRestore(ctx context.Context, db *store.DB, id string, tr fwstate.Transition, now time.Time) error {
	err := db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error {
		if _, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, "DELETE FROM firewall_restores"); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		_, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, "INSERT INTO firewall_restores (snapshot_id, transition, started_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
			id, string(tr), formatSnapshotTime(now))
		return err
	})
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("firewall: record the restore of snapshot %s: %w", id, err)
	}
	return nil
}

// restoreIntent returns the transition of an unfinished restore of snapshot
// id; ok is false when none is recorded.
func restoreIntent(ctx context.Context, db *store.DB, id string) (fwstate.Transition, bool, error) {
	var tr string
	err := db.Read().QueryRowContext(ctx, "SELECT transition FROM firewall_restores WHERE snapshot_id = ?", id).Scan(&tr)
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
		return "", false, nil
	case err != nil:
		return "", false, fmt.Errorf("firewall: read the restore of snapshot %s: %w", id, err)
	}
	return fwstate.Transition(tr), true, nil
}

// pendingRestore returns the snapshot of the unfinished restore, if any.
func pendingRestore(ctx context.Context, db *store.DB) (string, bool, error) {
	var id string
	err := db.Read().QueryRowContext(ctx, "SELECT snapshot_id FROM firewall_restores").Scan(&id)
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
		return "", false, nil
	case err != nil:
		return "", false, fmt.Errorf("firewall: read the unfinished restore: %w", err)
	}
	return id, true, nil
}

// endRestore deletes the restore record of snapshot id.
func endRestore(ctx context.Context, db *store.DB, id string) error {
	err := db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error {
		_, err := tx.ExecContext(ctx, "DELETE FROM firewall_restores WHERE snapshot_id = ?", id)
		return err
	})
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("firewall: clear the restore of snapshot %s: %w", id, err)
	}
	return nil
}
```

### Task 38: Render the files UFW writes

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/modules/firewall/predict/render.go`
- Test: `internal/modules/firewall/predict/render_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `fwstate.Config`, `model.Tuple`, `model.TuplePrefix`, `model.Any`, the `model` enums; `conf.Read` and `fwstate.StateFiles` in the test (base).
- Produces: `Files` and the unexported rendering helpers of Part contracts Task 38; the shared test helpers `predictGolden`, `predictImages`, `predictConfig`.

**Depends on:** Task 25, Task 33

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-sonnet-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 2 - risk 2 = 5

`Files(cfg)` returns the bytes UFW writes for a configuration: `user.rules` and `user6.rules` exactly as `_write_rules` in `backend_iptables.py` writes them (the header, each `### tuple ###` line, the iptables lines of `format_rule` and `_get_rules_from_formatted`, the logging section of `_get_logging_rules`, the rate-limit section, `COMMIT`), and `ufw.conf` and `/etc/default/ufw` as `cfg.Files` holds them with only the keys UFW would read differently rewritten as `set_default` writes them. The effects journal's expected after-state hashes come from these bytes (spec 2.5), so the comparison is byte for byte. `TestFilesGolden` renders every golden scenario whose files UFW wrote (all but `fresh`, whose files are the package templates) on all four images. `TestFilesLogLevels` and `TestFilesRuleLines` compare with sections ufw 0.36.2-6 wrote in a container for the log levels, policies and rule shapes the goldens lack.

```go
package predict

import (
	"bytes"
	"maps"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/conf"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/model"
)

// predictGolden is the golden tree testdata/capture.sh writes (spec 2.3).
const predictGolden = "../testdata/golden"

var predictImages = []string{"ubuntu-22.04", "ubuntu-24.04", "debian-12", "debian-13"}

// predictConfig reads one golden scenario's configured state.
func predictConfig(t *testing.T, image, scenario string) fwstate.Config {
	t.Helper()
	cfg, err := conf.Read(filepath.Join(predictGolden, image, scenario, "files"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return cfg
}

// TestFilesGolden renders every scenario UFW has written its files in (all
// but fresh, whose files are the package's templates) and compares the
// bytes with the capture.
func TestFilesGolden(t *testing.T) {
	for _, img := range predictImages {
		for _, sc := range []string{"enabled", "rules", "disabled", "ipv6no", "logging", "manual", "sysctl"} {
			cfg := predictConfig(t, img, sc)
			got, err := Files(cfg)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("%s/%s: %v", img, sc, err)
			}
			if len(got) != 4 {
				t.Errorf("%s/%s: Files returned %d files, want 4", img, sc, len(got))
			}
			for path, data := range got {
				want, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(predictGolden, img, sc, "files", path)) //nolint:gosec // G304: a state file under the golden directory
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
				if !bytes.Equal(data, want) {
					t.Errorf("%s/%s %s differs:\n--- got\n%s--- want\n%s", img, sc, path, data, want)
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

func TestFilesLogLevels(t *testing.T) {
	base := predictConfig(t, "ubuntu-24.04", "enabled")
	for _, tc := range filesTestLevels {
		cfg := base
		cfg.LogLevel, cfg.DefaultInput, cfg.DefaultOutput, cfg.DefaultForward = tc.level, tc.input, tc.output, tc.forward
		got, err := Files(cfg)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("%s: %v", tc.name, err)
		}
		path := userRules
		if tc.v6 {
			path = userRules6
		}
		_, section, ok := strings.Cut(string(got[path]), "\n### LOGGING ###\n")
		if !ok || "### LOGGING ###\n"+section != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("%s: logging section\n%s\nwant\n%s", tc.name, "### LOGGING ###\n"+section, tc.want)
		}
	}
}

// TestFilesRuleLines renders tuples the golden scenarios lack and compares
// the rule section with what ufw 0.36.2-6 wrote on ubuntu:24.04 for
// "allow proto tcp from 10.0.0.0/8 port 1000:2000 to any port 80,443",
// "deny out proto udp from any port 53", "reject in log-all to 192.0.2.1
// port 25", "limit in log proto tcp to any port 22", "route deny in on eth0
// out on eth1" and "allow in on eth0 log-all from 2001:db8::/32 to any port
// 8080:8090 proto udp".
func TestFilesRuleLines(t *testing.T) {
	cfg := predictConfig(t, "ubuntu-24.04", "enabled")
	cfg.Rules4, cfg.Rules6 = filesTestTuples(t, filesTestRules4, false), filesTestTuples(t, filesTestRules6, true)
	got, err := Files(cfg)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for path, want := range map[string]string{userRules: filesTestRules4, userRules6: filesTestRules6} {
		if !strings.Contains(string(got[path]), "\n"+want) {
			t.Errorf("%s rendered\n%s\nwant the section\n%s", path, got[path], want)
		}
	}
}

func filesTestTuples(t *testing.T, section string, v6 bool) []model.Tuple {
	t.Helper()
	var out []model.Tuple
	for _, line := range strings.Split(section, "\n") {
		if strings.HasPrefix(line, model.TuplePrefix) {
			tp, err := model.ParseTuple(line, v6)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			out = append(out, tp)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// TestFilesConfKeys checks that ufw.conf and /etc/default/ufw change only
// in the keys whose value UFW would read differently, written as
// set_default writes them, and that a missing key is appended.
func TestFilesConfKeys(t *testing.T) {
	cfg := predictConfig(t, "debian-13", "enabled")
	cfg.Files = maps.Clone(cfg.Files)
	conf := cfg.Files[ufwConf]
	conf.Data = []byte("# comment\nENABLED=YES\nLOGLEVEL=low")
	cfg.Files[ufwConf] = conf
	defs := cfg.Files[defaultsUFW]
	defs.Data = []byte("IPV6=yes\nDEFAULT_INPUT_POLICY=\"DROP\"\nDEFAULT_OUTPUT_POLICY=ACCEPT\n")
	cfg.Files[defaultsUFW] = defs
	cfg.Enabled, cfg.LogLevel = true, "low"
	cfg.DefaultInput, cfg.DefaultOutput, cfg.DefaultForward = "DROP", "ACCEPT", "DROP"
	got, err := Files(cfg)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if string(got[ufwConf]) != "# comment\nENABLED=YES\nLOGLEVEL=low" {
		t.Errorf("unchanged ufw.conf = %q", got[ufwConf])
	}
	if want := "IPV6=yes\nDEFAULT_INPUT_POLICY=\"DROP\"\nDEFAULT_OUTPUT_POLICY=ACCEPT\nDEFAULT_FORWARD_POLICY=\"DROP\"\n"; string(got[defaultsUFW]) != want {
		t.Errorf("/etc/default/ufw = %q, want %q", got[defaultsUFW], want)
	}
	cfg.Enabled, cfg.LogLevel, cfg.DefaultOutput = false, "full", "REJECT"
	if got, err = Files(cfg); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if want := "# comment\nENABLED=no\nLOGLEVEL=full\n"; string(got[ufwConf]) != want {
		t.Errorf("ufw.conf = %q, want %q", got[ufwConf], want)
	}
	if want := "IPV6=yes\nDEFAULT_INPUT_POLICY=\"DROP\"\nDEFAULT_OUTPUT_POLICY=\"REJECT\"\nDEFAULT_FORWARD_POLICY=\"DROP\"\n"; string(got[defaultsUFW]) != want {
		t.Errorf("/etc/default/ufw = %q, want %q", got[defaultsUFW], want)
	}
}

func TestFilesRefuses(t *testing.T) {
	base := predictConfig(t, "debian-13", "enabled")
	for name, edit := range map[string]func(*fwstate.Config){
		"log level": func(c *fwstate.Config) { c.LogLevel = "loud" },
		"policy":    func(c *fwstate.Config) { c.DefaultForward = "drop" },
	} {
		cfg := base
		edit(&cfg)
		if _, err := Files(cfg); err == nil || !strings.HasPrefix(err.Error(), "predict: ") {
			t.Errorf("%s: err = %v, want a predict error", name, err)
		}
	}
}
```
