Create `internal/modules/firewall/predict/render.go`:

```go
// Package predict simulates UFW 0.36 (spec 2.3, 2.5): how one ufw command
// changes the configured state and the files UFW writes, the netfilter
// state UFW loads from a configuration, and the loaded state a transition
// leaves behind.
package predict

import (
	"encoding/hex"
	"fmt"
	"regexp"
	"slices"
	"strings"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/model"
)

// The files Files renders.
const (
	userRules   = "/etc/ufw/user.rules"
	userRules6  = "/etc/ufw/user6.rules"
	ufwConf     = "/etc/ufw/ufw.conf"
	defaultsUFW = "/etc/default/ufw"
)

// logLevels ranks ufw.conf's LOGLEVEL values as UFW's backend does.
var logLevels = map[string]int{"off": 0, "low": 100, "medium": 200, "high": 300, "full": 400}

// Files returns the bytes UFW writes for cfg the next time it writes each
// file: user.rules and user6.rules rendered from the tuples, the log level
// and the default policies as backend_iptables.py's _write_rules does, and
// ufw.conf and /etc/default/ufw as cfg.Files holds them with each key whose
// value UFW would read differently from cfg rewritten as UFW's set_default
// writes it. With IPv6 off UFW keeps no IPv6 rules in memory, so
// user6.rules renders without tuples, logging or rate-limit chains. A log
// level or default policy UFW refuses is an error.
func Files(cfg fwstate.Config) (map[string][]byte, error) {
	if err := checkRenderable(cfg); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	out := map[string][]byte{
		userRules:  renderUser(cfg, false),
		userRules6: renderUser(cfg, true),
	}
	conf := ufwDefaults(cfg.Files[ufwConf].Data)
	data := cfg.Files[ufwConf].Data
	if (conf["enabled"] == "yes") != cfg.Enabled {
		data = setDefault(data, "ENABLED", yesNo(cfg.Enabled))
	}
	if conf["loglevel"] != cfg.LogLevel {
		data = setDefault(data, "LOGLEVEL", cfg.LogLevel)
	}
	out[ufwConf] = data
	defs := ufwDefaults(cfg.Files[defaultsUFW].Data)
	data = cfg.Files[defaultsUFW].Data
	for _, p := range policyKeys(cfg) {
		if defs[strings.ToLower(p.key)] != strings.ToLower(p.value) {
			data = setDefault(data, p.key, `"`+p.value+`"`)
		}
	}
	out[defaultsUFW] = data
	return out, nil
}

// checkRenderable refuses what UFW itself refuses before it writes: a log
// level _get_logging_rules rejects and a default policy _get_defaults
// rejects.
func checkRenderable(cfg fwstate.Config) error {
	if _, ok := logLevels[cfg.LogLevel]; !ok {
		return fmt.Errorf("predict: log level %q is not one UFW accepts", cfg.LogLevel)
	}
	for _, p := range policyKeys(cfg) {
		if !slices.Contains([]string{"ACCEPT", "DROP", "REJECT"}, p.value) {
			return fmt.Errorf("predict: %s %q is not ACCEPT, DROP or REJECT", p.key, p.value)
		}
	}
	return nil
}

type policyKey struct{ key, value string }

func policyKeys(cfg fwstate.Config) []policyKey {
	return []policyKey{
		{"DEFAULT_INPUT_POLICY", cfg.DefaultInput},
		{"DEFAULT_OUTPUT_POLICY", cfg.DefaultOutput},
		{"DEFAULT_FORWARD_POLICY", cfg.DefaultForward},
	}
}

func yesNo(b bool) string {
	if b {
		return "yes"
	}
	return "no"
}

var ufwDefaultRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^\w+="?\w+"?`)

// ufwDefaults reads KEY=value lines as UFW's _get_defaults does: keys and
// values lower-cased, quotes stripped, the last assignment winning.
func ufwDefaults(data []byte) map[string]string {
	out := map[string]string{}
	for _, line := range strings.Split(string(data), "\n") {
		if !ufwDefaultRe.MatchString(line) {
			continue
		}
		f := strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(line), "=")
		out[strings.ToLower(f[0])] = strings.Trim(strings.ToLower(f[1]), `"'`)
	}
	return out
}

// setDefault rewrites every line that starts with "opt=" as "opt=value", or
// appends that line when none does, as UFW's set_default does.
func setDefault(data []byte, opt, value string) []byte {
	var b strings.Builder
	found := false
	for _, line := range strings.SplitAfter(string(data), "\n") {
		if strings.HasPrefix(line, opt+"=") {
			b.WriteString(opt + "=" + value + "\n")
			found = true
			continue
		}
		b.WriteString(line)
	}
	if !found {
		b.WriteString(opt + "=" + value + "\n")
	}
	return []byte(b.String())
}

// chainPrefix is UFW's chain prefix for a family.
func chainPrefix(v6 bool) string {
	if v6 {
		return "ufw6"
	}
	return "ufw"
}

// renderUser renders user.rules (v6 false) or user6.rules as _write_rules
// writes it. Rate limiting is assumed available in IPv4 and, with IPv6 on,
// in IPv6, as on every supported image; with IPv6 off UFW skips the IPv6
// capability check and writes neither the IPv6 limit chains nor any IPv6
// tuple or logging rule.
func renderUser(cfg fwstate.Config, v6 bool) []byte {
	p := chainPrefix(v6)
	limit := !v6 || cfg.IPv6
	rules := cfg.Rules4
	if v6 {
		rules = nil
		if cfg.IPv6 {
			rules = cfg.Rules6
		}
	}
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString("*filter\n")
	for _, c := range []string{"user-input", "user-output", "user-forward",
		"before-logging-input", "before-logging-output", "before-logging-forward",
		"user-logging-input", "user-logging-output", "user-logging-forward",
		"after-logging-input", "after-logging-output", "after-logging-forward",
		"logging-deny", "logging-allow"} {
		b.WriteString(":" + p + "-" + c + " - [0:0]\n")
	}
	if limit {
		b.WriteString(":" + p + "-user-limit - [0:0]\n")
		b.WriteString(":" + p + "-user-limit-accept - [0:0]\n")
	}
	b.WriteString("### RULES ###\n")
	for _, t := range rules {
		b.WriteString("\n" + tupleLine(t) + "\n")
		suffix := "input"
		if t.Route {
			suffix = "forward"
		} else if t.Direction == model.DirOut {
			suffix = "output"
		}
		for _, s := range rulesFromFormatted("-A "+p+"-user-"+suffix+" "+formatRule(t)+"\n", p, suffix) {
			b.WriteString(s)
		}
	}
	b.WriteString("\n### END RULES ###\n")
	b.WriteString("\n### LOGGING ###\n")
	if !v6 || cfg.IPv6 {
		for _, r := range loggingRules(cfg, p) {
			if r[0] == "-D" {
				continue
			}
			line := strings.Join(r, " ")
			line = strings.ReplaceAll(line, "[", `"[`)
			line = strings.ReplaceAll(line, "] ", `] "`)
			b.WriteString(line + "\n")
		}
	}
	b.WriteString("### END LOGGING ###\n")
	if limit {
		b.WriteString("\n### RATE LIMITING ###\n")
		if cfg.LogLevel != "off" {
			b.WriteString("-A " + p + "-user-limit -m limit --limit 3/minute -j LOG --log-prefix \"[UFW LIMIT BLOCK] \"\n")
		}
		b.WriteString("-A " + p + "-user-limit -j REJECT\n")
		b.WriteString("-A " + p + "-user-limit-accept -j ACCEPT\n")
		b.WriteString("### END RATE LIMITING ###\n")
	}
	b.WriteString("COMMIT\n")
	return []byte(b.String())
}

// tupleLine is the "### tuple ###" line _write_rules writes for t.
func tupleLine(t model.Tuple) string {
	action := string(t.Action)
	if t.Route {
		action = "route:" + action
	}
	if t.Log != model.LogOff && t.Log != "" {
		action += "_" + string(t.Log)
	}
	var ifaces string
	switch {
	case t.InIface == "" && t.OutIface == "":
		ifaces = string(t.Direction)
	case t.InIface != "" && t.OutIface != "":
		ifaces = "in_" + t.InIface + "!out_" + t.OutIface
	case t.InIface != "":
		ifaces = string(t.Direction) + "_" + t.InIface
	default:
		ifaces = string(t.Direction) + "_" + t.OutIface
	}
	f := []string{model.TuplePrefix, action, string(t.Proto), t.DPort, t.Dst, t.SPort, t.Src}
	if t.DApp != "" || t.SApp != "" {
		f = append(f, appField(t.DApp), appField(t.SApp))
	}
	f = append(f, ifaces)
	line := strings.Join(f, " ")
	if t.Comment != "" {
		line += " comment=" + hex.EncodeToString([]byte(t.Comment))
	}
	return line
}

func appField(name string) string {
	if name == "" {
		return "-"
	}
	return strings.ReplaceAll(name, " ", "%20")
}

// multiPort reports whether UFW's set_port marks a rule with these ports
// multiport: a list or a range in either port.
func multiPort(t model.Tuple) bool {
	for _, p := range []string{t.DPort, t.SPort} {
		if p != model.Any && strings.ContainsAny(p, ",:") {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// formatRule is UFWRule.format_rule: the iptables options of t after
// "-A <chain>", before _get_rules_from_formatted adjusts them.
func formatRule(t model.Tuple) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	if t.InIface != "" {
		b.WriteString(" -i " + t.InIface)
	}
	if t.OutIface != "" {
		b.WriteString(" -o " + t.OutIface)
	}
	multi := multiPort(t)
	if t.Proto == model.ProtoAny {
		b.WriteString(" -p all")
	} else {
		b.WriteString(" -p " + string(t.Proto))
		if multi {
			b.WriteString(" -m multiport")
			switch {
			case t.DPort != model.Any && t.SPort != model.Any:
				b.WriteString(" --dports " + t.DPort + " -m multiport --sports " + t.SPort)
			case t.DPort != model.Any:
				b.WriteString(" --dports " + t.DPort)
			case t.SPort != model.Any:
				b.WriteString(" --sports " + t.SPort)
			}
		}
	}
	if t.Dst != "0.0.0.0/0" && t.Dst != "::/0" {
		b.WriteString(" -d " + t.Dst)
	}
	if !multi && t.DPort != model.Any {
		b.WriteString(" --dport " + t.DPort)
	}
	if t.Src != "0.0.0.0/0" && t.Src != "::/0" {
		b.WriteString(" -s " + t.Src)
	}
	if !multi && t.SPort != model.Any {
		b.WriteString(" --sport " + t.SPort)
	}
	lstr := ""
	if t.Log != model.LogOff && t.Log != "" {
		lstr = "_" + string(t.Log)
	}
	switch t.Action {
	case model.ActionAllow:
		b.WriteString(" -j ACCEPT" + lstr)
	case model.ActionReject:
		b.WriteString(" -j REJECT" + lstr)
		if t.Proto == model.ProtoTCP {
			b.WriteString(" --reject-with tcp-reset")
		}
	case model.ActionLimit:
		b.WriteString(" -j LIMIT" + lstr)
	default:
		b.WriteString(" -j DROP" + lstr)
	}
	if t.DApp != "" || t.SApp != "" {
		var apps []string
		if t.DApp != "" {
			apps = append(apps, "dapp_"+strings.ReplaceAll(t.DApp, " ", "%20"))
		}
		if t.SApp != "" {
			apps = append(apps, "sapp_"+strings.ReplaceAll(t.SApp, " ", "%20"))
		}
		b.WriteString(" -m comment --comment '" + strings.Join(apps, ",") + "'")
	}
	return strings.TrimSpace(b.String())
}

var (
	fmtProtoRe  = regexp.MustCompile(`-p all `)
	fmtPortRe   = regexp.MustCompile(`port `)
	fmtRejectRe = regexp.MustCompile(`-j (REJECT(_log(-all)?)?)`)
	fmtLogRe    = regexp.MustCompile(`(.*)-j ([A-Z]+)_log(-all)?(.*)`)
	fmtLogAllRe = regexp.MustCompile(`-j [A-Z]+_log-all`)
	fmtChainRe  = regexp.MustCompile(`(-A|-D) ([a-zA-Z0-9\-]+)`)
	fmtLimitRe  = regexp.MustCompile(` -j LIMIT`)
)

// rulesFromFormatted is _get_rules_from_formatted: it splits a "proto any"
// rule with a port into tcp and udp rules, expands a logging rule into its
// logging chain's LOG and RETURN rules and the jump to that chain, and
// expands limit into the recent rules. The text manipulation follows UFW's
// regular expressions so unusual names come out as UFW writes them.
func rulesFromFormatted(frule, prefix, suffix string) []string {
	var snippets []string
	switch {
	case !fmtProtoRe.MatchString(frule):
		snippets = append(snippets, frule)
	case fmtPortRe.MatchString(frule):
		if fmtRejectRe.MatchString(frule) {
			snippets = append(snippets, fmtProtoRe.ReplaceAllString(
				fmtRejectRe.ReplaceAllString(frule, "-j ${1} --reject-with tcp-reset"), "-p tcp "))
		} else {
			snippets = append(snippets, fmtProtoRe.ReplaceAllString(frule, "-p tcp "))
		}
		snippets = append(snippets, fmtProtoRe.ReplaceAllString(frule, "-p udp "))
	default:
		snippets = append(snippets, fmtProtoRe.ReplaceAllString(frule, ""))
	}

	logChain := prefix + "-user-logging-" + suffix
	limitArgs := "-m limit --limit 3/min --limit-burst 10"
	for i := 0; i < len(snippets); i++ {
		s := snippets[i]
		if !fmtLogRe.MatchString(s) {
			continue
		}
		policy := "BLOCK"
		switch strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(fmtLogRe.ReplaceAllString(s, "${2}"))) {
		case "accept":
			policy = "ALLOW"
		case "limit":
			policy = "LIMIT"
		}
		lstr := limitArgs + ` -j LOG --log-prefix "[UFW ` + policy + `] "`
		if !fmtLogAllRe.MatchString(s) {
			lstr = "-m conntrack --ctstate NEW " + lstr
		}
		inChain := func(t string) string { return fmtChainRe.ReplaceAllString(t, "${1} "+logChain) }
		snippets[i] = fmtLogRe.ReplaceAllString(s, "${1}-j ${2}${4}")
		snippets = slices.Insert(snippets, i,
			inChain(fmtLogRe.ReplaceAllString(s, "${1}"+lstr)),
			inChain(fmtLogRe.ReplaceAllString(s, "${1}-j RETURN")),
			fmtLogRe.ReplaceAllString(s, "${1}-j "+logChain))
	}

	for i := 0; i < len(snippets); i++ {
		s := snippets[i]
		if !fmtLimitRe.MatchString(s) {
			continue
		}
		set := fmtLimitRe.ReplaceAllString(s, " -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m recent --set")
		update := fmtLimitRe.ReplaceAllString(s, " -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m recent --update --seconds 30 --hitcount 6 -j "+prefix+"-user-limit")
		snippets[i] = fmtLimitRe.ReplaceAllString(s, " -j "+prefix+"-user-limit-accept")
		snippets = slices.Insert(snippets, i, set, update)
	}
	return snippets
}

// loggingRules is _get_logging_rules for one family's chains (prefix "ufw"
// or "ufw6"), in UFW's order: each rule as the argument list UFW passes to
// iptables, the chain name second.
func loggingRules(cfg fwstate.Config, p string) [][]string {
	level := logLevels[cfg.LogLevel]
	userChains := []string{p + "-user-logging-input", p + "-user-logging-output", p + "-user-logging-forward"}
	var out [][]string
	if level == logLevels["off"] {
		for _, c := range userChains {
			out = append(out, []string{"-I", c, "-j", "RETURN"})
		}
		return out
	}
	for _, c := range userChains {
		out = append(out, []string{"-D", c, "-j", "RETURN"})
	}
	limitArgs := []string{"-m", "limit", "--limit", "3/min", "--limit-burst", "10"}
	policy := map[string]string{"input": cfg.DefaultInput, "output": cfg.DefaultOutput, "forward": cfg.DefaultForward}
	if level >= logLevels["low"] {
		var largs []string
		if level < logLevels["high"] {
			largs = limitArgs
		}
		for _, t := range []string{"input", "output", "forward"} {
			c := p + "-after-logging-" + t
			switch {
			case policy[t] == "REJECT" || policy[t] == "DROP":
				out = append(out, append([]string{"-A", c, "-j", "LOG", "--log-prefix", "[UFW BLOCK] "}, largs...))
			case level >= logLevels["medium"]:
				out = append(out, append([]string{"-A", c, "-j", "LOG", "--log-prefix", "[UFW ALLOW] "}, largs...))
			}
		}
		for _, c := range []string{p + "-logging-deny", p + "-logging-allow"} {
			prefix := "[UFW ALLOW] "
			if strings.HasSuffix(c, "deny") {
				prefix = "[UFW BLOCK] "
				if level < logLevels["medium"] {
					out = append(out, append([]string{"-I", c, "-m", "conntrack", "--ctstate", "INVALID", "-j", "RETURN"}, largs...))
				} else {
					out = append(out, append([]string{"-A", c, "-m", "conntrack", "--ctstate", "INVALID", "-j", "LOG", "--log-prefix", "[UFW AUDIT INVALID] "}, largs...))
				}
			}
			out = append(out, append([]string{"-A", c, "-j", "LOG", "--log-prefix", prefix}, largs...))
		}
	}
	if level >= logLevels["medium"] {
		var largs []string
		if level < logLevels["full"] {
			largs = limitArgs
		}
		if level < logLevels["high"] {
			largs = append([]string{"-m", "conntrack", "--ctstate", "NEW"}, limitArgs...)
		}
		for _, t := range []string{"input", "output", "forward"} {
			out = append(out, append([]string{"-I", p + "-before-logging-" + t, "-j", "LOG", "--log-prefix", "[UFW AUDIT] "}, largs...))
		}
	}
	return out
}
```

### Task 39: UFW golden verdicts

**Files:**
- Test: `internal/modules/firewall/eval/ufw_golden_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `Evaluate` (Task 30, matches from Task 35), `evalRuleset`, `evalPacket`, `evalCheck`, and the golden captures `internal/modules/firewall/testdata/golden/<image>/{rules,ipv6no,disabled}/save/nft-<v4|v6>-<table>.txt` (merged)
- Produces: test-only names `ufwGoldenImages`, `ufwGoldenRuleset`, `ufwGoldenCase`, `ufwGoldenPacket`, `ufwGoldenRun`

**Depends on:** Task 33, Task 35

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-sonnet-low
**Evaluation:** files 0 - spec 0 - coupling 1 - risk 0 = 1

Checks the evaluator against UFW's real loaded state on all four OS images. In the `rules` scenario SSH on port 22 is accepted from any source in both families; port 2222 is `unknown` because `ufw limit` builds a rule whose `recent --update` match decides a jump to `ufw-user-limit`, which rejects (`ufw-user-input#3` for IPv4, `ufw6-user-input#4` for IPv6); port 3000 is rejected for TCP and UDP; the default incoming policy drops everything else; the IPv4 port list from 10.0.0.0/8, the route rule, outgoing traffic, loopback and established traffic are accepted. With `IPV6=no` IPv6 SSH is dropped by the plain table's policy; disabled UFW accepts everything. No implementation: the expectations hold on Tasks 30 and 35's code (and stay true with Task 41 and Task 52, since these captures have no nat, mangle or mark rules).

```go
// ufwGoldenRuleset joins one capture's five save files for a family.
func ufwGoldenRuleset(t *testing.T, image, scenario string, fam fwstate.Family) *netfilter.Ruleset {
	t.Helper()
	var b strings.Builder
	for _, table := range netfilter.Tables() {

// ufwGoldenCase is one packet and the verdict the capture must give it.
type ufwGoldenCase struct {
	name    string
	edit    func(p *fwstate.Packet)
	verdict fwstate.Verdict

// ufwGoldenPacket is evalPacket in the family, with the documentation
// prefix 2001:db8::/32 standing in for IPv4's documentation ranges.
func ufwGoldenPacket(fam fwstate.Family) fwstate.Packet {
	p := evalPacket()
	if fam == fwstate.V6 {
		p.Family = fwstate.V6
		p.Src, p.Dst = netip.MustParseAddr("2001:db8:1::7"), netip.MustParseAddr("2001:db8::1")
	}
	return p
}

func ufwGoldenRun(t *testing.T, scenario string, fam fwstate.Family, cases []ufwGoldenCase) {
	t.Helper()
	for _, image := range ufwGoldenImages {
		rs := ufwGoldenRuleset(t, image, scenario, fam)
		for _, c := range cases {
			t.Run(image+"/"+string(fam)+"/"+c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
				p := ufwGoldenPacket(fam)
				c.edit(&p)
				evalCheck(t, Evaluate(rs, p, nil), c.verdict, nil, c.reason)
			})
		}
	}
}
```

**Lenses:** security

The reader of the loaded state's tables (spec 2.1). It asks `/usr/sbin/iptables --version` and `/usr/sbin/ip6tables --version` which variant each family uses, runs that variant's explicit `<tool>-<variant>-save -t <table>` for the five tables (for the legacy variant only the tables `/proc/net/ip_tables_names` or `ip6_tables_names` lists, because asking a legacy save tool for any other table creates that table and loads its kernel module), parses each output with `netfilter.Parse` and merges the tables into one ruleset per family. `saveTables` also records iptables-nft-save's legacy-tables warning, which 1.8.7 prints with the rules and later versions print on standard error; Task 56 relies on it. A missing `ip6tables` leaves `V6` nil; a family whose variant differs from IPv4's, and a table iptables-nft-save calls incompatible, become `Unsupported` reasons; any other failure (a tool that fails, an empty or truncated capture, which `netfilter.Parse` reports as `ErrNoTables`) is an error. The tests drive `read` with a fake runner that answers from the golden captures of all four images and eight scenarios and refuses any vector the agent's exec allowlist would refuse. Test helpers carry the prefix `ld`; Tasks 56 and 60 reuse them.

```go
package loaded

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io/fs"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"reflect"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"syscall"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netfilter"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netstat"
)

// The golden captures of testdata/capture.sh, one directory per image and
// scenario.
const ldGoldenDir = "../testdata/golden"

var (
	ldImages    = []string{"ubuntu-22.04", "ubuntu-24.04", "debian-12", "debian-13"}
	ldScenarios = []string{"fresh", "enabled", "rules", "disabled", "ipv6no", "logging", "manual", "sysctl"}
)

// ldResult is what the fake runner answers for one argument vector.
type ldResult struct {
	out, stderr string
	code        int
	err         error
}

// ldRunner is a fake core.Runner keyed by "<path> <args...>". It refuses a
// vector the agent's exec allowlist would refuse and any vector it has no
// answer for, and records every call.
type ldRunner struct {
	answers map[string]ldResult
	calls   []string
}

func (r *ldRunner) Run(_ context.Context, cmd core.Cmd) (core.CmdResult, error) {
	key := strings.Join(append([]string{cmd.Path}, cmd.Args...), " ")
	r.calls = append(r.calls, key)
	allowed := false
	for _, rule := range platform.ProductionRules() {
		if rule.Path == cmd.Path && rule.Match(cmd.Args) == nil {
			allowed = true
		}
	}
	if !allowed {
		return core.CmdResult{}, fmt.Errorf("ldRunner: %q is not in the exec allowlist", key)
	}
	a, ok := r.answers[key]
	if !ok {
		return core.CmdResult{}, fmt.Errorf("ldRunner: unexpected command %q", key)
	}
	return core.CmdResult{Stdout: []byte(a.out), Stderr: []byte(a.stderr), ExitCode: a.code}, a.err
}

// ldMissing is the runner's error for a program that is not installed.
func ldMissing(path string) error {
	return fmt.Errorf("platform: run %s: %w", path, &fs.PathError{Op: "fork/exec", Path: path, Err: syscall.ENOENT})
}

// ldGolden answers the version and save commands of one golden scenario.
func ldGolden(t *testing.T, image, scenario string) *ldRunner {
	t.Helper()
	dir := filepath.Join(ldGoldenDir, image, scenario)
	version, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, "version.txt")) //nolint:gosec // G304: a fixed name under the golden directory
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	line, _, _ := strings.Cut(string(version), "\n")
	r := &ldRunner{answers: map[string]ldResult{
		"/usr/sbin/iptables --version":  {out: line + "\n"},
		"/usr/sbin/ip6tables --version": {out: "ip6" + line + "\n"},
	}}
	for _, fam := range []string{"v4", "v6"} {
		tool := "iptables"
		if fam == "v6" {
			tool = "ip6tables"
		}
		for _, table := range netfilter.Tables() {
			data, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, "save", "nft-"+fam+"-"+table+".txt")) //nolint:gosec // G304: a fixed name under the golden directory
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			r.answers["/usr/sbin/"+tool+"-nft-save -t "+table] = ldResult{out: string(data)}
		}
	}
	return r
}

// ldFiles is a fake core.FileWriter that answers ReadSysctl from a map; a
// key not in the map fails as the agent's Files fails for a key the kernel
// lacks. Every other method is left to the nil embedded interface and
// panics.
type ldFiles struct {
	core.FileWriter
	sysctl map[string]string
	reads  []string
}

func (f *ldFiles) ReadSysctl(_ context.Context, module, key string) (string, error) {
	f.reads = append(f.reads, module+" "+key)
	v, ok := f.sysctl[key]
	if !ok {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("platform: open sysctl %s: %w", key, syscall.ENOENT)
	}
	return v, nil
}

// ldEnv is an Env whose runner and files are the fakes.
func ldEnv(x core.Runner, sysctl map[string]string) core.Env {
	return core.Env{Exec: x, Files: &ldFiles{sysctl: sysctl}}
}

// ldReader is a Reader that sees no interfaces and no nf_tables module, so
// it reads nothing of the host it runs on.
func ldReader() Reader {
	return Reader{
		Interfaces:     func() ([]netstat.Interface, error) { return nil, nil },
		NFTablesLoaded: func() bool { return false },
	}
}

func ldParse(t *testing.T, text string) *netfilter.Ruleset {
	t.Helper()
	rs, err := netfilter.Parse(strings.NewReader(text))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return rs
}

func TestReadGolden(t *testing.T) {
	for _, img := range ldImages {
		for _, sc := range ldScenarios {
			x := ldGolden(t, img, sc)
			st, err := ldReader().read(context.Background(), ldEnv(x, nil), t.TempDir())
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("%s/%s: %v", img, sc, err)
			}
			if st.Variant != "nft" || len(st.Unsupported) != 0 {
				t.Errorf("%s/%s: variant %q, unsupported %q", img, sc, st.Variant, st.Unsupported)
			}
			for fam, rs := range map[string]*netfilter.Ruleset{"v4": st.V4, "v6": st.V6} {
				if rs == nil {
					t.Fatalf("%s/%s: %s is nil", img, sc, fam)
				}
				var names []string
				for _, tb := range rs.Tables {
					names = append(names, tb.Name)
					data, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(ldGoldenDir, img, sc, "save", "nft-"+fam+"-"+tb.Name+".txt")) //nolint:gosec // G304: a fixed name under the golden directory
					if err != nil {
						t.Fatal(err)
					}
					if want := ldParse(t, string(data)).Tables[0]; !reflect.DeepEqual(tb, want) {
						t.Errorf("%s/%s: %s table %s differs from the capture", img, sc, fam, tb.Name)
					}
				}
				if !slices.Equal(names, netfilter.Tables()) {
					t.Errorf("%s/%s: %s tables %v", img, sc, fam, names)
				}
			}
			if len(x.calls) != 12 {
				t.Errorf("%s/%s: %d commands: %q", img, sc, len(x.calls), x.calls)
			}
		}
	}
}

const ldLegacyFilter = `# Generated by iptables-save v1.8.9 on Sat Oct 24 04:31:06 2026
*filter
:INPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
:FORWARD ACCEPT [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
-A INPUT -s 198.51.100.7/32 -j DROP
COMMIT
# Completed on Sat Oct 24 04:31:06 2026
`

const ldLegacyRaw = `*raw
:PREROUTING ACCEPT [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
COMMIT
`

func TestReadLegacy(t *testing.T) {
	procNet := t.TempDir()
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(procNet, "ip_tables_names"), []byte("raw\nfilter\nbogus\n"), 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	x := &ldRunner{answers: map[string]ldResult{
		"/usr/sbin/iptables --version":             {out: "iptables v1.8.9 (legacy)\n"},
		"/usr/sbin/ip6tables --version":            {out: "ip6tables v1.8.9 (legacy)\n"},
		"/usr/sbin/iptables-legacy-save -t filter": {out: ldLegacyFilter},
		"/usr/sbin/iptables-legacy-save -t raw":    {out: ldLegacyRaw},
	}}
	st, err := ldReader().read(context.Background(), ldEnv(x, nil), procNet)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if st.Variant != "legacy" || len(st.Unsupported) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("variant %q, unsupported %q", st.Variant, st.Unsupported)
	}
	if len(st.V4.Tables) != 2 || st.V4.Tables[0].Name != "filter" || st.V4.Tables[1].Name != "raw" {
		t.Fatalf("v4 tables %+v", st.V4.Tables)
	}
	if got := st.V4.Table("filter").Chain("INPUT").Rules[0].Text; got != "-A INPUT -s 198.51.100.7/32 -j DROP" {
		t.Errorf("filter INPUT rule %q", got)
	}
	if st.V6 == nil || len(st.V6.Tables) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("v6 = %+v, want an empty ruleset: no legacy IPv6 table exists", st.V6)
	}
}

func TestReadWithoutIP6tables(t *testing.T) {
	x := ldGolden(t, "debian-12", "rules")
	x.answers["/usr/sbin/ip6tables --version"] = ldResult{err: ldMissing("/usr/sbin/ip6tables")}
	st, err := ldReader().read(context.Background(), ldEnv(x, nil), t.TempDir())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if st.V6 != nil || st.V4 == nil {
		t.Errorf("v4 %v, v6 %v; want only v4", st.V4 != nil, st.V6 != nil)
	}

		if strings.Contains(c, "ip6tables-") {
			t.Errorf("ran %q without ip6tables", c)
		}
	}
}

func TestReadMixedVariants(t *testing.T) {
	x := ldGolden(t, "debian-12", "rules")
	x.answers["/usr/sbin/ip6tables --version"] = ldResult{out: "ip6tables v1.8.9 (legacy)\n"}
	st, err := ldReader().read(context.Background(), ldEnv(x, nil), t.TempDir())

	}

func TestReadErrors(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name string
		key  string
		res  ldResult
		want string
	}{
		{"no iptables", "/usr/sbin/iptables --version", ldResult{err: ldMissing("/usr/sbin/iptables")}, "loaded: /usr/sbin/iptables is not installed"},
		{"old iptables", "/usr/sbin/iptables --version", ldResult{out: "iptables v1.6.1\n"}, `loaded: cannot tell the iptables variant from "iptables v1.6.1"`},
		{"version fails", "/usr/sbin/ip6tables --version", ldResult{code: 1, stderr: "boom\nmore"}, "loaded: /usr/sbin/ip6tables --version exited with status 1: boom"},
		{"runner error", "/usr/sbin/iptables-nft-save -t nat", ldResult{err: context.DeadlineExceeded}, "loaded: /usr/sbin/iptables-nft-save -t nat: context deadline exceeded"},
		{"save fails", "/usr/sbin/ip6tables-nft-save -t raw", ldResult{code: 1, stderr: "ip6tables-nft-save: table raw: permission denied\n"}, "loaded: /usr/sbin/ip6tables-nft-save -t raw exited with status 1: ip6tables-nft-save: table raw: permission denied"},
		{"empty save", "/usr/sbin/iptables-nft-save -t mangle", ldResult{}, "loaded: /usr/sbin/iptables-nft-save -t mangle: netfilter: no tables in the input"},
		{"wrong table", "/usr/sbin/iptables-nft-save -t security", ldResult{out: "*raw\n:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]\nCOMMIT\n"}, "loaded: /usr/sbin/iptables-nft-save -t security printed 1 tables; want exactly table security"},
		{"bad save", "/usr/sbin/iptables-nft-save -t filter", ldResult{out: "*filter\n:INPUT ACCEPT [0:0]\n"}, "loaded: /usr/sbin/iptables-nft-save -t filter: netfilter: table filter has no COMMIT"},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			x := ldGolden(t, "debian-12", "rules")
			x.answers[c.key] = c.res
			_, err := ldReader().read(context.Background(), ldEnv(x, nil), t.TempDir())
			if err == nil || err.Error() != c.want {
				t.Fatalf("err = %v, want %q", err, c.want)
			}
			if c.name == "empty save" && !errors.Is(err, netfilter.ErrNoTables) {
				t.Errorf("err does not wrap netfilter.ErrNoTables")
```

```go
// Package loaded reads the firewall's loaded state (spec 2.1): the
// netfilter tables of the iptables variant UFW uses, the foreign netfilter
// hooks that make a host unsupported and the live values of the supported
// sysctl keys. It also predicts the sysctl effect of a UFW start and
// compares two loaded states (2.3). It reads the host and never writes it.
package loaded

import (
	"bufio"
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io/fs"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"slices"
	"strings"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netfilter"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netstat"
)

const (
	variantNFT    = "nft"
	variantLegacy = "legacy"

	// procNet holds the lists of the legacy tables that exist.
	procNet = "/proc/net"
	// maxStderr bounds the standard error an error message quotes.
	maxStderr = 200
	// legacyWarning starts iptables-nft-save's note that legacy tables exist.
	legacyWarning = "# Warning: iptables-legacy tables present"
)

// family is one IP family as the iptables tools name it.
type family struct {
	fam   fwstate.Family
	tool  string // "iptables" or "ip6tables"
	names string // the procNet file listing the family's legacy tables
}

var families = []family{
	{fam: fwstate.V4, tool: "iptables", names: "ip_tables_names"},
	{fam: fwstate.V6, tool: "ip6tables", names: "ip6_tables_names"},
}

// Reader reads the loaded state of the host it runs on.
type Reader struct {
	Interfaces     func() ([]netstat.Interface, error) // nil: netstat.Interfaces
	NFTablesLoaded func() bool                         // nil: /sys/module/nf_tables exists
}

// Read returns the loaded state: Variant from /usr/sbin/iptables --version,
// V4 and V6 from that variant's save tools, and Unsupported naming what
// makes the host unpredictable. A table the save tool does not print is
// absent; ip6tables not being installed leaves V6 nil. Every other failure
// to run or parse a tool is an error, never an empty firewall.
func (r Reader) Read(ctx context.Context, env core.Env) (fwstate.Loaded, error) {
	return r.read(ctx, env, procNet)
}

func (r Reader) read(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, procNet string) (fwstate.Loaded, error) {
	var st fwstate.Loaded
	for _, f := range families {
		v, ok, err := toolVariant(ctx, env.Exec, f.tool)
		if err != nil {
			return fwstate.Loaded{}, err
		}
		if !ok {
			if f.fam == fwstate.V4 {
				return fwstate.Loaded{}, errors.New("loaded: /usr/sbin/iptables is not installed")
			}
			continue
		}
		if f.fam == fwstate.V4 {
			st.Variant = v
		} else if v != st.Variant {
			st.Unsupported = append(st.Unsupported, fmt.Sprintf("ip6tables uses the %s variant but iptables uses the %s variant", v, st.Variant))
		}
		tables := netfilter.Tables()
		if v == variantLegacy {
			if tables, err = legacyTables(procNet, f); err != nil {
				return fwstate.Loaded{}, err
			}
		}
		rs, err := saveTables(ctx, env.Exec, f.tool, v, tables)
		if err != nil {
			return fwstate.Loaded{}, err
		}
		for _, t := range rs.Tables {
			if t.Incompatible != "" {
				st.Unsupported = append(st.Unsupported, fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s table %s: %s", f.tool, v, t.Name, t.Incompatible))
			}
		}
		if f.fam == fwstate.V4 {
			st.V4 = rs
		} else {
			st.V6 = rs
		}
	}
	return st, nil
}

// toolVariant runs /usr/sbin/<tool> --version and returns the variant it
// names; ok is false when the tool is not installed.
func toolVariant(ctx context.Context, x core.Runner, tool string) (variant string, ok bool, err error) {
	out, err := run(ctx, x, "/usr/sbin/"+tool, "--version")
	if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
		return "", false, nil
	}
	if err != nil {
		return "", false, err
	}
	line, _, _ := strings.Cut(string(out), "\n")
	switch {
	case strings.HasSuffix(line, " (nf_tables)"):
		return variantNFT, true, nil
	case strings.HasSuffix(line, " (legacy)"):
		return variantLegacy, true, nil
	}
	return "", false, fmt.Errorf("loaded: cannot tell the %s variant from %q", tool, truncate(line))
}

// legacyTables returns the legacy tables of f that exist, from the kernel's
// list. Asking a legacy save tool for any other table would create it, and
// load its kernel module, so only listed tables are ever read. No list
// means the legacy ip_tables module is not loaded and no table exists.
func legacyTables(procNet string, f family) ([]string, error) {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(procNet, f.names)) //nolint:gosec // G304: a fixed name under /proc/net, read-only
	if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
		return nil, nil
	}
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("loaded: %w", err)
	}
	var out []string
	sc := bufio.NewScanner(bytes.NewReader(data))
	for sc.Scan() {
		name := strings.TrimSpace(sc.Text())
		if slices.Contains(netfilter.Tables(), name) && !slices.Contains(out, name) {
			out = append(out, name)
		}
	}
	// Keep the order of netfilter.Tables, whatever order the kernel lists.
	slices.SortFunc(out, func(a, b string) int {
		return slices.Index(netfilter.Tables(), a) - slices.Index(netfilter.Tables(), b)
	})
	return out, nil
}

// saveTables runs /usr/sbin/<tool>-<variant>-save -t <table> for each table
// and merges the tables into one ruleset, in the order given.
func saveTables(ctx context.Context, x core.Runner, tool, variant string, tables []string) (*netfilter.Ruleset, error) {
	merged := &netfilter.Ruleset{}
	path := "/usr/sbin/" + tool + "-" + variant + "-save"
	for _, table := range tables {
		res, err := runResult(ctx, x, path, "-t", table)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		rs, err := netfilter.Parse(bytes.NewReader(res.Stdout))
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("loaded: %s -t %s: %w", path, table, err)
		}
		t := rs.Table(table)
		if t == nil || len(rs.Tables) != 1 {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("loaded: %s -t %s printed %d tables; want exactly table %s", path, table, len(rs.Tables), table)
		}
		merged.Tables = append(merged.Tables, *t)
		// iptables-nft-save 1.8.7 prints its legacy warning with the rules,
		// later versions print it on standard error.
		merged.LegacyPresent = merged.LegacyPresent || rs.LegacyPresent || bytes.Contains(res.Stderr, []byte(legacyWarning))
	}
	return merged, nil
}

// run runs one read-only command and returns its standard output.
func run(ctx context.Context, x core.Runner, path string, args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
	res, err := runResult(ctx, x, path, args...)
	return res.Stdout, err
}

// runResult runs one read-only command. A non-zero exit is an error quoting
// the start of its standard error; a program that is not installed fails
// with an error wrapping fs.ErrNotExist, as the agent's runner reports it.
func runResult(ctx context.Context, x core.Runner, path string, args ...string) (core.CmdResult, error) {
	res, err := x.Run(ctx, core.Cmd{Path: path, Args: args})
	cmd := strings.Join(append([]string{path}, args...), " ")
	if err != nil {
		return core.CmdResult{}, fmt.Errorf("loaded: %s: %w", cmd, err)
	}
	if res.ExitCode != 0 {
		line, _, _ := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(string(res.Stderr)), "\n")
		return core.CmdResult{}, fmt.Errorf("loaded: %s exited with status %d: %s", cmd, res.ExitCode, truncate(line))
	}
	return res, nil
}

func truncate(s string) string {
	if len(s) > maxStderr {
		return s[:maxStderr] + "..."
	}
	return s
}
```

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/modules/firewall/eval/hooks.go`
- Modify: `internal/modules/firewall/eval/eval.go`
- Test: `internal/modules/firewall/eval/hooks_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: Task 30's `walker`, `hook`, `stop`, `decides`, `target`; Task 35's `origDst`/`origPort`/`dnat` fields
- Produces: `run`, `steps`, `reroute`, `natRules`, `natTarget`, `natDestination` of Part contracts Task 41

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-sonnet-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 1 - risk 3 = 5
**Lenses:** security

Replaces the filter-only walk with every hook the packet traverses, in the kernel's priority order: raw, mangle and nat PREROUTING (or OUTPUT), then mangle, filter and security INPUT or FORWARD (or filter and security OUTPUT), then mangle and nat POSTROUTING for a packet that leaves. `DNAT` rewrites the destination and port, after which the walk asks the `Router` for the new path and out-interface; `SNAT` and `MASQUERADE` end the nat hook. Only a new connection's first packet passes the nat chains; a RELATED packet facing nat rules, rules in nat INPUT, a DNAT range, a NAT target outside the nat table, a missing router and a failed or impossible route are `unknown`. The test walks a Docker-shaped ruleset (published port, raw protection drop, masquerade, local DNAT through nat OUTPUT) and checks what the router is asked.

```go
// hooksRouter routes the containers' 172.18.0.0/16 out of docker0, this
// host's 192.0.2.1 locally, and fails for anything else. It records the
// packets it was asked about.
type hooksRouter struct{ asked []fwstate.Packet }

func (r *hooksRouter) route(p fwstate.Packet) (string, string, error) {
	r.asked = append(r.asked, p)
	switch {
	case netip.MustParsePrefix("172.18.0.0/16").Contains(p.Dst) && p.Path == "output":
		return "output", "docker0", nil
	case netip.MustParsePrefix("172.18.0.0/16").Contains(p.Dst):
		return "forward", "docker0", nil
	case p.Dst == netip.MustParseAddr("192.0.2.1") && p.Path == "output":
		return "output", "lo", nil
	case p.Dst == netip.MustParseAddr("192.0.2.1"):
		return "input", "", nil
	}
	return "", "", errors.New("no route to host")
}

func TestEvaluateRouterContract(t *testing.T) {
	rs := evalRuleset(t, hooksRules)
	p := evalPacket()
	p.DstPort = 8080
	r := &hooksRouter{}
	Evaluate(rs, p, r.route)
	if len(r.asked) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("router asked %d times, want once", len(r.asked))
	}
	got := r.asked[0]
	if got.Dst != netip.MustParseAddr("172.18.0.2") || got.DstPort != 80 || got.Src != p.Src || got.InIface != "eth0" {
		t.Fatalf("router asked about %+v, want the rewritten packet", got)
	}

	p.DstPort = 22
	r = &hooksRouter{}
	Evaluate(rs, p, r.route)
	if len(r.asked) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("router asked %d times without DNAT, want never", len(r.asked))
	}

	p.DstPort = 8080
	evalCheck(t, Evaluate(rs, p, nil), fwstate.Unknown, nil, "no router")

	wrong := func(fwstate.Packet) (string, string, error) { return "output", "eth0", nil }
	evalCheck(t, Evaluate(rs, p, wrong), fwstate.Unknown, nil, `gave path "output"`)
	noOut := func(fwstate.Packet) (string, string, error) { return "forward", "", nil }
	evalCheck(t, Evaluate(rs, p, noOut), fwstate.Unknown, nil, `gave path "forward"`)
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the implementation**

Create `internal/modules/firewall/eval/hooks.go`:

```go
package eval

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net/netip"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netfilter"
)

// step is one table's built-in chain on the packet's path.
type step struct{ table, chain string }

// run walks the hooks the packet traverses (spec 2.3), each in the
// kernel's priority order: raw, mangle and nat before routing; mangle,
// filter and security on the input or forward path; then mangle and nat
// POSTROUTING for a packet that leaves.
func (w *walker) run() fwstate.Result {
	before := []step{{"raw", "PREROUTING"}, {"mangle", "PREROUTING"}, {"nat", "PREROUTING"}}
	if w.pkt.Path == "output" {
		before = []step{{"raw", "OUTPUT"}, {"mangle", "OUTPUT"}, {"nat", "OUTPUT"}}
	}
	if !w.steps(before) || !w.reroute() {
		return w.res
	}
	var after []step
	switch w.pkt.Path {
	case "input":
		after = []step{{"mangle", "INPUT"}, {"filter", "INPUT"}, {"security", "INPUT"}}
	case "forward":
		after = []step{{"mangle", "FORWARD"}, {"filter", "FORWARD"}, {"security", "FORWARD"},
			{"mangle", "POSTROUTING"}, {"nat", "POSTROUTING"}}
	default:
		after = []step{{"filter", "OUTPUT"}, {"security", "OUTPUT"}, {"mangle", "POSTROUTING"}, {"nat", "POSTROUTING"}}
	}
	if !w.steps(after) {
		return w.res
	}
	// nat INPUT runs after security INPUT; its SNAT rules are outside the
	// model.
	if w.pkt.Path == "input" && (w.pkt.CtState == "NEW" || w.pkt.CtState == "RELATED") && w.natRules("INPUT") {
		w.stop(fwstate.Unknown, "nat/INPUT has rules; the walk does not model that hook")
		return w.res
	}
	w.res.Verdict = fwstate.Accept
	return w.res
}

// steps walks each step's hook and reports whether the packet survived.
func (w *walker) steps(seq []step) bool {
	for _, s := range seq {
		// Only a connection's first packet passes the nat table's chains;
		// later packets reuse the mapping conntrack recorded. A related
		// connection passes them only when its expectation set no mapping,
		// which the walk cannot see.
		if s.table == "nat" && w.pkt.CtState != "NEW" {
			if w.pkt.CtState == "RELATED" && w.natRules(s.chain) {
				w.stop(fwstate.Unknown, "nat/"+s.chain+" has rules a related connection may or may not pass")
				return false
			}
			continue
		}
		if w.hook(s.table, s.chain) == final {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

// natRules reports whether the nat table's built-in chain has rules, or
// cannot be read.
func (w *walker) natRules(chain string) bool {
	t := w.rs.Table("nat")
	if t == nil {
		return false
	}
	if t.Incompatible != "" {
		return true
	}
	c := t.Chain(chain)
	return c != nil && len(c.Rules) > 0
}

// reroute asks the router where the packet goes after nat rewrote its
// destination, and reports whether the walk can go on.
func (w *walker) reroute() bool {
	if !w.dnat {
		return true
	}
	dst := w.pkt.Dst.String()
	if w.route == nil {
		w.stop(fwstate.Unknown, "the destination was rewritten to "+dst+" and no router was given")
		return false
	}
	path, out, err := w.route(w.pkt)
	if err != nil {
		w.stop(fwstate.Unknown, fmt.Sprintf("route to %s: %v", dst, err))
		return false
	}
	valid := path == "input" || path == "forward" && out != ""
	if w.pkt.Path == "output" {
		valid = path == "output" && out != ""
	}
	if !valid {
		w.stop(fwstate.Unknown, fmt.Sprintf("route to %s gave path %q out %q", dst, path, out))
		return false
	}
	w.pkt.Path, w.pkt.OutIface = path, out
	if path == "input" {
		w.pkt.OutIface = ""
	}
	return true
}

// natTarget applies DNAT, SNAT and MASQUERADE, which end the nat table's
// hook. Only DNAT matters to the verdict: it changes where the packet goes.
func (w *walker) natTarget(t *netfilter.Table, tg netfilter.Target, ref string) outcome {
	if t.Name != "nat" {
		return w.stop(fwstate.Unknown, ref+": target "+tg.Name+" outside the nat table")
	}
	if tg.Name != "DNAT" {
		return accept
	}
	to := ""
	for _, o := range tg.Options {
		if o.Name == "to-destination" {
			to = o.Values[0]
		}
	}
	addr, port, err := natDestination(to, w.pkt.Family)
	if err != nil {
		return w.stop(fwstate.Unknown, ref+": "+err.Error())
	}
	w.pkt.Dst, w.dnat = addr, true
	if port != 0 {
		w.pkt.DstPort = port
	}
	return accept
}

// natDestination parses DNAT's --to-destination as iptables-save prints it:
// "addr", "addr:port", "[v6addr]" or "[v6addr]:port". Address and port
// ranges spread connections over several destinations, which a single walk
// cannot follow.
func natDestination(s string, fam fwstate.Family) (netip.Addr, uint16, error) {
	if s == "" {
		return netip.Addr{}, 0, errors.New("DNAT without --to-destination")
	}
	host, port := s, ""
	switch {
	case strings.HasPrefix(s, "["):
		h, rest, ok := strings.Cut(s[1:], "]")
		p, hasPort := strings.CutPrefix(rest, ":")
		if !ok || rest != "" && !hasPort {
			return netip.Addr{}, 0, fmt.Errorf("DNAT destination %q is malformed", s)
		}
		host, port = h, p
	case fam == fwstate.V4:
		host, port, _ = strings.Cut(s, ":")
	}
	if strings.Contains(host, "-") || strings.Contains(port, "-") {
		return netip.Addr{}, 0, fmt.Errorf("DNAT to a range %q is not modelled", s)
	}
	a, err := netip.ParseAddr(host)
	if err != nil || a.Is4() != (fam == fwstate.V4) || a.Zone() != "" {
		return netip.Addr{}, 0, fmt.Errorf("DNAT destination %q is not a %s address", s, fam)
	}
	if port == "" {
		return a, 0, nil
	}
	n, err := strconv.ParseUint(port, 10, 16)
	if err != nil || n == 0 {
		return netip.Addr{}, 0, fmt.Errorf("DNAT destination %q has a bad port", s)
	}
	return a, uint16(n), nil
}
```

### Task 42: Unknown source port

**Files:**
- Modify: `internal/modules/firewall/eval/match.go`
- Test: `internal/modules/firewall/eval/srcport_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: Task 35's `portOption`, `maybe`; `evalRuleset`, `evalPacket`, `evalCheck`
- Produces: the `Packet.SrcPort == 0` contract of Part contracts Task 42; test-only name `srcPortFilter`

**Depends on:** Task 35

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-sonnet-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 1 - risk 3 = 5
**Lenses:** security

A guard flow describes a connection that does not exist yet, so its source port is not known: the caller passes `Packet.SrcPort` 0. `--sport` and `--sports` (in `tcp`, `udp` and `multiport`) are then undecidable, negated or not, and follow the rule for undecidable matches: `unknown` when the rule's target decides, ignored for no target, `LOG`, `TCPMSS`, `SNAT` and `MASQUERADE`. A false match elsewhere in the same rule still makes the rule miss. The test covers a deciding rule, a multiport list, a negated port, a LOG rule, a rule another match rules out, and unchanged behaviour for a known port.

`Check` ties the part together: it gathers the facts, builds the flows, evaluates every probe with `in.Eval` against the ruleset of its family (passing the router as the `fwstate.Router`), and reports `firewall.lockout`, failed when any flow is not accepted, with a message naming each failing flow and its reason. The tests use a fake evaluator (part E drafts in parallel, so the real `Evaluate` is the actions part's end-to-end test): every flow passing, each flow refusing alone, strict `rp_filter` excluding an interface, an unresolvable route, an incomplete topology, break-glass with live facts only, a retired exposure, a missing IPv6 ruleset, the Router given to `Eval`, the error paths and the verdict text.

Create `internal/modules/firewall/guard/guard_test.go`:

```go
package guard

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"net/netip"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netfilter"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netstat"
)

// ckV4 and ckV6 are distinct rulesets, so a test can see which one the
// evaluator was given.
var ckV4, ckV6 = &netfilter.Ruleset{}, &netfilter.Ruleset{}

// ckState is a checked state holding ckV4 and ckV6.
func ckState() fwstate.Loaded { return fwstate.Loaded{Variant: "nft", V4: ckV4, V6: ckV6} }

// ckEval drops a packet deny matches and accepts the rest, and fails the
// test when it gets the ruleset of the wrong family.
func ckEval(t *testing.T, deny func(p fwstate.Packet) bool) func(*netfilter.Ruleset, fwstate.Packet, fwstate.Router) fwstate.Result {
	return func(rs *netfilter.Ruleset, p fwstate.Packet, _ fwstate.Router) fwstate.Result {
		if (p.Family == fwstate.V4) != (rs == ckV4) {
			t.Errorf("packet %+v evaluated against the other family's ruleset", p)
		}
		if deny != nil && deny(p) {
			return fwstate.Result{Verdict: fwstate.Drop, Reason: "filter/ufw-user-input#1", Trace: []string{"filter/INPUT#0", "filter/ufw-user-input#1"}}
		}
		return fwstate.Result{Verdict: fwstate.Accept}
	}
}

// ckHost is a host with an SSH session, a running local controller, the
// agent's own link to a controller, and tailscaled.
func ckHost() *gHost {
	return &gHost{
		ifaces: gIfaces(),
		pid:    99,
		sockets: []netstat.Socket{
			flSock(netstat.ProtoTCP, netstat.StateListen, "0.0.0.0:22", "", "sshd", 10),
			flSock(netstat.ProtoTCP, netstat.StateEstablished, "192.0.2.1:22", "203.0.113.7:50000", "sshd-session", 11),
			flSock(netstat.ProtoTCP, netstat.StateEstablished, "192.0.2.1:40100", "198.51.100.9:7443", "darkpanel-agent", 99),
			flSock(netstat.ProtoUDP, netstat.StateClose, "0.0.0.0:41641", "", "tailscaled", 300),
		},
		routes: map[netstat.RouteQuery]netstat.Route{
			rtQuery("198.51.100.9", "192.0.2.1", ""):          rtVia("eth0", "192.0.2.1"),
			rtQuery("198.51.100.1", "", ""):                   rtVia("eth0", "192.0.2.1"),
			rtQuery("198.51.100.1", "172.30.0.3", "dp-panel"): rtVia("eth0", ""),
		},
	}
}

// ckInput is a plan from a direct client and an apply refresh that came
// through a tunnel exposure.
func ckInput(t *testing.T, deny func(p fwstate.Packet) bool) Input {
	return Input{
		Plan: &core.GuardContext{
			Client:      &core.Peer{Addr: netip.MustParseAddr("203.0.113.7"), Port: 51000},
			PanelListen: flAddrPorts("192.0.2.1:443"),
			AgentListen: flAddrPorts("192.0.2.1:7443"),
			AgentPeers:  []netip.Addr{netip.MustParseAddr("198.51.100.7")},
			Complete:    true,
		},
		Refresh: &core.GuardContext{
			Via: &core.ProxyPath{ExposureID: "exp2", Kind: "tunnel", ProxyAddr: netip.MustParseAddr("172.30.0.3"),
				ListenerAddr: netip.MustParseAddrPort("172.30.0.1:8080")},
			Complete: true,
		},
		Eval: ckEval(t, deny),
	}
}

// ckAllFlows are the flows of ckHost and ckInput, in order.
var ckAllFlows = []string{
	"ssh from 203.0.113.7 to 192.0.2.1:22 on eth0",
	"ssh from 203.0.113.7 to 192.0.2.1:22 on eth1",
	"panel from 203.0.113.7 to 192.0.2.1:443 on eth0",
	"panel from 203.0.113.7 to 192.0.2.1:443 on eth1",
	"exposure exp2 proxy from 172.30.0.3 to 172.30.0.1:8080 on dp-panel",
	"exposure exp2 tunnel udp from 172.30.0.3 to 198.51.100.1:7844 on dp-panel out eth0",
	"exposure exp2 tunnel from 172.30.0.3 to 198.51.100.1:7844 on dp-panel out eth0",
	"exposure exp2 tunnel from 172.30.0.3 to 198.51.100.1:443 on dp-panel out eth0",
	"agent link from 198.51.100.7 to 192.0.2.1:7443 on eth0",
	"agent link from 198.51.100.7 to 192.0.2.1:7443 on eth1",
	"controller link from 192.0.2.1 to 198.51.100.9:7443 out eth0",
	"tailscale udp from 192.0.2.1 to 198.51.100.1:41641 out eth0",
	"tailscale from 192.0.2.1 to 198.51.100.1:443 out eth0",
}

// ckRunning makes the controller unit of env run with main PID 4242.
func ckRunning(env core.Env) {
	env.Units.(*gUnits).state = core.UnitState{LoadState: "loaded", ActiveState: "active", SubState: "running", MainPID: 4242}
}

// ckFailing lists the flows of results that were not accepted.
func ckFailing(results []FlowResult) []string {
	var out []string
	for _, r := range results {
		if r.Result.Verdict != fwstate.Accept {
			out = append(out, r.Flow)
		}
	}
	return out
}

func TestCheckAllPass(t *testing.T) {
	env, _, _ := gEnv()
	ckRunning(env)
	g, results, err := Checker{Host: ckHost()}.Check(context.Background(), env, ckState(), ckInput(t, nil))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var flows []string
	for _, r := range results {
		flows = append(flows, r.Flow)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(flows, ckAllFlows) {
		t.Errorf("flows =\n%q\nwant\n%q", flows, ckAllFlows)
	}
	want := core.Guard{ID: "firewall.lockout", OK: true, Message: "every protected flow passes (13 checked)"}
	if g != want {
		t.Errorf("guard = %+v, want %+v", g, want)
	}
}

func TestCheckEachFlowRefusingAlone(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name string
		deny func(p fwstate.Packet) bool
		want []string
	}{
		{"ssh", func(p fwstate.Packet) bool { return p.DstPort == 22 }, ckAllFlows[0:2]},
		{"panel on one interface", func(p fwstate.Packet) bool { return p.DstPort == 443 && p.InIface == "eth1" }, ckAllFlows[3:4]},
		{"exposure proxy", func(p fwstate.Packet) bool { return p.DstPort == 8080 }, ckAllFlows[4:5]},
		{"tunnel over udp", func(p fwstate.Packet) bool { return p.DstPort == 7844 && p.Proto == "udp" }, ckAllFlows[5:6]},
		{"agent link", func(p fwstate.Packet) bool { return p.DstPort == 7443 && p.Path == "input" }, ckAllFlows[8:10]},
		{"controller link", func(p fwstate.Packet) bool { return p.DstPort == 7443 && p.Path == "output" }, ckAllFlows[10:11]},
		{"tailscale", func(p fwstate.Packet) bool { return p.DstPort == 41641 }, ckAllFlows[11:12]},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			env, _, _ := gEnv()
			ckRunning(env)
			g, results, err := Checker{Host: ckHost()}.Check(context.Background(), env, ckState(), ckInput(t, tc.deny))
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if got := ckFailing(results); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, tc.want) {
				t.Errorf("failing flows = %q, want %q", got, tc.want)
			}
			parts := make([]string, len(tc.want))
			for i, f := range tc.want {
				parts[i] = f + ": drop (filter/ufw-user-input#1)"
			}
			want := core.Guard{ID: "firewall.lockout", Message: "the change would cut " + strings.Join(parts, "; ")}
			if g != want {
				t.Errorf("guard = %+v\nwant %+v", g, want)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestCheckStrictRPFilter(t *testing.T) {
	denyEth1 := func(p fwstate.Packet) bool { return p.InIface == "eth1" }
	host := func() *gHost {
		return &gHost{ifaces: gIfaces(), sockets: ckHost().sockets[:2], routes: map[netstat.RouteQuery]netstat.Route{
			rtQuery("203.0.113.7", "192.0.2.1", ""): rtVia("eth0", "192.0.2.1"),
		}}
	}
	env, files, _ := gEnv()
	g, _, err := Checker{Host: host()}.Check(context.Background(), env, ckState(), Input{Eval: ckEval(t, denyEth1)})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if g.OK {
		t.Fatalf("with rp_filter 0 the flow on eth1 counts: %+v", g)
	}
	files.sysctl["net/ipv4/conf/all/rp_filter"] = "1"
	g, results, err := Checker{Host: host()}.Check(context.Background(), env, ckState(), Input{Eval: ckEval(t, denyEth1)})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !g.OK || len(results) != 1 || results[0].Flow != "ssh from 203.0.113.7 to 192.0.2.1:22 on eth0" {
		t.Errorf("strict rp_filter: guard %+v, results %+v; want only eth0, passing", g, results)
	}
}

	if g.OK || g.Message != "the change would cut "+want {

	}
}

func TestCheckIncompleteTopology(t *testing.T) {

	ckRunning(env)
	h := &gHost{ifaces: gIfaces(), routes: map[netstat.RouteQuery]netstat.Route{
		rtQuery("172.17.0.5", "198.51.100.1", "eth0"): rtVia("docker0", ""),
	}}
	in := Input{
		Plan: &core.GuardContext{Via: &core.ProxyPath{ExposureID: "exp1", Kind: "npm", ProxyAddr: netip.MustParseAddr("172.30.0.2"),
			ListenerAddr: netip.MustParseAddrPort("172.30.0.1:8080"), Public: flAddrPorts("192.0.2.1:80")}, Complete: true},
		Eval: func(_ *netfilter.Ruleset, p fwstate.Packet, route fwstate.Router) fwstate.Result {
			if p.DstPort != 80 {
				return fwstate.Result{Verdict: fwstate.Accept}
			}
			p.Dst = netip.MustParseAddr("172.17.0.5")
			path, oif, err := route(p)
			switch {
			case err != nil:
				return fwstate.Result{Verdict: fwstate.Unknown, Reason: err.Error()}
			case path == "forward" && oif == "docker0":
				return fwstate.Result{Verdict: fwstate.Accept}
			}
			return fwstate.Result{Verdict: fwstate.Drop}
		},
	}
	g, results, err := Checker{Host: h}.Check(context.Background(), env, ckState(), in)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	want := "exposure exp1 public from 198.51.100.1 to 192.0.2.1:80 on eth1: unknown (firewall: route to 172.17.0.5 from 198.51.100.1 on eth1: netstat: no route)"
	if g.OK || g.Message != "the change would cut "+want {
		t.Errorf("guard = %+v, want only eth1 failing with %q", g, want)
	}
	if len(results) != 3 {
		t.Errorf("%d results, want the proxy flow and the public flow on two interfaces", len(results))
	}
}

func TestCheckErrors(t *testing.T) {
	env, _, _ := gEnv()
	if _, _, err := (Checker{Host: ckHost()}).Check(context.Background(), env, ckState(), Input{}); err == nil {
		t.Error("Check without an evaluator succeeded")
	}
	h := ckHost()
	h.socketsErr = netstat.ErrNoSocketTables
	g, results, err := Checker{Host: h}.Check(context.Background(), env, ckState(), Input{Eval: ckEval(t, nil)})
	if !errors.Is(err, netstat.ErrNoSocketTables) {
		t.Errorf("Check on a host without socket tables: %v, want ErrNoSocketTables", err)
	}
	if g != (core.Guard{}) || results != nil {
		t.Errorf("a failed Check returned a guard %+v and results %+v", g, results)
	}
}

func TestVerdict(t *testing.T) {
	if g := verdict(nil); g != (core.Guard{ID: "firewall.lockout", OK: true, Message: "no protected flow to check"}) {
		t.Errorf("no flows: %+v", g)
	}
	g := verdict([]FlowResult{
		{Flow: "a", Result: fwstate.Result{Verdict: fwstate.Accept}},
		{Flow: "b", Result: fwstate.Result{Verdict: fwstate.Reject, Reason: "filter/ufw-user-input#2"}},
		{Flow: "c", Result: fwstate.Result{Verdict: fwstate.Unknown, Reason: "limit on a deciding rule"}},
		{Flow: "d", Result: fwstate.Result{}},
	})
	want := core.Guard{ID: "firewall.lockout",
		Message: "the change would cut b: reject (filter/ufw-user-input#2); c: unknown (limit on a deciding rule); d: no verdict"}
	if g != want {
		t.Errorf("verdict = %+v\nwant %+v", g, want)
	}
}
```

```go
package guard

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netfilter"
)

// GuardID is the id of the firewall's lockout guard.
const GuardID = "firewall.lockout"

// FlowResult is one protected flow on one in-interface and its verdict.
type FlowResult struct {
	Flow   string // human-readable: "ssh from 203.0.113.7 to 192.0.2.1:22 on eth0"
	Result fwstate.Result
}

// Checker runs the lockout guard against a host.
type Checker struct {
	Host Host // nil: LiveHost{}
}

// Check runs the lockout guard against this host; see Checker.Check.
func Check(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, st fwstate.Loaded, in Input) (core.Guard, []FlowResult, error) {
	return Checker{}.Check(ctx, env, st, in)
}

// Check gathers the host's live facts, builds every protected flow from
// them and from in, evaluates each flow with in.Eval against st on every
// eligible in-interface, and returns the firewall.lockout guard with one
// FlowResult per flow and interface. The guard fails when any flow is not
// accepted. Check never decides overridability or hard refusals; a fact it
// cannot read is an error.
func (c Checker) Check(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, st fwstate.Loaded, in Input) (core.Guard, []FlowResult, error) {
	if in.Eval == nil {
		return core.Guard{}, nil, errors.New("firewall: the guard has no evaluator")
	}
	h := c.Host
	if h == nil {
		h = LiveHost{}
	}
	f, err := gatherFacts(ctx, env, h)
	if err != nil {
		return core.Guard{}, nil, err
	}
	r := newRouter(h, f, st)
	var results []FlowResult
	for _, fl := range buildFlows(in, f) {
		for _, p := range r.probes(fl) {
			results = append(results, FlowResult{Flow: p.desc, Result: evaluate(r, p, in.Eval)})
		}
	}
	return verdict(results), results, nil
}

// evaluate walks one probe through the ruleset of its family.
func evaluate(r *router, p probe, eval func(*netfilter.Ruleset, fwstate.Packet, fwstate.Router) fwstate.Result) fwstate.Result {
	if p.unknown != "" {
		return fwstate.Result{Verdict: fwstate.Unknown, Reason: p.unknown}
	}
	rs := r.st.V4
	if p.pkt.Family == fwstate.V6 {
		rs = r.st.V6
	}
	if rs == nil {
		return fwstate.Result{Verdict: fwstate.Unknown, Reason: "no " + string(p.pkt.Family) + " ruleset was read"}
	}
	return eval(rs, p.pkt, r.route)
}

// verdict is the guard for the results: OK only when every flow is
// accepted, so a drop, a reject, an unknown and any verdict the guard does
// not know all fail it.
func verdict(results []FlowResult) core.Guard {
	var failed []string
	for _, fr := range results {
		if fr.Result.Verdict == fwstate.Accept {
			continue
		}
		v := string(fr.Result.Verdict)
		if v == "" {
			v = "no verdict"
		}
		s := fr.Flow + ": " + v
		if fr.Result.Reason != "" {
			s += " (" + fr.Result.Reason + ")"
		}
		failed = append(failed, s)
	}
	switch {
	case len(failed) > 0:
		return core.Guard{ID: GuardID, Message: "the change would cut " + strings.Join(failed, "; ")}
	case len(results) == 0:
		return core.Guard{ID: GuardID, OK: true, Message: "no protected flow to check"}
	}
	return core.Guard{ID: GuardID, OK: true, Message: fmt.Sprintf("every protected flow passes (%d checked)", len(results))}
}
```

**Files:**

- Consumes: `facts`, `gatherFacts`, `gFiles`, `gEnv`, `gHost`, `gIfaces` (Task 17); `flow`, `flPkt` (Task 31); `router`, `newRouter`, `(*router).probes`, `(*router).eligible`, `rtFacts`, `rtQuery`, `rtVia` (Task 36); `netstat.Interface` (merged code).
- Produces: `readRPFilter`, `tailnetIface`, `tailnetRanges`, `(*router).fromTailnet`, the `gFiles.errs` field (Part contracts, Task 44).

**Items:** 80

**Depends on:** Task 17, Task 31, Task 36

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-opus-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 1 - coupling 1 - risk 3 = 6
**Lenses:** security

Two controller rulings on eligible in-interfaces. First, a flow from a Tailscale address (`100.64.0.0/10`, `fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48`) is checked only on `tailscale0` while that interface is up, because tailscaled's `ts-input` drops such sources on every other interface and checking them there would refuse every change while a tailnet SSH session is open. Second, an interface whose `rp_filter` key vanished between listing the interfaces and reading the key is left out of the facts instead of failing the check; any other read error, and a missing `all` key, stay errors. The tests prove both rules, the fallback to the normal rule without an up `tailscale0`, that other sources are unaffected, and that other read errors still fail.

Replace the whole of `internal/modules/firewall/guard/facts.go` with:

```go
// Package guard is the firewall's lockout guard (spec 2.3, 1.5): it
// gathers this host's live facts, builds every protected flow from them and
// from the controller's guard context, evaluates each flow on every
// eligible in-interface against a predicted or loaded state, and reports
// the firewall.lockout guard.
package guard

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io/fs"
	"os"
	"strconv"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netstat"
)

// moduleID is the module every env.Files call names.
const moduleID = "firewall"

// controllerUnit is the controller's systemd unit; the firewall's manifest
// declares it as an external unit with the state operation (owner ruling
// R3).
const controllerUnit = "darkpanel-controller.service"

// Host reads the live facts of the host the agent runs on. LiveHost is the
// production implementation.
type Host interface {
	Sockets() ([]netstat.Socket, error)
	Interfaces() ([]netstat.Interface, error)
	RouteGet(q netstat.RouteQuery) (netstat.Route, error)
	PID() int // the agent's own process id
}

// LiveHost reads this host through internal/platform/netstat.
type LiveHost struct {
	ProcRoot string // the proc root sockets are read from; "" is /proc
}

// Sockets reads the socket table under ProcRoot.
func (h LiveHost) Sockets() ([]netstat.Socket, error) {
	root := h.ProcRoot
	if root == "" {
		root = "/proc"
	}
	return netstat.Table{Root: root}.Sockets()
}

// Interfaces lists the host's interfaces.
func (LiveHost) Interfaces() ([]netstat.Interface, error) { return netstat.Interfaces() }

// RouteGet asks the kernel for the route of q.
func (LiveHost) RouteGet(q netstat.RouteQuery) (netstat.Route, error) { return netstat.RouteGet(q) }

// PID is os.Getpid.
func (LiveHost) PID() int { return os.Getpid() }

// facts are the live facts one guard check uses.
type facts struct {
	sockets    []netstat.Socket
	ifaces     []netstat.Interface // without an interface that vanished before its rp_filter read
	rpFilter   map[string]int      // live net/ipv4/conf/<name>/rp_filter for "all" and every up, non-loopback interface
	controller int                 // MainPID of a running local darkpanel-controller.service; 0 when none
	pid        int                 // the agent's own process id
}

// gatherFacts reads the socket table, the interfaces, the live rp_filter
// values and the local controller's main process. Any read that fails is an
// error, so a guard never passes on facts it could not read; in particular a
// proc root without socket tables (netstat.ErrNoSocketTables) is not a host
// without sessions. The one exception is an interface whose rp_filter key
// no longer exists: it vanished after the interfaces were listed, so no
// packet can arrive on it, and it is left out.
func gatherFacts(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, h Host) (facts, error) {
	if env.Files == nil || env.Units == nil {
		return facts{}, errors.New("firewall: the guard needs the file writer and the unit client")
	}
	socks, err := h.Sockets()
	if err != nil {
		return facts{}, fmt.Errorf("firewall: read the socket table: %w", err)
	}
	ifaces, err := h.Interfaces()
	if err != nil {
		return facts{}, fmt.Errorf("firewall: read the interfaces: %w", err)
	}
	f := facts{sockets: socks, rpFilter: map[string]int{}, pid: h.PID()}
	if f.rpFilter["all"], err = readRPFilter(ctx, env, "all"); err != nil {
		return facts{}, err
	}
	for _, i := range ifaces {
		if i.Up && !i.Loopback {
			n, err := readRPFilter(ctx, env, i.Name)
			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
				continue
			}
			if err != nil {
				return facts{}, err
			}
			f.rpFilter[i.Name] = n
		}
		f.ifaces = append(f.ifaces, i)
	}
	st, err := env.Units.State(ctx, controllerUnit)
	if err != nil {
		return facts{}, fmt.Errorf("firewall: state of %s: %w", controllerUnit, err)
	}
	if st.LoadState != "not-found" && st.ActiveState != "inactive" {
		f.controller = int(st.MainPID)
	}
	return f, nil
}

// readRPFilter reads the live net/ipv4/conf/<name>/rp_filter. A read error
// is wrapped, so a key that does not exist still matches fs.ErrNotExist.
func readRPFilter(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, name string) (int, error) {
	key := "net/ipv4/conf/" + name + "/rp_filter"
	v, err := env.Files.ReadSysctl(ctx, moduleID, key)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("firewall: read %s: %w", key, err)
	}
	n, err := strconv.Atoi(v)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("firewall: %s is %q, not a number", key, v)
	}
	return n, nil
}
```

```go
// fromTailnet reports whether src is a tailnet address and tailscale0 is up.
func (r *router) fromTailnet(src netip.Addr) bool {
	in := false
	for _, p := range tailnetRanges {
		in = in || p.Contains(src.Unmap())
	}
	if !in {
		return false
	}
	for _, i := range r.f.ifaces {
		if i.Name == tailnetIface && i.Up {
			return true
		}
	}
```

### Task 45: Snapshot capture

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/modules/firewall/deps.go`
- Create: `internal/modules/firewall/snapshot.go`
- Test: `internal/modules/firewall/host_test.go`
- Test: `internal/modules/firewall/snapshot_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `takeImage` (Task 32); `saveSnapshot`, `attachNewest`, `setPostHashes`, `fileHash`, `getSnapshot`, `fwTestDB` (Task 37); `fwstate.Config`, `fwstate.StateFiles` (Task 18); `conf.Read` (Task 29); `coretest.NewFakeClock` (merged).
- Produces: `deps`, `snapshotEntries`, `fileHashes`, `systemActor`, `capture`, `attach`, `recordPostHashes` (Part contracts, Task 45); the shared fake host of `host_test.go` (Part constraints).

**Depends on:** Task 33, Task 37

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-opus-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 2 - risk 3 = 6
**Lenses:** silent-failures

The dependency seam the part brief fixes, and `capture`, which the engine calls as a revertible action's `Snapshot` before the change exists (spec 2.5, content). It records every UFW state file and the sysctl file, the live supported sysctl values, the guard context of the change's plan for a later connectivity exception, and, for a repair, the before-image. It returns the row id as the snapshot bytes. `attach` links the row to its change in Apply, and `recordPostHashes` records the files' hashes after the whole apply. The task also adds `host_test.go`, the fake host every later task tests with. It has UFW's files under a temporary root, read by the real `conf.Read`, a scripted ufw, the live sysctl values and loaded state, and an in-memory effects journal. The tests prove what a capture records, the before-image, an absent file, the system flag, that a failed capture saves nothing, the entry rules, attaching, and the post-apply hashes.

```go
package firewall

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"io/fs"
	"log/slog"
	"maps"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
```
