```go
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/coretest"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/store"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/conf"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netfilter"
)

// Rule tuples as UFW 0.36 writes them (captured in containers): fhRule22
// is a both-family Darkpanel rule tagged fhTag, fhRule3000 an IPv4 manual
// rule, fhRule53 an IPv6 manual rule.
const (
	fhTag        = "01J00000000000000000000001"
	fhRule22v4   = "### tuple ### allow tcp 22 0.0.0.0/0 any 0.0.0.0/0 in comment=6461726b70616e656c3a30314a3030303030303030303030303030303030303030303031"
	fhRule22v6   = "### tuple ### allow tcp 22 ::/0 any ::/0 in comment=6461726b70616e656c3a30314a3030303030303030303030303030303030303030303031"
	fhRule3000v4 = "### tuple ### allow tcp 3000 0.0.0.0/0 any 10.0.0.0/8 in"
	fhRule53v6   = "### tuple ### deny udp 53 ::/0 any 2001:db8::/32 in"
)

// fhSave is the loaded state every fake host starts with.
const fhSave = "*filter\n:INPUT DROP [0:0]\n:FORWARD DROP [0:0]\n:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]\n:ufw-user-input - [0:0]\n" +
	"-A INPUT -j ufw-user-input\n-A ufw-user-input -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT\nCOMMIT\n"

// fhState is what the scripted ufw edits: the values of the four files ufw
// writes.
type fhState struct {
	Enabled                bool
	LogLevel               string
	IPv6                   bool
	Input, Output, Forward string
	Rules4, Rules6         []string // tuple lines
}

// fhStateOf reads the edited values back from a configuration.
func fhStateOf(cfg fwstate.Config) fhState {
	s := fhState{Enabled: cfg.Enabled, LogLevel: cfg.LogLevel, IPv6: cfg.IPv6,
		Input: cfg.DefaultInput, Output: cfg.DefaultOutput, Forward: cfg.DefaultForward}
	for _, t := range cfg.Rules4 {
		s.Rules4 = append(s.Rules4, t.Raw)
	}
	for _, t := range cfg.Rules6 {
		s.Rules6 = append(s.Rules6, t.Raw)
	}
	return s
}

func fhRules(lines []string) []byte {
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString("*filter\n### RULES ###\n")
	for _, l := range lines {
		b.WriteString(l + "\n")
	}
	b.WriteString("### END RULES ###\nCOMMIT\n")
	return []byte(b.String())
}

func fhYes(v bool) string {
	if v {
		return "yes"
	}
	return "no"
}

// files renders the four files ufw writes, by absolute path.
func (s fhState) files() map[string][]byte {
	return map[string][]byte{
		"/etc/ufw/user.rules":  fhRules(s.Rules4),
		"/etc/ufw/user6.rules": fhRules(s.Rules6),
		"/etc/ufw/ufw.conf":    []byte(fmt.Sprintf("ENABLED=%s\nLOGLEVEL=%s\n", fhYes(s.Enabled), s.LogLevel)),
		"/etc/default/ufw": []byte(fmt.Sprintf("IPV6=%s\nDEFAULT_INPUT_POLICY=%q\nDEFAULT_OUTPUT_POLICY=%q\n"+
			"DEFAULT_FORWARD_POLICY=%q\nMANAGE_BUILTINS=no\nIPT_SYSCTL=/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf\n",
			fhYes(s.IPv6), s.Input, s.Output, s.Forward)),
	}
}

// fakeHost is a test host: UFW's files under a temporary root, which the
// real conf.Read parses; a scripted ufw; other programs that only record
// their input; the live sysctl values; the loaded state; and an in-memory
// effects journal. It implements core.Runner and core.FileWriter.
type fakeHost struct {
	t    *testing.T
	root string
	db   *store.DB

	// ufw scripts the ufw vectors by strings.Join(args, " "): the function
	// edits the files' values and returns ufw's exit code. An unscripted
	// vector exits 1 and changes nothing.
	ufw map[string]func(s *fhState) int
	// onRun runs after every other program and may change the host.
	onRun  func(h *fakeHost, cmd core.Cmd) core.CmdResult
	runErr map[string]error // Run fails before the program starts, by "<path> <args>"
	calls  []string         // "run <path> <args>", "restore <path>", "sysctl <key>=<value>", in order
	stdin  map[string][]byte

	sysctl     map[string]string // live values, by /proc/sys key
	sysctlFail map[string]error  // WriteSysctl fails, by key
	sysctlLie  map[string]string // ReadSysctl answers this instead, by key

	loaded     fwstate.Loaded // V4 and V6 readLoaded returns; Sysctl comes from sysctl
	loadErr    error
	predicted  *fwstate.Loaded // what predict returns; nil means loaded
	predictErr error
	diffs      []fwstate.ChainDiff // what compare returns
	keeps      []func(f fwstate.Family, table, chain string) bool

	guardOK     bool
	guardDetail string
	guardErr    error
	guardCalls  int

	journal *fhJournal
	clock   *coretest.FakeClock
}

// newFakeHost writes a host whose UFW is active with fhRule22 and
// fhRule3000, and whose loaded state is fhSave.
func newFakeHost(t *testing.T) *fakeHost {
	t.Helper()
	h := &fakeHost{
		t: t, root: t.TempDir(), db: fwTestDB(t),
		ufw:   map[string]func(s *fhState) int{},
		stdin: map[string][]byte{}, runErr: map[string]error{},
		sysctl: map[string]string{
			"net/ipv4/ip_forward": "0", "net/ipv4/conf/all/rp_filter": "2", "net/ipv4/conf/default/rp_filter": "1",
			"net/ipv4/conf/eth0/rp_filter": "1", "net/ipv6/conf/all/forwarding": "0", "net/ipv6/conf/eth0/accept_ra": "1",
		},
		sysctlFail: map[string]error{}, sysctlLie: map[string]string{},
		guardOK: true,
		journal: &fhJournal{},
		clock:   coretest.NewFakeClock(time.Date(2026, 10, 24, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)),
	}
	for p, data := range map[string]string{
		"/etc/ufw/before.rules": "*filter\n# before\nCOMMIT\n", "/etc/ufw/before6.rules": "*filter\n# before6\nCOMMIT\n",
		"/etc/ufw/after.rules": "*filter\n# after\nCOMMIT\n", "/etc/ufw/after6.rules": "*filter\n# after6\nCOMMIT\n",
		"/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf": "net/ipv4/ip_forward=0\n",
	} {
		h.writeFile(p, []byte(data))
	}
	h.setState(fhState{Enabled: true, LogLevel: "low", IPv6: true, Input: "DROP", Output: "ACCEPT", Forward: "DROP",
		Rules4: []string{fhRule22v4, fhRule3000v4}, Rules6: []string{fhRule22v6}})
	h.loaded = fwstate.Loaded{Variant: "nft", V4: fhParse(t, fhSave), V6: fhParse(t, fhSave)}
	return h
}

func fhParse(t *testing.T, text string) *netfilter.Ruleset {
	t.Helper()
	rs, err := netfilter.Parse(strings.NewReader(text))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return rs
}

func (h *fakeHost) writeFile(p string, data []byte) {
	h.t.Helper()
	full := filepath.Join(h.root, p)
	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(full), 0o750); err != nil {
		h.t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(full, data, 0o600); err != nil {
		h.t.Fatal(err)
	}
}

// setState writes the four files ufw writes.
func (h *fakeHost) setState(s fhState) {
	h.t.Helper()
	for p, data := range s.files() {
		h.writeFile(p, data)
	}
}

// config reads the host's configuration as production does.
func (h *fakeHost) config() fwstate.Config {
	h.t.Helper()
	cfg, err := conf.Read(h.root)
	if err != nil {
		h.t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return cfg
}

// state reads the values ufw edits from the host's files.
func (h *fakeHost) state() fhState { return fhStateOf(h.config()) }

func (h *fakeHost) Run(_ context.Context, cmd core.Cmd) (core.CmdResult, error) {
	key := strings.TrimSpace(cmd.Path + " " + strings.Join(cmd.Args, " "))
	h.calls = append(h.calls, "run "+key)
	if err := h.runErr[key]; err != nil {
		return core.CmdResult{}, err
	}
	if cmd.Path != "/usr/sbin/ufw" {
		h.stdin[cmd.Path] = cmd.Stdin
		if h.onRun != nil {
			return h.onRun(h, cmd), nil
		}
		return core.CmdResult{}, nil
	}
	f, ok := h.ufw[strings.Join(cmd.Args, " ")]
	if !ok {
		return core.CmdResult{ExitCode: 1, Stderr: []byte("ERROR: unscripted vector\n")}, nil
	}
	s := h.state()
	code := f(&s)
	h.setState(s)
	return core.CmdResult{ExitCode: code}, nil
}

var errFakeUnused = errors.New("fake: not used by the firewall")

func (h *fakeHost) WriteFile(context.Context, string, string, []byte, fs.FileMode) error {
	return errFakeUnused
}
func (h *fakeHost) ReplaceBlock(context.Context, string, string, string, []byte) error {
	return errFakeUnused
}
func (h *fakeHost) RemoveBlock(context.Context, string, string, string) error { return errFakeUnused }
func (h *fakeHost) Remove(context.Context, string, string) error              { return errFakeUnused }
func (h *fakeHost) WriteManaged(context.Context, string, string, string, []byte, fs.FileMode, int, int) error {
	return errFakeUnused
}
func (h *fakeHost) RemoveManaged(context.Context, string, string, string) error { return errFakeUnused }
func (h *fakeHost) Rename(context.Context, string, string, string) error        { return errFakeUnused }
func (h *fakeHost) EnsureServiceDir(context.Context, string, string) error      { return errFakeUnused }
func (h *fakeHost) RenameIn(context.Context, string, string, string, string) error {
	return errFakeUnused
}
func (h *fakeHost) RemoveIn(context.Context, string, string, string) error { return errFakeUnused }
func (h *fakeHost) RemoveServiceDir(context.Context, string, string) error { return errFakeUnused }
func (h *fakeHost) Owns(context.Context, string, string) (bool, error)     { return false, errFakeUnused }

// Restore writes or removes a file under the root, as platform.Files does.
func (h *fakeHost) Restore(_ context.Context, module string, e core.RestoreEntry) error {
	if module != ID {
		return fmt.Errorf("fake: module %s restores %s", module, e.Path)
	}
	h.calls = append(h.calls, "restore "+e.Path)
	full := filepath.Join(h.root, e.Path)
	if !e.Present {
		if err := os.Remove(full); err != nil && !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
			return err
		}
		return nil
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(full, e.Data, e.Mode); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return os.Chmod(full, e.Mode)
}

func (h *fakeHost) ReadSysctl(_ context.Context, module, key string) (string, error) {
	if module != ID {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("fake: module %s reads sysctl %s", module, key)
	}
	if v, ok := h.sysctlLie[key]; ok {
		return v, nil
	}
	v, ok := h.sysctl[key]
	if !ok {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("fake: sysctl %s: %w", key, fs.ErrNotExist)
	}
	return v, nil
}

func (h *fakeHost) WriteSysctl(_ context.Context, module, key, value string) error {
	if module != ID {
		return fmt.Errorf("fake: module %s writes sysctl %s", module, key)
	}
	h.calls = append(h.calls, "sysctl "+key+"="+value)
	if err := h.sysctlFail[key]; err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if _, ok := h.sysctl[key]; !ok {
		return fmt.Errorf("fake: sysctl %s: %w", key, fs.ErrNotExist)
	}
	h.sysctl[key] = value
	return nil
}

// env is the Env of change c1 by user:u1 on this host.
func (h *fakeHost) env() core.Env {
	return core.Env{
		HostID: "h1", ChangeID: "c1", Principal: core.Principal{Actor: "user:u1", Scope: core.ScopeAdmin},
		Effects: h.journal, DB: h.db, Exec: h, Files: h, Clock: h.clock,
		Log: slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(io.Discard, nil)),
	}
}

// deps are the host-facing functions over this host: the real conf.Read
// and scripted readers, predictor, comparison and guard.
func (h *fakeHost) deps() deps {
	return deps{
		root:       h.root,
		readConfig: conf.Read,
		readLoaded: func(context.Context, core.Env) (fwstate.Loaded, error) {
			st := h.loaded
			st.Sysctl = maps.Clone(h.sysctl)
			return st, h.loadErr
		},
		predict: func(fwstate.Config, fwstate.Loaded, fwstate.Transition) (fwstate.Loaded, error) {
			if h.predicted != nil {
				return *h.predicted, h.predictErr
			}
			return h.loaded, h.predictErr
		},
		edit: func(cfg fwstate.Config, args []string) (fwstate.Config, error) {
			f, ok := h.ufw[strings.Join(args, " ")]
			if !ok {
				return fwstate.Config{}, fmt.Errorf("fake: unscripted vector %q", args)
			}
			s := fhStateOf(cfg)
			f(&s)
			root := h.t.TempDir()
			for p, e := range cfg.Files {
				if e.Present {
					if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(filepath.Join(root, p)), 0o750); err != nil {
						return fwstate.Config{}, err
					}
					if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(root, p), e.Data, 0o600); err != nil {
						return fwstate.Config{}, err
					}
				}
			}
			for p, data := range s.files() {
				if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(root, p), data, 0o600); err != nil {
					return fwstate.Config{}, err
				}
			}
			return conf.Read(root)
		},
		files: func(cfg fwstate.Config) (map[string][]byte, error) { return fhStateOf(cfg).files(), nil },
		compare: func(_, _ fwstate.Loaded, keep func(f fwstate.Family, table, chain string) bool) []fwstate.ChainDiff {
			h.keeps = append(h.keeps, keep)
			return h.diffs
		},
		sysctl: func(_ fwstate.Config, cur map[string]string, _ fwstate.Transition) (map[string]string, error) {
			return cur, nil
		},
		lockout: func(context.Context, core.Env, fwstate.Loaded, *core.GuardContext) (bool, string, error) {
			h.guardCalls++
			return h.guardOK, h.guardDetail, h.guardErr
		},
	}
}

// fhJournal is an in-memory core.EffectJournal.
type fhJournal struct {
	effects []core.Effect
	failOn  string // "intend", "made" or "skipped": that method fails
}

func (j *fhJournal) Intend(_ context.Context, e core.Effect, _ []byte) (int, error) {
	if j.failOn == "intend" {
		return 0, errors.New("fake: journal unavailable")
	}
	e.Seq, e.State, e.ChangeID = len(j.effects)+1, core.EffectIntended, "c1"
	j.effects = append(j.effects, e)
	return e.Seq, nil
}

func (j *fhJournal) find(seq int) (*core.Effect, error) {
	if seq < 1 || seq > len(j.effects) || j.effects[seq-1].State != core.EffectIntended {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("fake: effect %d is not intended", seq)
	}
	return &j.effects[seq-1], nil
}

func (j *fhJournal) Made(_ context.Context, seq int, resource string, post core.StateDoc) error {
	if j.failOn == "made" {
		return errors.New("fake: journal unavailable")
	}
	e, err := j.find(seq)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	e.State, e.Resource, e.Post = core.EffectMade, resource, &post
	return nil
}

func (j *fhJournal) Skipped(_ context.Context, seq int) error {
	if j.failOn == "skipped" {
		return errors.New("fake: journal unavailable")
	}
	e, err := j.find(seq)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	e.State = core.EffectSkipped
	return nil
}

func (j *fhJournal) List(context.Context) ([]core.Effect, error) {
	return append([]core.Effect(nil), j.effects...), nil
}

func (j *fhJournal) Secret(context.Context, int) ([]byte, error) { return nil, nil }

var (
	_ core.Runner        = (*fakeHost)(nil)
	_ core.FileWriter    = (*fakeHost)(nil)
	_ core.EffectJournal = (*fhJournal)(nil)
)
```

Create `internal/modules/firewall/snapshot_test.go`:

```go
package firewall

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"maps"
	"net/netip"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"reflect"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
)

func TestCaptureRecordsTheLogicalState(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newFakeHost(t)
	gc := &core.GuardContext{AgentPeers: []netip.Addr{netip.MustParseAddr("192.0.2.7")}, Complete: true}
	raw, err := capture(ctx, h.env(), h.deps(), gc, false)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	s, err := getSnapshot(ctx, h.db, string(raw))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	wantPaths := append(append([]string(nil), fwstate.StateFiles...), "/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf")
	if len(s.Entries) != len(wantPaths) {
		t.Fatalf("%d entries, want %d", len(s.Entries), len(wantPaths))
	}
	for i, e := range s.Entries {
		if e.Path != wantPaths[i] {
			t.Errorf("entry %d is %s, want %s", i, e.Path, wantPaths[i])
		}
		data, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(h.root, e.Path))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if !e.Present || string(e.Data) != string(data) || e.Mode != 0o600 {
			t.Errorf("entry %s = present %v mode %o, %d bytes; want the file", e.Path, e.Present, e.Mode, len(e.Data))
		}
		if s.Hashes[e.Path] != fileHash(e) {
			t.Errorf("hash of %s = %s, want %s", e.Path, s.Hashes[e.Path], fileHash(e))
		}
	}
	if len(s.Hashes) != len(wantPaths) {
		t.Errorf("%d hashes, want %d", len(s.Hashes), len(wantPaths))
	}
	want := snapshotState{Enabled: true, Sysctl: h.sysctl, Guard: gc}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(s.State, want) {
		t.Errorf("state = %+v, want %+v", s.State, want)
	}
	if s.Actor != "user:u1" || s.System || !s.Baseline || s.ChangeID != "" || s.PostHashes != nil {
		t.Errorf("snapshot = actor %s system %v baseline %v change %q post %v", s.Actor, s.System, s.Baseline, s.ChangeID, s.PostHashes)
	}
	if !s.CreatedAt.Equal(h.clock.Now()) {
		t.Errorf("created at %v, want %v", s.CreatedAt, h.clock.Now())
	}
}

func TestCaptureRepairBeforeImage(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newFakeHost(t)
	raw, err := capture(ctx, h.env(), h.deps(), nil, true)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	s, err := getSnapshot(ctx, h.db, string(raw))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(s.State.Image, takeImage(h.loaded)) {
		t.Errorf("before-image = %+v, want the loaded state's", s.State.Image)
	}
	if s.State.Guard != nil {
		t.Errorf("guard = %+v, want none", s.State.Guard)
	}
}

func TestCaptureAbsentFileAndSystemActor(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newFakeHost(t)
	if err := os.Remove(filepath.Join(h.root, "/etc/ufw/after6.rules")); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	env := h.env()
	env.Principal.Actor = "system:firewall.reconcile"
	raw, err := capture(ctx, env, h.deps(), nil, false)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	s, err := getSnapshot(ctx, h.db, string(raw))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !s.System {
		t.Error("a firewall background task's snapshot is not system")
	}
	if e := s.Entries[5]; e.Path != "/etc/ufw/after6.rules" || e.Present || s.Hashes[e.Path] != "absent" {
		t.Errorf("absent file recorded as %+v, hash %s", e, s.Hashes[e.Path])
	}
	for actor, want := range map[string]bool{
		"system:firewall.reconcile": true, "system:recovery": false, "system:revert-timer": false,
		"user:u1": false, "system:firewallx.a": false,
	} {
		if got := systemActor(actor); got != want {
			t.Errorf("systemActor(%q) = %v, want %v", actor, got, want)
		}
	}
}

func TestCaptureFailsWithoutSaving(t *testing.T) {

func TestSnapshotEntries(t *testing.T) {
	files := map[string]core.RestoreEntry{}
	for _, p := range fwstate.StateFiles {
		files[p] = core.RestoreEntry{Path: p, Present: true}
	}
	entries, err := snapshotEntries(fwstate.Config{Files: maps.Clone(files)})
	if err != nil || len(entries) != len(fwstate.StateFiles) {
		t.Errorf("without a sysctl file: %d entries, %v", len(entries), err)
	}
	missing := maps.Clone(files)
	delete(missing, "/etc/ufw/user6.rules")
	if _, err := snapshotEntries(fwstate.Config{Files: missing}); err == nil {
		t.Error("a configuration without user6.rules gave entries")
	}
	foreign := maps.Clone(files)
	foreign["/etc/sysctl.conf"] = core.RestoreEntry{Path: "/etc/sysctl.conf", Present: true}
	if _, err := snapshotEntries(fwstate.Config{Files: foreign}); err == nil {
		t.Error("a file outside /etc/ufw became an entry")
	}
}

func TestAttachAndPostHashes(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newFakeHost(t)
	env, d := h.env(), h.deps()
	raw, err := capture(ctx, env, d, nil, false)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	id, err := attach(ctx, env)
	if err != nil || id != string(raw) {
		t.Fatalf("attach = %s, %v; want %s", id, err, raw)
	}
	noChange := env
	noChange.ChangeID = ""
	if _, err := attach(ctx, noChange); err == nil {
		t.Error("attach without a change id succeeded")
	}
	s := h.state()
	s.Rules4 = s.Rules4[:1]
	h.setState(s)
	if err := recordPostHashes(ctx, env, d, id); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	got, err := getSnapshot(ctx, h.db, id)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if want := fileHashes(h.config().Files); !reflect.DeepEqual(got.PostHashes, want) {
		t.Errorf("post hashes = %v, want %v", got.PostHashes, want)
	}
	if got.PostHashes["/etc/ufw/user.rules"] == got.Hashes["/etc/ufw/user.rules"] {
		t.Error("the post-apply hash of a changed file equals its capture hash")
	}
	if got.ChangeID != "c1" {
		t.Errorf("attached to %q, want c1", got.ChangeID)
	}
}
```

```go
package firewall

import (
	"context"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
)

// deps are the firewall's host-facing functions. Production values come
// from conf, loaded, predict and guard; tests replace them.
type deps struct {
	root       string // "/" in production; the root conf.Read reads under
	readConfig func(root string) (fwstate.Config, error)
	readLoaded func(ctx context.Context, env core.Env) (fwstate.Loaded, error)
	predict    func(cfg fwstate.Config, cur fwstate.Loaded, tr fwstate.Transition) (fwstate.Loaded, error)
	edit       func(cfg fwstate.Config, args []string) (fwstate.Config, error)
	files      func(cfg fwstate.Config) (map[string][]byte, error)
	compare    func(a, b fwstate.Loaded, keep func(f fwstate.Family, table, chain string) bool) []fwstate.ChainDiff
	sysctl     func(cfg fwstate.Config, cur map[string]string, tr fwstate.Transition) (map[string]string, error)
	// lockout evaluates the lockout guard on st for the connectivity
	// exception; gc is the GuardContext the snapshot recorded.
	lockout func(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, st fwstate.Loaded, gc *core.GuardContext) (ok bool, detail string, err error)
}
```

Create `internal/modules/firewall/snapshot.go`:

```go
package firewall

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/rand"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"maps"
	"slices"
	"strings"

	"github.com/oklog/ulid/v2"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
)

// snapshotEntries returns the files a snapshot holds (spec 2.5): every
// state file in fwstate.StateFiles order, then UFW's sysctl file when the
// configuration records it.
func snapshotEntries(cfg fwstate.Config) ([]core.RestoreEntry, error) {
	var out []core.RestoreEntry
	for _, p := range fwstate.StateFiles {
		e, ok := cfg.Files[p]
		if !ok {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("firewall: the configuration does not record %s", p)
		}
		out = append(out, e)
	}
	for _, p := range slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(cfg.Files)) {
		if slices.Contains(fwstate.StateFiles, p) {
			continue
		}
		if !strings.HasPrefix(p, "/etc/ufw/") {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("firewall: the configuration records %s, which is not a UFW file", p)
		}
		out = append(out, cfg.Files[p])
	}
	return out, nil
}

// fileHashes returns fileHash of every file, by path.
func fileHashes(files map[string]core.RestoreEntry) map[string]string {
	out := make(map[string]string, len(files))
	for p, e := range files {
		out[p] = fileHash(e)
	}
	return out
}

// systemActor reports whether actor is one of the firewall's background
// tasks (actor system:<task id>, task ids firewall.<name>), whose changes
// count against the system snapshots' retention.
func systemActor(actor string) bool { return strings.HasPrefix(actor, "system:"+ID+".") }

// capture takes the firewall's logical snapshot before a change (spec 2.5)
// and returns the snapshot bytes the engine stores: the snapshot's id. The
// engine calls it before the change exists, so the snapshot is attached
// later (attach). gc is the guard context of the change's plan, kept for
// the connectivity exception of a revert; withImage also takes a repair's
// loaded-state before-image (spec 2.3). The host's first snapshot becomes
// its baseline, and retention prunes in the same transaction.
func capture(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, d deps, gc *core.GuardContext, withImage bool) ([]byte, error) {
	cfg, err := d.readConfig(d.root)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("firewall: snapshot: %w", err)
	}
	entries, err := snapshotEntries(cfg)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("firewall: snapshot: %w", err)
	}
	st, err := d.readLoaded(ctx, env)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("firewall: snapshot: %w", err)
	}
	state := snapshotState{Enabled: cfg.Enabled, Sysctl: maps.Clone(st.Sysctl), Guard: gc}
	if state.Sysctl == nil {
		state.Sysctl = map[string]string{}
	}
	if withImage {
		state.Image = takeImage(st)
	}
	now := env.Clock.Now()
	s := snapshot{
		ID:        ulid.MustNew(ulid.Timestamp(now), rand.Reader).String(),
		CreatedAt: now,
		Actor:     env.Principal.Actor,
		System:    systemActor(env.Principal.Actor),
		Entries:   entries,
		State:     state,
		Hashes:    fileHashes(cfg.Files),
	}
	if _, err := saveSnapshot(ctx, env.DB, s); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return []byte(s.ID), nil
}

// attach records env.ChangeID on the snapshot captured for it and returns
// the snapshot's id; Apply calls it first. It is idempotent.
func attach(ctx context.Context, env core.Env) (string, error) {
	if env.ChangeID == "" {
		return "", errors.New("firewall: attach needs the change id")
	}
	return attachNewest(ctx, env.DB, env.ChangeID)
}

// recordPostHashes records on snapshot id the hash of every UFW file as it
// stands right after the change applied (spec 2.5); Apply calls it last.
func recordPostHashes(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, d deps, id string) error {
	cfg, err := d.readConfig(d.root)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("firewall: post-apply hashes: %w", err)
	}
	return setPostHashes(ctx, env.DB, id, fileHashes(cfg.Files))
}
```

### Task 46: Parse ufw argument vectors

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/modules/firewall/predict/vector.go`
- Test: `internal/modules/firewall/predict/vector_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `tupleLine`, `multiPort` (Task 38); `model.AddArgs`, `model.DeleteArgs`, `model.InsertArgs`, `model.ParseTuple`, `model.Protos` (base).
- Produces: `parseVector`, `vector`, the `vec*` kinds, `forFamily`, `normalizeTuple`, `normalizeAddr`, `sortPorts` (Part contracts Task 46); the shared test helper `predictShellSplit`.

**Depends on:** Task 38

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-sonnet-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 2 - risk 2 = 5

`parseVector` reads one ufw argument vector as UFW 0.36's parser does, for the forms Darkpanel writes: `model.AddArgs`, `DeleteArgs` and `InsertArgs` vectors, the same full form without `from` or `to` (the golden `commands.txt` lines), `default`, `logging`, `--force enable`, `disable` and `reload`. Everything else is refused, including what ufw accepts but Darkpanel never writes (short form, application rules, service names, dotted netmasks, interface names outside the rule model's pattern, non-UTF-8 comments, `prepend`, delete by number). `forFamily` is the tuple UFW stores in one family's file (`set_v6`, then `normalize`). `TestParseVectorRules` compares the tuple lines with those ufw wrote for the same commands (golden `rules` scenario and container captures) and checks that each reads back through `model.ParseTuple`.

```go
package predict

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/model"
)

// predictShellSplit splits a commands.txt line as the shell does for the
// quoting the golden scenarios use: words separated by spaces, single
// quotes grouping.
func predictShellSplit(line string) []string {
	var out []string
	var b strings.Builder
	inWord, quoted := false, false
	for _, r := range line {
		switch {
		case r == '\'':
			quoted, inWord = !quoted, true
		case r == ' ' && !quoted:
			if inWord {
				out = append(out, b.String())
				b.Reset()
			}
			inWord = false
		default:
			b.WriteRune(r)
			inWord = true
		}
	}
	if inWord {
		out = append(out, b.String())
	}
	return out
}

// vectorTestRule is a model rule whose argument vectors the tests parse.
var vectorTestRule = model.Rule{ID: "01J00000000000000000000000", Action: model.ActionDeny, Direction: model.DirRoute,
	Proto: model.ProtoUDP, From: "10.0.0.0/8", FromPort: "53", To: model.Any, ToPort: "1000:2000,80",
	InIface: "eth0", OutIface: "docker0", Family: model.FamilyV4, Log: model.LogAll, Comment: "dns"}

// TestParseVectorRules checks the tuple lines a vector gives in each
// family against the lines ufw wrote for the same command (the golden
// "rules" scenario and the captures of TestFilesRuleLines), and against
// the model's own vectors.

			want4: "### tuple ### allow tcp 22 0.0.0.0/0 any 0.0.0.0/0 in comment=6461726b70616e656c3a30314a303030303030303030303030303030303030303030303020737368",
			want6: "### tuple ### allow tcp 22 ::/0 any ::/0 in comment=6461726b70616e656c3a30314a303030303030303030303030303030303030303030303020737368"},
		{args: predictShellSplit("deny in proto udp from 2001:db8::/32 to any port 5000:5100"),
			want6: "### tuple ### deny udp 5000:5100 ::/0 any 2001:db8::/32 in"},
		{args: predictShellSplit("route allow out on eth0 proto tcp to 172.17.0.2 port 80"),
			want4: "### tuple ### route:allow tcp 80 172.17.0.2 any 0.0.0.0/0 out_eth0"},

		{args: predictShellSplit("reject in to any port 3000"),
			want4: "### tuple ### reject any 3000 0.0.0.0/0 any 0.0.0.0/0 in", want6: "### tuple ### reject any 3000 ::/0 any ::/0 in"},
		{args: predictShellSplit("allow in log proto tcp from 10.0.0.0/8 to any port 443,8000:8100"),

		{args: predictShellSplit("allow in on eth0 log-all from 2001:db8::/32 to any port 8080:8090 proto udp"),

		{args: model.InsertArgs(3, vectorTestRule), position: 3,
			want4: "### tuple ### route:deny_log-all udp 80,1000:2000 0.0.0.0/0 53 10.0.0.0/8 in_eth0!out_docker0 comment=6461726b70616e656c3a30314a303030303030303030303030303030303030303030303020646e73"},
		{args: []string{"allow", "in", "proto", "tcp", "from", "10.1.2.3/8", "to", "192.0.2.7/32", "port", "22"},
			want4: "### tuple ### allow tcp 22 192.0.2.7 any 10.0.0.0/8 in"},
	} {
		v, err := parseVector(tc.args)
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("%q: %v", tc.args, err)
			continue
		}
		if v.kind != vecRule || v.remove != tc.remove || v.position != tc.position {
			t.Errorf("%q: kind %s remove %v position %d", tc.args, v.kind, v.remove, v.position)
		}
		for _, f := range []struct {
			fam  model.Family
			want string
		}{{model.FamilyV4, tc.want4}, {model.FamilyV6, tc.want6}} {
			in := v.iptype == model.FamilyBoth || v.iptype == f.fam
			if in != (f.want != "") {
				t.Errorf("%q: iptype %s, want %s line %q", tc.args, v.iptype, f.fam, f.want)
				continue
			}
			if !in {
				continue
			}
			got, err := forFamily(v.rule, f.fam)
			if err != nil {
				t.Errorf("%q %s: %v", tc.args, f.fam, err)
				continue
			}
			if got.Raw != f.want {
				t.Errorf("%q %s:\n got %s\nwant %s", tc.args, f.fam, got.Raw, f.want)
			}
			parsed, err := model.ParseTuple(got.Raw, f.fam == model.FamilyV6)
			if err != nil || parsed != got {
				t.Errorf("%q %s: tuple %+v does not read back as %+v (%v)", tc.args, f.fam, got, parsed, err)
			}
		}
	}
}

func TestParseVectorCommands(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		args []string
		want vector
	}{
		{[]string{"--force", "enable"}, vector{kind: vecEnable}},
		{[]string{"disable"}, vector{kind: vecDisable}},
		{[]string{"reload"}, vector{kind: vecReload}},
		{[]string{"default", "allow", "outgoing"}, vector{kind: vecDefault, policy: "allow", chain: "OUTPUT"}},
		{[]string{"default", "reject", "incoming"}, vector{kind: vecDefault, policy: "reject", chain: "INPUT"}},
		{[]string{"default", "deny", "routed"}, vector{kind: vecDefault, policy: "deny", chain: "FORWARD"}},
		{[]string{"logging", "on"}, vector{kind: vecLogging, level: "on"}},
		{[]string{"logging", "high"}, vector{kind: vecLogging, level: "high"}},
	} {
		got, err := parseVector(tc.args)
		if err != nil || got != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("%q = %+v, %v; want %+v", tc.args, got, err, tc.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestParseVectorRefuses(t *testing.T) {
	for _, line := range []string{
		"",
		"enable",
		"status",
		"allow 22/tcp",
		"allow 'DP Web'",
		"allow in proto tcp to any app 'DP Web'",
		"allow in proto tcp to any port ssh",
		"prepend allow in proto tcp to any port 22",
		"delete 3",
		"insert 0 allow in proto tcp to any port 22",
		"insert x allow in proto tcp to any port 22",
		"default allow input",
		"default permit incoming",
		"logging loud",
		"allow log in proto tcp to any port 22",
		"route allow in proto tcp to any port 80",
		"allow in proto tcp from 10.0.0.1 to 2001:db8::1 port 22",
		"allow in proto ipv6 from 2001:db8::1",
		"allow in proto esp to any port 22",
		"allow in to any port 80,443",
		"allow in proto vrrp from any",
		"allow in from 10.0.0.0/255.0.0.0",
		"allow in",
		"allow in on eth0!x proto esp",
		"route allow in on 00 out on %0",
		"allow in on eth0.verylongname proto esp",
		"allow in proto tcp to any to 10.0.0.1",
		"allow in proto tcp to any port 0",
		"allow in proto tcp to any port 22:22",
		"allow in proto tcp port 22",
		"allow in proto tcp to fe80::1%eth0",
		"allow in on eth0 out on eth1 proto esp",
		"allow in proto tcp to any port 22 extra",
	} {
		vectorTestRefused(t, predictShellSplit(line))
	}
	vectorTestRefused(t, []string{"allow", "in", "proto", "tcp", "to", "any", "port", "22", "comment", "it's"})
	vectorTestRefused(t, []string{"deny", "to", "any", "comment", "\xe5"})
}

func vectorTestRefused(t *testing.T, args []string) {
	t.Helper()
	if v, err := parseVector(args); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("%q parsed as %+v, want a refusal", args, v)
	} else if !strings.HasPrefix(err.Error(), "predict: ufw ") {
		t.Errorf("%q: error %q lacks the prefix", args, err)
	}
}

func TestNormalize(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		in   string
		v6   bool
		want string
	}{
		{"10.0.0.1/8", false, "10.0.0.0/8"},
		{"10.0.0.1/32", false, "10.0.0.1"},
		{"10.1.2.3/255.255.0.0", false, "10.1.0.0/16"},
		{"10.1.2.3/255.0.255.0", false, "10.0.2.0/255.0.255.0"},
		{"0.0.0.0/0", false, "0.0.0.0/0"},
		{"2001:db8::1/32", true, "2001:db8::1/32"},
		{"2001:0db8::1/128", true, "2001:db8::1"},
		{"::/0", true, "::/0"},
	} {
		if got, err := normalizeAddr(tc.in, tc.v6); err != nil || got != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("normalizeAddr(%q) = %q, %v; want %q", tc.in, got, err, tc.want)
		}
	}
	if _, err := normalizeAddr("10.0.0.1", true); err == nil {
		t.Error("an IPv4 address normalized as IPv6")
	}
	if got := sortPorts("8000:8100,443,22:30,22,1000:1100,1000:1050"); got != "22,22:30,443,1000:1050,1000:1100,8000:8100" {
		t.Errorf("sortPorts = %q", got)
	}
}
```

```go
package predict

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"fmt"
	"math/bits"
	"net/netip"
	"regexp"
	"slices"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"unicode/utf8"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/model"
)

// The kinds of ufw command Edit simulates.
const (
	vecRule    = "rule"
	vecDefault = "default"
	vecLogging = "logging"
	vecEnable  = "enable"
	vecDisable = "disable"
	vecReload  = "reload"
)

// vector is one parsed ufw argument vector.
type vector struct {
	kind string
	// rule: the rule before UFW fixes its addresses for a family; Src and
	// Dst are "0.0.0.0/0" for any, Family is unset and Raw empty.
	rule     model.Tuple
	iptype   model.Family // rule: the families UFW writes it to
	remove   bool         // rule: delete
	position int          // rule: insert position, 0 to append
	policy   string       // default: allow, deny or reject
	chain    string       // default: INPUT, OUTPUT or FORWARD
	level    string       // logging: off, on, low, medium, high or full
}

var (
	vecPortRe   = regexp.MustCompile(`^\d([0-9,:]*\d+)*$`)
	vecRangeRe  = regexp.MustCompile(`^\d+:\d+$`)
	vecNumberRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^\d+$`)
	vecIfaceRe  = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_.+-]{0,14}$`)
)

// parseVector reads one ufw argument vector as UFW 0.36's parser does, for
// the forms Darkpanel issues: the full rule form model.AddArgs, DeleteArgs
// and InsertArgs write (and the same form with "from" or "to" left out),
// "default <allow|deny|reject> <incoming|outgoing|routed>", "logging
// <off|on|low|medium|high|full>", "--force enable", "disable" and
// "reload". Anything else is refused, including what ufw would accept
// but Darkpanel never writes: the short form, application rules, service
// names, dotted netmasks, a comment that is not UTF-8 (UFW drops the
// invalid bytes), interface names outside the rule model's pattern
// (UFW accepts some it cannot read back, such as "%0"), "prepend" and
// deleting by number.
func parseVector(args []string) (vector, error) {
	refuse := func(why string) (vector, error) {
		return vector{}, fmt.Errorf("predict: ufw %s: %s", strings.Join(args, " "), why)
	}
	switch {
	case len(args) == 0:
		return refuse("no arguments")
	case slices.Equal(args, []string{"--force", "enable"}):
		return vector{kind: vecEnable}, nil
	case slices.Equal(args, []string{"disable"}):
		return vector{kind: vecDisable}, nil
	case slices.Equal(args, []string{"reload"}):
		return vector{kind: vecReload}, nil
	case args[0] == "default":
		chain := map[string]string{"incoming": "INPUT", "outgoing": "OUTPUT", "routed": "FORWARD"}
		if len(args) != 3 || !slices.Contains([]string{"allow", "deny", "reject"}, args[1]) || chain[args[2]] == "" {
			return refuse("want default <allow|deny|reject> <incoming|outgoing|routed>")
		}
		return vector{kind: vecDefault, policy: args[1], chain: chain[args[2]]}, nil
	case args[0] == "logging":
		if len(args) != 2 || !slices.Contains([]string{"off", "on", "low", "medium", "high", "full"}, args[1]) {
			return refuse("want logging <off|on|low|medium|high|full>")
		}
		return vector{kind: vecLogging, level: args[1]}, nil
	}
	v, err := parseRuleVector(args)
	if err != nil {
		return refuse(err.Error())
	}
	return v, nil
}

// parseRuleVector reads "[route] [delete | insert <n>] <action> <spec>".
func parseRuleVector(args []string) (vector, error) {
	v := vector{kind: vecRule, rule: model.Tuple{
		Proto: model.ProtoAny, DPort: model.Any, SPort: model.Any,
		Dst: "0.0.0.0/0", Src: "0.0.0.0/0", Direction: model.DirIn, Log: model.LogOff,
	}}
	a := args
	if a[0] == "route" {
		v.rule.Route, a = true, a[1:]
	}
	switch {
	case len(a) > 0 && a[0] == "delete":
		v.remove, a = true, a[1:]
	case len(a) > 0 && a[0] == "insert":
		if len(a) < 4 {
			return v, fmt.Errorf("insert needs a position and a rule")
		}
		n, err := strconv.Atoi(a[1])
		if err != nil || n < 1 {
			return v, fmt.Errorf("insert position %q is not a positive number", a[1])
		}
		v.position, a = n, a[2:]
	}
	if len(a) == 0 || !slices.Contains([]model.Action{model.ActionAllow, model.ActionDeny, model.ActionReject, model.ActionLimit}, model.Action(a[0])) {
		return v, fmt.Errorf("want allow, deny, reject or limit")
	}
	v.rule.Action, a = model.Action(a[0]), a[1:]

	hasIface := false
	setIface := func(dir, name string) error {
		if !vecIfaceRe.MatchString(name) {
			return fmt.Errorf("bad interface name %q", name)
		}
		if dir == "in" {
			if v.rule.InIface != "" {
				return fmt.Errorf("two in interfaces")
			}
			v.rule.InIface = name
		} else {
			if v.rule.OutIface != "" {
				return fmt.Errorf("two out interfaces")
			}
			v.rule.OutIface = name
		}
		hasIface = true
		return nil
	}
	if len(a) > 0 && (a[0] == "in" || a[0] == "out") {
		v.rule.Direction = model.Direction(a[0])
		switch {
		case len(a) > 2 && a[1] == "on":
			if err := setIface(a[0], a[2]); err != nil {
				return v, err
			}
			a = a[3:]
		case v.rule.Route:
			return v, fmt.Errorf("a route rule needs an interface with in or out")
		default:
			a = a[1:]
		}
		if v.rule.Route && len(a) > 2 && (a[0] == "in" || a[0] == "out") && a[1] == "on" {
			if err := setIface(a[0], a[2]); err != nil {
				return v, err
			}
			a = a[3:]
		}
	}
	if len(a) > 0 && (a[0] == "log" || a[0] == "log-all") {
		v.rule.Log, a = model.Log(a[0]), a[1:]
	}
	if len(a)%2 != 0 {
		return v, fmt.Errorf("wrong number of arguments")
	}
	fromType, toType := "any", "any"
	seen := map[string]bool{}
	loc := ""
	for i := 0; i < len(a); i += 2 {
		key, val := a[i], a[i+1]
		if key != "port" && seen[key] {
			return v, fmt.Errorf("%s given twice", key)
		}
		seen[key] = true
		switch key {
		case "proto":
			p := model.Proto(val)
			if !slices.Contains(model.Protos(), p) {
				return v, fmt.Errorf("unsupported protocol %q", val)
			}
			v.rule.Proto = p
		case "from", "to":
			addr, typ, err := vecAddr(val)
			if err != nil {
				return v, err
			}
			if key == "from" {
				v.rule.Src, fromType, loc = addr, typ, "src"
			} else {
				v.rule.Dst, toType, loc = addr, typ, "dst"
			}
		case "port":
			if loc == "" {
				return v, fmt.Errorf("port needs from or to before it")
			}
			if seen["port "+loc] {
				return v, fmt.Errorf("two ports for one address")
			}
			seen["port "+loc] = true
			if err := vecPort(val); err != nil {
				return v, err
			}
			if loc == "src" {
				v.rule.SPort = val
			} else {
				v.rule.DPort = val
			}
		case "comment":
			if strings.Contains(val, "'") || !utf8.ValidString(val) {
				return v, fmt.Errorf("a comment may not contain ' and must be UTF-8")
			}
			v.rule.Comment = val
		default:
			return v, fmt.Errorf("unexpected %q", key)
		}
	}
	if !seen["from"] && !seen["to"] && !hasIface {
		return v, fmt.Errorf("need a from, to or interface clause")
	}
	switch {
	case fromType == "any" && toType == "any":
		v.iptype = model.FamilyBoth
	case fromType != "any" && toType != "any" && fromType != toType:
		return v, fmt.Errorf("mixed IP versions for from and to")
	case fromType != "any":
		v.iptype = model.Family(fromType)
	default:
		v.iptype = model.Family(toType)
	}
	ipv4Only := v.rule.Proto == model.ProtoIPv6 || v.rule.Proto == model.ProtoIGMP
	if ipv4Only && v.iptype == model.FamilyBoth {
		v.iptype = model.FamilyV4
	}
	if ipv4Only && v.iptype == model.FamilyV6 {
		return v, fmt.Errorf("protocol %s has no IPv6 form", v.rule.Proto)
	}
	portless := !slices.Contains([]model.Proto{model.ProtoTCP, model.ProtoUDP, model.ProtoAny}, v.rule.Proto)
	if portless && (v.rule.DPort != model.Any || v.rule.SPort != model.Any) {
		return v, fmt.Errorf("protocol %s takes no port", v.rule.Proto)
	}
	if multiPort(v.rule) && v.rule.Proto != model.ProtoTCP && v.rule.Proto != model.ProtoUDP {
		return v, fmt.Errorf("multiple ports need tcp or udp")
	}
	return v, nil
}

// vecAddr checks an address argument: any, or an address or CIDR without a
// zone. It returns the address as UFW stores it before normalizing (lower
// case, any as 0.0.0.0/0) and its type: any, v4 or v6. A literal
// 0.0.0.0/0 is v4 and ::/0 is v6, as in UFW.
func vecAddr(s string) (string, string, error) {
	s = strings.ToLower(s)
	if s == model.Any {
		return "0.0.0.0/0", "any", nil
	}
	addr, _, hasMask := strings.Cut(s, "/")
	a, err := netip.ParseAddr(addr)
	if err == nil && hasMask {
		_, err = netip.ParsePrefix(s)
	}
	if err != nil || a.Zone() != "" {
		return "", "", fmt.Errorf("bad address %q", s)
	}
	if a.Is4() {
		return s, string(model.FamilyV4), nil
	}
	return s, string(model.FamilyV6), nil
}

// vecPort checks a port argument as UFW's parser and set_port do once
// service names are excluded.
func vecPort(s string) error {
	bad := fmt.Errorf("bad port %q", s)
	if !vecPortRe.MatchString(s) || strings.Count(s, ",")+strings.Count(s, ":") > 14 {
		return bad
	}
	for _, p := range strings.Split(s, ",") {
		switch {
		case vecRangeRe.MatchString(p):
			lo, hi, _ := strings.Cut(p, ":")
			a, _ := strconv.Atoi(lo)
			b, _ := strconv.Atoi(hi)
			if a < 1 || b > 65535 || a >= b {
				return bad
			}
		case vecNumberRe.MatchString(p):
			if n, _ := strconv.Atoi(p); n < 1 || n > 65535 {
				return bad
			}
		default:
			return bad
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// forFamily is the rule as UFW writes it into one family's file: set_v6
// turns any into the family's form, normalize gives the addresses their
// standard form and sorts the ports, and Raw is the tuple line.
func forFamily(t model.Tuple, fam model.Family) (model.Tuple, error) {
	v6 := fam == model.FamilyV6
	t.Family = fam
	for _, a := range []*string{&t.Src, &t.Dst} {
		switch {
		case v6 && (*a == model.Any || *a == "0.0.0.0/0"):
			*a = "::/0"
		case !v6 && (*a == model.Any || *a == "::/0"):
			*a = "0.0.0.0/0"
		}
	}
	var err error
	if t, err = normalizeTuple(t); err != nil {
		return t, err
	}
	t.Raw = tupleLine(t)
	return t, nil
}

// normalizeTuple is UFWRule.normalize for a rule of t.Family: addresses as
// util.normalize_address writes them, port lists in human_sort order.
func normalizeTuple(t model.Tuple) (model.Tuple, error) {
	v6 := t.Family == model.FamilyV6
	for _, a := range []*string{&t.Src, &t.Dst} {
		n, err := normalizeAddr(*a, v6)
		if err != nil {
			return t, err
		}
		*a = n
	}
	t.DPort, t.SPort = sortPorts(t.DPort), sortPorts(t.SPort)
	return t, nil
}

// normalizeAddr is util.normalize_address: a host prefix is dropped, the
// address takes its standard text form, and an IPv4 network is masked
// (IPv6 keeps its host bits). A dotted IPv4 netmask becomes a prefix
// length when it is contiguous.
func normalizeAddr(s string, v6 bool) (string, error) {
	addr, mask, hasMask := strings.Cut(s, "/")
	if hasMask && ((v6 && mask == "128") || (!v6 && (mask == "32" || mask == "255.255.255.255"))) {
		hasMask = false
	}
	a, err := netip.ParseAddr(addr)
	if err != nil || a.Is4() == v6 {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("predict: address %q is not valid in this family", s)
	}
	if !hasMask {
		return a.String(), nil
	}
	if !v6 && strings.Contains(mask, ".") {
		m, err := netip.ParseAddr(mask)
		if err != nil || !m.Is4() {
			return "", fmt.Errorf("predict: netmask %q is not valid", mask)
		}
		mb := m.As4()
		mv := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(mb[:])
		ones := bits.LeadingZeros32(^mv)
		if ones == 32 || mv == ^uint32(0)<<(32-ones) {
			mask = strconv.Itoa(ones)
		} else {
			ab := a.As4()
			binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(ab[:], binary.BigEndian.Uint32(ab[:])&mv)
			return netip.AddrFrom4(ab).String() + "/" + mask, nil
		}
	}
	p, err := netip.ParsePrefix(a.String() + "/" + mask)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("predict: address %q is not valid", s)
	}
	if v6 {
		return p.String(), nil
	}
	return p.Masked().String(), nil
}

// sortPorts sorts a port list as util.human_sort does: by the first port
// of each entry, a single port before a range starting at it, then by the
// range's end.
func sortPorts(s string) string {
	if s == model.Any || !strings.Contains(s, ",") {
		return s
	}
	ports := strings.Split(s, ",")
	slices.SortStableFunc(ports, func(x, y string) int {
		xa, xb, xr := strings.Cut(x, ":")
		ya, yb, yr := strings.Cut(y, ":")
		if c := atoiCmp(xa, ya); c != 0 {
			return c
		}
		switch {
		case xr != yr && !xr:
			return -1
		case xr != yr:
			return 1
		}
		return atoiCmp(xb, yb)
	})
	return strings.Join(ports, ",")
}

func atoiCmp(a, b string) int {
	x, _ := strconv.Atoi(a)
	y, _ := strconv.Atoi(b)
	return x - y
}
```

```go
package eval

import (
	"errors"
	"net/netip"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
)

// docker28Save reads one family's capture from testdata/docker28.
func docker28Save(t *testing.T, fam fwstate.Family) string {
	t.Helper()
	data, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join("testdata", "docker28", string(fam)+".save")) //nolint:gosec // G304: the path is built from constants of this test.
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return string(data)
}

// docker28Route routes the capture's default bridge, 172.18.0.0/16, out of
// docker0, and this host's 192.0.2.10 locally.
func docker28Route(p fwstate.Packet) (string, string, error) {
	switch {
	case netip.MustParsePrefix("172.18.0.0/16").Contains(p.Dst) && p.Path == "output":
		return "output", "docker0", nil
	case netip.MustParsePrefix("172.18.0.0/16").Contains(p.Dst):
		return "forward", "docker0", nil
	case p.Dst == netip.MustParseAddr("192.0.2.10"):
		return "input", "", nil
	}
	return "", "", errors.New("no route")
}

func TestDocker28(t *testing.T) {
	v4 := docker28Save(t, fwstate.V4)
	if !strings.Contains(v4, "--to-destination 172.18.0.2:80") {
		t.Fatal("the capture does not publish 172.18.0.2:80; rerun capture.sh")
	}
	userDrop := strings.Replace(v4, "-A FORWARD -j DOCKER-USER\n",
		"-A FORWARD -j DOCKER-USER\n-A DOCKER-USER -s 203.0.113.0/24 -j DROP\n", 1)
	published := func(p *fwstate.Packet) { p.Dst, p.DstPort = netip.MustParseAddr("192.0.2.10"), 8080 }
	tests := []struct {
		name    string
		save    string
		edit    func(p *fwstate.Packet)
		verdict fwstate.Verdict
		trace   []string
		reason  string
	}{
		{
			name:    "a published port is reachable from outside through DNAT and DOCKER-USER",
			save:    v4,
			edit:    published,
			verdict: fwstate.Accept,
			trace: []string{"nat/PREROUTING#1", "nat/DOCKER#2", "filter/FORWARD#1", "filter/FORWARD#2",
				"filter/DOCKER-FORWARD#1", "filter/DOCKER-FORWARD#2", "filter/DOCKER-FORWARD#3",
				"filter/DOCKER-BRIDGE#1", "filter/DOCKER#1"},
		},
		{
			name:    "a DOCKER-USER rule decides before Docker's own chains",
			save:    userDrop,
			edit:    published,
			verdict: fwstate.Drop,
			trace:   []string{"nat/PREROUTING#1", "nat/DOCKER#2", "filter/FORWARD#1", "filter/DOCKER-USER#1"},
			reason:  "filter/DOCKER-USER#1 drops",

		{
			name: "direct access to the container from outside is dropped in raw",
			save: v4,

			},

			trace:   []string{"raw/PREROUTING#1"},
		},
		{

			save: v4,
			edit: func(p *fwstate.Packet) {
				p.Path, p.InIface, p.OutIface = "forward", "docker0", "eth0"
				p.Src, p.Dst, p.DstPort = netip.MustParseAddr("172.18.0.2"), netip.MustParseAddr("198.51.100.2"), 443
			},

				"filter/DOCKER-FORWARD#2", "filter/DOCKER-ISOLATION-STAGE-1#1", "filter/DOCKER-FORWARD#3",
				"filter/DOCKER-FORWARD#4", "nat/POSTROUTING#1"},
		},
		{
			name: "a local connection to the published port is DNATed in nat OUTPUT",
			save: v4,
			edit: func(p *fwstate.Packet) {

				p.Src, p.Dst, p.DstPort = netip.MustParseAddr("192.0.2.10"), netip.MustParseAddr("192.0.2.10"), 8080
			},
			verdict: fwstate.Accept,
			trace:   []string{"nat/OUTPUT#1", "nat/DOCKER#2"},
		},
		{
			name: "an IPv6 connection to the published port reaches the host, where docker-proxy serves it",
			save: docker28Save(t, fwstate.V6),
			edit: func(p *fwstate.Packet) {
				p.Family, p.DstPort = fwstate.V6, 8080
				p.Src, p.Dst = netip.MustParseAddr("2001:db8:1::7"), netip.MustParseAddr("2001:db8::10")
			},
			verdict: fwstate.Accept,
			trace:   []string{"nat/PREROUTING#1"},
		},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			p := evalPacket()
			tt.edit(&p)
			evalCheck(t, Evaluate(evalRuleset(t, tt.save), p, docker28Route), tt.verdict, tt.trace, tt.reason)
		})
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the implementation**

Create `internal/modules/firewall/eval/testdata/docker28/capture.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Captures Docker 28's netfilter rules for the evaluator's golden test: a
# docker:28.5.2-dind daemon in a privileged container, its default bridge
# pinned to 172.18.0.1/16, and one container publishing host port 8080 on
# its port 80. Everything runs in the container's own network namespace,
# which is removed on exit; the host's firewall is never touched.
#
# Usage: capture.sh <outdir>
#   for example: capture.sh internal/modules/firewall/eval/testdata/docker28
# Writes <outdir>/v4.save and <outdir>/v6.save (the five tables of each
# family, without the "# Generated by" and "# Completed on" lines and with
# chain counters written [0:0]) and <outdir>/version.txt.
set -euo pipefail

if [ $# -ne 1 ]; then
	echo "usage: $0 <outdir>" >&2
	exit 2
fi
out=$1
name=dp-w1-E-docker28
image=docker:28.5.2-dind

docker rm -f "$name" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
trap 'docker rm -f "$name" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT
docker run -d --privileged --name "$name" "$image" --bip=172.18.0.1/16 >/dev/null
for _ in $(seq 1 120); do
	docker exec "$name" docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 && break
	sleep 1
done
docker exec "$name" docker info >/dev/null
docker exec "$name" docker run -d --name web -p 8080:80 busybox:1.37 httpd -f -p 80 >/dev/null

mkdir -p "$out"
for fam in v4 v6; do
	bin=iptables
	[ "$fam" = v6 ] && bin=ip6tables
	for t in filter nat raw mangle security; do
		docker exec "$name" "$bin-nft-save" -t "$t"
	done | sed -e '/^# Generated by /d' -e '/^# Completed on /d' -e 's/^\(:.*\) \[[0-9]*:[0-9]*\]$/\1 [0:0]/' > "$out/$fam.save"
done
docker exec "$name" sh -c 'printf "docker %s\n" "$(docker version --format "{{.Server.Version}}")"; iptables --version' > "$out/version.txt"
```

Make it executable and run it (it starts and removes the container `dp-w1-E-docker28`):

```bash
(cd internal/modules/firewall/eval/testdata/docker28 && sha256sum v4.save v6.save version.txt)
```

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/modules/firewall/loaded/nft.go`
- Test: `internal/modules/firewall/loaded/nft_test.go`
- Create: `internal/modules/firewall/loaded/testdata/nft/tables.txt`
- Create: `internal/modules/firewall/loaded/testdata/nft/inet-dpforeign.txt`
- Create: `internal/modules/firewall/loaded/testdata/nft/netdev-dpnetdev.txt`
- Create: `internal/modules/firewall/loaded/testdata/nft/ip-dpnat.txt`
- Create: `internal/modules/firewall/loaded/testdata/nft/ip6-dpsetonly.txt`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `truncate` (Task 40, `read.go`).
- Produces: Part contracts Task 48: `nftTable`, `nftChain`, `parseNFTTables`, `parseNFTTable`, `maxNFTLine`; unexported helpers `nftStatement`, `nftWordAfter`, `nftBraces`; shared test helpers `nftTestDir`, `nftTestRead`.

**Depends on:** Task 40

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-opus-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 2 - risk 3 = 6
**Lenses:** security

A small parser of `nft list tables` and `nft list table <family> <name>` output, reading only what deciding a foreign hook needs (spec 2.1): each chain's name, whether it is a base chain with its hook and policy, and how many statements it holds. Sets, maps, flowtables and other objects are skipped; braces inside quoted strings do not count; a statement nft prints over several lines counts once; output it cannot follow is an error and no input panics (`FuzzParseNFTTable`). The five testdata files are real output captured in privileged containers on all four images (nft 1.0.2, 1.0.6, 1.0.9 and 1.1.3 print them byte for byte alike); copy them exactly, including the tab indentation and the blank lines.

Create `internal/modules/firewall/loaded/nft_test.go`:

```go
package loaded

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// The captures were made with nft 1.0.2, 1.0.6, 1.0.9 and 1.1.3, which
// print them byte for byte alike.
const nftTestDir = "testdata/nft"

func nftTestRead(t testing.TB, name string) []byte {
	t.Helper()
	data, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(nftTestDir, name)) //nolint:gosec // G304: a fixed name under testdata
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return data
}

func TestParseNFTTables(t *testing.T) {
	tables, bad := parseNFTTables(nftTestRead(t, "tables.txt"))
	want := []nftTable{{"inet", "dpforeign"}, {"netdev", "dpnetdev"}, {"ip", "dpnat"}, {"ip6", "dpsetonly"}, {"ip", "filter"}}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(tables, want) || bad != nil {
		t.Errorf("tables %v, bad %q", tables, bad)
	}
	tables, bad = parseNFTTables([]byte("table ip a\n\ntable ip b c\ntable\nchain ip x\n  table inet -dash  \n"))
	if want := []nftTable{{"ip", "a"}, {"inet", "-dash"}}; !reflect.DeepEqual(tables, want) {
		t.Errorf("tables %v, want %v", tables, want)
	}
	if want := []string{"table ip b c", "table", "chain ip x"}; !reflect.DeepEqual(bad, want) {
		t.Errorf("bad %q, want %q", bad, want)
	}
}

func TestParseNFTTableCaptures(t *testing.T) {
	cases := map[string][]nftChain{
		"inet-dpforeign.txt": {
			{Name: "empty", Base: true, Hook: "input", Policy: "accept"},
			{Name: "dropper", Base: true, Hook: "forward", Policy: "drop"},
			{Name: "ruled", Base: true, Hook: "input", Policy: "accept", Rules: 2},
			{Name: "regular", Rules: 2},
			{Name: "commented", Base: true, Hook: "output", Policy: "accept"},
		},
		"netdev-dpnetdev.txt": {{Name: "ingress", Base: true, Hook: "ingress", Policy: "accept"}},
		"ip-dpnat.txt":        {{Name: "post", Base: true, Hook: "postrouting", Policy: "accept", Rules: 1}},
		"ip6-dpsetonly.txt":   {{Name: "regular", Rules: 1}},
	}
	for name, want := range cases {
		got, err := parseNFTTable(nftTestRead(t, name))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("%s: %v", name, err)
		}
		if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
			t.Errorf("%s:\n got %+v\nwant %+v", name, got, want)
		}
	}
}

func TestParseNFTTableShapes(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name string
		in   string
		want []nftChain
	}{
		{"empty table", "table ip t {\n}\n", nil},
		{"multi-line statement", "table inet t {\n\tchain c {\n\t\ttype filter hook input priority 0; policy accept;\n" +
			"\t\ttcp dport vmap {\n\t\t\t22 : accept,\n\t\t\t80 : drop\n\t\t}\n\t\tdrop\n\t}\n}\n",
			[]nftChain{{Name: "c", Base: true, Hook: "input", Policy: "accept", Rules: 2}}},
		{"braces in strings", "table ip t {\n\tchain \"odd name\" {\n\t\tcomment \"{ not a block\"\n" +
			"\t\ttype filter hook output priority 0; policy drop;\n\t\tmeta mark 1 counter comment \"}}\" accept\n\t}\n}\n",
			[]nftChain{{Name: "odd name", Base: true, Hook: "output", Policy: "drop", Rules: 1}}},
		{"policy on its own line", "table ip t {\n\tchain c {\n\t\ttype filter hook input priority 0;\n\t\tpolicy drop;\n\t}\n}\n",
			[]nftChain{{Name: "c", Base: true, Hook: "input", Policy: "drop"}}},
		{"no policy printed", "table ip t {\n\tchain c {\n\t\ttype filter hook input priority 0;\n\t}\n}\n",
			[]nftChain{{Name: "c", Base: true, Hook: "input"}}},
		{"netdev devices", "table netdev t {\n\tchain c {\n\t\ttype filter hook ingress priority 0; policy accept;\n" +
			"\t\tdevices = { eth0, eth1 }\n\t}\n}\n",
			[]nftChain{{Name: "c", Base: true, Hook: "ingress", Policy: "accept"}}},
		{"objects skipped", "table ip t {\n\tflags dormant\n\tcounter cnt {\n\t\tpackets 0 bytes 0\n\t}\n" +
			"\tmap m {\n\t\ttype ipv4_addr : verdict\n\t\telements = { 192.0.2.1 : drop,\n\t\t\t     192.0.2.2 : accept }\n\t}\n}\n",
			nil},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		got, err := parseNFTTable([]byte(c.in))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("%s: %v", c.name, err)
		}
		if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, c.want) {
			t.Errorf("%s:\n got %+v\nwant %+v", c.name, got, c.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestParseNFTTableErrors(t *testing.T) {
	cases := map[string]string{
		"":                                   "the table block is missing or not closed",
		"table ip t {\n\tchain c {\n\t}\n":   "the table block is missing or not closed",
		"table ip t {\n}\n}\n":               "want one table block",
		"table ip t {\n}}\n":                 "unbalanced braces",
		"table ip t {\n}\ntable ip u {\n}\n": "want one table block",
		"chain c {\n}\n":                     "want one table block",
		"table ip t {\n\tcomment \"x\n}\n":   "unterminated string",
		"table ip t { }\n":                   "want one table block",
		"table ip t {\n" + strings.Repeat("x", maxNFTLine+1) + "\n}\n": "token too long",
	}
	for in, want := range cases {
		_, err := parseNFTTable([]byte(in))
		if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
			t.Errorf("%.40q: err = %v, want %q", in, err, want)
		}
	}
}

func FuzzParseNFTTable(f *testing.F) {
	for _, name := range []string{"inet-dpforeign.txt", "netdev-dpnetdev.txt", "ip-dpnat.txt", "ip6-dpsetonly.txt", "tables.txt"} {
		f.Add(nftTestRead(f, name))
	}
	f.Add([]byte("table ip t {\n\tchain c {\n\t\ttcp dport vmap {\n\t\t\t22 : accept\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n"))
	f.Fuzz(func(t *testing.T, data []byte) {
		chains, err := parseNFTTable(data)
		if err != nil && chains != nil {
			t.Fatal("chains returned with an error")
		}
		for _, c := range chains {
			if c.Rules < 0 || !c.Base && (c.Hook != "" || c.Policy != "") {
				t.Fatalf("inconsistent chain %+v", c)
			}
		}
		parseNFTTables(data)
	})
}
```

```go
package loaded

import (
	"bufio"
	"bytes"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"strings"
)

// maxNFTLine bounds one line of nft output; nft prints far shorter ones.
const maxNFTLine = 1 << 20

// nftTable is one "table <family> <name>" line of `nft list tables`.
type nftTable struct{ Family, Name string }

// nftChain is one chain of `nft list table <family> <name>`.
type nftChain struct {
	Name   string
	Base   bool   // declared with "type ... hook ..."
	Hook   string // the hook of a base chain: "input", "forward", "ingress", ...
	Policy string // a base chain's policy as printed ("accept", "drop"); "" when none is printed
	Rules  int    // statements in the chain; a statement nft prints over several lines counts once
}

// parseNFTTables reads `nft list tables`. A line that is not exactly
// "table <family> <name>" is returned in bad, so the caller can report what
// it could not read instead of skipping a table.
func parseNFTTables(out []byte) (tables []nftTable, bad []string) {
	for line := range strings.Lines(string(out)) {
		line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
		if line == "" {
			continue
		}
		f := strings.Fields(line)
		if len(f) != 3 || f[0] != "table" {
			bad = append(bad, line)
			continue
		}
		tables = append(tables, nftTable{Family: f[1], Name: f[2]})
	}
	return tables, bad
}

// parseNFTTable reads the chains of one table from `nft list table`
// output. It reads only what deciding a foreign hook needs: each chain's
// name, whether it is a base chain with its hook and policy, and how many
// statements it holds. Sets, maps, flowtables and other objects are
// skipped. Output it cannot follow (unbalanced braces, an unterminated
// string, text outside the table block) is an error; no input panics.
func parseNFTTable(out []byte) ([]nftChain, error) {
	var (
		chains []nftChain
		cur    *nftChain // the chain whose block is open
		depth  int       // braces open before the current line
		seen   bool      // the table block has been opened
		lineNo int
	)
	sc := bufio.NewScanner(bytes.NewReader(out))
	sc.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, 64<<10), maxNFTLine)
	for sc.Scan() {
		lineNo++
		line := strings.TrimSpace(sc.Text())
		if line == "" {
			continue
		}
		opens, closes, err := nftBraces(line)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("loaded: nft line %d: %w", lineNo, err)
		}
		switch {
		case depth == 0:
			if seen || !strings.HasPrefix(line, "table ") || opens != 1 || closes != 0 {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("loaded: nft line %d: want one table block, got %q", lineNo, truncate(line))
			}
			seen = true
		case depth == 1 && strings.HasPrefix(line, "chain ") && opens == 1 && closes == 0:
			name := strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimPrefix(line, "chain "), "{"))
			chains = append(chains, nftChain{Name: strings.Trim(name, `"`)})
			cur = &chains[len(chains)-1]
		case depth == 2 && cur != nil && line != "}":
			nftStatement(cur, line)
		}
		depth += opens - closes
		if depth < 0 {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("loaded: nft line %d: unbalanced braces", lineNo)
		}
		if depth <= 1 {
			cur = nil
		}
	}
	if err := sc.Err(); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("loaded: nft output: %w", err)
	}
	if !seen || depth != 0 {
		return nil, errors.New("loaded: nft output: the table block is missing or not closed")
	}
	return chains, nil
}

// nftStatement reads one line at the top level of a chain block.
func nftStatement(c *nftChain, line string) {
	switch {
	case strings.HasPrefix(line, "type ") && strings.Contains(line, " hook "):
		c.Base = true
		c.Hook = nftWordAfter(line, "hook")
		if p := nftWordAfter(line, "policy"); p != "" {
			c.Policy = p
		}
	case strings.HasPrefix(line, "policy ") && c.Base:
		c.Policy = nftWordAfter(line, "policy")
	case strings.HasPrefix(line, "comment "), strings.HasPrefix(line, "devices "):
		// A chain's comment and a netdev chain's device list declare the
		// chain; they are not statements.
	default:
		c.Rules++
	}
}

// nftWordAfter returns the word after the first word key of line, without
// a trailing semicolon; "" when key is not followed by a word.
func nftWordAfter(line, key string) string {
	f := strings.Fields(line)
	for i := 0; i+1 < len(f); i++ {
		if f[i] == key {
			return strings.TrimSuffix(f[i+1], ";")
		}
	}
	return ""
}

// nftBraces counts the braces of line outside double-quoted strings.
func nftBraces(line string) (opens, closes int, err error) {
	quoted := false
	for i := 0; i < len(line); i++ {
		switch c := line[i]; {
		case c == '\\' && quoted:
			i++
		case c == '"':
			quoted = !quoted
		case c == '{' && !quoted:
			opens++
		case c == '}' && !quoted:
			closes++
		}
	}
	if quoted {
		return 0, 0, errors.New("unterminated string")
	}
	return opens, closes, nil
}
```

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/modules/firewall/loaded/sysctl_predict.go`
- Test: `internal/modules/firewall/loaded/sysctl_predict_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `fwstate.Config`, `fwstate.SysctlSetting`, `fwstate.Transition` and its constants (merged); `conf.SupportedSysctl` and, in the test, `conf.Read` (merged); `errcode.New`, `errcode.FirewallUnsupportedConfiguration`; the golden `rules` and `sysctl` scenarios. Task 40 only for the package comment.
- Produces: Part contracts Task 49: `PredictSysctl`; unexported `sysctlPattern`, `sysctlDefaultCopy`, `sysctlBoolean`, `sysctlTristate`, `keyV6AllFwd`, `prefixV4Conf`, `prefixV6Conf`, `ifaceDefault`, `ifaceAll`, `suffixFwd`.

**Depends on:** Task 40

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-opus-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 2 - risk 3 = 6
**Lenses:** security

`PredictSysctl(cfg, cur, tr)` (spec 2.1): the supported sysctl values after a transition. UFW applies its sysctl file only in `ufw_start`, which `ufw enable` from an inactive firewall and `ufw reload` while enabled reach, so only `TransEnable` and `TransReload` with `cfg.Enabled` apply `cfg.Sysctl`, in file order, skipping keys `cur` does not hold. Kernel side effects, measured in a container on 2026-10-24: writing `net/ipv6/conf/all/forwarding` sets `default` and every interface, even without a change; writing `net/ipv4/ip_forward` changes no other supported key (only `conf/*/forwarding` and `all/accept_redirects`, neither supported); IPv6 `default` writes, `net/ipv6/conf/all/accept_ra` and IPv4 `all` writes do not spread. An IPv4 `default` write may be copied by the kernel to interfaces never set explicitly, which live values cannot tell, so a write that could change an interface whose value equals the old default is refused; so is a value outside the firewall's sysctl patterns (`^[01]$`, `^[012]$` for `accept_ra` and `rp_filter`). Both refusals are `firewall.unsupported_configuration`. The golden test predicts the `sysctl` scenario's values from the `rules` scenario's on all four images. Test helpers carry the prefix `sp`.

```go
package loaded

import (
	"errors"
	"maps"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/conf"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
)

const spGoldenDir = "../testdata/golden"

var spImages = []string{"ubuntu-22.04", "ubuntu-24.04", "debian-12", "debian-13"}

// spValues reads a golden sysctl.txt of key=value lines.
func spValues(t *testing.T, path string) map[string]string {
	t.Helper()
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path) //nolint:gosec // G304: a fixed name under the golden directory
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	out := map[string]string{}
	for line := range strings.Lines(string(data)) {
		k, v, ok := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(line), "=")
		if !ok {
			t.Fatalf("%s: line %q", path, line)
		}
		out[k] = v
	}
	return out
}

func TestPredictSysctlGolden(t *testing.T) {
	for _, img := range spImages {
		cfg, err := conf.Read(filepath.Join(spGoldenDir, img, "sysctl", "files"))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		before := spValues(t, filepath.Join(spGoldenDir, img, "rules", "sysctl.txt"))
		after := spValues(t, filepath.Join(spGoldenDir, img, "sysctl", "sysctl.txt"))
		if maps.Equal(before, after) {
			t.Fatalf("%s: the scenario changes nothing", img)
		}
		for _, tr := range []fwstate.Transition{fwstate.TransEnable, fwstate.TransReload} {
			got, err := PredictSysctl(cfg, before, tr)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("%s %s: %v", img, tr, err)
			}
			if !maps.Equal(got, after) {
				t.Errorf("%s %s:\n got %v\nwant %v", img, tr, got, after)
			}
		}
		for _, tr := range []fwstate.Transition{fwstate.TransNone, fwstate.TransDisable} {
			got, err := PredictSysctl(cfg, before, tr)
			if err != nil || !maps.Equal(got, before) {
				t.Errorf("%s %s: %v, %v; want the values unchanged", img, tr, got, err)
			}
		}
		cfg.Enabled = false
		if got, err := PredictSysctl(cfg, before, fwstate.TransReload); err != nil || !maps.Equal(got, before) {
			t.Errorf("%s: reload while disabled changed %v, %v", img, got, err)
		}
	}
}

// spCur is a host with one interface, eth0, and the loopback interface.
func spCur() map[string]string {
	cur := map[string]string{"net/ipv4/ip_forward": "0"}
	for _, d := range []string{"all", "default", "eth0", "lo"} {
		cur["net/ipv6/conf/"+d+"/forwarding"] = "0"
		cur["net/ipv6/conf/"+d+"/accept_ra"] = "1"
		cur["net/ipv4/conf/"+d+"/rp_filter"] = "2"
		cur["net/ipv4/conf/"+d+"/accept_source_route"] = "0"
	}
	return cur
}

func spConfig(lines ...string) fwstate.Config {
	cfg := fwstate.Config{Enabled: true, SysctlFile: "/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf"}
	for _, l := range lines {
		k, v, _ := strings.Cut(l, "=")
		cfg.Sysctl = append(cfg.Sysctl, fwstate.SysctlSetting{Key: k, Value: v})
	}
	return cfg
}

func TestPredictSysctlEffects(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name   string
		lines  []string
		before map[string]string // changes to spCur before the transition
		want   map[string]string // changes to spCur expected after it
	}{
		{"ipv4 forwarding resets no supported key", []string{"net/ipv4/ip_forward=1"},
			map[string]string{"net/ipv4/conf/eth0/rp_filter": "1", "net/ipv4/conf/eth0/accept_source_route": "1"},
			map[string]string{"net/ipv4/ip_forward": "1", "net/ipv4/conf/eth0/rp_filter": "1", "net/ipv4/conf/eth0/accept_source_route": "1"}},
		{"ipv6 all forwarding sets every interface", []string{"net/ipv6/conf/all/forwarding=1"}, nil,
			map[string]string{"net/ipv6/conf/all/forwarding": "1", "net/ipv6/conf/default/forwarding": "1",
				"net/ipv6/conf/eth0/forwarding": "1", "net/ipv6/conf/lo/forwarding": "1"}},
		{"ipv6 all forwarding resets an interface without a change", []string{"net/ipv6/conf/all/forwarding=0"},
			map[string]string{"net/ipv6/conf/eth0/forwarding": "1"}, map[string]string{"net/ipv6/conf/eth0/forwarding": "0"}},
		{"file order", []string{"net/ipv6/conf/all/forwarding=1", "net/ipv6/conf/eth0/forwarding=0"}, nil,
			map[string]string{"net/ipv6/conf/all/forwarding": "1", "net/ipv6/conf/default/forwarding": "1",
				"net/ipv6/conf/eth0/forwarding": "0", "net/ipv6/conf/lo/forwarding": "1"}},
		{"ipv6 defaults do not spread", []string{"net/ipv6/conf/default/forwarding=1", "net/ipv6/conf/default/accept_ra=0", "net/ipv6/conf/all/accept_ra=2"}, nil,
			map[string]string{"net/ipv6/conf/default/forwarding": "1", "net/ipv6/conf/default/accept_ra": "0", "net/ipv6/conf/all/accept_ra": "2"}},
		{"missing keys and other keys are skipped", []string{"net/ipv6/conf/eth9/forwarding=1", "net/ipv4/conf/all/accept_redirects=0", "net/ipv4/icmp_echo_ignore_all=1"}, nil, nil},
		{"ipv4 all values do not spread", []string{"net/ipv4/conf/all/rp_filter=1", "net/ipv4/conf/all/accept_source_route=1"}, nil,
			map[string]string{"net/ipv4/conf/all/rp_filter": "1", "net/ipv4/conf/all/accept_source_route": "1"}},
		{"ipv4 default leaves explicit interfaces", []string{"net/ipv4/conf/default/rp_filter=1"},
			map[string]string{"net/ipv4/conf/eth0/rp_filter": "0", "net/ipv4/conf/lo/rp_filter": "1"},
			map[string]string{"net/ipv4/conf/default/rp_filter": "1", "net/ipv4/conf/eth0/rp_filter": "0", "net/ipv4/conf/lo/rp_filter": "1"}},
		{"ipv4 default after the interfaces", []string{"net/ipv4/conf/eth0/accept_source_route=0", "net/ipv4/conf/lo/accept_source_route=0", "net/ipv4/conf/default/accept_source_route=1"}, nil,
			map[string]string{"net/ipv4/conf/default/accept_source_route": "1"}},
		{"ipv4 default unchanged", []string{"net/ipv4/conf/default/rp_filter=2"}, nil, nil},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		cur := spCur()
		maps.Copy(cur, c.before)
		want, kept := maps.Clone(cur), maps.Clone(cur)
		maps.Copy(want, c.want)
		got, err := PredictSysctl(spConfig(c.lines...), cur, fwstate.TransEnable)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("%s: %v", c.name, err)
		}
		if !maps.Equal(got, want) {
			t.Errorf("%s:\n got %v\nwant %v", c.name, got, want)
		}
		if !maps.Equal(cur, kept) {
			t.Errorf("%s: the current values were changed", c.name)
		}
	}
}

func TestPredictSysctlRefusals(t *testing.T) {
	cases := map[string]string{
		"net/ipv4/ip_forward=2":            `/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf sets net/ipv4/ip_forward to "2"; Darkpanel supports only values matching ^[01]$`,
		"net/ipv6/conf/eth0/accept_ra=3":   `/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf sets net/ipv6/conf/eth0/accept_ra to "3"; Darkpanel supports only values matching ^[012]$`,
		"net/ipv6/conf/eth9/forwarding=on": `/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf sets net/ipv6/conf/eth9/forwarding to "on"; Darkpanel supports only values matching ^[01]$`,
		"net/ipv4/conf/default/rp_filter=1": "/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf sets net/ipv4/conf/default/rp_filter to 1, which the kernel may also copy to " +
			"net/ipv4/conf/eth0/rp_filter; Darkpanel cannot predict that, so set the interface's own value earlier in the file",
	}
	for line, want := range cases {
		_, err := PredictSysctl(spConfig(line), spCur(), fwstate.TransReload)
		var ce *errcode.Error
		if !errors.As(err, &ce) || ce.Code != errcode.FirewallUnsupportedConfiguration || ce.Detail != want {
			t.Errorf("%s: err = %v, want %q", line, err, want)
		}
	}
}

func TestPredictSysctlNilValues(t *testing.T) {
	got, err := PredictSysctl(spConfig("net/ipv4/ip_forward=1"), nil, fwstate.TransEnable)
	if err != nil || got == nil || len(got) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("got %v, %v; want an empty map", got, err)
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the implementation**

Create `internal/modules/firewall/loaded/sysctl_predict.go`:

```go
package loaded

import (
	"fmt"
	"maps"
	"regexp"
	"slices"
	"strings"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/conf"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
)

const (
	keyV6AllFwd  = "net/ipv6/conf/all/forwarding"
	prefixV4Conf = "net/ipv4/conf/"
	prefixV6Conf = "net/ipv6/conf/"
	ifaceDefault = "default"
	ifaceAll     = "all"
	suffixFwd    = "/forwarding"
)

// The value patterns of the firewall's sysctl owned paths (spec 2.1).
var (
	sysctlBoolean  = regexp.MustCompile("^[01]$")
	sysctlTristate = regexp.MustCompile("^[012]$")
)

// PredictSysctl returns the supported sysctl values (in /proc/sys form, as
// in Loaded.Sysctl) after tr, starting from cur. UFW applies its sysctl
// file only when it starts: on TransEnable, and on TransReload while
// cfg.Enabled (ufw reload stops and starts UFW, and skips both when UFW is
// not enabled). Any other transition returns a copy of cur.
//
// The file's supported settings apply in file order; a key that cur does
// not hold (an absent interface, IPv6 disabled, the loopback interface) is
// skipped, as sysctl -e skips a missing key. The kernel's side effects on
// supported keys are modelled: writing net/ipv6/conf/all/forwarding sets
// default and every interface's forwarding, even when the value does not
// change. Writing net/ipv4/ip_forward changes no other supported key (the
// kernel sets every forwarding value under net/ipv4/conf and resets
// all/accept_redirects, none of them supported). Writing an IPv4 default
// value can be copied by the kernel to every interface never set
// explicitly, which the live values cannot tell, so a write that could
// change such an interface is an error, as is a value the firewall's
// sysctl declarations would not let a revert write back. Both errors are
// firewall.unsupported_configuration.
func PredictSysctl(cfg fwstate.Config, cur map[string]string, tr fwstate.Transition) (map[string]string, error) {
	out := maps.Clone(cur)
	if out == nil {
		out = map[string]string{}
	}
	if tr != fwstate.TransEnable && (tr != fwstate.TransReload || !cfg.Enabled) {
		return out, nil
	}
	written := map[string]bool{}
	for _, s := range cfg.Sysctl {
		if !conf.SupportedSysctl(s.Key) {
			continue
		}
		pattern := sysctlPattern(s.Key)
		if !pattern.MatchString(s.Value) {
			return nil, errcode.New(errcode.FirewallUnsupportedConfiguration,
				fmt.Sprintf("%s sets %s to %q; Darkpanel supports only values matching %s", cfg.SysctlFile, s.Key, s.Value, pattern))
		}
		old, ok := out[s.Key]
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		if err := sysctlDefaultCopy(cfg, out, written, s, old); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		out[s.Key] = s.Value
		written[s.Key] = true
		if s.Key == keyV6AllFwd {
			for k := range out {
				if strings.HasPrefix(k, prefixV6Conf) && strings.HasSuffix(k, suffixFwd) {
					out[k] = s.Value
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return out, nil
}

// sysctlPattern is the value pattern of a supported key.
func sysctlPattern(key string) *regexp.Regexp {
	if strings.HasSuffix(key, "/accept_ra") || strings.HasSuffix(key, "/rp_filter") {
		return sysctlTristate
	}
	return sysctlBoolean
}

// sysctlDefaultCopy refuses a write of an IPv4 default value that the kernel
// might copy to an interface: one not written earlier in the file whose
// value equals the old default. An interface whose value differs from the
// default has been set explicitly, so the kernel leaves it alone.
func sysctlDefaultCopy(cfg fwstate.Config, cur map[string]string, written map[string]bool, s fwstate.SysctlSetting, old string) error {
	param, ok := strings.CutPrefix(s.Key, prefixV4Conf+ifaceDefault+"/")
	if !ok || s.Value == old {
		return nil
	}
	for _, k := range slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(cur)) {
		iface, rest, _ := strings.Cut(strings.TrimPrefix(k, prefixV4Conf), "/")
		if !strings.HasPrefix(k, prefixV4Conf) || rest != param || iface == ifaceAll || iface == ifaceDefault || written[k] || cur[k] != old {
			continue
		}
		return errcode.New(errcode.FirewallUnsupportedConfiguration, fmt.Sprintf(
			"%s sets %s to %s, which the kernel may also copy to %s; Darkpanel cannot predict that, so set the interface's own value earlier in the file",
			cfg.SysctlFile, s.Key, s.Value, k))
	}
	return nil
}
```

**Lenses:** security

`Compare(a, b, keep)` (spec 2.3, in sync and verify): the chains whose rules or policy differ between two loaded states, per family, table and chain that `keep` selects (nil selects all), in a fixed order (family v4 then v6, table in `netfilter.Tables` order, chain name). Rules are compared by `netfilter.Key` in the chain's family, so formatting differences never count; `OnlyA`/`OnlyB` hold the keys one side lacks, counting duplicates; `OrderDiffers` reports that the rules both sides hold appear in a different order. A built-in chain missing on one side compares as an empty chain with policy `ACCEPT`, which is what an absent table does (iptables-nft-save prints a table the kernel does not have as exactly that); a user chain declared on one side only always differs, even when empty. Test helpers carry the prefix `cmp`.

```go
func TestCompareDuplicates(t *testing.T) {

	d := Compare(cmpV4(t, dup), cmpV4(t, moved), nil)
	if len(d) != 1 || !d[0].OrderDiffers || d[0].OnlyA != nil || d[0].OnlyB != nil {
		t.Errorf("a moved duplicate: %+v", d)
	}
	once := strings.Replace(dup, "-A INPUT -s 192.0.2.1/32 -j DROP\nCOMMIT", "COMMIT", 1)
	d = Compare(cmpV4(t, dup), cmpV4(t, once), nil)
	if len(d) != 1 || len(d[0].OnlyA) != 1 || d[0].OrderDiffers {
		t.Errorf("a removed duplicate: %+v", d)
	}
}
```
