```go
// refusalTestState returns a golden scenario's loaded state with extra
// IPv6 filter chains (written as iptables -S prints them) and extra rules
// appended to built-in chains.
func refusalTestState(t *testing.T, scenario string, chains map[string][]string, rules map[string]string) fwstate.Loaded {
	t.Helper()
	st := predictLoaded(t, "debian-13", scenario)
	f := st.V6.Table("filter")
	for name, rs := range chains {
		f.Chains = append(f.Chains, *predictTestChain(t, "filter", name, "-", rs...))
	}
	for chain, rule := range rules {
		c := f.Chain(chain)
		c.Rules = append(c.Rules, predictTestChain(t, "filter", chain, "ACCEPT", rule).Rules...)
	}
	return st
}

func TestIPv6Refusal(t *testing.T) {
	noV6 := predictConfig(t, "debian-13", "ipv6no")
	withV6 := predictConfig(t, "debian-13", "rules")
	disabled := noV6
	disabled.Enabled = false
	docker := refusalTestState(t, "rules", map[string][]string{"DOCKER-USER": {"-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN"}}, nil)
	tailscale := refusalTestState(t, "ipv6no", nil, map[string]string{"INPUT": "-A INPUT -i tailscale0 -j ACCEPT"})
	matchedJump := refusalTestState(t, "rules", nil, map[string]string{"FORWARD": "-A FORWARD -i eth0 -j ufw6-before-forward"})
	noIP6 := predictLoaded(t, "debian-13", "rules")
	noIP6.V6 = nil
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name string
		cfg  fwstate.Config
		cur  fwstate.Loaded
		tr   fwstate.Transition
		want []string // substrings of the detail; nil for no refusal
	}{
		{"IPv6 on", withV6, docker, fwstate.TransEnable, nil},
		{"no ip6tables", noV6, noIP6, fwstate.TransEnable, nil},
		{"disable", noV6, docker, fwstate.TransDisable, nil},
		{"none", noV6, docker, fwstate.TransNone, nil},
		{"reload while disabled", disabled, docker, fwstate.TransReload, nil},
		{"fresh host", noV6, predictLoaded(t, "debian-13", "fresh"), fwstate.TransEnable, nil},
		{"UFW's IPv6 chains", noV6, predictLoaded(t, "debian-13", "rules"), fwstate.TransReload, nil},
		{"UFW's plain table", noV6, predictLoaded(t, "debian-13", "ipv6no"), fwstate.TransReload, nil},
		{"Docker chain", noV6, docker, fwstate.TransEnable, []string{"chain DOCKER-USER", "IPV6=yes"}},
		{"tailscale rule", noV6, tailscale, fwstate.TransReload, []string{"INPUT rule 2 (-A INPUT -i tailscale0 -j ACCEPT)"}},
		{"jump with a match", noV6, matchedJump, fwstate.TransEnable, []string{"FORWARD rule 7 (-A FORWARD -i eth0 -j ufw6-before-forward)"}},
	} {
		err := IPv6Refusal(tc.cfg, tc.cur, tc.tr)
		if tc.want == nil {
			if err != nil {
				t.Errorf("%s: %v", tc.name, err)
			}
			continue
		}
		var ce *errcode.Error
		if !errors.As(err, &ce) || ce.Code != errcode.FirewallUnsupportedConfiguration {
			t.Errorf("%s: err = %v, want %s", tc.name, err, errcode.FirewallUnsupportedConfiguration)
			continue
		}
		for _, w := range tc.want {
			if !strings.Contains(ce.Detail, w) {
				t.Errorf("%s: detail %q lacks %q", tc.name, ce.Detail, w)
			}
		}
	}
}

// TestIPv6RefusalUFWItems checks the items UFW owns in the built-in
// chains against the keys netfilter gives the rules UFW writes.
func TestIPv6RefusalUFWItems(t *testing.T) {
	rs, err := netfilter.ParseRestore(strings.NewReader("*filter\n:ufw6-before-input - [0:0]\n" +
		"-A INPUT -j ufw6-before-input\n-A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT\n-A OUTPUT -o lo -j ACCEPT\n-A OUTPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT\nCOMMIT\n"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	f := rs.Table("filter")
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		chain string
		i     int
		want  bool
	}{{"INPUT", 0, true}, {"INPUT", 1, true}, {"OUTPUT", 0, true}, {"OUTPUT", 1, false}} {
		if got := ufwBuiltinRule(tc.chain, f.Chain(tc.chain).Rules[tc.i]); got != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("%s rule %d: %v, want %v", tc.chain, tc.i+1, got, tc.want)
		}
	}
}
```

```go
package predict

import (
	"fmt"
	"slices"
	"strings"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netfilter"
)

// IPv6Refusal returns nil, or a firewall.unsupported_configuration error
// (a hard refusal) when tr starts UFW with IPV6=no (TransEnable, or
// TransReload of an enabled UFW) while cur's IPv6 filter table holds a
// chain or rule UFW did not create (spec 2.3). Such a start replaces the
// whole IPv6 filter table with UFW's plain one, which no snapshot can
// undo. UFW's own items are its ufw6- chains, bare jumps to them from
// INPUT, OUTPUT and FORWARD, and the plain table's loopback rules; the
// error's detail names every other chain and rule and suggests IPV6=yes.
func IPv6Refusal(cfg fwstate.Config, cur fwstate.Loaded, tr fwstate.Transition) error {
	starts := tr == fwstate.TransEnable || (tr == fwstate.TransReload && cfg.Enabled)
	if cfg.IPv6 || !starts || cur.V6 == nil {
		return nil
	}
	f := cur.V6.Table("filter")
	if f == nil {
		return nil
	}
	var foreign []string
	for _, c := range f.Chains {
		switch {
		case strings.HasPrefix(c.Name, "ufw6-"):
		case !slices.Contains(filterBuiltins, c.Name):
			foreign = append(foreign, "chain "+c.Name)
		default:
			for i, r := range c.Rules {
				if !ufwBuiltinRule(c.Name, r) {
					foreign = append(foreign, fmt.Sprintf("%s rule %d (%s)", c.Name, i+1, strings.Join(strings.Fields(r.Text), " ")))
				}
			}
		}
	}
	if len(foreign) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	return errcode.New(errcode.FirewallUnsupportedConfiguration, fmt.Sprintf(
		"starting UFW with IPV6=no would replace the IPv6 filter table and remove what UFW did not create, which no snapshot can rebuild: %s; set IPV6=yes in /etc/default/ufw",
		strings.Join(foreign, ", ")))
}

// ufwBuiltinRule reports whether a rule of a built-in IPv6 filter chain is
// one UFW creates: a bare jump to one of its chains, or the plain table's
// loopback rule.
func ufwBuiltinRule(chain string, r netfilter.Rule) bool {
	key := netfilter.Key(r, true)
	if r.Target.Chain && strings.HasPrefix(r.Target.Name, "ufw6-") && key == "-j "+r.Target.Name {
		return true
	}
	return (chain == "INPUT" && key == "-i lo -j ACCEPT") || (chain == "OUTPUT" && key == "-o lo -j ACCEPT")
}
```

### Task 62: Snapshot restore

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/modules/firewall/restore.go`
- Test: `internal/modules/firewall/restore_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `planImage`, `imageMismatch`, `restoreProgram`, `builtinChains`, `firewallChain`, `chainRef` (Task 32); `snapshot`, `beginRestore`, `restoreIntent`, `endRestore`, `fileHash` (Task 37); `capture`, `fileHashes`, the fake host (Task 45); `enableOp`, `ufwPath`, `ufwFailure` (Task 59).
- Produces: `restoreReport`, `chooseTransition`, `transitionArgs`, `restoreKeep`, `restore`, `writeBackSysctl` (Part contracts, Task 62); the shared test helpers `rsTestSnap` and `rsTestRuns`.

**Depends on:** Task 59

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-opus-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 2 - risk 3 = 6
**Lenses:** security

The whole-snapshot restore of spec 2.5, which a revert, its connectivity exception, a repair and `firewall.snapshot.restore` share. It is crash-safe: the restore is recorded with its UFW transition before the first write. That transition is chosen from the snapshot's `ENABLED` and the current one, never assumed. A run after a crash finishes the same way. The restore writes every file through `FileWriter.Restore` and runs the transition (for a repair snapshot, it loads the before-image instead). It writes the sysctl values back, global keys first and only for interfaces that still exist, and verifies `ENABLED`, the files, the loaded chains and every sysctl value before clearing the record. The tests prove the exact order of writes, the four transitions plus the unreadable-configuration fallback, finishing a recorded restore, eight failures that keep the record, loading a before-image, leaving a changed built-in chain, and the sysctl order.

```go
package firewall

import (

// rsTestSnap captures a snapshot of h and reads it back.
func rsTestSnap(t *testing.T, h *fakeHost, withImage bool) snapshot {
	t.Helper()
	raw, err := capture(context.Background(), h.env(), h.deps(), nil, withImage)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	s, err := getSnapshot(context.Background(), h.db, string(raw))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return s
}

func rsTestRuns(h *fakeHost) []string {
	var out []string
	for _, c := range h.calls {
		if strings.HasPrefix(c, "run ") {
			out = append(out, c)
		}
	}
	return out
}

func TestChooseTransition(t *testing.T) {
	for _, c := range []struct {
		snap, cur bool
		want      fwstate.Transition
	}{
		{true, true, fwstate.TransReload},
		{true, false, fwstate.TransEnable},
		{false, true, fwstate.TransDisable},
		{false, false, fwstate.TransNone},
	} {
		if got := chooseTransition(c.snap, c.cur); got != c.want {
			t.Errorf("chooseTransition(%v, %v) = %s, want %s", c.snap, c.cur, got, c.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestRestoreWholeSnapshot(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newFakeHost(t)
	snap := rsTestSnap(t, h, false)
	s := h.state()
	s.Rules4, s.LogLevel = s.Rules4[:1], "high"
	h.setState(s)
	if err := os.Remove(filepath.Join(h.root, "/etc/ufw/after6.rules")); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	h.sysctl["net/ipv4/ip_forward"] = "1"
	h.sysctl["net/ipv4/conf/eth0/rp_filter"] = "0"
	h.sysctl["net/ipv4/conf/all/rp_filter"] = "0"
	delete(h.sysctl, "net/ipv6/conf/eth0/accept_ra")
	h.ufw["reload"] = func(*fhState) int { return 0 }
	h.calls = nil
	rep, err := restore(ctx, h.env(), h.deps(), snap)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if rep.Transition != fwstate.TransReload || !reflect.DeepEqual(rep.Vanished, []string{"net/ipv6/conf/eth0/accept_ra"}) || rep.Excluded != nil {
		t.Errorf("report = %+v", rep)
	}
	var want []string
	for _, e := range snap.Entries {
		want = append(want, "restore "+e.Path)
	}
	want = append(want, "run /usr/sbin/ufw reload",
		"sysctl net/ipv4/ip_forward=0", "sysctl net/ipv4/conf/all/rp_filter=2", "sysctl net/ipv6/conf/all/forwarding=0",
		"sysctl net/ipv4/conf/default/rp_filter=1", "sysctl net/ipv4/conf/eth0/rp_filter=1")
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(h.calls, want) {
		t.Errorf("calls =\n%s\nwant\n%s", strings.Join(h.calls, "\n"), strings.Join(want, "\n"))
	}
	if got := fileHashes(h.config().Files); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, snap.Hashes) {
		t.Errorf("files after the restore = %v, want %v", got, snap.Hashes)
	}
	if _, ok, _ := pendingRestore(ctx, h.db); ok {
		t.Error("a finished restore left its record")
	}
	keep := h.keeps[0]
	for _, c := range []struct {
		table, chain string
		want         bool
	}{{"filter", "ufw-user-input", true}, {"filter", "INPUT", true}, {"filter", "DOCKER", false}, {"nat", "INPUT", false}, {"nat", "darkpanel-nat", true}} {
		if got := keep(fwstate.V4, c.table, c.chain); got != c.want {
			t.Errorf("restore verifies %s/%s = %v, want %v", c.table, c.chain, got, c.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestRestoreChoosesTheTransition(t *testing.T) {
	for _, c := range []struct {
		name          string
		snapEnabled   bool
		curEnabled    bool
		breakConf     bool
		wantRuns      []string
		wantRecording fwstate.Transition
	}{
		{"enable", true, false, false, []string{"run /usr/sbin/ufw --force enable"}, fwstate.TransEnable},
		{"disable", false, true, false, []string{"run /usr/sbin/ufw disable"}, fwstate.TransDisable},
		{"none", false, false, false, nil, fwstate.TransNone},
		{"unreadable, snapshot active", true, true, true, []string{"run /usr/sbin/ufw --force enable"}, fwstate.TransEnable},
		{"unreadable, snapshot inactive", false, false, true, []string{"run /usr/sbin/ufw disable"}, fwstate.TransDisable},
	} {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			ctx := context.Background()
			h := newFakeHost(t)
			s := h.state()
			s.Enabled = c.snapEnabled
			h.setState(s)
			snap := rsTestSnap(t, h, false)
			s.Enabled = c.curEnabled
			h.setState(s)
			if c.breakConf {
				if err := os.Remove(filepath.Join(h.root, "/etc/ufw/ufw.conf")); err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
			}
			h.ufw["--force enable"] = func(s *fhState) int { s.Enabled = true; return 0 }
			h.ufw["disable"] = func(s *fhState) int { s.Enabled = false; return 0 }
			h.calls = nil
			rep, err := restore(ctx, h.env(), h.deps(), snap)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if rep.Transition != c.wantRecording {
				t.Errorf("transition = %s, want %s", rep.Transition, c.wantRecording)
			}
			if got := rsTestRuns(h); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, c.wantRuns) {
				t.Errorf("runs = %v, want %v", got, c.wantRuns)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestRestoreFinishesARecordedRestore(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newFakeHost(t)
	s := h.state()
	s.Enabled = false
	h.setState(s)
	snap := rsTestSnap(t, h, false)
	// A first run recorded "disable" and wrote the files, then the process
	// died before ufw ran: ufw.conf already says disabled, UFW still runs.
	if err := beginRestore(ctx, h.db, snap.ID, fwstate.TransDisable, h.clock.Now()); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	h.ufw["disable"] = func(s *fhState) int { s.Enabled = false; return 0 }
	h.calls = nil
	rep, err := restore(ctx, h.env(), h.deps(), snap)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if rep.Transition != fwstate.TransDisable || !reflect.DeepEqual(rsTestRuns(h), []string{"run /usr/sbin/ufw disable"}) {
		t.Errorf("transition %s runs %v, want the recorded disable", rep.Transition, rsTestRuns(h))
	}
	if _, ok, _ := pendingRestore(ctx, h.db); ok {
		t.Error("the finished restore left its record")
	}
}

func TestRestoreFailures(t *testing.T) {

		{"sysctl write fails", func(h *fakeHost) { h.sysctlFail["net/ipv4/ip_forward"] = errors.New("read-only") }, true},
		{"sysctl reads back wrong", func(h *fakeHost) { h.sysctlLie["net/ipv4/conf/eth0/rp_filter"] = "2" }, true},

// rsTestSave4 is fhSave with a foreign chain jumped to from INPUT.
const rsTestSave4 = "*filter\n:INPUT DROP [0:0]\n:FORWARD DROP [0:0]\n:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]\n:fw-foreign - [0:0]\n" +
	":ufw-user-input - [0:0]\n-A INPUT -j fw-foreign\n-A INPUT -j ufw-user-input\n" +
	"-A ufw-user-input -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT\nCOMMIT\n"

func TestRestoreLoadsABeforeImage(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newFakeHost(t)
	h.loaded.V4 = fhParse(t, rsTestSave4)
	snap := rsTestSnap(t, h, true)
	imaged := h.loaded
	h.loaded.V4 = fhParse(t, strings.Replace(rsTestSave4, "--dport 22", "--dport 2222", 1))
	h.loaded.V6 = fhParse(t, strings.Replace(fhSave, ":INPUT DROP", ":INPUT ACCEPT", 1))
	want := planImage(snap.State.Image, h.loaded)
	h.onRun = func(h *fakeHost, cmd core.Cmd) core.CmdResult {
		if cmd.Path == "/usr/sbin/ip6tables-nft-restore" {
			h.loaded = imaged
		}
		return core.CmdResult{}
	}
	h.calls = nil
	rep, err := restore(ctx, h.env(), h.deps(), snap)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if rep.Transition != fwstate.TransNone || rep.Excluded != nil {
		t.Errorf("report = %+v", rep)
	}
	if got := rsTestRuns(h); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, []string{"run /usr/sbin/iptables-nft-restore -n", "run /usr/sbin/ip6tables-nft-restore -n"}) {
		t.Errorf("runs = %v", got)
	}
	if string(h.stdin["/usr/sbin/iptables-nft-restore"]) != string(want.Restore4) || string(h.stdin["/usr/sbin/ip6tables-nft-restore"]) != string(want.Restore6) {
		t.Errorf("restore input =\n%s\n%s", h.stdin["/usr/sbin/iptables-nft-restore"], h.stdin["/usr/sbin/ip6tables-nft-restore"])
	}
	if len(h.keeps) != 0 {
		t.Error("a before-image restore compared chains with the prediction")
	}
}

func TestRestoreLeavesAChangedBuiltinChain(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newFakeHost(t)
	h.loaded.V4 = fhParse(t, rsTestSave4)
	snap := rsTestSnap(t, h, true)
	changed := strings.Replace(rsTestSave4, "-A INPUT -j ufw-user-input\n", "-A INPUT -j ufw-user-input\n-A INPUT -s 192.0.2.9/32 -j DROP\n", 1)
	h.loaded.V4 = fhParse(t, changed)
	h.calls = nil
	rep, err := restore(ctx, h.env(), h.deps(), snap)
	if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "v4 filter/INPUT") {
		t.Fatalf("restore = %v, want an error naming v4 filter/INPUT", err)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(rep.Excluded, []chainRef{{fwstate.V4, "filter", "INPUT"}}) {
		t.Errorf("excluded = %v", rep.Excluded)
	}
	if strings.Contains(string(h.stdin["/usr/sbin/iptables-nft-restore"]), "-F INPUT") {
		t.Error("the restore input flushes the changed INPUT chain")
	}
	if _, ok, _ := pendingRestore(ctx, h.db); ok {
		t.Error("a restore that did what it could left its record")
	}
}

	h.onRun = nil
	h.loaded.V4 = fhParse(t, strings.Replace(fhSave, "--dport 22", "--dport 23", 1))
	if _, err := restore(ctx, h.env(), h.deps(), snap); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "differ from the before-image") {
		t.Errorf("restore = %v, want a mismatch with the before-image", err)
	}
}

func TestWriteBackSysctlOrder(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newFakeHost(t)
	want := map[string]string{
		"net/ipv6/conf/eth0/accept_ra": "2", "net/ipv4/conf/default/rp_filter": "0", "net/ipv4/ip_forward": "1",
		"net/ipv4/conf/all/rp_filter": "1", "net/ipv4/conf/eth1/rp_filter": "1", "net/ipv6/conf/all/forwarding": "1",
	}
	vanished, err := writeBackSysctl(ctx, h.env(), want, h.sysctl)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(vanished, []string{"net/ipv4/conf/eth1/rp_filter"}) {
		t.Errorf("vanished = %v", vanished)
	}
	wantCalls := []string{"sysctl net/ipv4/ip_forward=1", "sysctl net/ipv4/conf/all/rp_filter=1", "sysctl net/ipv6/conf/all/forwarding=1",
		"sysctl net/ipv4/conf/default/rp_filter=0", "sysctl net/ipv6/conf/eth0/accept_ra=2"}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(h.calls, wantCalls) {
		t.Errorf("calls = %v, want %v", h.calls, wantCalls)
	}
	if slices.Contains(h.calls, "sysctl net/ipv4/conf/eth1/rp_filter=1") {
		t.Error("a vanished interface's key was written")
	}
}
```

```go
package firewall

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"slices"
	"strings"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
)

// restoreReport is what a restore did besides restoring.
type restoreReport struct {
	Transition fwstate.Transition
	Vanished   []string   // per-interface sysctl keys not written back: the interface has gone (spec 2.1)
	Excluded   []chainRef // before-image built-in chains left as they are (spec 2.3)
}

// chooseTransition is the UFW transition that takes UFW from its current
// enabled state to the snapshot's (spec 2.5). "ufw reload" on an inactive
// UFW only prints that it skips, so the transition is chosen, never
// assumed.
func chooseTransition(snapEnabled, curEnabled bool) fwstate.Transition {
	switch {
	case snapEnabled && curEnabled:
		return fwstate.TransReload
	case snapEnabled:
		return fwstate.TransEnable
	case curEnabled:
		return fwstate.TransDisable
	}
	return fwstate.TransNone
}

// transitionArgs is the ufw vector of a transition; nil for none.
func transitionArgs(tr fwstate.Transition) []string {
	switch tr {
	case fwstate.TransReload:
		return []string{"reload"}
	case fwstate.TransEnable:
		return enableOp(true).Args
	case fwstate.TransDisable:
		return enableOp(false).Args
	}
	return nil
}

// restoreKeep selects the chains a restore verifies against the
// prediction: UFW's and Darkpanel's chains, and the filter table's built-in
// chains, which hold UFW's jumps and policies.
func restoreKeep(_ fwstate.Family, table, chain string) bool {
	return firewallChain(chain) || (table == "filter" && slices.Contains(builtinChains, chain))
}

// restore restores snapshot snap whole (spec 2.5). It records the restore
// with its UFW transition before the first write, chosen from the
// snapshot's ENABLED and the current one (when the current configuration
// cannot be read, an explicit enable or disable), so that a restore cut off
// by a crash, run again, finishes the same way. Then it writes every file
// with FileWriter.Restore and runs the transition, or, for a repair
// snapshot, loads its loaded-state before-image with *-restore -n instead
// (spec 2.3); writes the sysctl values back (spec 2.1); verifies ENABLED and
// the files, the loaded chains against d.predict of the restored
// configuration (or the before-image) and every sysctl value; and clears
// the record. Built-in chains the before-image had to leave as they are
// make it fail after the rest is restored and verified.
func restore(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, d deps, snap snapshot) (restoreReport, error) {
	var rep restoreReport
	tr, recorded, err := restoreIntent(ctx, env.DB, snap.ID)
	if err != nil {
		return rep, err
	}
	if !recorded {
		switch cur, err := d.readConfig(d.root); {
		case snap.State.Image != nil:
			tr = fwstate.TransNone
		case err != nil && snap.State.Enabled:
			tr = fwstate.TransEnable
		case err != nil:
			tr = fwstate.TransDisable
		default:
			tr = chooseTransition(snap.State.Enabled, cur.Enabled)
		}
		if err := beginRestore(ctx, env.DB, snap.ID, tr, env.Clock.Now()); err != nil {
			return rep, err
		}
	}
	rep.Transition = tr
	for _, e := range snap.Entries {
		if err := env.Files.Restore(ctx, ID, e); err != nil {
			return rep, fmt.Errorf("firewall: restore %s: %w", e.Path, err)
		}
	}
	before, err := d.readLoaded(ctx, env)
	if err != nil {
		return rep, fmt.Errorf("firewall: restore: %w", err)
	}
	var plan imagePlan
	if img := snap.State.Image; img != nil {
		plan = planImage(img, before)
		rep.Excluded = plan.Excluded
		for _, f := range []struct {
			fam   fwstate.Family
			input []byte
		}{{fwstate.V4, plan.Restore4}, {fwstate.V6, plan.Restore6}} {
			if f.input == nil {
				continue
			}
			cmd := core.Cmd{Path: restoreProgram(f.fam, before.Variant), Args: []string{"-n"}, Stdin: f.input}
			if res, err := env.Exec.Run(ctx, cmd); err != nil || res.ExitCode != 0 {
				return rep, fmt.Errorf("firewall: load the %s before-image: %w", f.fam, runFailure(cmd, res, err))
			}
		}
	} else if args := transitionArgs(tr); args != nil {
		if res, err := env.Exec.Run(ctx, core.Cmd{Path: ufwPath, Args: args}); err != nil || res.ExitCode != 0 {
			return rep, ufwFailure(args, res, err)
		}
	}
	after, err := d.readLoaded(ctx, env)
	if err != nil {
		return rep, fmt.Errorf("firewall: restore: %w", err)
	}
	if rep.Vanished, err = writeBackSysctl(ctx, env, snap.State.Sysctl, after.Sysctl); err != nil {
		return rep, err
	}
	if err := verifyRestore(d, snap, tr, before, after, plan); err != nil {
		return rep, err
	}
	if err := endRestore(ctx, env.DB, snap.ID); err != nil {
		return rep, err
	}
	if len(rep.Excluded) > 0 {
		return rep, fmt.Errorf("firewall: the before-image left %s as they are: their rules other than UFW's and Darkpanel's changed since the snapshot",
			joinRefs(rep.Excluded))
	}
	return rep, nil
}

func joinRefs(refs []chainRef) string {
	s := make([]string, len(refs))
	for i, r := range refs {
		s[i] = r.String()
	}
	return strings.Join(s, ", ")
}

// runFailure describes a program run that failed.
func runFailure(cmd core.Cmd, res core.CmdResult, err error) error {
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", cmd.Path, err)
	}
	return fmt.Errorf("%s exited %d: %s", cmd.Path, res.ExitCode, strings.TrimSpace(string(res.Stderr)))
}

// verifyRestore checks a restore's result: ENABLED and every file as the
// snapshot holds them, and the loaded chains as d.predict says the
// restored configuration loads with transition tr from before (or, for a
// before-image, as the image holds them, except the chains it left).
func verifyRestore(d deps, snap snapshot, tr fwstate.Transition, before, after fwstate.Loaded, plan imagePlan) error {
	cfg, err := d.readConfig(d.root)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("firewall: verify the restore: %w", err)
	}
	if cfg.Enabled != snap.State.Enabled {
		return fmt.Errorf("firewall: verify the restore: ENABLED is %v, the snapshot's is %v", cfg.Enabled, snap.State.Enabled)
	}
	for _, e := range snap.Entries {
		if got := fileHash(cfg.Files[e.Path]); got != fileHash(e) {
			return fmt.Errorf("firewall: verify the restore: %s is %s, the snapshot's is %s", e.Path, got, fileHash(e))
		}
	}
	if snap.State.Image != nil {
		if bad := imageMismatch(snap.State.Image, after, plan.Excluded); len(bad) > 0 {
			return fmt.Errorf("firewall: verify the restore: %s differ from the before-image", joinRefs(bad))
		}
		return nil
	}
	want, err := d.predict(cfg, before, tr)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("firewall: verify the restore: %w", err)
	}
	if diffs := d.compare(want, after, restoreKeep); len(diffs) > 0 {
		refs := make([]chainRef, len(diffs))
		for i, df := range diffs {
			refs[i] = chainRef{df.Family, df.Table, df.Chain}
		}
		return fmt.Errorf("firewall: verify the restore: %s differ from the prediction", joinRefs(refs))
	}
	return nil
}

// sysctlRank orders sysctl keys for writing back (spec 2.1): writing
// net.ipv4.ip_forward resets IPv4's per-interface values and the all keys
// change every interface, so the global keys go first, then all, then
// default, then each interface's.
func sysctlRank(key string) int {
	switch iface := sysctlIface(key); {
	case key == "net/ipv4/ip_forward":
		return 0
	case iface == "all":
		return 1
	case iface == "default":
		return 2
	}
	return 3
}

// sysctlIface returns the <iface> component of net/ipv4/conf/<iface>/...
// and net/ipv6/conf/<iface>/..., or "".
func sysctlIface(key string) string {
	parts := strings.Split(key, "/")
	if len(parts) == 5 && parts[0] == "net" && (parts[1] == "ipv4" || parts[1] == "ipv6") && parts[2] == "conf" {
		return parts[3]
	}
	return ""
}

// writeBackSysctl writes want's values in sysctlRank order and reads each
// back. A per-interface key absent from present (the live keys) belongs to
// an interface that has gone: it is not written and is returned instead.
func writeBackSysctl(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, want, present map[string]string) ([]string, error) {
	keys := make([]string, 0, len(want))
	for k := range want {
		keys = append(keys, k)
	}
	slices.SortFunc(keys, func(a, b string) int {
		if ra, rb := sysctlRank(a), sysctlRank(b); ra != rb {
			return ra - rb
		}
		return strings.Compare(a, b)
	})
	var vanished, written []string
	for _, k := range keys {
		if sysctlRank(k) == 3 && sysctlIface(k) != "" {
			if _, ok := present[k]; !ok {
				vanished = append(vanished, k)
				continue
			}
		}
		if err := env.Files.WriteSysctl(ctx, ID, k, want[k]); err != nil {
			return vanished, fmt.Errorf("firewall: write sysctl %s back: %w", k, err)
		}
		written = append(written, k)
	}
	for _, k := range written {
		got, err := env.Files.ReadSysctl(ctx, ID, k)
		if err != nil {
			return vanished, fmt.Errorf("firewall: read sysctl %s back: %w", k, err)
		}
		if got != want[k] {
			return vanished, fmt.Errorf("firewall: sysctl %s reads back %q, the snapshot's value is %q", k, got, want[k])
		}
	}
	return vanished, nil
}
```

### Task 63: Effect inverses

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/modules/firewall/inverse.go`
- Test: `internal/modules/firewall/inverse_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `observe`, `ruleState`, `ufwVersion`, `splitResource`, `mustJSON` (Task 54); `defaultOp`, `loggingOp`, `enableOp`, `jsonEqual`, `ufwFailure`, `ufwPath` (Task 59); `writeBackSysctl` (Task 62); `snapshot`, `fileHash` (Task 37); `model.ParseTuple`, `model.Merge`, `model.AddArgs`, `model.InsertArgs`, `model.DeleteArgs` (Task 13, Task 25).
- Produces: `inverse`, `ufw`, `stateTuples`, `ruleOf`, `deleteAdded`, `reinsert`, `restoreFile`, `writeBackLive` (Part contracts, Task 63).

**Depends on:** Task 62

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-opus-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 2 - risk 3 = 6
**Lenses:** security

Step 3 of a revert applies the journaled effects' inverses (spec 2.5). `inverse` undoes one effect from its journal record alone: it deletes an added rule, re-inserts a deleted rule at its positions, sets a default, the level or the enabled state back, writes a file back from the snapshot, or writes a sysctl value back. It then checks that the resource is as before. A deleted both-family rule comes back as two single-family inserts, the controller's ruling. Containers proved that this restores both rule files byte for byte, and that a position past the end must append (Assumptions). The tests run each forward effect through `runUfw` and undo it. They prove the vectors for a middle, a last and an IPv6-only rule, the failure when ufw skips an insert or fails, the value inverses (with the sysctl write-back after an enable or disable), file and sysctl inverses, and the refusals.

```go
package firewall

import (

// ivTestForward runs op forward on h and returns its made effect.
func ivTestForward(t *testing.T, h *fakeHost, op ufwOp) core.Effect {
	t.Helper()
	h.journal.effects = nil
	if err := runUfw(context.Background(), h.env(), h.deps(), op); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	e := efTestOnly(t, h)
	if e.State != core.EffectMade {
		t.Fatalf("forward effect is %s", e.State)
	}
	return e
}

func ivTestInsert(lines []string, i int, line string) []string {
	return slices.Insert(slices.Clone(lines), i, line)
}

func TestInverseDeletesAnAddedRule(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newFakeHost(t)

	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	h.ufw[strings.Join(op.Args, " ")] = func(s *fhState) int {
		s.Rules4, s.Rules6 = append(s.Rules4, v4), append(s.Rules6, v6)
		return 0
	}
	e := ivTestForward(t, h, op)
	del := strings.Join(model.DeleteArgs(efTestRule), " ")
	h.ufw[del] = func(s *fhState) int {

	}
}

			removeAt4: 1, removeAt6: 1,

				"allow in proto tcp from 0.0.0.0/0 to 0.0.0.0/0 port 8080 comment darkpanel:" + efTestID,
				"allow in proto tcp from ::/0 to ::/0 port 8080 comment darkpanel:" + efTestID,
			},

			removeAt4: -1, removeAt6: 0,
			wantInsert: []string{"insert 2 deny in proto udp from 2001:db8::/32 to ::/0 port 53"},

			}

					} else {

			}
			if !reflect.DeepEqual(runs, c.wantInsert) {
				t.Errorf("ufw ran %q, want %q", runs, c.wantInsert)
			}
			if got := fileHashes(h.config().Files); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, snap.Hashes) {
				t.Error("the files differ from before the rule was deleted")
			}
		})
	}
}

	}{

		{logging, func(s *fhState) { s.LogLevel = "full" }, func(s *fhState) { s.LogLevel = "low" }, "logging low"},
		{enableOp(false), func(s *fhState) { s.Enabled = false }, func(s *fhState) { s.Enabled = true }, "--force enable"},
	} {
		edit, undo := c.edit, c.undo
		h.ufw[strings.Join(c.forward.Args, " ")] = func(s *fhState) int { edit(s); return 0 }
		h.ufw[c.undoArgs] = func(s *fhState) int { undo(s); return 0 }
		e := ivTestForward(t, h, c.forward)
		h.sysctl["net/ipv4/ip_forward"] = "1"
		h.calls = nil
		if err := inverse(ctx, h.env(), h.deps(), snap, e); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("undo %s: %v", c.undoArgs, err)
		}
		if h.calls[0] != "run /usr/sbin/ufw "+c.undoArgs {
			t.Errorf("undo ran %v, want %q first", h.calls, c.undoArgs)
		}
		wroteSysctl := slices.Contains(h.calls, "sysctl net/ipv4/ip_forward=0")
		if wroteSysctl != (c.forward.Resource == resourceEnabled) {
			t.Errorf("undo of %s wrote the sysctl values back: %v", c.forward.Resource, wroteSysctl)
		}
	}
	if got := fileHashes(h.config().Files); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, snap.Hashes) {
		t.Error("the files differ from the snapshot after every undo")
	}
}

func TestInverseFileAndSysctl(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newFakeHost(t)
	snap := rsTestSnap(t, h, false)
	entry := h.config().Files["/etc/ufw/after.rules"]
	entry.Data = []byte("*filter\n# edited\nCOMMIT\n")
	h.journal.effects = nil
	if err := writeFileEffect(ctx, h.env(), h.deps(), entry); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	fileEffect := efTestOnly(t, h)
	if err := inverse(ctx, h.env(), h.deps(), snap, fileEffect); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got := fileHash(h.config().Files[entry.Path]); got != snap.Hashes[entry.Path] {
		t.Errorf("after.rules = %s, want the snapshot's", got)
	}
	other := fileEffect
	other.Before = core.StateDoc{State: mustJSON("sha256:00")}
	if err := inverse(ctx, h.env(), h.deps(), snap, other); err == nil {
		t.Error("a file effect whose before the snapshot does not hold was undone")
	}
	h.journal.effects = nil
	if err := writeSysctlEffect(ctx, h.env(), h.deps(), "net/ipv4/conf/default/rp_filter", "2"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := inverse(ctx, h.env(), h.deps(), snap, efTestOnly(t, h)); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if h.sysctl["net/ipv4/conf/default/rp_filter"] != "1" {
		t.Errorf("rp_filter = %s after the undo, want 1", h.sysctl["net/ipv4/conf/default/rp_filter"])
	}
}

func TestInverseRefusesWhatItCannotUndo(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newFakeHost(t)
	snap := rsTestSnap(t, h, false)
	for name, e := range map[string]core.Effect{
		"unknown noun":       {Seq: 1, Kind: core.EffectModify, Resource: "firewall.thing:x"},
		"added without post": {Seq: 1, Kind: core.EffectCreate, Resource: ruleResource(fhTag)},
		"doubled rule": {Seq: 1, Kind: core.EffectCreate, Resource: ruleResource(fhTag),
			Post: &core.StateDoc{State: mustJSON(ruleState{Matches: 2})}},
		"application rule": {Seq: 1, Kind: core.EffectDelete, Resource: ruleResource("manual-0000000000000000"),
			Before: core.StateDoc{State: mustJSON(ruleState{V4: "### tuple ### allow any any 0.0.0.0/0 any 0.0.0.0/0 OpenSSH - in"}), Version: mustJSON(ufwVersion{Pos4: 1})}},
	} {
		if err := inverse(ctx, h.env(), h.deps(), snap, e); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("%s: inverse succeeded", name)
		}
	}
	if slices.ContainsFunc(h.calls, func(c string) bool { return strings.HasPrefix(c, "run ") }) {
		t.Errorf("a refused undo ran %v", h.calls)
	}
}
```

```go
package firewall

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/model"
)

// inverse undoes one made effect (spec 2.5) from the journal alone, never
// from the change's input: a rule added is deleted by the tuples in its
// Post; a rule deleted is inserted again at the positions in its Before,
// the IPv4 and IPv6 halves of a both-family rule separately, because ufw
// puts the other half of one insert at the end; a default, the logging
// level or the enabled state is set back to its Before (after an enable or
// disable, with the snapshot's sysctl values written back, since UFW's
// start applies its sysctl file); a file gets the snapshot's entry whose
// hash is its Before; a sysctl key gets its Before. The resource is then
// observed, and anything but its Before's State is an error.
func inverse(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, d deps, snap snapshot, e core.Effect) error {
	noun, ident, err := splitResource(e.Resource)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	switch noun {
	case nounRule:
		if e.Kind == core.EffectCreate {
			err = deleteAdded(ctx, env, e)
		} else {
			err = reinsert(ctx, env, d, e)
		}
	case nounDefault:
		var policy string
		if err = json.Unmarshal(e.Before.State, &policy); err == nil {
			var op ufwOp
			if op, err = defaultOp(ident, policy); err == nil {
				err = ufw(ctx, env, op.Args)
			}
		}
	case nounLogging:
		var level string
		if err = json.Unmarshal(e.Before.State, &level); err == nil {
			var op ufwOp
			if op, err = loggingOp(level); err == nil {
				err = ufw(ctx, env, op.Args)
			}
		}
	case nounState:
		var enabled bool
		if err = json.Unmarshal(e.Before.State, &enabled); err == nil {
			if err = ufw(ctx, env, enableOp(enabled).Args); err == nil {
				err = writeBackLive(ctx, env, d, snap)
			}
		}
	case nounFile:
		err = restoreFile(ctx, env, snap, ident, e.Before)
	case nounSysctl:
		var value string
		if err = json.Unmarshal(e.Before.State, &value); err == nil {
			err = env.Files.WriteSysctl(ctx, ID, ident, value)
		}
	default:
		err = fmt.Errorf("firewall: effect resource %q has no firewall noun", e.Resource)
	}
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("firewall: undo effect %d (%s): %w", e.Seq, e.Resource, err)
	}
	obs, err := observe(ctx, env, d, e)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("firewall: undo effect %d (%s): %w", e.Seq, e.Resource, err)
	}
	if !jsonEqual(obs.Current.State, e.Before.State) {
		return fmt.Errorf("firewall: undo effect %d (%s) left %s, want %s", e.Seq, e.Resource, obs.Current.State, e.Before.State)
	}
	return nil
}

// ufw runs one ufw vector and fails on a non-zero exit.
func ufw(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, args []string) error {
	res, err := env.Exec.Run(ctx, core.Cmd{Path: ufwPath, Args: args})
	if err != nil || res.ExitCode != 0 {
		return ufwFailure(args, res, err)
	}
	return nil
}

// stateTuples parses a ruleState's tuple lines.
func stateTuples(raw json.RawMessage) (rs ruleState, v4, v6 []model.Tuple, err error) {
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &rs); err != nil {
		return rs, nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("rule state %s: %w", raw, err)
	}
	if rs.Matches > 0 || (rs.V4 == "" && rs.V6 == "") {
		return rs, nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("rule state %s names no single rule", raw)
	}
	for _, f := range []struct {
		line string
		v6   bool
		dst  *[]model.Tuple
	}{{rs.V4, false, &v4}, {rs.V6, true, &v6}} {
		if f.line == "" {
			continue
		}
		t, err := model.ParseTuple(f.line, f.v6)
		if err != nil {
			return rs, nil, nil, err
		}
		*f.dst = []model.Tuple{t}
	}
	return rs, v4, v6, nil
}

// ruleOf converts one tuple, or one rule's two halves, into the rule the
// argument vectors render.
func ruleOf(v4, v6 []model.Tuple) (model.Rule, error) {
	rules := model.Merge(v4, v6)
	if len(rules) != 1 {
		return model.Rule{}, fmt.Errorf("the tuples are %d rules, not one", len(rules))
	}
	if rules[0].Raw != "" {
		return model.Rule{}, fmt.Errorf("rule %s is outside the model and cannot be written", rules[0].ID)
	}
	return rules[0], nil
}

// deleteAdded deletes the rule a "rule added" effect made, as its Post
// records it.
func deleteAdded(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, e core.Effect) error {
	if e.Post == nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("effect %d has no post state", e.Seq)
	}
	_, v4, v6, err := stateTuples(e.Post.State)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	r, err := ruleOf(v4, v6)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return ufw(ctx, env, model.DeleteArgs(r))
}

// reinsert adds the rule a "rule deleted" effect removed at the positions
// its Before records: the IPv4 half at its place among user.rules' tuples,
// then the IPv6 half at its place among user6.rules' tuples, which ufw
// numbers after every IPv4 rule. A place past the end appends, since ufw
// refuses to insert there.
func reinsert(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, d deps, e core.Effect) error {
	_, v4, v6, err := stateTuples(e.Before.State)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	var ver ufwVersion
	if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Before.Version, &ver); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("rule positions %s: %w", e.Before.Version, err)
	}
	for _, half := range []struct {
		tuples []model.Tuple
		pos    int
		v6     bool
	}{{v4, ver.Pos4, false}, {v6, ver.Pos6, true}} {
		if half.tuples == nil {
			continue
		}
		var r model.Rule
		if half.v6 {
			r, err = ruleOf(nil, half.tuples)
		} else {
			r, err = ruleOf(half.tuples, nil)
		}
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		cfg, err := d.readConfig(d.root)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		n, offset := len(cfg.Rules4), 0
		if half.v6 {
			n, offset = len(cfg.Rules6), len(cfg.Rules4)
		}
		args := model.AddArgs(r)
		if half.pos >= 1 && half.pos <= n {
			args = model.InsertArgs(offset+half.pos, r)
		}
		if err := ufw(ctx, env, args); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// restoreFile writes back the snapshot's entry of path, which must be the
// file as before (its hash is before's State).
func restoreFile(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, snap snapshot, path string, before core.StateDoc) error {
	for _, entry := range snap.Entries {
		if entry.Path == path && jsonEqual(mustJSON(fileHash(entry)), before.State) {
			return env.Files.Restore(ctx, ID, entry)
		}
	}
	return fmt.Errorf("snapshot %s holds no entry of %s with hash %s", snap.ID, path, before.State)
}

// writeBackLive writes the snapshot's sysctl values back over the live
// ones; a vanished interface's keys are skipped.
func writeBackLive(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, d deps, snap snapshot) error {
	st, err := d.readLoaded(ctx, env)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	_, err = writeBackSysctl(ctx, env, snap.State.Sysctl, st.Sysctl)
	return err
}
```

### Task 64: Revert

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/modules/firewall/revert.go`
- Test: `internal/modules/firewall/revert_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `snapshot`, `getSnapshot`, `attachSnapshot`, `restoreIntent`, `setPinned`, `snapshotOfChange` (Task 37); `deps`, `fileHashes` (Task 45); `observe`, `splitResource`, `ufwVersion`, `mustJSON` (Task 54); `stateEqual` (Task 59); `restore`, `restoreKeep`, `transitionArgs` (Task 62); `inverse`, `ufw` (Task 63).
- Produces: `revert`, `overrideDetail`, `hashesAsApplied`, `expectedHashes`, `undoNewestFirst`, `ufwEffect`, `reloadIfActive`, `unpinChangeSnapshot` (Part contracts, Task 64).

**Depends on:** Task 63

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-opus-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 0 - coupling 2 - risk 3 = 6
**Lenses:** security

The firewall's `Revert`, which spec 2.5's steps 1 to 5 and spec 1.2's precedence rule define. It checks every made effect against its `Post` and lets an unresolved effect block every write. It restores the snapshot whole only when nothing conflicts and the files are as the change left them; otherwise it undoes the effects newest first, leaving conflicts and other edits. When that did not restore the prior state, it evaluates the lockout guard. A failing guard restores whole over everything and returns `Override` with the emergency restore record; a passing one leaves the host and reports the error or the conflicts. Every ending but `reverted` pins the snapshot. These tests are the safety net of R41 and R42. The table covers 17 branches: the untouched change, a mid-apply crash, nothing to undo, an edit elsewhere, a conflict with the guard passing and failing, an unresolved and an intended effect, a failing inverse, a failing whole restore with the guard passing and failing, an unevaluable guard, an unobservable effect, and an interrupted restore with and without an unresolved effect. Further tests check the override record's content, foreign snapshots, the expected hashes and unpinning.

```go
// rvTestSetup returns a host on which change c1, after its snapshot, added
// efTestRule (effect 1) and set the outgoing default to DROP (effect 2),
// with the post-apply hashes recorded. The inverses and "ufw reload" are
// scripted.
func rvTestSetup(t *testing.T) (*fakeHost, snapshot) {
	t.Helper()

	h := newFakeHost(t)
	env, d := h.env(), h.deps()
	raw, err := capture(ctx, env, d, &core.GuardContext{Complete: true}, false)

		t.Fatal(err)

	if err != nil {

	h.ufw[strings.Join(add.Args, " ")] = func(s *fhState) int {

	h.ufw[strings.Join(model.DeleteArgs(efTestRule), " ")] = func(s *fhState) int {
		s.Rules4 = slices.DeleteFunc(s.Rules4, func(l string) bool { return l == v4 })
		s.Rules6 = slices.DeleteFunc(s.Rules6, func(l string) bool { return l == v6 })
		return 0
	}
	h.ufw["default allow outgoing"] = func(s *fhState) int { s.Output = "ACCEPT"; return 0 }

type rvTestEffect struct {
	seq     int
	state   core.EffectState
	reason  string
	current string // the Current State's JSON; "" for none
}

func TestRevert(t *testing.T) {
	undone := []rvTestEffect{{1, core.EffectUndone, "", ""}, {2, core.EffectUndone, "", ""}}
	for _, c := range []struct {
		name         string
		set          func(t *testing.T, h *fakeHost, snap snapshot)
		wantErr      string // a substring of the error; "" for none
		wantOverride bool
		wantEffects  []rvTestEffect
		wantRestored bool     // every state file is the snapshot's
		wantRuns     []string // the ufw vectors run, in order; nil to skip the check
		wantGuard    int
		wantPinned   bool
		wantManual   bool // the manual rule outside the change survives
	}{
		{
			name: "untouched: whole restore", set: func(*testing.T, *fakeHost, snapshot) {},
			wantEffects: undone, wantRestored: true, wantRuns: []string{"reload"},
		},
		{
			name:        "mid-apply crash: no post hashes, files as after the last effect",
			set:         func(t *testing.T, h *fakeHost, _ snapshot) { rvTestNoPostHashes(t, h) },
			wantEffects: undone, wantRestored: true, wantRuns: []string{"reload"},
		},

			name: "no post hashes and no settled effect: nothing to undo",
			set: func(t *testing.T, h *fakeHost, snap snapshot) {
				rvTestNoPostHashes(t, h)

					h.journal.effects[i].State = core.EffectSkipped
				}

		},

			wantEffects: undone, wantManual: true,

				h.guardOK = false
			},
			wantOverride: true, wantRestored: true, wantGuard: 1, wantPinned: true, wantEffects: undone,
		},
		{
			name: "whole restore fails, guard passes",
			set: func(_ *testing.T, h *fakeHost, _ snapshot) {
				h.ufw["reload"] = func(*fhState) int { return 1 }
			},
			wantErr: "stopped", wantRuns: []string{"reload"}, wantGuard: 1, wantPinned: true, wantRestored: true,
		},
		{
			name: "whole restore fails, guard fails: the emergency restore fails too",
			set: func(_ *testing.T, h *fakeHost, _ snapshot) {
				h.ufw["reload"] = func(*fhState) int { return 1 }
				h.guardOK = false
			},
			wantErr: "emergency restore", wantRuns: []string{"reload", "reload"}, wantGuard: 1, wantPinned: true, wantRestored: true,
		},
		{
			name: "guard cannot be evaluated: treated as failing",
			set: func(_ *testing.T, h *fakeHost, _ snapshot) {
				rvTestRemoveOwnRule(h)
				h.guardErr = errors.New("routes unreadable")
			},
			wantOverride: true, wantRestored: true, wantGuard: 1, wantPinned: true,
			wantEffects: []rvTestEffect{{1, core.EffectUnresolved, core.ReasonConflict, "null"}, {2, core.EffectUndone, "", ""}},
		},
		{
			name: "an effect cannot be observed: left as uncertain",
			set: func(_ *testing.T, h *fakeHost, _ snapshot) {
				h.journal.effects[0].Resource = "firewall.thing:x"
			},
			wantEffects: []rvTestEffect{{1, core.EffectUnresolved, core.ReasonUncertain, ""}, {2, core.EffectUndone, "", ""}},
			wantRuns:    []string{"default allow outgoing", "reload"}, wantGuard: 1, wantPinned: true,
		},
		{
			name: "interrupted restore: finished whatever the checks say",
			set: func(t *testing.T, h *fakeHost, snap snapshot) {
				rvTestManualEdit(h)
				if err := beginRestore(context.Background(), h.db, snap.ID, fwstate.TransReload, h.clock.Now()); err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
			},
			wantEffects: undone, wantRestored: true, wantRuns: []string{"reload"},
		},
		{
			name: "interrupted emergency restore: finished, still an override",
			set: func(t *testing.T, h *fakeHost, snap snapshot) {
				h.journal.effects[1].State, h.journal.effects[1].Reason = core.EffectUnresolved, core.ReasonAmbiguous
				if err := beginRestore(context.Background(), h.db, snap.ID, fwstate.TransReload, h.clock.Now()); err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
			},
			wantOverride: true, wantRestored: true, wantRuns: []string{"reload"}, wantPinned: true,
			wantEffects: []rvTestEffect{{1, core.EffectUndone, "", ""}, {2, core.EffectUnresolved, core.ReasonAmbiguous, ""}},
		},
	} {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			ctx := context.Background()
			h, snap := rvTestSetup(t)
			c.set(t, h, snap)
			out, err := revert(ctx, h.env(), h.deps(), []byte(snap.ID))
			switch {
			case c.wantErr == "" && err != nil:
				t.Fatalf("revert: %v", err)
			case c.wantErr != "" && (err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), c.wantErr)):
				t.Fatalf("revert = %v, want an error containing %q", err, c.wantErr)
			}
			if out.Override != c.wantOverride {
				t.Errorf("override = %v, want %v", out.Override, c.wantOverride)
			}
			var got []rvTestEffect
			for _, o := range out.Effects {
				e := rvTestEffect{o.Seq, o.State, o.Reason, ""}
				if o.Current != nil {
					e.current = string(o.Current.State)
				}
				got = append(got, e)
			}
			if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, c.wantEffects) {
				t.Errorf("effects = %+v, want %+v", got, c.wantEffects)
			}
			restored := reflect.DeepEqual(fileHashes(h.config().Files), snap.Hashes)
			if restored != c.wantRestored {
				t.Errorf("files restored = %v, want %v", restored, c.wantRestored)
			}
			if c.wantRuns != nil {
				runs := []string{}
				for _, call := range rsTestRuns(h) {
					runs = append(runs, strings.TrimPrefix(call, "run /usr/sbin/ufw "))
				}
				if !reflect.DeepEqual(runs, c.wantRuns) {
					t.Errorf("ufw ran %q, want %q", runs, c.wantRuns)
				}
			}
			if h.guardCalls != c.wantGuard {
				t.Errorf("guard evaluated %d times, want %d", h.guardCalls, c.wantGuard)
			}
			s, err := getSnapshot(ctx, h.db, snap.ID)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if s.Pinned != c.wantPinned {
				t.Errorf("pinned = %v, want %v", s.Pinned, c.wantPinned)
			}
			if manual := slices.Contains(h.state().Rules6, fhRule53v6); manual != c.wantManual {
				t.Errorf("manual rule kept = %v, want %v", manual, c.wantManual)
			}
			if c.wantOverride {
				var detail overrideDetail
				if err := json.Unmarshal(out.Detail, &detail); err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
				if detail.Snapshot != snap.ID || detail.Guard == "" || !detail.At.Equal(h.clock.Now()) {
					t.Errorf("override detail = %+v", detail)
				}
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestRevertOverrideDetail(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h, snap := rvTestSetup(t)
	h.journal.effects[1].State, h.journal.effects[1].Reason = core.EffectUnresolved, core.ReasonAmbiguous
	h.guardOK, h.guardDetail = false, "ssh from 203.0.113.7 to 192.0.2.1:22 on eth0 is dropped"
	delete(h.sysctl, "net/ipv6/conf/eth0/accept_ra")
	// The restore's verify compares first and must agree; the record then
	// compares the loaded state before and after the restore.
	d, compared := h.deps(), 0
	d.compare = func(_, _ fwstate.Loaded, _ func(f fwstate.Family, table, chain string) bool) []fwstate.ChainDiff {
		if compared++; compared == 1 {
			return nil
		}
		return []fwstate.ChainDiff{{Family: fwstate.V4, Table: "filter", Chain: "ufw-user-output", OnlyA: []string{"a"}, OnlyB: []string{"b"}}}
	}
	out, err := revert(ctx, h.env(), d, []byte(snap.ID))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var detail overrideDetail
	if err := json.Unmarshal(out.Detail, &detail); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if detail.Guard != h.guardDetail {
		t.Errorf("guard = %q", detail.Guard)
	}
	var paths []string
	for _, f := range detail.Files {
		paths = append(paths, f.Path)
		if f.Now != snap.Hashes[f.Path] || f.Was == f.Now || f.Was == "" {
			t.Errorf("file %+v", f)
		}
	}
	if want := []string{"/etc/ufw/user.rules", "/etc/ufw/user6.rules", "/etc/default/ufw"}; !reflect.DeepEqual(paths, want) {
		t.Errorf("overwritten files = %v, want %v", paths, want)
	}
	if len(detail.Chains) != 1 || detail.Chains[0].Chain != "ufw-user-output" || detail.Chains[0].Removed[0] != "a" || detail.Chains[0].Added[0] != "b" {
		t.Errorf("chains = %+v", detail.Chains)
	}
	if len(detail.Effects) != 1 || detail.Effects[0].Seq != 2 || string(detail.Effects[0].Was) != `"DROP"` {
		t.Errorf("effects = %+v", detail.Effects)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(detail.Vanished, []string{"net/ipv6/conf/eth0/accept_ra"}) {
		t.Errorf("vanished = %v", detail.Vanished)
	}
}

func TestRevertRefusesAForeignSnapshot(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h, snap := rvTestSetup(t)
	if _, err := revert(ctx, h.env(), h.deps(), []byte("01J0000000000000000000NONE")); err == nil {
		t.Error("revert of a missing snapshot succeeded")

	other := h.env()
	other.ChangeID = "c2"
	if _, err := revert(ctx, other, h.deps(), []byte(snap.ID)); err == nil {
		t.Error("change c2 reverted change c1's snapshot")

		t.Errorf("a refused revert ran %v", h.calls)
	}
}
```

```go
package firewall

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
)

// overrideDetail is the emergency restore record of the connectivity
// exception (spec 2.5): RevertOutcome.Detail, which the engine stores as
// core_changes.override_json and shows the operator.
type overrideDetail struct {
	At       time.Time         `json:"at"`
	Snapshot string            `json:"snapshot"`
	Guard    string            `json:"guard"`                    // why the lockout guard failed
	Files    []fileOverwrite   `json:"files,omitempty"`          // state files the restore rewrote
	Chains   []chainOverwrite  `json:"chains,omitempty"`         // loaded chains the restore changed
	Effects  []effectOverwrite `json:"effects,omitempty"`        // effects left unresolved, with what the restore overwrote
	Vanished []string          `json:"vanishedSysctl,omitempty"` // sysctl keys of interfaces that have gone, not restored
}

type fileOverwrite struct {
	Path string `json:"path"`
	Was  string `json:"was"` // fileHash before the restore
	Now  string `json:"now"` // the snapshot's
}

type chainOverwrite struct {
	Family    fwstate.Family `json:"family"`
	Table     string         `json:"table"`
	Chain     string         `json:"chain"`
	PolicyWas string         `json:"policyWas,omitempty"`
	PolicyNow string         `json:"policyNow,omitempty"`
	Removed   []string       `json:"removed,omitempty"` // rule keys the restore removed
	Added     []string       `json:"added,omitempty"`   // rule keys the restore added
	Reordered bool           `json:"reordered,omitempty"`
}

type effectOverwrite struct {
	Seq      int             `json:"seq"`
	Resource string          `json:"resource"`
	Was      json.RawMessage `json:"was,omitempty"` // the observed State the restore overwrote; absent when it could not be observed
}

// revert reverts a firewall change from its snapshot (spec 2.5, revert of
// a change; spec 1.2, one precedence rule), deciding before it writes:
//
//  1. Check: every made effect is observed against its Post; one that
//     differs is a conflict, left in place. An effect already unresolved
//     (or still intended) blocks every write.
//  2. Whole restore, when nothing is unresolved, nothing conflicts and
//     every state file's hash equals the post-apply hash (after a mid-apply
//     crash: the hash expected after the last settled effect; with neither
//     recorded, never).
//  3. Otherwise the inverses of the made effects, newest first, skipping
//     conflicts and stopping at the first failure, then "ufw reload" when
//     a rule, default or logging inverse ran on an active UFW.
//  4. Whenever that did not restore the prior state, the lockout guard on
//     the loaded state now, with the snapshot's guard context. A failing
//     (or unevaluable) guard restores the snapshot whole over everything
//     and returns Override with the emergency restore record; a passing one
//     leaves the host as it is and returns an error when an effect was
//     unresolved or a write failed, else the conflicts.
//  5. Every ending other than reverted pins the snapshot until a repair
//     unpins it (unpinChangeSnapshot).
//
// A restore of this snapshot that a crash cut off is finished first,
// whatever the checks would say: the files are partly the snapshot's.
func revert(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, d deps, snapBytes []byte) (core.RevertOutcome, error) {
	snap, err := getSnapshot(ctx, env.DB, string(snapBytes))
	if err != nil {
		return core.RevertOutcome{}, fmt.Errorf("firewall: revert: %w", err)
	}
	if env.ChangeID != "" {
		if err := attachSnapshot(ctx, env.DB, snap.ID, env.ChangeID); err != nil {
			return core.RevertOutcome{}, fmt.Errorf("firewall: revert: %w", err)
		}
	}
	effects, err := env.Effects.List(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return core.RevertOutcome{}, fmt.Errorf("firewall: revert: read the effects: %w", err)
	}
	var blocked, made []core.Effect
	for _, e := range effects {
		switch e.State {
		case core.EffectUnresolved, core.EffectIntended:
			blocked = append(blocked, e)
		case core.EffectMade:
			made = append(made, e)
		}
	}
	if _, pending, err := restoreIntent(ctx, env.DB, snap.ID); err != nil {
		return core.RevertOutcome{}, err
	} else if pending {
		return finishRestore(ctx, env, d, snap, blocked, made)
	}

	conflicts := map[int]core.EffectOutcome{}
	for _, e := range made {
		obs, err := observe(ctx, env, d, e)
		switch {
		case err != nil:
			env.Log.Warn("firewall: revert cannot observe an effect", "change", env.ChangeID, "effect", e.Seq, "error", err)
			conflicts[e.Seq] = core.EffectOutcome{Seq: e.Seq, State: core.EffectUnresolved, Reason: core.ReasonUncertain}
		case e.Post == nil || !stateEqual(obs.Current, *e.Post):
			cur := obs.Current
			conflicts[e.Seq] = core.EffectOutcome{Seq: e.Seq, State: core.EffectUnresolved, Reason: core.ReasonConflict, Current: &cur}
		}
	}

	var writeErr error
	if len(blocked) == 0 {
		if len(conflicts) == 0 && hashesAsApplied(d, snap, made) {
			rep, err := restore(ctx, env, d, snap)
			if err == nil {
				logVanished(env, rep.Vanished)
				return core.RevertOutcome{Effects: undoneOutcomes(made, nil)}, nil
			}
			writeErr = err
		} else {
			writeErr = undoNewestFirst(ctx, env, d, snap, made, conflicts)
		}
	}
	if len(blocked) == 0 && len(conflicts) == 0 && writeErr == nil {
		return core.RevertOutcome{Effects: undoneOutcomes(made, nil)}, nil
	}

	pin(ctx, env, snap.ID)
	st, err := d.readLoaded(ctx, env)
	ok, why := false, ""
	if err != nil {
		why = "the loaded state cannot be read: " + err.Error()
	} else if ok, why, err = d.lockout(ctx, env, st, snap.State.Guard); err != nil {
		ok, why = false, "the lockout guard cannot be evaluated: "+err.Error()
	}
	if !ok {
		return emergencyRestore(ctx, env, d, snap, why, blocked, made, conflicts, writeErr)
	}
	if len(blocked) > 0 {
		return core.RevertOutcome{}, fmt.Errorf("firewall: the revert left the host as it is: effects %s are unresolved; resolve them, then repair the change",
			seqList(blocked))
	}
	if writeErr != nil {
		return core.RevertOutcome{}, fmt.Errorf("firewall: the revert stopped: %w", writeErr)
	}
	out := undoneOutcomes(made, conflicts)
	for _, e := range made {
		if c, ok := conflicts[e.Seq]; ok {
			out = append(out, c)
		}
	}
	slices.SortFunc(out, func(a, b core.EffectOutcome) int { return a.Seq - b.Seq })
	return core.RevertOutcome{Effects: out}, nil
}

// undoneOutcomes reports every made effect not in skip as undone.
func undoneOutcomes(made []core.Effect, skip map[int]core.EffectOutcome) []core.EffectOutcome {
	var out []core.EffectOutcome
	for _, e := range made {
		if _, ok := skip[e.Seq]; !ok {
			out = append(out, core.EffectOutcome{Seq: e.Seq, State: core.EffectUndone})
		}
	}
	return out
}

func seqList(effects []core.Effect) string {
	s := make([]string, len(effects))
	for i, e := range effects {
		s[i] = fmt.Sprintf("%d (%s)", e.Seq, e.Resource)
	}
	return strings.Join(s, ", ")
}

// hashesAsApplied reports whether every state file's hash equals the hash
// recorded right after the change applied, or, without that record (a
// mid-apply crash or a failed apply), the hash expected after the last
// settled effect: the capture hash overlaid, effect by effect, with each
// made effect's post-call hashes. With neither, it is false.
func hashesAsApplied(d deps, snap snapshot, made []core.Effect) bool {
	expected := snap.PostHashes
	if expected == nil {
		expected = expectedHashes(snap, made)
	}
	if expected == nil {
		return false
	}
	cfg, err := d.readConfig(d.root)
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}
	for _, e := range snap.Entries {
		want, ok := expected[e.Path]
		if !ok || fileHash(cfg.Files[e.Path]) != want {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

// expectedHashes returns the state files' hashes after the made effects,
// or nil when no made effect records a file's hash.
func expectedHashes(snap snapshot, made []core.Effect) map[string]string {
	out := make(map[string]string, len(snap.Hashes))
	for p, h := range snap.Hashes {
		out[p] = h
	}
	recorded := false
	for _, e := range made {
		if e.Post == nil {
			continue
		}
		noun, ident, err := splitResource(e.Resource)
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		if noun == nounFile {
			var h string
			if json.Unmarshal(e.Post.State, &h) == nil {
				out[ident], recorded = h, true
			}
			continue
		}
		var v ufwVersion
		if len(e.Post.Version) > 0 && json.Unmarshal(e.Post.Version, &v) == nil && len(v.Files) > 0 {
			for p, h := range v.Files {
				out[p] = h
			}
			recorded = true
		}
	}
	if !recorded {
		return nil
	}
	return out
}

// undoNewestFirst runs the inverses of the made effects not in conflicts,
// newest first, stopping at the first failure, then reloads an active UFW
// when a ufw inverse ran.
func undoNewestFirst(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, d deps, snap snapshot, made []core.Effect, conflicts map[int]core.EffectOutcome) error {
	reload := false
	for i := len(made) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		e := made[i]
		if _, ok := conflicts[e.Seq]; ok {
			continue
		}
		if err := inverse(ctx, env, d, snap, e); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		reload = reload || ufwEffect(e)
	}
	if reload {
		return reloadIfActive(ctx, env, d)
	}
	return nil
}

// ufwEffect reports whether undoing e runs ufw for a rule, a default or the
// logging level, which a running UFW loads completely only on a reload.
func ufwEffect(e core.Effect) bool {
	noun, _, err := splitResource(e.Resource)
	return err == nil && (noun == nounRule || noun == nounDefault || noun == nounLogging)
}

// reloadIfActive runs "ufw reload" when the configuration says UFW is
// active; on an inactive UFW it would only print that it skips.
func reloadIfActive(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, d deps) error {
	cfg, err := d.readConfig(d.root)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if !cfg.Enabled {
		return nil
	}
	return ufw(ctx, env, transitionArgs(fwstate.TransReload))
}

// finishRestore finishes a restore of snap that a crash cut off. With an
// effect unresolved, only the connectivity exception restores whole, so
// the finished restore is that exception's and returns Override.
func finishRestore(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, d deps, snap snapshot, blocked, made []core.Effect) (core.RevertOutcome, error) {
	rep, err := restore(ctx, env, d, snap)
	if err != nil {
		pin(ctx, env, snap.ID)
		return core.RevertOutcome{}, fmt.Errorf("firewall: finish the interrupted restore of snapshot %s: %w", snap.ID, err)
	}
	logVanished(env, rep.Vanished)
	out := undoneOutcomes(made, nil)
	if len(blocked) == 0 {
		return core.RevertOutcome{Effects: out}, nil
	}
	pin(ctx, env, snap.ID)
	detail := overrideDetail{At: env.Clock.Now().UTC(), Snapshot: snap.ID, Guard: "an interrupted emergency restore was finished", Vanished: rep.Vanished}
	for _, e := range blocked {
		out = append(out, core.EffectOutcome{Seq: e.Seq, State: core.EffectUnresolved, Reason: e.Reason})
		detail.Effects = append(detail.Effects, effectOverwrite{Seq: e.Seq, Resource: e.Resource})
	}
	slices.SortFunc(out, func(a, b core.EffectOutcome) int { return a.Seq - b.Seq })
	return core.RevertOutcome{Effects: out, Override: true, Detail: mustJSON(detail)}, nil
}

// emergencyRestore is the connectivity exception (spec 2.5 step 4): the
// lockout guard failed on the state the revert left, so the snapshot is
// restored whole over unresolved effects, conflicts and manual edits. It
// settles nothing: each unresolved effect and conflict is reported
// unresolved with what the restore overwrote; the other made effects are
// undone.
func emergencyRestore(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, d deps, snap snapshot, why string, blocked, made []core.Effect,
	conflicts map[int]core.EffectOutcome, writeErr error) (core.RevertOutcome, error) {
	if why == "" {
		why = "the lockout guard failed"
	}
	detail := overrideDetail{At: env.Clock.Now().UTC(), Snapshot: snap.ID, Guard: why}
	var out []core.EffectOutcome
	for _, e := range blocked {
		o := core.EffectOutcome{Seq: e.Seq, State: core.EffectUnresolved, Reason: e.Reason}
		ow := effectOverwrite{Seq: e.Seq, Resource: e.Resource}
		if obs, err := observe(ctx, env, d, e); err == nil {
			cur := obs.Current
			o.Current, ow.Was = &cur, cur.State
		}
		out = append(out, o)
		detail.Effects = append(detail.Effects, ow)
	}
	for _, e := range made {
		c, ok := conflicts[e.Seq]
		if !ok {
			out = append(out, core.EffectOutcome{Seq: e.Seq, State: core.EffectUndone})
			continue
		}
		out = append(out, c)
		ow := effectOverwrite{Seq: e.Seq, Resource: e.Resource}
		if c.Current != nil {
			ow.Was = c.Current.State
		}
		detail.Effects = append(detail.Effects, ow)
	}
	slices.SortFunc(out, func(a, b core.EffectOutcome) int { return a.Seq - b.Seq })
	slices.SortFunc(detail.Effects, func(a, b effectOverwrite) int { return a.Seq - b.Seq })

	beforeFiles := map[string]string{}
	if cfg, err := d.readConfig(d.root); err == nil {
		beforeFiles = fileHashes(cfg.Files)
	}
	beforeLoaded, beforeErr := d.readLoaded(ctx, env)
	rep, err := restore(ctx, env, d, snap)
	if err != nil {
		return core.RevertOutcome{}, fmt.Errorf("firewall: the lockout guard failed (%s) and the emergency restore of snapshot %s failed: %w",
			why, snap.ID, errors.Join(err, writeErr))
	}
	detail.Vanished = rep.Vanished
	logVanished(env, rep.Vanished)
	for _, e := range snap.Entries {
		if was, now := beforeFiles[e.Path], fileHash(e); was != now {
			detail.Files = append(detail.Files, fileOverwrite{Path: e.Path, Was: was, Now: now})
		}
	}
	if afterLoaded, err := d.readLoaded(ctx, env); err == nil && beforeErr == nil {
		for _, df := range d.compare(beforeLoaded, afterLoaded, restoreKeep) {
			detail.Chains = append(detail.Chains, chainOverwrite{Family: df.Family, Table: df.Table, Chain: df.Chain,
				PolicyWas: df.PolicyA, PolicyNow: df.PolicyB, Removed: df.OnlyA, Added: df.OnlyB, Reordered: df.OrderDiffers})
		}
	}
	return core.RevertOutcome{Effects: out, Override: true, Detail: mustJSON(detail)}, nil
}

// pin pins a snapshot whose change will need repair. A failure is only
// logged: retention also keeps the snapshot of every change in
// needs_repair.
func pin(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, id string) {
	if err := setPinned(ctx, env.DB, id, true); err != nil {
		env.Log.Warn("firewall: cannot pin the snapshot of a change that needs repair", "snapshot", id, "error", err)
	}
}

func logVanished(env core.Env, keys []string) {
	if len(keys) > 0 {
		env.Log.Warn("firewall: the restore skipped the sysctl keys of interfaces that have gone", "change", env.ChangeID, "keys", keys)
	}
}

// unpinChangeSnapshot unpins the snapshot of changeID; the repair that
// ends that change's needs_repair calls it when it completes.
func unpinChangeSnapshot(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, changeID string) error {
	id, err := snapshotOfChange(ctx, env.DB, changeID)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return setPinned(ctx, env.DB, id, false)
}
```

```go
func wrSameFunc(t *testing.T, name string, got, want any) {

// TestProductionFW: the module's production functions are the readers,
// predictor, comparison and guard of the firewall's packages, rooted at /.

	if f.d.root != "/" {
		t.Errorf("root = %q, want /", f.d.root)

	wrSameFunc(t, "ipv6Refusal", f.ipv6Refusal, predict.IPv6Refusal)
	wrSameFunc(t, "check", f.check, guard.Check)
}

// TestLockoutVia: the revert's guard evaluates the snapshot's guard
// context with the real evaluator and no apply-time refresh, and answers
// the guard's verdict and message; a check that fails is an error.
func TestLockoutVia(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	gc := &core.GuardContext{Complete: true}
	st := fwstate.Loaded{Variant: "nft"}
	var got []guard.Input
	answer := core.Guard{ID: guard.GuardID, OK: false, Message: "the change would cut ssh from 203.0.113.7 to 192.0.2.1:22 on eth0: drop"}
	var answerErr error
	lockout := lockoutVia(func(_ context.Context, _ core.Env, s fwstate.Loaded, in guard.Input) (core.Guard, []guard.FlowResult, error) {
		if s.Variant != "nft" {
			t.Errorf("state %+v, want the state passed in", s)
		}
		got = append(got, in)
		return answer, nil, answerErr
	})

	ok, detail, err := lockout(ctx, core.Env{}, st, gc)
	if ok || detail != answer.Message || err != nil {
		t.Errorf("lockout = %v, %q, %v; want false, %q, nil", ok, detail, err, answer.Message)
	}
	if len(got) != 1 || got[0].Plan != gc || got[0].Refresh != nil || got[0].Retired != nil {
		t.Fatalf("inputs %+v, want one with Plan the snapshot's context and no refresh", got)
	}
	wrSameFunc(t, "Eval", got[0].Eval, eval.Evaluate)

	answer = core.Guard{ID: guard.GuardID, OK: true, Message: "every protected flow passes (3 checked)"}
	if ok, detail, err := lockout(ctx, core.Env{}, st, nil); !ok || detail != answer.Message || err != nil {
		t.Errorf("lockout = %v, %q, %v; want true, %q, nil", ok, detail, err, answer.Message)
	}

	answerErr = errors.New("firewall: read the socket table: netstat: no socket tables under the proc root")
	if ok, _, err := lockout(ctx, core.Env{}, st, gc); ok || !errors.Is(err, answerErr) {
		t.Errorf("lockout = %v, %v; want false and the check's error", ok, err)
	}
}
```

```go
package firewall

import (
	"context"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/conf"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/eval"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/guard"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/loaded"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/predict"
)

// checkFunc runs the lockout guard on st: guard.Check, or a test's stand-in.
type checkFunc func(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, st fwstate.Loaded, in guard.Input) (core.Guard, []guard.FlowResult, error)

// fw is everything the firewall's handlers use: the host-facing functions
// of deps and, for plans, the IPV6=no refusal and the lockout guard.
type fw struct {
	d           deps
	ipv6Refusal func(cfg fwstate.Config, cur fwstate.Loaded, tr fwstate.Transition) error
	check       checkFunc
}

// productionFW is the firewall over this host.
func productionFW() fw {
	return fw{
		d: deps{
			root:       "/",
			readConfig: conf.Read,
			readLoaded: loaded.Reader{}.Read,
			predict:    predict.Predict,
			edit:       predict.Edit,
			files:      predict.Files,
			compare:    loaded.Compare,
			sysctl:     loaded.PredictSysctl,
			lockout:    lockoutVia(guard.Check),
		},
		ipv6Refusal: predict.IPv6Refusal,
		check:       guard.Check,
	}
}

// lockoutVia is the lockout guard of a revert's connectivity exception
// (deps.lockout): check evaluates, with the real evaluator, the flows of
// the snapshot's guard context and of the host's live facts. A revert has
// no apply-time refresh and no retired exposure.
func lockoutVia(check checkFunc) func(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, st fwstate.Loaded, gc *core.GuardContext) (bool, string, error) {
	return func(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, st fwstate.Loaded, gc *core.GuardContext) (bool, string, error) {
		g, _, err := check(ctx, env, st, guard.Input{Plan: gc, Eval: eval.Evaluate})
		if err != nil {
			return false, "", err
		}
		return g.OK, g.Message, nil
	}
}
```

```go
package firewall

import (
	"reflect"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/model"
)

// dgRule80v4 is a Darkpanel IPv4 rule tagged 01J00000000000000000000002
// with the label "web".
const dgRule80v4 = "### tuple ### allow tcp 80 0.0.0.0/0 any 0.0.0.0/0 in comment=6461726b70616e656c3a30314a303030303030303030303030303030303030303030303220776562"

// dgRuleRaw is a manual rule the model cannot express (UFW keeps the IPv6
// host bits of 2001:db8::1/32).
const dgRuleRaw = "### tuple ### deny any any ::/0 any 2001:db8::1/32 in"

func dgLogical(t *testing.T, h *fakeHost, s fhState, sysctl map[string]string) logical {
	t.Helper()
	h.setState(s)
	return logical{cfg: h.config(), sysctl: sysctl}
}

// TestStateDiff: every change from one logical state to another is a line
// (R39): the UFW state, each removed and added rule with manual rules
// marked, a reordering, each default policy, the logging level, IPv6 and
// each sysctl value; no change is no line.
func TestStateDiff(t *testing.T) {
	h := newFakeHost(t)
	base := h.state()
	a := dgLogical(t, h, base, map[string]string{"net/ipv4/ip_forward": "0", "net/ipv4/conf/eth0/rp_filter": "1"})
	if got := stateDiff(a, a); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("diff of a state with itself = %+v, want none", got)
	}

	next := base
	next.Enabled, next.IPv6, next.LogLevel, next.Input, next.Forward = false, false, "medium", "ACCEPT", "REJECT"
	next.Rules4 = []string{fhRule3000v4, fhRule22v4, dgRule80v4}
	b := dgLogical(t, h, next, map[string]string{"net/ipv4/ip_forward": "1", "net/ipv6/conf/all/forwarding": "0"})
	want := []core.DiffLine{
		{Op: "-", Text: "UFW enabled"},
		{Op: "+", Text: "UFW disabled"},
		{Op: "+", Text: `rule 01J00000000000000000000002: allow in proto tcp from 0.0.0.0/0 to 0.0.0.0/0 port 80 comment "web"`},
		{Op: " ", Text: "rules reordered: manual-" + manualOf(t, a, 1) + ", 01J00000000000000000000001"},
		{Op: "-", Text: "default incoming DROP"},
		{Op: "+", Text: "default incoming ACCEPT"},
		{Op: "-", Text: "default routed DROP"},
		{Op: "+", Text: "default routed REJECT"},
		{Op: "-", Text: "logging low"},
		{Op: "+", Text: "logging medium"},
		{Op: "-", Text: "IPV6 yes"},
		{Op: "+", Text: "IPV6 no"},
		{Op: "-", Text: "sysctl net/ipv4/conf/eth0/rp_filter=1"},
		{Op: "-", Text: "sysctl net/ipv4/ip_forward=0"},
		{Op: "+", Text: "sysctl net/ipv4/ip_forward=1"},
		{Op: "+", Text: "sysctl net/ipv6/conf/all/forwarding=0"},
	}
	got := stateDiff(a, b)
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("diff\n%+v\nwant\n%+v", got, want)
	}
}

// manualOf returns the hex digits of the id of a's rule i, which must be a
// manual rule.
func manualOf(t *testing.T, a logical, i int) string {
	t.Helper()
	r := model.Merge(a.cfg.Rules4, a.cfg.Rules6)[i]
	if r.Origin != model.OriginManual {
		t.Fatalf("rule %d is %s", i, r.Origin)
	}
	return r.ID[len("manual-"):]
}

// TestStateDiffManual: manual rules are marked and listed by
// manualChanges; an unrepresentable one shows its raw tuple; a new rule of
// a plan shows as new.
func TestStateDiffManual(t *testing.T) {
	h := newFakeHost(t)
	base := h.state()
	a := dgLogical(t, h, base, nil)
	next := base
	next.Rules4 = []string{fhRule22v4}
	next.Rules6 = []string{fhRule22v6, dgRuleRaw}
	b := dgLogical(t, h, next, nil)
	manual := model.Merge(a.cfg.Rules4, a.cfg.Rules6)[1]
	raw := model.Merge(b.cfg.Rules4, b.cfg.Rules6)[1]
	want := []core.DiffLine{
		{Op: "-", Text: "rule " + manual.ID + " (manual): allow in proto tcp from 10.0.0.0/8 to 0.0.0.0/0 port 3000"},
		{Op: "+", Text: "rule " + raw.ID + " (manual, read-only): " + dgRuleRaw},
	}
	if got := stateDiff(a, b); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("diff\n%+v\nwant\n%+v", got, want)
	}
	if got := manualChanges(a, b); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, []string{manual.ID, raw.ID}) {
		t.Errorf("manualChanges = %v, want %v", got, []string{manual.ID, raw.ID})
	}
	if got := manualChanges(a, a); got != nil {
		t.Errorf("manualChanges of no change = %v", got)
	}

	r := model.Rule{ID: planRuleID, Action: model.ActionDeny, Direction: model.DirIn, Proto: model.ProtoUDP, From: "2001:db8::/32",
		To: model.Any, ToPort: "5000:5100", Family: model.FamilyV6, Comment: "lab"}
	if got, want := ruleText(r), `rule new: deny in proto udp from 2001:db8::/32 to ::/0 port 5000:5100 comment "lab"`; got != want {
		t.Errorf("ruleText = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the implementation**

Create `internal/modules/firewall/diff.go`:

```go
package firewall

import (
	"maps"
	"slices"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/model"
)

// planRuleID is the id a new rule carries in a plan, which has no change
// yet; Apply gives the rule its change's id (a ULID).
const planRuleID = "00000000000000000000000000"

// logical is the logical state a diff compares: UFW's configured state and
// the supported sysctl values.
type logical struct {
	cfg    fwstate.Config
	sysctl map[string]string
}

// stateDiff lists every change from a to b (R39), each as a "-" line for
// the old value and a "+" line for the new one: UFW's state; every rule
// removed (in a's order) and added (in b's order), a manual rule marked,
// and a reordering of the rules both hold; each default policy; the
// logging level; IPV6; and each sysctl value. Equal states give no line.
func stateDiff(a, b logical) []core.DiffLine {
	var out []core.DiffLine
	pair := func(old, now string) {
		if old != now {
			out = append(out, core.DiffLine{Op: "-", Text: old}, core.DiffLine{Op: "+", Text: now})
		}
	}
	pair(enabledText(a.cfg.Enabled), enabledText(b.cfg.Enabled))

	ra, rb := model.Merge(a.cfg.Rules4, a.cfg.Rules6), model.Merge(b.cfg.Rules4, b.cfg.Rules6)
	inA, inB := ruleTexts(ra), ruleTexts(rb)
	var keptA, keptB []string
	for _, r := range ra {
		if t := ruleText(r); inB[t] {
			keptA = append(keptA, r.ID)
		} else {
			out = append(out, core.DiffLine{Op: "-", Text: t})
		}
	}
	for _, r := range rb {
		if t := ruleText(r); inA[t] {
			keptB = append(keptB, r.ID)
		} else {
			out = append(out, core.DiffLine{Op: "+", Text: t})
		}
	}
	if !slices.Equal(keptA, keptB) {
		out = append(out, core.DiffLine{Op: " ", Text: "rules reordered: " + strings.Join(keptB, ", ")})
	}

	pair("default incoming "+a.cfg.DefaultInput, "default incoming "+b.cfg.DefaultInput)
	pair("default outgoing "+a.cfg.DefaultOutput, "default outgoing "+b.cfg.DefaultOutput)
	pair("default routed "+a.cfg.DefaultForward, "default routed "+b.cfg.DefaultForward)
	pair("logging "+a.cfg.LogLevel, "logging "+b.cfg.LogLevel)
	pair("IPV6 "+yesNo(a.cfg.IPv6), "IPV6 "+yesNo(b.cfg.IPv6))

	keys := slices.Collect(maps.Keys(a.sysctl))
	for k := range b.sysctl {
		if _, ok := a.sysctl[k]; !ok {
			keys = append(keys, k)
		}
	}
	slices.Sort(keys)
	for _, k := range keys {
		va, inA := a.sysctl[k]
		vb, inB := b.sysctl[k]
		if inA && inB && va == vb {
			continue
		}
		if inA {
			out = append(out, core.DiffLine{Op: "-", Text: "sysctl " + k + "=" + va})
		}
		if inB {
			out = append(out, core.DiffLine{Op: "+", Text: "sysctl " + k + "=" + vb})
		}
	}
	return out
}

// manualChanges returns the ids of the manual rules a change from a to b
// removes or adds (spec 2.2: they need manual: true), in stateDiff's order.
func manualChanges(a, b logical) []string {
	ra, rb := model.Merge(a.cfg.Rules4, a.cfg.Rules6), model.Merge(b.cfg.Rules4, b.cfg.Rules6)
	inA, inB := ruleTexts(ra), ruleTexts(rb)
	var out []string
	for _, f := range []struct {
		rules []model.Rule
		other map[string]bool
	}{{ra, inB}, {rb, inA}} {
		for _, r := range f.rules {
			if r.Origin == model.OriginManual && !f.other[ruleText(r)] {
				out = append(out, r.ID)
			}
		}
	}
	return out
}

func ruleTexts(rules []model.Rule) map[string]bool {
	out := make(map[string]bool, len(rules))
	for _, r := range rules {
		out[ruleText(r)] = true
	}
	return out
}

// ruleText describes a rule for a diff: its id, a manual rule marked, and
// the ufw rule without the comment argument followed by its label or
// comment; a manual rule the model cannot express shows its raw tuple.
func ruleText(r model.Rule) string {
	id := r.ID
	if id == planRuleID {
		id = "new"
	}
	if r.Raw != "" {
		return "rule " + id + " (manual, read-only): " + r.Raw
	}
	args := model.AddArgs(r)
	if n := len(args); n >= 2 && args[n-2] == "comment" {
		args = args[:n-2]
	}
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString("rule " + id)
	if r.Origin == model.OriginManual {
		b.WriteString(" (manual)")
	}
	b.WriteString(": " + strings.Join(args, " "))
	if r.Comment != "" {
		b.WriteString(" comment " + strconv.Quote(r.Comment))
	}
	return b.String()
}

func enabledText(enabled bool) string {
	if enabled {
		return "UFW enabled"
	}
	return "UFW disabled"
}

func yesNo(v bool) string {
	if v {
		return "yes"
	}
	return "no"
}
```
