```go
package firewall

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io/fs"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/guard"
)

// The declaration every mutating firewall action shares (section 5).
const (
	lockKey      = ID
	repairAction = ID + ".state.repair"
	// applyTimeout bounds apply and verify: a batch runs ufw once per
	// rule and then reloads UFW, each run taking up to seconds.
	applyTimeout = 45 * time.Second
)

// ChangeOutput is the output of every mutating firewall action (v1).
type ChangeOutput struct {
	Snapshot      string   `json:"snapshot"`                // the logical snapshot taken before the change
	Rules         []string `json:"rules,omitempty"`         // the ids of the Darkpanel rules the change added
	RepairOutcome string   `json:"repairOutcome,omitempty"` // firewall.state.repair of a change: restored or kept
}

// mutation is the handler of one mutating firewall action (spec 2.3-2.5):
// Plan and Apply share the plan pipeline, Verify compares the loaded state
// with the configuration's prediction, and Snapshot, Revert and Observe are
// the snapshot part's.
type mutation[In any] struct {
	f fw
	// image makes the snapshot hold a loaded-state before-image
	// (firewall.state.repair, spec 2.3).
	image   bool
	guarded func(in In) core.Guarded
	manual  func(in In) bool // nil: never
	build   func(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, in In) buildFunc
	// check is the action's own verify on the configuration after the
	// change, run before the comparison; nil means none.
	check func(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, in In, cfg fwstate.Config) error
	// finish fills the action's own output fields after a successful
	// apply; nil means none.
	finish func(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, in In, out *ChangeOutput) error
}

// defineMutation declares a mutating firewall action from spec's Name,
// Summary and Converges: revertible, agent-side, under the firewall lock,
// repaired by firewall.state.repair, with the overridable lockout guard.
func defineMutation[In any](spec core.ActionSpec, m mutation[In]) core.ActionDef {
	spec.Version, spec.Side = 1, core.SideAgent
	spec.LockKeys, spec.RepairedBy, spec.ApplyTimeout = []string{lockKey}, repairAction, applyTimeout
	spec.Guards = []core.GuardSpec{{ID: guard.GuardID, Overridable: true}}
	return core.DefineRevertible[In, ChangeOutput](spec, m)
}

// Plan plans the change (fw.plan).
func (m mutation[In]) Plan(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, in In) (core.PlanOutcome, error) {
	req := planReq{input: in, guarded: m.guarded(in), build: m.build(ctx, env, in)}
	if m.manual != nil {
		req.manual = m.manual(in)
	}
	return m.f.plan(ctx, env, req)
}

// Snapshot captures the logical snapshot with the plan's guard context.
func (m mutation[In]) Snapshot(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, in In) ([]byte, error) {
	return capture(ctx, env, m.f.d, m.guarded(in).Guard, m.image)
}

// Apply attaches the snapshot, makes the change as journaled effects
// (fw.run) and records the post-apply file hashes.
func (m mutation[In]) Apply(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, in In) (ChangeOutput, error) {
	id, err := attach(ctx, env)
	if err != nil {
		return ChangeOutput{}, err
	}
	p, err := m.f.prepare(ctx, env, m.build(ctx, env, in))
	if err != nil {
		return ChangeOutput{}, err
	}
	if err := m.f.run(ctx, env, p); err != nil {
		return ChangeOutput{}, err
	}
	if err := recordPostHashes(ctx, env, m.f.d, id); err != nil {
		return ChangeOutput{}, err
	}
	out := ChangeOutput{Snapshot: id}
	if m.finish != nil {
		if err := m.finish(ctx, env, in, &out); err != nil {
			return ChangeOutput{}, err
		}
	}
	return out, nil
}

// Verify runs the action's own check, then compares the loaded state with
// what the configuration now predicts, over UFW's and Darkpanel's chains
// and the filter built-ins (fw.syncDiffs): a difference means UFW did not
// do what the prediction said (firewall.prediction_mismatch, which
// reverts). It reads only the host, so it also serves startup recovery.
func (m mutation[In]) Verify(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, in In, _ ChangeOutput) error {
	cfg, err := m.f.d.readConfig(m.f.d.root)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("firewall: verify: %w", err)
	}
	if m.check != nil {
		if err := m.check(ctx, env, in, cfg); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	st, err := m.f.d.readLoaded(ctx, env)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("firewall: verify: %w", err)
	}
	diffs, err := m.f.syncDiffs(cfg, st)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("firewall: verify: %w", err)
	}
	if len(diffs) > 0 {
		texts := make([]string, len(diffs))
		for i, d := range diffs {
			texts[i] = chainDiffText(d)
		}
		return errcode.New(errcode.FirewallPredictionMismatch, "the loaded state differs from the prediction: "+strings.Join(texts, "; "))
	}
	return nil
}

// Revert reverts the change from its snapshot (revert).
func (m mutation[In]) Revert(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, snapshot []byte) (core.RevertOutcome, error) {
	return revert(ctx, env, m.f.d, snapshot)
}

// Observe reads the resource of one effect (observe).
func (m mutation[In]) Observe(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, e core.Effect) (core.Observation, error) {
	return observe(ctx, env, m.f.d, e)
}

// run makes a prepared change, each step a journaled effect (spec 2.5),
// stopping at the first failure: a restore's files, the change's ufw
// commands, the transition commands, and a restore's sysctl values.
func (f fw) run(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, p prepared) error {
	if p.c.restore != nil {
		if err := f.writeRestored(ctx, env, p); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	for _, op := range p.c.ops {
		if err := runUfw(ctx, env, f.d, op); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	for _, args := range p.tg.cmds {
		if err := runUfw(ctx, env, f.d, transitionOp(args)); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	if p.c.restore != nil {
		return f.restoreSysctl(ctx, env, p.c.restore.State.Sysctl)
	}
	return nil
}

// transitionOp is the effect of a transition command: UFW's enabled state.
func transitionOp(args []string) ufwOp {
	switch {
	case slices.Equal(args, enableArgs):
		return enableOp(true)
	case slices.Equal(args, disableArgs):
		return enableOp(false)
	}
	return ufwOp{Kind: core.EffectModify, Resource: resourceEnabled, Args: args}
}

// writeRestored writes each file of a restore's snapshot that differs from
// the host's, as one effect each. Each file is written once, before any ufw
// command rewrites it, so its effect's before-state is the change's own
// snapshot's entry, which the inverse restores. When the restore changes
// UFW's enabled state, ufw.conf is written with the current ENABLED value
// (as UFW edits it), and the enable or disable that follows sets it, as a
// separate effect whose inverse sets it back.
func (f fw) writeRestored(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, p prepared) error {
	snap := p.c.restore
	for _, e := range snap.Entries {
		want := e
		if e.Path == "/etc/ufw/ufw.conf" && snap.State.Enabled != p.cfg0.Enabled {
			args := disableArgs
			if !snap.State.Enabled {
				args = enableArgs
			}
			cfg, err := f.edit(p.tg.cfgN, args)
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			want.Data = cfg.Files[e.Path].Data
		}
		cur, err := f.d.readConfig(f.d.root)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("firewall: restore %s: %w", e.Path, err)
		}
		if fileHash(cur.Files[e.Path]) == fileHash(want) {
			continue
		}
		if err := writeFileEffect(ctx, env, f.d, want); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// restoreSysctl writes back each of a snapshot's sysctl values that
// differs from the live one, as one effect each, in the order of spec 2.1
// (net.ipv4.ip_forward, all, default, each interface). A key that no
// longer exists belongs to an interface that has gone and is skipped.
func (f fw) restoreSysctl(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, want map[string]string) error {
	keys := make([]string, 0, len(want))
	for k := range want {
		keys = append(keys, k)
	}
	slices.SortFunc(keys, func(a, b string) int {
		if ra, rb := sysctlRank(a), sysctlRank(b); ra != rb {
			return ra - rb
		}
		return strings.Compare(a, b)
	})
	for _, k := range keys {
		live, err := env.Files.ReadSysctl(ctx, ID, k)
		switch {
		case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist):
			continue
		case err != nil:
			return fmt.Errorf("firewall: read sysctl %s: %w", k, err)
		case live == want[k]:
			continue
		}
		if err := writeSysctlEffect(ctx, env, f.d, k, want[k]); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	return nil
}
```

```go
package firewall

import (

)

// acHost is a fake host whose ufw sets the enabled state, the defaults and
// the logging level.
func acHost(t *testing.T, enabled bool) (*fakeHost, fw) {
	t.Helper()
	h := newFakeHost(t)
	s := h.state()
	s.Enabled = enabled
	h.setState(s)
	if !enabled {
		h.loaded = fwstate.Loaded{Variant: "nft", V4: fhParse(t, tgStopped), V6: fhParse(t, tgStopped)}
	}
	h.ufw["--force enable"] = func(s *fhState) int { s.Enabled = true; return 0 }
	h.ufw["disable"] = func(s *fhState) int { s.Enabled = false; return 0 }
	h.ufw["reload"] = func(*fhState) int { return 0 }
	for policy, verb := range policyVerbs {
		h.ufw["default "+verb+" incoming"] = func(s *fhState) int { s.Input = policy; return 0 }
		h.ufw["default "+verb+" outgoing"] = func(s *fhState) int { s.Output = policy; return 0 }
		h.ufw["default "+verb+" routed"] = func(s *fhState) int { s.Forward = policy; return 0 }
	}
	for _, level := range []string{"off", "low", "medium", "high", "full"} {
		h.ufw["logging "+level] = func(s *fhState) int { s.LogLevel = level; return 0 }
	}
	f, _ := newFW(h)
	return h, f
}

// acRun plans, snapshots, applies and verifies def with input raw, and
// returns the plan and the ufw vectors the apply ran.
func acRun(t *testing.T, h *fakeHost, def core.ActionDef, raw string) (core.PlanOutcome, []string) {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	if err := schema.NewValidator().ValidateInput(def, json.RawMessage(raw)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("%s input %s: %v", def.Spec.Name, raw, err)
	}
	out, err := def.Handler.Plan(ctx, h.env(), json.RawMessage(raw))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("%s plan: %v", def.Spec.Name, err)
	}
	if _, err := def.Handler.Snapshot(ctx, h.env(), json.RawMessage(raw)); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	n := len(h.calls)
	res, err := def.Handler.Apply(ctx, h.env(), json.RawMessage(raw))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("%s apply: %v", def.Spec.Name, err)
	}
	if err := def.Handler.Verify(ctx, h.env(), json.RawMessage(raw), res); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("%s verify: %v", def.Spec.Name, err)
	}
	var ran []string
	for _, c := range h.calls[n:] {
		if v, ok := strings.CutPrefix(c, "run /usr/sbin/ufw "); ok {
			ran = append(ran, v)
		}
	}
	return out, ran
}

func acDiff(out core.PlanOutcome) []string {
	var d []string
	for _, l := range out.Diff {
		d = append(d, l.Op+" "+l.Text)
	}
	return d
}

// TestStateActions: enable starts an inactive UFW and disable stops an
// active one; each is a no-op when UFW is already so.
func TestStateActions(t *testing.T) {
	h, f := acHost(t, false)
	out, ran := acRun(t, h, f.stateEnable(), `{}`)
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(acDiff(out), []string{"- UFW disabled", "+ UFW enabled"}) || !reflect.DeepEqual(ran, []string{"--force enable"}) {
		t.Errorf("enable: diff %q ran %q", acDiff(out), ran)
	}
	out, ran = acRun(t, h, f.stateEnable(), `{}`)
	if len(out.Diff) != 0 || len(ran) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("enable again: diff %q ran %q, want nothing", acDiff(out), ran)
	}

	h, f = acHost(t, true)
	out, ran = acRun(t, h, f.stateDisable(), `{}`)
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(acDiff(out), []string{"- UFW enabled", "+ UFW disabled"}) || !reflect.DeepEqual(ran, []string{"disable"}) {
		t.Errorf("disable: diff %q ran %q", acDiff(out), ran)
	}
	if h.state().Enabled {
		t.Error("UFW is still enabled")
	}
}

// TestDefaultsAndLogging: the defaults and the logging level are set for
// what changes, then an active UFW reloads; nothing to change is a no-op;
// a request without any direction is refused.
func TestDefaultsAndLogging(t *testing.T) {
	h, f := acHost(t, true)
	out, ran := acRun(t, h, f.defaultsSet(), `{"incoming":"ACCEPT","outgoing":"ACCEPT","routed":"REJECT"}`)
	wantDiff := []string{"- default incoming DROP", "+ default incoming ACCEPT", "- default routed DROP", "+ default routed REJECT"}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(acDiff(out), wantDiff) || !reflect.DeepEqual(ran, []string{"default allow incoming", "default reject routed", "reload"}) {
		t.Errorf("defaults: diff %q ran %q", acDiff(out), ran)
	}
	if out, ran = acRun(t, h, f.defaultsSet(), `{"routed":"REJECT"}`); len(out.Diff) != 0 || len(ran) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("defaults again: diff %q ran %q, want nothing", acDiff(out), ran)
	}
	_, err := f.defaultsSet().Handler.Plan(context.Background(), h.env(), json.RawMessage(`{}`))
	if e := errcode.From(err); e.Code != errcode.InvalidInput || len(e.Fields) != 1 || e.Fields[0].Path != "/incoming" {
		t.Errorf("defaults without a direction = %v, want an invalid input", err)
	}
	if err := schema.NewValidator().ValidateInput(f.defaultsSet(), json.RawMessage(`{"incoming":"allow"}`)); err == nil {
		t.Error("the schema accepts the policy allow")
	}

	out, ran = acRun(t, h, f.loggingSet(), `{"level":"high"}`)
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(acDiff(out), []string{"- logging low", "+ logging high"}) || !reflect.DeepEqual(ran, []string{"logging high", "reload"}) {
		t.Errorf("logging: diff %q ran %q", acDiff(out), ran)
	}
	h, f = acHost(t, false)
	if _, ran = acRun(t, h, f.loggingSet(), `{"level":"off"}`); !reflect.DeepEqual(ran, []string{"logging off"}) {
		t.Errorf("logging on an inactive UFW ran %q, want no reload", ran)
	}
	if err := schema.NewValidator().ValidateInput(f.loggingSet(), json.RawMessage(`{"level":"on"}`)); err == nil {
		t.Error("the schema accepts the level on")
	}
}

// TestStateActionsVerify: verify fails when the configuration does not
// show what the action set.
func TestStateActionsVerify(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h, f := acHost(t, true)
	for _, c := range []struct {
		def core.ActionDef
		raw string
	}{
		{f.stateEnable(), `{}`}, {f.defaultsSet(), `{"outgoing":"DROP"}`}, {f.loggingSet(), `{"level":"full"}`},
	} {
		s := h.state()
		s.Enabled = false
		h.setState(s)
		err := c.def.Handler.Verify(ctx, h.env(), json.RawMessage(c.raw), json.RawMessage(`{"snapshot":""}`))
		if errcode.From(err).Code != errcode.FirewallPredictionMismatch {
			t.Errorf("%s verify = %v, want a prediction mismatch", c.def.Spec.Name, err)
		}
	}
	s := h.state()
	s.Enabled = true
	h.setState(s)
	if err := f.stateDisable().Handler.Verify(ctx, h.env(), json.RawMessage(`{}`), json.RawMessage(`{}`)); errcode.From(err).Code != errcode.FirewallPredictionMismatch {
		t.Errorf("disable verify = %v, want a prediction mismatch", err)
	}
}
```

```go
package firewall

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
)

// StateInput is the input of firewall.state.enable and
// firewall.state.disable (v1).
type StateInput struct {
	core.Guarded
}

// DefaultsInput is the input of firewall.defaults.set (v1): the default
// policies to set, as /etc/default/ufw spells them; an omitted direction
// keeps its policy, and at least one is set.
type DefaultsInput struct {
	core.Guarded
	Incoming string `json:"incoming,omitempty" jsonschema:"enum=ACCEPT,enum=DROP,enum=REJECT" jsonschema_description:"Default policy for incoming traffic."`
	Outgoing string `json:"outgoing,omitempty" jsonschema:"enum=ACCEPT,enum=DROP,enum=REJECT" jsonschema_description:"Default policy for outgoing traffic."`
	Routed   string `json:"routed,omitempty" jsonschema:"enum=ACCEPT,enum=DROP,enum=REJECT" jsonschema_description:"Default policy for routed (forwarded) traffic."`
}

// LoggingInput is the input of firewall.logging.set (v1).
type LoggingInput struct {
	core.Guarded
	Level string `json:"level" jsonschema:"enum=off,enum=low,enum=medium,enum=high,enum=full" jsonschema_description:"UFW's logging level."`
}

// mismatch is a verify failure: the configuration does not show what the
// change made.
func mismatch(format string, args ...any) error {
	return errcode.New(errcode.FirewallPredictionMismatch, fmt.Sprintf(format, args...))
}

// stateEnable is firewall.state.enable: start UFW (spec 2.3, transition
// enable), a no-op when it is enabled.
func (f fw) stateEnable() core.ActionDef {
	return f.stateAction("firewall.state.enable", "Enable UFW.", true)
}

// stateDisable is firewall.state.disable: stop UFW, a no-op when it is
// disabled.
func (f fw) stateDisable() core.ActionDef {
	return f.stateAction("firewall.state.disable", "Disable UFW.", false)
}

func (f fw) stateAction(name, summary string, enable bool) core.ActionDef {
	return defineMutation(core.ActionSpec{Name: name, Summary: summary}, mutation[StateInput]{
		f:       f,
		guarded: func(in StateInput) core.Guarded { return in.Guarded },
		build: func(context.Context, core.Env, StateInput) buildFunc {
			return func(fwstate.Config, fwstate.Loaded) (change, error) { return change{enable: &enable}, nil }
		},
		check: func(_ context.Context, _ core.Env, _ StateInput, cfg fwstate.Config) error {
			if cfg.Enabled != enable {
				return mismatch("UFW's ENABLED is %s after the change", yesNo(cfg.Enabled))
			}
			return nil
		},
	})
}

// defaultsSet is firewall.defaults.set: set the default policies that
// differ.
func (f fw) defaultsSet() core.ActionDef {
	dirs := func(in DefaultsInput) [][2]string {
		return [][2]string{{"incoming", in.Incoming}, {"outgoing", in.Outgoing}, {"routed", in.Routed}}
	}
	return defineMutation(core.ActionSpec{Name: "firewall.defaults.set", Summary: "Set UFW's default policies."}, mutation[DefaultsInput]{
		f:       f,
		guarded: func(in DefaultsInput) core.Guarded { return in.Guarded },
		build: func(_ context.Context, _ core.Env, in DefaultsInput) buildFunc {
			return func(cfg fwstate.Config, _ fwstate.Loaded) (change, error) {
				if in.Incoming == "" && in.Outgoing == "" && in.Routed == "" {
					return change{}, &errcode.Error{Code: errcode.InvalidInput, Detail: "set at least one default policy",
						Fields: []errcode.FieldError{{Path: "/incoming", Message: "set incoming, outgoing or routed"}}}
				}
				var c change
				for _, d := range dirs(in) {
					cur, err := policyOf(cfg, d[0])
					if err != nil {
						return change{}, err
					}
					if d[1] == "" || d[1] == cur {
						continue
					}
					op, err := defaultOp(d[0], d[1])
					if err != nil {
						return change{}, err
					}
					c.ops = append(c.ops, op)
				}
				return c, nil
			}
		},
		check: func(_ context.Context, _ core.Env, in DefaultsInput, cfg fwstate.Config) error {
			for _, d := range dirs(in) {
				if cur, err := policyOf(cfg, d[0]); err != nil || (d[1] != "" && cur != d[1]) {
					return mismatch("the default %s policy is %s after the change, not %s", d[0], cur, d[1])
				}
			}
			return nil
		},
	})
}

// loggingSet is firewall.logging.set: set UFW's logging level.
func (f fw) loggingSet() core.ActionDef {
	return defineMutation(core.ActionSpec{Name: "firewall.logging.set", Summary: "Set UFW's logging level."}, mutation[LoggingInput]{
		f:       f,
		guarded: func(in LoggingInput) core.Guarded { return in.Guarded },
		build: func(_ context.Context, _ core.Env, in LoggingInput) buildFunc {
			return func(cfg fwstate.Config, _ fwstate.Loaded) (change, error) {
				if cfg.LogLevel == in.Level {
					return change{}, nil
				}
				op, err := loggingOp(in.Level)
				if err != nil {
					return change{}, errcode.New(errcode.InvalidInput, err.Error())
				}
				return change{ops: []ufwOp{op}}, nil
			}
		},
		check: func(_ context.Context, _ core.Env, in LoggingInput, cfg fwstate.Config) error {
			if cfg.LogLevel != in.Level {
				return mismatch("the logging level is %s after the change, not %s", cfg.LogLevel, in.Level)
			}
			return nil
		},
	})
}
```

**Lenses:** security

`firewall.rule.add` takes one rule without an id and tags it with its change's id (a ULID; the plan shows `rule new`), refusing a rule with an id, a manual rule, one outside UFW's grammar and one UFW would skip as a duplicate; `firewall.rule.delete` deletes by id, a manual rule only with `manual: true`, and refuses an unknown id and an unrepresentable rule. Field errors carry the input's JSON pointers.

```go
package firewall

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/hex"
	"encoding/json"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/schema"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/model"
)

// ruChange is the change id of the rule tests; rule.add gives the new rule
// this id.
const ruChange = "01J00000000000000000000077"

// ruTuple is the IPv4 tuple UFW writes for an incoming TCP rule to port
// with the given comment.
func ruTuple(port, comment string) string {
	return "### tuple ### allow tcp " + port + " 0.0.0.0/0 any 0.0.0.0/0 in comment=" + hex.EncodeToString([]byte(comment))
}

// ruHost is a fake host whose ufw adds the rule for port 8080 (as change
// ruChange or in a plan) and deletes its rules.
func ruHost(t *testing.T) (*fakeHost, fw, core.Env) {
	t.Helper()
	h := newFakeHost(t)
	h.ufw["reload"] = func(*fhState) int { return 0 }
	for _, id := range []string{ruChange, planRuleID} {
		r := model.Rule{ID: id, Action: model.ActionAllow, Direction: model.DirIn, Proto: model.ProtoTCP, From: model.Any,
			To: model.Any, ToPort: "8080", Family: model.FamilyV4, Comment: "web"}
		h.ufw[strings.Join(model.AddArgs(r), " ")] = func(s *fhState) int {
			s.Rules4 = append(s.Rules4, ruTuple("8080", model.Tag(id, "web")))
			return 0
		}
	}
	h.ufw["delete allow in proto tcp from any to any port 22"] = func(s *fhState) int {
		s.Rules4, s.Rules6 = ruWithout(s.Rules4, fhRule22v4), ruWithout(s.Rules6, fhRule22v6)
		return 0
	}
	h.ufw["delete allow in proto tcp from 10.0.0.0/8 to 0.0.0.0/0 port 3000"] = func(s *fhState) int {
		s.Rules4 = ruWithout(s.Rules4, fhRule3000v4)
		return 0
	}
	f, _ := newFW(h)
	env := h.env()
	env.ChangeID = ruChange
	return h, f, env
}

func ruWithout(lines []string, line string) []string {
	var out []string
	for _, l := range lines {
		if l != line {
			out = append(out, l)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// ruApply plans (without a change id, as the engine does), snapshots,
// applies and verifies def under env.
func ruApply(t *testing.T, env core.Env, def core.ActionDef, raw string) (core.PlanOutcome, ChangeOutput) {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	if err := schema.NewValidator().ValidateInput(def, json.RawMessage(raw)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("input %s: %v", raw, err)
	}
	planEnv := env
	planEnv.ChangeID = ""
	plan, err := def.Handler.Plan(ctx, planEnv, json.RawMessage(raw))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("plan: %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := def.Handler.Snapshot(ctx, env, json.RawMessage(raw)); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	res, err := def.Handler.Apply(ctx, env, json.RawMessage(raw))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("apply: %v", err)
	}
	if err := def.Handler.Verify(ctx, env, json.RawMessage(raw), res); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("verify: %v", err)
	}
	var out ChangeOutput
	if err := json.Unmarshal(res, &out); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return plan, out
}

// TestRuleAdd: the new rule gets its change's id as its tag; the plan shows
// it as new.
func TestRuleAdd(t *testing.T) {
	h, f, env := ruHost(t)
	raw := `{"rule":{"action":"allow","direction":"in","proto":"tcp","from":"any","to":"any","toPort":"8080","family":"v4","comment":"web"}}`
	plan, out := ruApply(t, env, f.ruleAdd(), raw)
	if want := []string{"+ rule new: allow in proto tcp from 0.0.0.0/0 to 0.0.0.0/0 port 8080 comment \"web\""}; !reflect.DeepEqual(acDiff(plan), want) {
		t.Errorf("diff %q, want %q", acDiff(plan), want)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(out.Rules, []string{ruChange}) || out.Snapshot == "" {
		t.Errorf("output %+v, want the new rule's id", out)
	}
	if rules := findRules(h.config(), ruChange); len(rules) != 1 || rules[0].Rule.Comment != "web" || rules[0].Rule.Origin != model.OriginDarkpanel {
		t.Errorf("rules %+v, want the tagged rule", rules)
	}
	s := h.state()
	s.Rules4 = s.Rules4[:2]
	h.setState(s)
	if err := f.ruleAdd().Handler.Verify(context.Background(), env, json.RawMessage(raw), json.RawMessage(`{}`)); errcode.From(err).Code != errcode.FirewallPredictionMismatch {
		t.Errorf("verify without the rule = %v, want a prediction mismatch", err)
	}
}

// TestRuleAddRefuses: a rule with an id, a manual rule, one outside UFW's
// grammar and one UFW already holds are refused.
func TestRuleAddRefuses(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h, f, env := ruHost(t)
	env.ChangeID = ""
	h.ufw["allow in proto tcp from any to any port 22 comment darkpanel:"+planRuleID] = func(*fhState) int { return 0 }
	for _, c := range []struct {
		raw, path string
	}{
		{`{"rule":{"id":"01J00000000000000000000005","action":"allow","direction":"in","proto":"tcp","from":"any","to":"any","toPort":"80","family":"v4"}}`, "/rule/id"},
		{`{"rule":{"action":"allow","direction":"in","proto":"tcp","from":"any","to":"any","toPort":"80","family":"v4","origin":"manual"}}`, "/rule/origin"},
		{`{"rule":{"action":"limit","direction":"out","proto":"tcp","from":"any","to":"any","toPort":"80","family":"v4"}}`, "/rule/action"},
		{`{"rule":{"action":"allow","direction":"in","proto":"tcp","from":"any","to":"any","toPort":"22","family":"both"}}`, "/rule"},
	} {
		_, err := f.ruleAdd().Handler.Plan(ctx, env, json.RawMessage(c.raw))
		e := errcode.From(err)
		if e.Code != errcode.InvalidInput || len(e.Fields) == 0 || e.Fields[0].Path != c.path {
			t.Errorf("plan %s = %v, want an invalid input at %s", c.raw, err, c.path)
		}
		if c.path == "/rule" && !strings.Contains(e.Detail, "already holds") {
			t.Errorf("plan %s = %v, want the duplicate refused", c.raw, err)
		}
	}
}

// TestRuleDelete: a Darkpanel rule is deleted by id; a manual rule needs
// manual: true; an unknown id and a rule outside the model are refused.
func TestRuleDelete(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h, f, env := ruHost(t)
	plan, out := ruApply(t, env, f.ruleDelete(), `{"id":"`+fhTag+`"}`)
	if len(plan.Diff) != 1 || plan.Diff[0].Op != "-" || !strings.Contains(plan.Diff[0].Text, fhTag) || len(out.Rules) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("diff %q output %+v, want the rule's removal", acDiff(plan), out)
	}
	if len(findRules(h.config(), fhTag)) != 0 {
		t.Error("the rule is still there")
	}

	manual := model.Merge(h.config().Rules4, nil)[0].ID
	_, err := f.ruleDelete().Handler.Plan(ctx, env, json.RawMessage(`{"id":"`+manual+`"}`))
	if errcode.From(err).Code != errcode.FirewallManualRequired {
		t.Errorf("deleting a manual rule = %v, want manual required", err)
	}
	if plan, _ := ruApply(t, env, f.ruleDelete(), `{"id":"`+manual+`","manual":true}`); !strings.Contains(acDiff(plan)[0], "(manual)") {
		t.Errorf("diff %q, want the manual rule marked", acDiff(plan))
	}

	h, f, env = ruHost(t)
	s := h.state()
	s.Rules6 = append(s.Rules6, suRuleRaw)
	h.setState(s)
	raw := model.Merge(nil, []model.Tuple{h.config().Rules6[1]})[0].ID
	for _, id := range []string{"01J00000000000000000000099", raw} {
		_, err := f.ruleDelete().Handler.Plan(ctx, env, json.RawMessage(`{"id":"`+id+`","manual":true}`))
		if e := errcode.From(err); e.Code != errcode.InvalidInput || len(e.Fields) != 1 || e.Fields[0].Path != "/id" {
			t.Errorf("deleting %s = %v, want an invalid input at /id", id, err)
		}
	}
	if err := f.ruleDelete().Handler.Verify(ctx, env, json.RawMessage(`{"id":"`+fhTag+`"}`), json.RawMessage(`{}`)); errcode.From(err).Code != errcode.FirewallPredictionMismatch {
		t.Errorf("verify with the rule present = %v, want a prediction mismatch", err)
	}
}
```

```go
package firewall

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/model"
)

// RuleAddInput is the input of firewall.rule.add (v1): one rule without an
// id; the action tags it with its change's id.
type RuleAddInput struct {
	core.Guarded
	Rule model.Rule `json:"rule"`
}

// RuleDeleteInput is the input of firewall.rule.delete (v1).
type RuleDeleteInput struct {
	core.Guarded
	ID     string `json:"id" jsonschema:"pattern=^([0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}|manual-[0-9a-f]{16})$" jsonschema_description:"The rule's id, as firewall.status lists it."`
	Manual bool   `json:"manual,omitempty" jsonschema_description:"Confirms deleting a manual rule (spec 2.2)."`
}

// changeRuleID is the id rule.add gives its rule: the change's id, a ULID
// unique to the change; a plan, which has no change yet, uses planRuleID.
func changeRuleID(env core.Env) string {
	if env.ChangeID != "" {
		return env.ChangeID
	}
	return planRuleID
}

// fieldErrors prefixes the field paths of an invalid-input error.
func fieldErrors(err error, prefix string) error {
	var e *errcode.Error
	if !errors.As(err, &e) || e.Code != errcode.InvalidInput {
		return err
	}
	out := &errcode.Error{Code: e.Code, Detail: e.Detail}
	for _, fe := range e.Fields {
		out.Fields = append(out.Fields, errcode.FieldError{Path: prefix + fe.Path, Message: fe.Message})
	}
	return out
}

// newRule validates a rule a caller asks Darkpanel to add (spec 2.2): it
// carries no id, which the caller supplies, and is Darkpanel's; field
// paths start with path.
func newRule(r model.Rule, id, path string) (model.Rule, error) {
	var fields []errcode.FieldError
	if r.ID != "" {
		fields = append(fields, errcode.FieldError{Path: path + "/id", Message: "Darkpanel assigns the id"})
	}
	if r.Origin == model.OriginManual {
		fields = append(fields, errcode.FieldError{Path: path + "/origin", Message: "a rule Darkpanel adds is Darkpanel's"})
	}
	if len(fields) > 0 {
		return model.Rule{}, &errcode.Error{Code: errcode.InvalidInput, Detail: "the rule is not a new Darkpanel rule", Fields: fields}
	}
	r = r.Normalize()
	r.ID, r.Origin = id, model.OriginDarkpanel
	if err := r.Validate(); err != nil {
		return model.Rule{}, fieldErrors(err, path)
	}
	return r, nil
}

// addOp is the effect that adds r to cfg, with the configuration it
// leads to. UFW skips a rule it already holds under another comment, so a
// rule the prediction does not add is refused.
func (f fw) addOp(cfg fwstate.Config, r model.Rule, path string) (ufwOp, fwstate.Config, error) {
	op, err := addRuleOp(r)
	if err != nil {
		return ufwOp{}, fwstate.Config{}, err
	}
	next, err := f.d.edit(cfg, op.Args)
	if err != nil {
		return ufwOp{}, fwstate.Config{}, &errcode.Error{Code: errcode.InvalidInput, Detail: "UFW cannot add the rule: " + err.Error(),
			Fields: []errcode.FieldError{{Path: path, Message: err.Error()}}}
	}
	if len(findRules(next, r.ID)) == 0 {
		return ufwOp{}, fwstate.Config{}, &errcode.Error{Code: errcode.InvalidInput, Detail: "UFW already holds this rule",
			Fields: []errcode.FieldError{{Path: path, Message: "UFW already holds this rule under another comment"}}}
	}
	return op, next, nil
}

// ruleAdd is firewall.rule.add.
func (f fw) ruleAdd() core.ActionDef {
	return defineMutation(core.ActionSpec{Name: "firewall.rule.add", Summary: "Add a firewall rule."}, mutation[RuleAddInput]{
		f:       f,
		guarded: func(in RuleAddInput) core.Guarded { return in.Guarded },
		build: func(_ context.Context, env core.Env, in RuleAddInput) buildFunc {
			return func(cfg fwstate.Config, _ fwstate.Loaded) (change, error) {
				r, err := newRule(in.Rule, changeRuleID(env), "/rule")
				if err != nil {
					return change{}, err
				}
				op, _, err := f.addOp(cfg, r, "/rule")
				if err != nil {
					return change{}, err
				}
				return change{ops: []ufwOp{op}}, nil
			}
		},
		check: func(_ context.Context, env core.Env, _ RuleAddInput, cfg fwstate.Config) error {
			if n := len(findRules(cfg, env.ChangeID)); n != 1 {
				return mismatch("%d rules carry the tag %s after the change, not 1", n, env.ChangeID)
			}
			return nil
		},
		finish: func(_ context.Context, env core.Env, _ RuleAddInput, out *ChangeOutput) error {
			out.Rules = []string{env.ChangeID}
			return nil
		},
	})
}

// deleteOp is the effect that deletes the rule with id from cfg. A manual
// rule outside the model is kept by every operation (spec 2.2).
func deleteOp(cfg fwstate.Config, id, path string) (ufwOp, error) {
	refuse := func(msg string) error {
		return &errcode.Error{Code: errcode.InvalidInput, Detail: msg, Fields: []errcode.FieldError{{Path: path, Message: msg}}}
	}
	groups := findRules(cfg, id)
	switch {
	case len(groups) == 0:
		return ufwOp{}, refuse(fmt.Sprintf("no rule has the id %s", id))
	case len(groups) > 1:
		return ufwOp{}, refuse(fmt.Sprintf("%d rules carry the id %s", len(groups), id))
	case groups[0].Rule.Raw != "":
		return ufwOp{}, refuse(fmt.Sprintf("rule %s is outside the rules Darkpanel can write, so Darkpanel keeps it", id))
	}
	return deleteRuleOp(groups[0].Rule), nil
}

// ruleDelete is firewall.rule.delete.
func (f fw) ruleDelete() core.ActionDef {
	return defineMutation(core.ActionSpec{Name: "firewall.rule.delete", Summary: "Delete a firewall rule."}, mutation[RuleDeleteInput]{
		f:       f,
		guarded: func(in RuleDeleteInput) core.Guarded { return in.Guarded },
		manual:  func(in RuleDeleteInput) bool { return in.Manual },
		build: func(_ context.Context, _ core.Env, in RuleDeleteInput) buildFunc {
			return func(cfg fwstate.Config, _ fwstate.Loaded) (change, error) {
				op, err := deleteOp(cfg, in.ID, "/id")
				if err != nil {
					return change{}, err
				}
				return change{ops: []ufwOp{op}}, nil
			}
		},
		check: func(_ context.Context, _ core.Env, in RuleDeleteInput, cfg fwstate.Config) error {
			if len(findRules(cfg, in.ID)) > 0 {
				return mismatch("rule %s is still there after the change", in.ID)
			}
			return nil
		},
	})
}
```

```go
package firewall

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"regexp"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/model"
)

// RulesApplyInput is the input of firewall.rules.apply (v1): Darkpanel
// rules to add, with ids the caller chooses (ULIDs) and the batch's label
// as their comment, and rule ids to delete. A rule already present with
// the same definition, and an id already absent, are skipped, so run again
// with the same input it plans an empty diff (Converges).
type RulesApplyInput struct {
	core.Guarded
	Label  string       `json:"label,omitempty" jsonschema:"pattern=^[A-Za-z0-9 :._/-]{0\\,64}$" jsonschema_description:"The comment of every added rule, after the Darkpanel tag."`
	Add    []model.Rule `json:"add,omitempty" jsonschema_description:"Rules to add, each with its id and without a comment."`
	Delete []string     `json:"delete,omitempty" jsonschema_description:"Ids of rules to delete."`
	Manual bool         `json:"manual,omitempty" jsonschema_description:"Confirms deleting manual rules (spec 2.2)."`
}

var (
	ruleIDRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^([0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}|manual-[0-9a-f]{16})$`)
	ulidIDRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$`)
)

// batch validates a rules.apply input: each rule to add carries a ULID of
// its own, no comment (the label is its comment) and is Darkpanel's; ids
// are unique and none is both added and deleted; every id to delete is a
// rule id.
func batch(in RulesApplyInput) ([]model.Rule, error) {
	var fields []errcode.FieldError
	bad := func(path, msg string) { fields = append(fields, errcode.FieldError{Path: path, Message: msg}) }
	seen := map[string]bool{}
	var rules []model.Rule
	for i, r := range in.Add {
		path := fmt.Sprintf("/add/%d", i)
		switch {
		case !ulidIDRe.MatchString(r.ID):
			bad(path+"/id", "a rule to add carries its own ULID")
		case seen[r.ID]:
			bad(path+"/id", "the id is listed twice")
		}
		seen[r.ID] = true
		if r.Comment != "" {
			bad(path+"/comment", "the batch's label is every added rule's comment")
		}
		if len(fields) > 0 {
			continue
		}
		id := r.ID
		r.ID = ""
		nr, err := newRule(r, id, path)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		nr.Comment = in.Label
		if err := nr.Validate(); err != nil {
			return nil, fieldErrors(err, path)
		}
		rules = append(rules, nr)
	}
	for i, id := range in.Delete {
		path := fmt.Sprintf("/delete/%d", i)
		switch {
		case !ruleIDRe.MatchString(id):
			bad(path, "not a rule id")
		case seen[id]:
			bad(path, "the id is both added and deleted")
		}
	}
	if len(fields) > 0 {
		return nil, &errcode.Error{Code: errcode.InvalidInput, Detail: "the batch is invalid", Fields: fields}
	}
	return rules, nil
}

// rulesApply is firewall.rules.apply.
func (f fw) rulesApply() core.ActionDef {
	return defineMutation(core.ActionSpec{Name: "firewall.rules.apply", Summary: "Add and delete a batch of firewall rules.", Converges: true},
		mutation[RulesApplyInput]{
			f:       f,
			guarded: func(in RulesApplyInput) core.Guarded { return in.Guarded },
			manual:  func(in RulesApplyInput) bool { return in.Manual },
			build: func(_ context.Context, _ core.Env, in RulesApplyInput) buildFunc {
				return func(cfg fwstate.Config, _ fwstate.Loaded) (change, error) { return f.batchChange(cfg, in) }
			},
			check: func(_ context.Context, _ core.Env, in RulesApplyInput, cfg fwstate.Config) error {
				for _, r := range in.Add {
					if n := len(findRules(cfg, r.ID)); n != 1 {
						return mismatch("%d rules carry the id %s after the change, not 1", n, r.ID)
					}
				}
				for _, id := range in.Delete {
					if len(findRules(cfg, id)) > 0 {
						return mismatch("rule %s is still there after the change", id)
					}
				}
				return nil
			},
			finish: func(_ context.Context, _ core.Env, in RulesApplyInput, out *ChangeOutput) error {
				for _, r := range in.Add {
					out.Rules = append(out.Rules, r.ID)
				}
				return nil
			},
		})
}

// batchChange adds, in order, each rule not present yet, then deletes each
// rule still present. A rule present under its id with another definition
// is refused.
func (f fw) batchChange(cfg fwstate.Config, in RulesApplyInput) (change, error) {
	rules, err := batch(in)
	if err != nil {
		return change{}, err
	}
	var c change
	for i, r := range rules {
		path := fmt.Sprintf("/add/%d", i)
		switch groups := findRules(cfg, r.ID); {
		case len(groups) == 1 && ruleText(groups[0].Rule) == ruleText(r):
			continue
		case len(groups) > 0:
			return change{}, &errcode.Error{Code: errcode.InvalidInput, Detail: fmt.Sprintf("rule %s exists with another definition", r.ID),
				Fields: []errcode.FieldError{{Path: path, Message: "a rule with this id exists with another definition"}}}
		}
		op, next, err := f.addOp(cfg, r, path)
		if err != nil {
			return change{}, err
		}
		c.ops, cfg = append(c.ops, op), next
	}
	for i, id := range in.Delete {
		if len(findRules(cfg, id)) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		op, err := deleteOp(cfg, id, fmt.Sprintf("/delete/%d", i))
		if err != nil {
			return change{}, err
		}
		next, err := f.d.edit(cfg, op.Args)
		if err != nil {
			return change{}, errcode.New(errcode.InvalidInput, fmt.Sprintf("Darkpanel cannot predict deleting rule %s: %v", id, err))
		}
		c.ops, cfg = append(c.ops, op), next
	}
	return c, nil
}
```

```go
	ctx := context.Background()

	}
```

```go
package firewall

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
)

// SnapshotRestoreInput is the input of firewall.snapshot.restore (v1).
type SnapshotRestoreInput struct {
	core.Guarded
	ID     string `json:"id" jsonschema:"pattern=^[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$" jsonschema_description:"The snapshot's id, as firewall.snapshots lists it."`
	Manual bool   `json:"manual,omitempty" jsonschema_description:"Confirms the manual rules the restore adds or removes (spec 2.5)."`
}

// loadSnapshot reads snapshot id; an unknown id is invalid input at path.
func loadSnapshot(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, id, path string) (snapshot, error) {
	s, err := getSnapshot(ctx, env.DB, id)
	if errors.Is(err, errSnapshotNotFound) {
		return snapshot{}, &errcode.Error{Code: errcode.InvalidInput, Detail: fmt.Sprintf("no snapshot has the id %s", id),
			Fields: []errcode.FieldError{{Path: path, Message: "no snapshot has this id"}}}
	}
	return s, err
}

// snapshotRestore is firewall.snapshot.restore: bring a snapshot's files,
// UFW state and sysctl values back (spec 2.5), as journaled effects, so the
// restore itself is revertible from its own snapshot.
func (f fw) snapshotRestore() core.ActionDef {
	return defineMutation(core.ActionSpec{Name: "firewall.snapshot.restore", Summary: "Restore a firewall snapshot."}, mutation[SnapshotRestoreInput]{
		f:       f,
		guarded: func(in SnapshotRestoreInput) core.Guarded { return in.Guarded },
		manual:  func(in SnapshotRestoreInput) bool { return in.Manual },
		build: func(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, in SnapshotRestoreInput) buildFunc {
			return func(fwstate.Config, fwstate.Loaded) (change, error) {
				s, err := loadSnapshot(ctx, env, in.ID, "/id")
				if err != nil {
					return change{}, err
				}
				return change{restore: &s}, nil
			}
		},
		check: func(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, in SnapshotRestoreInput, cfg fwstate.Config) error {
			s, err := getSnapshot(ctx, env.DB, in.ID)
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			if cfg.Enabled != s.State.Enabled {
				return mismatch("UFW's ENABLED is %s after the restore, the snapshot's is %s", yesNo(cfg.Enabled), yesNo(s.State.Enabled))
			}
			return nil
		},
	})
}
```

```go
package firewall

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"maps"
	"slices"
	"time"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
)

// SnapshotList is the output of resource firewall.snapshots (v1): every
// logical snapshot, newest first.
type SnapshotList struct {
	Snapshots []SnapshotInfo `json:"snapshots"`
}

// SnapshotInfo is one logical snapshot (spec 2.5).
type SnapshotInfo struct {
	ID        string    `json:"id"`
	CreatedAt time.Time `json:"createdAt"`
	ChangeID  string    `json:"changeId,omitempty"` // the change it was taken before; empty until that change applied
	Actor     string    `json:"actor"`
	System    bool      `json:"system"`   // taken for a background task's change
	Pinned    bool      `json:"pinned"`   // kept while its change needs repair
	Baseline  bool      `json:"baseline"` // the host's first snapshot, never pruned
	Enabled   bool      `json:"enabled"`  // UFW's ENABLED in the snapshot
}

// SnapshotCompareInput is the input of firewall.snapshot.compare (v1): two
// snapshots, or one against the host now when to is omitted.
type SnapshotCompareInput struct {
	From string `json:"from" jsonschema:"pattern=^[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$" jsonschema_description:"The older snapshot's id."`
	To   string `json:"to,omitempty" jsonschema:"pattern=^[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$" jsonschema_description:"The newer snapshot's id; omitted: the host now."`
}

// SnapshotComparison is the output of firewall.snapshot.compare (v1): the
// changes from one state to the other as a plan lists them, and the state
// files whose hashes differ.
type SnapshotComparison struct {
	From  string          `json:"from"`
	To    string          `json:"to"` // a snapshot id, or "now"
	Diff  []core.DiffLine `json:"diff"`
	Files []FileChange    `json:"files"`
}

// FileChange is one state file whose content differs.
type FileChange struct {
	Path string `json:"path"`
	From string `json:"from"` // "sha256:<hex>", or "absent"
	To   string `json:"to"`
}

// readFunc is a read action's handler.
type readFunc[In, Out any] func(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, in In) (Out, error)

// Read runs the handler.
func (r readFunc[In, Out]) Read(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, in In) (Out, error) {
	return r(ctx, env, in)
}

// snapshots reads resource firewall.snapshots.
func (f fw) snapshots(ctx context.Context, env core.Env) (SnapshotList, error) {
	list, err := listSnapshots(ctx, env.DB, snapshotFilter{})
	if err != nil {
		return SnapshotList{}, err
	}
	out := SnapshotList{Snapshots: make([]SnapshotInfo, 0, len(list))}
	for _, s := range list {
		out.Snapshots = append(out.Snapshots, SnapshotInfo{
			ID: s.ID, CreatedAt: s.CreatedAt, ChangeID: s.ChangeID, Actor: s.Actor,
			System: s.System, Pinned: s.Pinned, Baseline: s.Baseline, Enabled: s.State.Enabled,
		})
	}
	return out, nil
}

// snapshotCompare is firewall.snapshot.compare.
func (f fw) snapshotCompare() core.ActionDef {
	return core.DefineRead[SnapshotCompareInput, SnapshotComparison](core.ActionSpec{
		Name: "firewall.snapshot.compare", Summary: "Compare two firewall snapshots, or one with the host now.", Version: 1, Side: core.SideAgent,
	}, readFunc[SnapshotCompareInput, SnapshotComparison](f.compareSnapshots))
}

// compareSnapshots compares two snapshots, or one with the host now.
func (f fw) compareSnapshots(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, in SnapshotCompareInput) (SnapshotComparison, error) {
	from, err := loadSnapshot(ctx, env, in.From, "/from")
	if err != nil {
		return SnapshotComparison{}, err
	}
	a, err := f.snapshotConfig(from)
	if err != nil {
		return SnapshotComparison{}, err
	}
	out := SnapshotComparison{From: from.ID, To: "now"}
	var b fwstate.Config
	var sysctl map[string]string
	if in.To != "" {
		to, err := loadSnapshot(ctx, env, in.To, "/to")
		if err != nil {
			return SnapshotComparison{}, err
		}
		if b, err = f.snapshotConfig(to); err != nil {
			return SnapshotComparison{}, err
		}
		out.To, sysctl = to.ID, to.State.Sysctl
	} else {
		if b, err = f.d.readConfig(f.d.root); err != nil {
			return SnapshotComparison{}, fmt.Errorf("firewall: read the configured state: %w", err)
		}
		st, err := f.d.readLoaded(ctx, env)
		if err != nil {
			return SnapshotComparison{}, fmt.Errorf("firewall: read the loaded state: %w", err)
		}
		sysctl = st.Sysctl
	}
	out.Diff = stateDiff(logical{cfg: a, sysctl: from.State.Sysctl}, logical{cfg: b, sysctl: sysctl})
	if out.Diff == nil {
		out.Diff = []core.DiffLine{}
	}
	out.Files = fileChanges(a.Files, b.Files)
	return out, nil
}

// fileChanges lists the state files whose hashes differ: fwstate.StateFiles
// in order, then any other file either side records.
func fileChanges(a, b map[string]core.RestoreEntry) []FileChange {
	paths := slices.Clone(fwstate.StateFiles)
	for _, m := range []map[string]core.RestoreEntry{a, b} {
		for _, p := range slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(m)) {
			if !slices.Contains(paths, p) {
				paths = append(paths, p)
			}
		}
	}
	out := []FileChange{}
	for _, p := range paths {
		if ha, hb := fileHash(a[p]), fileHash(b[p]); ha != hb {
			out = append(out, FileChange{Path: p, From: ha, To: hb})
		}
	}
	return out
}
```

```go
package firewall

import (

	"reflect"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/guard"
)

// rpRepaired is the change the repair tests repair.
const rpRepaired = "01J000000000000000000000R1"

// rpRun plans, snapshots and applies firewall.state.repair under env, then
// clears the host's differences (the reload repaired them) and verifies.
func rpRun(t *testing.T, h *fakeHost, f fw, env core.Env, raw string) (core.PlanOutcome, ChangeOutput) {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	def := f.stateRepair()
	if err := schema.NewValidator().ValidateInput(def, json.RawMessage(raw)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("input %s: %v", raw, err)
	}
	planEnv := env
	planEnv.ChangeID = ""
	plan, err := def.Handler.Plan(ctx, planEnv, json.RawMessage(raw))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("plan: %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := def.Handler.Snapshot(ctx, env, json.RawMessage(raw)); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	res, err := def.Handler.Apply(ctx, env, json.RawMessage(raw))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("apply: %v", err)
	}
	h.diffs = nil
	if err := def.Handler.Verify(ctx, env, json.RawMessage(raw), res); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("verify: %v", err)
	}
	var out ChangeOutput
	if err := json.Unmarshal(res, &out); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return plan, out
}

// rpTarget gives the repair tests a repaired change whose snapshot is the
// host now, pinned, and returns its id.
func rpTarget(t *testing.T, h *fakeHost, f fw) string {
	t.Helper()
	id := snCapture(t, h, f)
	if err := attachSnapshot(context.Background(), h.db, id, rpRepaired); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := setPinned(context.Background(), h.db, id, true); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return id
}

// TestRepairDirect: run on its own, the repair reloads UFW from its
// configuration on a host out of sync in UFW's chains, its guard runs and
// its snapshot holds the loaded-state before-image.
func TestRepairDirect(t *testing.T) {
	h, f, env := ruHost(t)
	h.diffs = []fwstate.ChainDiff{{Family: fwstate.V4, Table: "filter", Chain: "ufw-user-input", OnlyB: []string{"-j ACCEPT"}}}
	plan, out := rpRun(t, h, f, env, `{}`)
	if len(plan.Guards) != 1 || !plan.Guards[0].OK || !strings.HasPrefix(acDiff(plan)[0], "  out of sync: v4 filter/ufw-user-input") {
		t.Errorf("plan %+v, want the differing chain and a passing guard", plan)
	}
	if out.RepairOutcome != "" {
		t.Errorf("output %+v, want no repair outcome", out)
	}
	snap, err := getSnapshot(context.Background(), h.db, out.Snapshot)
	if err != nil || snap.State.Image == nil {
		t.Errorf("snapshot %+v (%v), want a before-image", snap.State, err)
	}
	if got := hkEffects(h); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, []string{"firewall.state:enabled made"}) {
		t.Errorf("effects %v, want the reload", got)
	}
	_, err = f.stateRepair().Handler.Plan(context.Background(), env, json.RawMessage(`{"outcome":"keep"}`))
	if e := errcode.From(err); e.Code != errcode.InvalidInput || len(e.Fields) != 1 || e.Fields[0].Path != "/outcome" {
		t.Errorf("an outcome without a repaired change = %v, want an invalid input at /outcome", err)
	}
	if def := f.stateRepair(); def.Spec.RepairedBy != "firewall.state.repair" || def.Spec.Guards[0].ID != guard.GuardID {
		t.Errorf("spec %+v", def.Spec)
	}
}

// TestRepairRestore: repairing a change, outcome restore (the default)
// returns the host to the change's snapshot, reports restored and unpins
// the snapshot.
func TestRepairRestore(t *testing.T) {
	h, f, env := ruHost(t)
	id := rpTarget(t, h, f)
	s := h.state()
	s.Rules4, s.Rules6 = s.Rules4[1:], nil
	h.setState(s)
	env.Call.RepairOf = rpRepaired
	plan, out := rpRun(t, h, f, env, `{}`)
	if len(plan.Diff) != 1 || !strings.Contains(plan.Diff[0].Text, fhTag) || plan.Diff[0].Op != "+" {
		t.Errorf("diff %q, want the rule the restore brings back", acDiff(plan))
	}
	if out.RepairOutcome != "restored" || len(findRules(h.config(), fhTag)) != 1 {
		t.Errorf("output %+v, want restored with the rule back", out)
	}
	if snap, _ := getSnapshot(context.Background(), h.db, id); snap.Pinned {
		t.Error("the repaired change's snapshot is still pinned")
	}
}

// TestRepairKeep: outcome keep reloads UFW from the files the change left,
// only while they still hash as it recorded them, and reports kept.
func TestRepairKeep(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h, f, env := ruHost(t)
	id := rpTarget(t, h, f)
	env.Call.RepairOf = rpRepaired
	_, err := f.stateRepair().Handler.Plan(ctx, env, json.RawMessage(`{"outcome":"keep"}`))
	if e := errcode.From(err); e.Code != errcode.InvalidInput || !strings.Contains(e.Detail, "no post-apply state") {
		t.Errorf("keep without post-apply hashes = %v, want an invalid input", err)
	}
	if err := setPostHashes(ctx, h.db, id, fileHashes(h.config().Files)); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	_, out := rpRun(t, h, f, env, `{"outcome":"keep"}`)
	if out.RepairOutcome != "kept" {
		t.Errorf("output %+v, want kept", out)
	}

	s := h.state()
	s.LogLevel = "full"
	h.setState(s)
	_, err = f.stateRepair().Handler.Plan(ctx, env, json.RawMessage(`{"outcome":"keep"}`))
	if e := errcode.From(err); e.Code != errcode.InvalidInput || !strings.Contains(e.Detail, "/etc/ufw/ufw.conf") {
		t.Errorf("keep with a changed file = %v, want an invalid input naming it", err)
	}
	err = f.stateRepair().Handler.Verify(ctx, env, json.RawMessage(`{"outcome":"keep"}`), json.RawMessage(`{}`))
	if errcode.From(err).Code != errcode.FirewallPredictionMismatch {
		t.Errorf("verify keep with a changed file = %v, want a prediction mismatch", err)
	}
	env.Call.RepairOf = "01J000000000000000000000R9"
	if _, err := f.stateRepair().Handler.Plan(ctx, env, json.RawMessage(`{}`)); err == nil {
		t.Error("repairing a change without a snapshot plans")
	}
}
```

```go
package firewall

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"maps"
	"slices"
	"strings"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
)

// The repair outcomes (spec 1.3, 2.5).
const (
	outcomeRestore = "restore"
	outcomeKeep    = "keep"
)

// RepairInput is the input of firewall.state.repair (v1). Repairing a
// change (darkpanel change repair), outcome restore, the default, returns
// the host to the change's snapshot, and keep brings UFW's loaded state to
// the files the change left. Run on its own, the repair takes no outcome
// and reloads UFW from its configuration.
type RepairInput struct {
	core.Guarded
	Outcome string `json:"outcome,omitempty" jsonschema:"enum=restore,enum=keep" jsonschema_description:"Repairing a change: restore (the default) or keep."`
}

// stateRepair is firewall.state.repair (spec 2.3, 2.5): from the actual
// loaded state to a target, allowed on a host out of sync in UFW's and
// Darkpanel's own chains, with a loaded-state before-image in its snapshot.
// It is every firewall action's RepairedBy, its own included (owner ruling
// R1).
func (f fw) stateRepair() core.ActionDef {
	return defineMutation(core.ActionSpec{Name: repairAction, Summary: "Repair the firewall: bring UFW's loaded state to its target."}, mutation[RepairInput]{
		f:       f,
		image:   true,
		guarded: func(in RepairInput) core.Guarded { return in.Guarded },
		build: func(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, in RepairInput) buildFunc {
			return func(cfg fwstate.Config, _ fwstate.Loaded) (change, error) { return repairChange(ctx, env, in, cfg) }
		},
		check: func(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, in RepairInput, cfg fwstate.Config) error {
			if env.Call.RepairOf == "" {
				return nil
			}
			s, err := repairedSnapshot(ctx, env)
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			if in.Outcome == outcomeKeep {
				if paths := changedFiles(cfg, s.PostHashes); len(paths) > 0 {
					return mismatch("%s differ from what change %s left", strings.Join(paths, ", "), env.Call.RepairOf)
				}
				return nil
			}
			if cfg.Enabled != s.State.Enabled {
				return mismatch("UFW's ENABLED is %s after the repair, the snapshot's is %s", yesNo(cfg.Enabled), yesNo(s.State.Enabled))
			}
			return nil
		},
		finish: func(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, in RepairInput, out *ChangeOutput) error {
			if env.Call.RepairOf == "" {
				return nil
			}
			out.RepairOutcome = "restored"
			if in.Outcome == outcomeKeep {
				out.RepairOutcome = "kept"
			}
			if err := unpinChangeSnapshot(ctx, env, env.Call.RepairOf); err != nil {
				env.Log.Warn("firewall: cannot unpin the repaired change's snapshot", "change", env.Call.RepairOf, "error", err)
			}
			return nil
		},
	})
}

// repairChange is the repair's change. Without a repaired change it reloads
// (or stops) UFW from its configuration. Repairing a change, restore brings
// the change's snapshot back, and keep reloads UFW from the files the
// change left, which must still hash as it recorded them right after it
// applied.
func repairChange(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, in RepairInput, cfg fwstate.Config) (change, error) {
	refuse := func(msg string) error {
		return &errcode.Error{Code: errcode.InvalidInput, Detail: msg, Fields: []errcode.FieldError{{Path: "/outcome", Message: msg}}}
	}
	if env.Call.RepairOf == "" {
		if in.Outcome != "" {
			return change{}, refuse("only the repair of a change takes an outcome")
		}
		return change{repair: true}, nil
	}
	s, err := repairedSnapshot(ctx, env)
	if err != nil {
		return change{}, err
	}
	if in.Outcome == "" || in.Outcome == outcomeRestore {
		return change{repair: true, restore: &s}, nil
	}
	if s.PostHashes == nil {
		return change{}, refuse(fmt.Sprintf("change %s recorded no post-apply state; repair it with outcome restore", env.Call.RepairOf))
	}
	if paths := changedFiles(cfg, s.PostHashes); len(paths) > 0 {
		return change{}, refuse(fmt.Sprintf("%s differ from what change %s left; repair it with outcome restore",
			strings.Join(paths, ", "), env.Call.RepairOf))
	}
	return change{repair: true}, nil
}

// repairedSnapshot is the snapshot of the change the repair repairs.
func repairedSnapshot(ctx context.Context, env core.Env) (snapshot, error) {
	id, err := snapshotOfChange(ctx, env.DB, env.Call.RepairOf)
	if err != nil {
		return snapshot{}, fmt.Errorf("firewall: the snapshot of change %s: %w", env.Call.RepairOf, err)
	}
	return getSnapshot(ctx, env.DB, id)
}

// changedFiles lists the files whose hashes differ from want, sorted.
func changedFiles(cfg fwstate.Config, want map[string]string) []string {
	var out []string
	for _, p := range slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(want)) {
		if fileHash(cfg.Files[p]) != want[p] {
			out = append(out, p)
		}
	}
	return out
}
```

**Lenses:** security

The firewall's uninstall step (spec 1.11, 2.9) with the option `rules`: `remove` (default) deletes every Darkpanel rule and keeps manual ones, `keep` leaves every rule, `baseline` logs the manual rules it adds or removes and restores the baseline snapshot. A host without UFW, a host without a baseline and a second run do nothing more.

Create `internal/modules/firewall/uninstall_test.go`:

```go
package firewall

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"log/slog"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
)

// unSetup is a fake host with ufw installed, the module over it and an env
// as uninstall builds it (no change, no journal) whose log is returned.
func unSetup(t *testing.T) (*fakeHost, module, core.Env, *bytes.Buffer) {
	t.Helper()
	h, f, _ := ruHost(t)
	h.writeFile(ufwPath, []byte("#!/bin/sh\n"))
	var log bytes.Buffer
	env := core.Env{DB: h.db, Exec: h, Files: h, Clock: h.clock, Log: slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(&log, nil))}
	return h, module{f: f}, env, &log
}

func unRan(h *fakeHost, from int) []string {
	var out []string
	for _, c := range h.calls[from:] {
		if v, ok := strings.CutPrefix(c, "run /usr/sbin/ufw "); ok {
			out = append(out, v)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// TestUninstallOptions: the module declares the option rules (spec 2.9).
func TestUninstallOptions(t *testing.T) {
	var _ core.Uninstaller = module{}
	got := module{}.UninstallOptions()
	if len(got) != 1 || got[0].Key != "rules" || !reflect.DeepEqual(got[0].Values, []string{"remove", "keep", "baseline"}) ||
		got[0].Default != "remove" || got[0].Help == "" {
		t.Errorf("options %+v, want rules=remove|keep|baseline, default remove", got)
	}
}

// TestUninstallRemove: remove deletes every Darkpanel rule, keeps manual
// rules and reloads an active UFW; run again it does nothing.
func TestUninstallRemove(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h, m, env, _ := unSetup(t)
	n := len(h.calls)
	if err := m.Uninstall(ctx, env, false, map[string]string{"rules": "remove"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got := unRan(h, n); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, []string{"delete allow in proto tcp from any to any port 22", "reload"}) {
		t.Errorf("ran %q, want the Darkpanel rule deleted and a reload", got)
	}
	if s := h.state(); !reflect.DeepEqual(s.Rules4, []string{fhRule3000v4}) || len(s.Rules6) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("rules %+v %+v, want only the manual rule", s.Rules4, s.Rules6)
	}
	n = len(h.calls)
	if err := m.Uninstall(ctx, env, false, map[string]string{"rules": "remove"}); err != nil || len(unRan(h, n)) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("a second uninstall = %v and ran %q, want nothing", err, unRan(h, n))
	}
}

// TestUninstallKeepAndRefusals: keep runs nothing; a host without UFW has
// nothing to do; an unknown value is an error.
func TestUninstallKeepAndRefusals(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h, m, env, _ := unSetup(t)
	n := len(h.calls)
	if err := m.Uninstall(ctx, env, true, map[string]string{"rules": "keep"}); err != nil || len(h.calls) != n {
		t.Errorf("keep = %v and ran %q, want nothing", err, h.calls[n:])
	}
	if err := m.Uninstall(ctx, env, false, map[string]string{"rules": "all"}); err == nil {
		t.Error("rules=all is accepted")
	}
	h2, m2, env2, _ := unSetup(t)
	pfRemove(t, h2.root, ufwPath)
	for _, v := range []string{"remove", "baseline"} {
		if err := m2.Uninstall(ctx, env2, false, map[string]string{"rules": v}); err != nil || len(h2.calls) != 0 {
			t.Errorf("rules=%s without UFW = %v and ran %q, want nothing", v, err, h2.calls)
		}
	}
}

// TestUninstallBaseline: baseline logs the manual rules the restore adds
// or removes, restores the baseline snapshot, and does it again when run
// again; without a baseline it does nothing.
func TestUninstallBaseline(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h, m, env, log := unSetup(t)
	if err := m.Uninstall(ctx, env, false, map[string]string{"rules": "baseline"}); err != nil || len(h.calls) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("baseline without a snapshot = %v and ran %q, want nothing", err, h.calls)
	}
	snCapture(t, h, m.f)
	before := h.state()
	s := h.state()
	s.Rules4 = []string{fhRule22v4}
	h.setState(s)

	for range 2 {
		if err := m.Uninstall(ctx, env, false, map[string]string{"rules": "baseline"}); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if !reflect.DeepEqual(h.state(), before) {
			t.Errorf("state %+v, want the baseline's %+v", h.state(), before)
		}
	}
	if !strings.Contains(log.String(), "adds the manual rule") || !strings.Contains(log.String(), "port 3000") {
		t.Errorf("log %q, want the manual rule the restore adds", log.String())
	}
}
```

```go
package firewall

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/model"
)

// The values of the uninstall option rules (spec 2.9).
const (
	rulesRemove   = "remove"
	rulesKeep     = "keep"
	rulesBaseline = "baseline"
)

// UninstallOptions declares the option rules (spec 1.11, 2.9).
func (module) UninstallOptions() []core.UninstallOption {
	return []core.UninstallOption{{
		Key: "rules", Values: []string{rulesRemove, rulesKeep, rulesBaseline}, Default: rulesRemove,
		Help: "remove deletes Darkpanel's rules and keeps manual ones; keep leaves every rule; baseline restores the firewall as it was before Darkpanel's first change",
	}}
}

// Uninstall applies the option rules (spec 2.9) and does nothing on a host
// without UFW. It succeeds again on a host where it already ran: remove
// finds no Darkpanel rule left, and baseline restores the same snapshot
// again. keepData does not change it: rules are the host's firewall, not
// Darkpanel's data.
func (m module) Uninstall(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, _ bool, opts map[string]string) error {
	v := opts["rules"]
	if v != rulesRemove && v != rulesKeep && v != rulesBaseline {
		return fmt.Errorf("firewall: uninstall option rules=%q is not remove, keep or baseline", v)
	}
	if v == rulesKeep {
		return nil
	}
	if err := m.f.regular(ufwPath); err != nil {
		var missing missingFile
		if errors.As(err, &missing) {
			env.Log.Info("firewall: UFW is not installed; the uninstall leaves the firewall as it is")
			return nil
		}
		return fmt.Errorf("firewall: uninstall: %w", err)
	}
	if v == rulesBaseline {
		return m.f.restoreBaseline(ctx, env)
	}
	return m.f.removeRules(ctx, env)
}

// removeRules deletes every Darkpanel rule, then reloads an active UFW. A
// tagged rule the model cannot express cannot be deleted by its arguments
// and is left, with a warning.
func (f fw) removeRules(ctx context.Context, env core.Env) error {
	cfg, err := f.d.readConfig(f.d.root)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("firewall: uninstall: %w", err)
	}
	deleted := 0
	for _, r := range model.Merge(cfg.Rules4, cfg.Rules6) {
		switch {
		case r.Origin != model.OriginDarkpanel:
			continue
		case r.Raw != "":
			env.Log.Warn("firewall: the uninstall leaves a Darkpanel rule it cannot express", "rule", r.ID, "tuple", r.Raw)
			continue
		}
		if err := ufw(ctx, env, model.DeleteArgs(r)); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("firewall: uninstall: delete rule %s: %w", r.ID, err)
		}
		env.Log.Info("firewall: the uninstall deleted a Darkpanel rule", "rule", ruleText(r))
		deleted++
	}
	if deleted > 0 && cfg.Enabled {
		return ufw(ctx, env, reloadArgs)
	}
	return nil
}

// restoreBaseline restores the baseline snapshot, the host's first, taken
// before Darkpanel's first change, after logging every manual rule the
// restore adds or removes. Without a baseline there is nothing to restore.
func (f fw) restoreBaseline(ctx context.Context, env core.Env) error {
	list, err := listSnapshots(ctx, env.DB, snapshotFilter{})
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("firewall: uninstall: %w", err)
	}
	var id string
	for _, s := range list {
		if s.Baseline {
			id = s.ID
		}
	}
	if id == "" {
		env.Log.Info("firewall: no baseline snapshot; the uninstall leaves the firewall as it is")
		return nil
	}
	snap, err := getSnapshot(ctx, env.DB, id)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("firewall: uninstall: %w", err)
	}
	cfgB, err := f.snapshotConfig(snap)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("firewall: uninstall: %w", err)
	}
	cur, err := f.d.readConfig(f.d.root)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("firewall: uninstall: %w", err)
	}
	from, to := model.Merge(cur.Rules4, cur.Rules6), model.Merge(cfgB.Rules4, cfgB.Rules6)
	inFrom, inTo := ruleTexts(from), ruleTexts(to)
	for _, r := range from {
		if r.Origin == model.OriginManual && !inTo[ruleText(r)] {
			env.Log.Info("firewall: restoring the baseline removes the manual rule", "rule", ruleText(r))
		}
	}
	for _, r := range to {
		if r.Origin == model.OriginManual && !inFrom[ruleText(r)] {
			env.Log.Info("firewall: restoring the baseline adds the manual rule", "rule", ruleText(r))
		}
	}
	rep, err := restore(ctx, env, f.d, snap)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("firewall: uninstall: restore the baseline snapshot %s: %w", id, err)
	}
	logVanished(env, rep.Vanished)
	return nil
}
```

```go
			t.Errorf("%s spec %+v", a.Ref(), s)
		}
	}
	want := []string{"firewall.state.enable", "firewall.state.disable", "firewall.state.repair", "firewall.defaults.set",
		"firewall.logging.set", "firewall.rules.apply", "firewall.rule.add", "firewall.rule.delete",
		"firewall.snapshot.restore", "firewall.snapshot.compare"}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(names, want) {
		t.Errorf("actions %v, want %v", names, want)
	}
	var resources []string
	for _, r := range m.Resources {
		resources = append(resources, r.Name)
		if _, err := schema.ResourceSnapshot(r); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("%s: %v", r.Name, err)
		}
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(resources, []string{"firewall.status", "firewall.snapshots"}) {
		t.Errorf("resources %v", resources)
	}
}
```

```go
// Package firewall is the UFW firewall module (spec section 2): rules, safe
// apply, snapshots, the Docker integration and the exposure view.
package firewall

import (
	"io/fs"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
)

// ID is the module id.
const ID = "firewall"

// controllerUnit is the controller's unit, whose state tells the guard
// whether a controller runs on this host (owner ruling R3).
const controllerUnit = "darkpanel-controller.service"

// ufwSysctlFile is the only sysctl file UFW may apply that Darkpanel
// supports; snapshots restore it.
const ufwSysctlFile = "/etc/ufw/sysctl.conf"

// sysctlKeys are the supported sysctl keys of spec 2.1 with the values
// Darkpanel writes back; <iface> is all, default or an interface.
var sysctlKeys = []struct{ key, pattern string }{
	{"net/ipv4/ip_forward", "^[01]$"},
	{"net/ipv6/conf/<iface>/forwarding", "^[01]$"},
	{"net/ipv6/conf/<iface>/accept_ra", "^[012]$"},
	{"net/ipv4/conf/<iface>/rp_filter", "^[012]$"},
	{"net/ipv4/conf/<iface>/accept_source_route", "^[01]$"},
}

type module struct{ f fw }

// Module returns the firewall module over this host.
func Module() core.Module { return module{f: productionFW()} }

// Manifest declares the module. Every module is enabled by default;
// preflight decides whether it is available on a host (R9).
func (m module) Manifest() core.Manifest {
	return core.Manifest{
		ID:             ID,
		Version:        1,
		DefaultEnabled: true,
		Actions:        m.f.actions(),
		Resources:      m.f.resources(),
		Preflight:      m.f.preflight(),
		OwnedPaths:     ownedPaths(),
		Migrations:     map[core.Side]fs.FS{core.SideAgent: agentMigrations()},
		ExternalUnits:  []core.ExternalUnit{{Name: controllerUnit, Ops: []string{core.UnitOpState}}},
	}
}

// ownedPaths are the files a snapshot restores (kind restore: UFW's state
// files and its sysctl file, which uninstall never removes) and the sysctl
// keys a restore writes back.
func ownedPaths() []core.OwnedPath {
	var out []core.OwnedPath
	for _, p := range append(append([]string(nil), fwstate.StateFiles...), ufwSysctlFile) {
		out = append(out, core.OwnedPath{Path: p, Kind: core.OwnedRestore})
	}
	for _, k := range sysctlKeys {
		out = append(out, core.OwnedPath{Path: k.key, Kind: core.OwnedSysctl, Pattern: k.pattern})
	}
	return out
}

// actions are the firewall's actions (section 5): every mutating one
// revertible under the firewall lock and repaired by firewall.state.repair,
// and the read firewall.snapshot.compare.
func (f fw) actions() []core.ActionDef {
	return []core.ActionDef{
		f.stateEnable(), f.stateDisable(), f.stateRepair(), f.defaultsSet(), f.loggingSet(),
		f.rulesApply(), f.ruleAdd(), f.ruleDelete(), f.snapshotRestore(), f.snapshotCompare(),
	}
}

// resources are firewall.status and firewall.snapshots.
func (f fw) resources() []core.ResourceDef {
	return []core.ResourceDef{core.DefineResource(ID+".status", f.status), core.DefineResource(ID+".snapshots", f.snapshots)}
}
```

```go
package firewall

// e2eGolden is the golden capture the end-to-end tests start from (part
// F2's, ubuntu:24.04, UFW 0.36.2).
const e2eGolden = "testdata/golden/ubuntu-24.04"

// e2eSSHRule is the Darkpanel rule of the golden "rules" scenario that
// allows SSH (tcp 22, label "ssh").
const e2eSSHRule = "01J00000000000000000000000"

// e2eHost is a whole host for the end-to-end tests: UFW's files, a golden
// capture's, under a temporary root, read by the real conf.Read; the
// kernel's tables, first read by the real loaded.Reader from the capture's
// save output and afterwards changed only by ufw runs, as part P's
// predictor models UFW; the live sysctl values; and a network on which
// sshd holds a session from 203.0.113.7 to 192.0.2.1:22 on eth0. It
// implements core.Runner and core.FileWriter.
type e2eHost struct {
	t      *testing.T
	root   string
	db     *store.DB
	golden string // the capture the kernel's tables are read from
	loaded fwstate.Loaded
	sysctl map[string]string
	ran    []string // the ufw argument vectors run, in order
	clock  *coretest.FakeClock
}

// newE2EHost builds a host from the golden scenario files (UFW's files and
// sysctl values) whose kernel holds the tables of scenario tables.
func newE2EHost(t *testing.T, files, tables string) *e2eHost {
	t.Helper()
	h := &e2eHost{t: t, root: t.TempDir(), db: fwTestDB(t), golden: filepath.Join(e2eGolden, tables), sysctl: map[string]string{},
		clock: coretest.NewFakeClock(time.Date(2026, 10, 24, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC))}
	src := filepath.Join(e2eGolden, files, "files")
	err := filepath.WalkDir(src, func(p string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
		if err != nil || d.IsDir() {
			return err
		}
		data, err := os.ReadFile(p) //nolint:gosec // G304: a golden capture under testdata
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		rel, _ := filepath.Rel(src, p)
		h.write("/"+filepath.ToSlash(rel), data)
		return nil
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	data, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(e2eGolden, files, "sysctl.txt")) //nolint:gosec // G304: a golden capture under testdata
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	sc := bufio.NewScanner(bytes.NewReader(data))
	for sc.Scan() {
		if k, v, ok := strings.Cut(sc.Text(), "="); ok && !strings.Contains(k, "/lo/") {
			h.sysctl[k] = v
		}
	}
	r := loaded.Reader{
		Interfaces:     func() ([]netstat.Interface, error) { return e2eNet{}.Interfaces() },
		NFTablesLoaded: func() bool { return false },
	}
	st, err := r.Read(context.Background(), core.Env{Exec: h, Files: h})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read the golden loaded state: %v", err)
	}
	if len(st.Unsupported) > 0 {
		t.Fatalf("golden loaded state unsupported: %v", st.Unsupported)
	}
	st.Sysctl = nil
	h.loaded = st
	return h
}

func (h *e2eHost) write(p string, data []byte) {
	h.t.Helper()
	full := filepath.Join(h.root, p)
	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(full), 0o750); err != nil {
		h.t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(full, data, 0o644); err != nil { //nolint:gosec // G306: UFW's files are world-readable
		h.t.Fatal(err)
	}
}

func (h *e2eHost) config() fwstate.Config {
	h.t.Helper()
	cfg, err := conf.Read(h.root)
	if err != nil {
		h.t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return cfg
}

// Run answers the loaded-state reader from the golden capture and runs ufw
// as the predictor models it: the command's edit of the files, then, for a
// transition, its prediction of the kernel's tables and sysctl values.
func (h *e2eHost) Run(_ context.Context, cmd core.Cmd) (core.CmdResult, error) {
	switch {
	case strings.HasSuffix(cmd.Path, "tables") && len(cmd.Args) == 1 && cmd.Args[0] == "--version":
		v, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(h.golden, "version.txt"))
		if err != nil {
			return core.CmdResult{}, err
		}
		line, _, _ := strings.Cut(string(v), "\n")
		return core.CmdResult{Stdout: []byte(strings.Replace(line, "iptables", filepath.Base(cmd.Path), 1) + "\n")}, nil
	case strings.HasSuffix(cmd.Path, "-nft-save") && len(cmd.Args) == 2 && cmd.Args[0] == "-t":
		fam := "v4"
		if strings.Contains(cmd.Path, "ip6tables") {
			fam = "v6"
		}
		out, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(h.golden, "save", "nft-"+fam+"-"+cmd.Args[1]+".txt")) //nolint:gosec // G304: a golden capture under testdata
		return core.CmdResult{Stdout: out}, err
	case cmd.Path == ufwPath:
		return h.ufw(cmd.Args), nil
	}
	return core.CmdResult{}, fmt.Errorf("e2e: %s %v is not modelled: %w", cmd.Path, cmd.Args, fs.ErrNotExist)
}

func (h *e2eHost) ufw(args []string) core.CmdResult {
	h.ran = append(h.ran, strings.Join(args, " "))
	cfg := h.config()
	next, err := predict.Edit(cfg, args)
	if err != nil {
		return core.CmdResult{ExitCode: 1, Stderr: []byte("ERROR: " + err.Error() + "\n")}
	}
	for p, e := range next.Files {
		if e.Present && !bytes.Equal(e.Data, cfg.Files[p].Data) {
			h.write(p, e.Data)
		}
	}
	tr := fwstate.TransNone
	switch strings.Join(args, " ") {
	case "reload":
		if cfg.Enabled {
			tr = fwstate.TransReload
		}
	case "--force enable":
		if chainOf(h.loaded.V4, "filter", "ufw-user-input") == nil {
			tr = fwstate.TransEnable
		}
	case "disable":
		tr = fwstate.TransDisable
	}
	if tr == fwstate.TransNone {
		return core.CmdResult{}
	}
	pred, err := predict.Predict(cfg, h.loaded, tr)
	if err != nil {
		return core.CmdResult{ExitCode: 1, Stderr: []byte("ERROR: " + err.Error() + "\n")}
	}
	sysctl, err := loaded.PredictSysctl(next, h.sysctl, tr)
	if err != nil {
		return core.CmdResult{ExitCode: 1, Stderr: []byte("ERROR: " + err.Error() + "\n")}
	}
	pred.Sysctl, h.loaded, h.sysctl = nil, pred, sysctl
	return core.CmdResult{}
}
```
